text_en: There was a man in the land of Hus, whose name was Job, and that man was simple and upright, and fearing God , and avoiding evil .
text_la: Vir erat in terra Hus, nomine Job : et erat vir ille simplex, et rectus, ac timens Deum, et recedens a malo.
text_pt: Havia um homem na terra de Uz, cujo nome era Jó; e era este homem íntegro, reto e temente a Deus e desviava-se do mal.
text_el: ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν ἐν χώρᾳ τῇ Αυσίτιδι ᾧ ὄνομα Ιωβ καὶ ἦν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ἀληθινός ἄμεμπτος δίκαιος θεοσεβής ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ παντὸς πονηροῦ πράγματος

text_en: And there were born to him seven sons and three daughters.
text_la: Natique sunt ei septem filii, et tres filiæ.
text_pt: E nasceram-lhe sete filhos e três filhas.
text_el: ἐγένοντο δὲ αὐτῷ υἱοὶ ἑπτὰ καὶ θυγατέρες τρεῖς

text_en: And his possession was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a family exceedingly great: and this man was great among all the people of the east.
text_la: Et fuit possessio ejus septem millia ovium, et tria millia camelorum, quingenta quoque juga boum, et quingentæ asinæ, ac familia multa nimis : eratque vir ille magnus inter omnes orientales.
text_pt: E o seu gado era de sete mil ovelhas, três mil camelos, quinhentas juntas de bois e quinhentas jumentas; eram também muitíssimos os servos a seu serviço, de maneira que este homem era maior do que todos os do oriente.
text_el: καὶ ἦν τὰ κτήνη αὐτοῦ πρόβατα ἑπτακισχίλια κάμηλοι τρισχίλιαι ζεύγη βοῶν πεντακόσια ὄνοι θήλειαι νομάδες πεντακόσιαι καὶ ὑπηρεσία πολλὴ σφόδρα καὶ ἔργα μεγάλα ἦν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἦν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος εὐγενὴς τῶν ἀφ' ἡλίου ἀνατολῶν

text_en: And his sons went, and made a feast by houses, every one in his day. And sending, they called their three sisters, to eat and drink with them.
text_la: Et ibant filii ejus, et faciebant convivium per domos, unusquisque in die suo. Et mittentes vocabant tres sorores suas, ut comederent et biberent cum eis.
text_pt: E iam seus filhos à casa uns dos outros e faziam banquetes cada um por sua vez; e mandavam convidar as suas três irmãs a comerem e beberem com eles.
text_el: συμπορευόμενοι δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἐποιοῦσαν πότον καθ' ἑκάστην ἡμέραν συμπαραλαμβάνοντες ἅμα καὶ τὰς τρεῖς ἀδελφὰς αὐτῶν ἐσθίειν καὶ πίνειν μετ' αὐτῶν

text_en: And when the days of their feasting had gone about, Job sent to them, and sanctified them: and rising up early, offered holocausts for every one of them. For he said: Lest perhaps my sons have sinned , and have blessed God in their hearts. So did Job all days.
text_la: Cumque in orbem transissent dies convivii, mittebat ad eos Job, et sanctificabat illos : consurgensque diluculo, offerebat holocausta pro singulis. Dicebat enim : Ne forte peccaverint filii mei, et benedixerint Deo in cordibus suis. Sic faciebat Job cunctis diebus.
text_pt: Sucedia, pois, que, decorrido o turno de dias de seus banquetes, enviava Jó, e os santificava, e se levantava de madrugada, e oferecia holocaustos segundo o número de todos eles; porque dizia Jó: Porventura pecaram meus filhos, e amaldiçoaram a Deus no seu coração. Assim fazia Jó continuamente.
text_el: καὶ ὡς ἂν συνετελέσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ πότου ἀπέστελλεν Ιωβ καὶ ἐκαθάριζεν αὐτοὺς ἀνιστάμενος τὸ πρωὶ καὶ προσέφερεν περὶ αὐτῶν θυσίας κατὰ τὸν ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν καὶ μόσχον ἕνα περὶ ἁμαρτίας περὶ τῶν ψυχῶν αὐτῶν ἔλεγεν γὰρ Ιωβ μήποτε οἱ υἱοί μου ἐν τῇ διανοίᾳ αὐτῶν κακὰ ἐνενόησαν πρὸς θεόν οὕτως οὖν ἐποίει Ιωβ πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας

text_en: Now on a certain day, when the sons of God came to stand before the Lord , Satan also was present among them.
text_la: Quadam autem die, cum venissent filii Dei ut assisterent coram Domino, affuit inter eos etiam Satan.
text_pt: E num dia em que os filhos de Deus vieram apresentar-se perante o Senhor, veio também Satanás entre eles.
text_el: καὶ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡ ἡμέρα αὕτη καὶ ἰδοὺ ἦλθον οἱ ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ παραστῆναι ἐνώπιον τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ὁ διάβολος ἦλθεν μετ' αὐτῶν

text_en: And the Lord said to him: Where are you coming from? And he answered and said: I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it.
text_la: Cui dixit Dominus : Unde venis? Qui respondens, ait : Circuivi terram, et perambulavi eam.
text_pt: Então o Senhor disse a Satanás: Donde vens? E Satanás respondeu ao Senhor, e disse: De rodear a terra, e passear por ela.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ διαβόλῳ πόθεν παραγέγονας καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ διάβολος τῷ κυρίῳ εἶπεν περιελθὼν τὴν γῆν καὶ ἐμπεριπατήσας τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανὸν πάρειμι

text_en: And the Lord said to him: Have you considered my servant, Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a simple and upright man , and fearing God , and avoiding evil ?
text_la: Dixitque Dominus ad eum : Numquid considerasti servum meum Job, quod non sit ei similis in terra, homo simplex et rectus, ac timens Deum, et recedens a malo?
text_pt: E disse o Senhor a Satanás: Observaste tu a meu servo Jó? Porque ninguém há na terra semelhante a ele, homem íntegro e reto, temente a Deus, e que se desvia do mal.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος προσέσχες τῇ διανοίᾳ σου κατὰ τοῦ παιδός μου Ιωβ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν κατ' αὐτὸν τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἄνθρωπος ἄμεμπτος ἀληθινός θεοσεβής ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ παντὸς πονηροῦ πράγματος

text_en: And Satan answering, said: Does Job fear God in vain?
text_la: Cui respondens Satan, ait : Numquid Job frustra timet Deum?
text_pt: Então respondeu Satanás ao Senhor, e disse: Porventura teme Jó a Deus debalde?
text_el: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ὁ διάβολος καὶ εἶπεν ἐναντίον τοῦ κυρίου μὴ δωρεὰν σέβεται Ιωβ τὸν θεόν

text_en: Have you not made a fence for him, and his house, and all his substance round about, blessed the works of his hands, and his possession has increased on the earth?
text_la: nonne tu vallasti eum, ac domum ejus, universamque substantiam per circuitum; operibus manuum ejus benedixisti, et possessio ejus crevit in terra?
text_pt: Porventura tu não cercaste de sebe, a ele, e a sua casa, e a tudo quanto tem? A obra de suas mãos abençoaste e o seu gado se tem aumentado na terra.
text_el: οὐ σὺ περιέφραξας τὰ ἔξω αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ ἔσω τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ ἔξω πάντων τῶν ὄντων αὐτῷ κύκλῳ τὰ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ εὐλόγησας καὶ τὰ κτήνη αὐτοῦ πολλὰ ἐποίησας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

text_en: But stretch forth your hand a little, and touch all that he has, and see if he bless you not to your face.
text_la: sed extende paululum manum tuam et tange cuncta quæ possidet, nisi in faciem benedixerit tibi.
text_pt: Mas estende a tua mão, e toca-lhe em tudo quanto tem, e verás se não blasfema contra ti na tua face.
text_el: ἀλλὰ ἀπόστειλον τὴν χεῖρά σου καὶ ἅψαι πάντων ὧν ἔχει εἰ μὴν εἰς πρόσωπόν σε εὐλογήσει

text_en: Then the Lord said to Satan : Behold, all that he has is in your hand: only put not forth your hand upon his person. And Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord .
text_la: Dixit ergo Dominus ad Satan : Ecce universa quæ habet in manu tua sunt : tantum in eum ne extendas manum tuam. Egressusque est Satan a facie Domini.
text_pt: E disse o Senhor a Satanás: Eis que tudo quanto ele tem está na tua mão; somente contra ele não estendas a tua mão. E Satanás saiu da presença do Senhor.
text_el: τότε εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ διαβόλῳ ἰδοὺ πάντα ὅσα ἔστιν αὐτῷ δίδωμι ἐν τῇ χειρί σου ἀλλὰ αὐτοῦ μὴ ἅψῃ καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ διάβολος παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου

text_en: Now upon a certain day, when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine, in the house of their eldest brother,
text_la: Cum autem quadam die filii et filiæ ejus comederent et biberent vinum in domo fratris sui primogeniti,
text_pt: E sucedeu um dia, em que seus filhos e suas filhas comiam, e bebiam vinho, na casa de seu irmão primogênito,
text_el: καὶ ἦν ὡς ἡ ἡμέρα αὕτη οἱ υἱοὶ Ιωβ καὶ αἱ θυγατέρες αὐτοῦ ἔπινον οἶνον ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτῶν τοῦ πρεσβυτέρου

text_en: there came a messenger to Job, and said: The oxen were ploughing, and the asses feeding beside them,
text_la: nuntius venit ad Job, qui diceret : Boves arabant, et asinæ pascebantur juxta eos:
text_pt: Que veio um mensageiro a Jó, e lhe disse: Os bois lavravam, e as jumentas pastavam junto a eles;
text_el: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος ἦλθεν πρὸς Ιωβ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ τὰ ζεύγη τῶν βοῶν ἠροτρία καὶ αἱ θήλειαι ὄνοι ἐβόσκοντο ἐχόμεναι αὐτῶν

text_en: and the Sabeans rushed in, and took all away, and slew the servants with the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.
text_la: et irruerunt Sabæi, tuleruntque omnia, et pueros percusserunt gladio : et evasi ego solus, ut nuntiarem tibi.
text_pt: E deram sobre eles os sabeus, e os tomaram, e aos servos feriram ao fio da espada; e só eu escapei para trazer-te a nova.
text_el: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ αἰχμαλωτεύοντες ᾐχμαλώτευσαν αὐτὰς καὶ τοὺς παῖδας ἀπέκτειναν ἐν μαχαίραις σωθεὶς δὲ ἐγὼ μόνος ἦλθον τοῦ ἀπαγγεῖλαί σοι

text_en: And while he was yet speaking, another came, and said: The fire of God fell from heaven , and striking the sheep and the servants, has consumed them; and I alone have escaped to tell you.
text_la: Cumque adhuc ille loqueretur, venit alter, et dixit : Ignis Dei cecidit e cælo, et tactas oves puerosque consumpsit : et effugi ego solus, ut nuntiarem tibi.
text_pt: Estando este ainda falando, veio outro e disse: Fogo de Deus caiu do céu, e queimou as ovelhas e os servos, e os consumiu, e só eu escapei para trazer-te a nova.
text_el: ἔτι τούτου λαλοῦντος ἦλθεν ἕτερος ἄγγελος καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς Ιωβ πῦρ ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατέκαυσεν τὰ πρόβατα καὶ τοὺς ποιμένας κατέφαγεν ὁμοίως καὶ σωθεὶς ἐγὼ μόνος ἦλθον τοῦ ἀπαγγεῖλαί σοι

text_en: And while he also was yet speaking, there came another, and said: The Chaldeans made three troops, and have fallen upon the camels, and taken them; moreover, they have slain the servants with the sword: and I alone have escaped to tell you.
text_la: Sed et illo adhuc loquente, venit alius, et dixit : Chaldæi fecerunt tres turmas, et invaserunt camelos, et tulerunt eos, necnon et pueros percusserunt gladio : et ego fugi solus, ut nuntiarem tibi.
text_pt: Estando ainda este falando, veio outro, e disse: Ordenando os caldeus três tropas, deram sobre os camelos, e os tomaram, e aos servos feriram ao fio da espada; e só eu escapei para trazer-te a nova.
text_el: ἔτι τούτου λαλοῦντος ἦλθεν ἕτερος ἄγγελος καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς Ιωβ οἱ ἱππεῖς ἐποίησαν ἡμῖν κεφαλὰς τρεῖς καὶ ἐκύκλωσαν τὰς καμήλους καὶ ᾐχμαλώτευσαν αὐτὰς καὶ τοὺς παῖδας ἀπέκτειναν ἐν μαχαίραις ἐσώθην δὲ ἐγὼ μόνος καὶ ἦλθον τοῦ ἀπαγγεῖλαί σοι

text_en: He was yet speaking, and behold another came in, and said: Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother,
text_la: Adhuc loquebatur ille, et ecce alius intravit, et dixit : Filiis tuis et filiabus vescentibus et bibentibus vinum in domo fratris sui primogeniti,
text_pt: Estando ainda este falando, veio outro, e disse: Estando teus filhos e tuas filhas comendo e bebendo vinho, em casa de seu irmão primogênito,
text_el: ἔτι τούτου λαλοῦντος ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἔρχεται λέγων τῷ Ιωβ τῶν υἱῶν σου καὶ τῶν θυγατέρων σου ἐσθιόντων καὶ πινόντων παρὰ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτῶν τῷ πρεσβυτέρῳ

text_en: a violent wind came on a sudden from the side of the desert , and shook the four corners of the house, and it fell upon your children, and they are dead: and I alone have escaped to tell you.
text_la: repente ventus vehemens irruit a regione deserti, et concussit quatuor angulos domus : quæ corruens oppressit liberos tuos, et mortui sunt : et effugi ego solus, ut nuntiarem tibi.
text_pt: Eis que um grande vento sobreveio dalém do deserto, e deu nos quatro cantos da casa, que caiu sobre os jovens, e morreram; e só eu escapei para trazer-te a nova.
text_el: ἐξαίφνης πνεῦμα μέγα ἐπῆλθεν ἐκ τῆς ἐρήμου καὶ ἥψατο τῶν τεσσάρων γωνιῶν τῆς οἰκίας καὶ ἔπεσεν ἡ οἰκία ἐπὶ τὰ παιδία σου καὶ ἐτελεύτησαν ἐσώθην δὲ ἐγὼ μόνος καὶ ἦλθον τοῦ ἀπαγγεῖλαί σοι

text_en: Then Job rose up, and rent his garments, and having shaven his head, fell down upon the ground, and worshipped,
text_la: Tunc surrexit Job, et scidit vestimenta sua : et tonso capite corruens in terram, adoravit,
text_pt: Então Jó se levantou, e rasgou o seu manto, e rapou a sua cabeça, e se lançou em terra, e adorou.
text_el: οὕτως ἀναστὰς Ιωβ διέρρηξεν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκείρατο τὴν κόμην τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ πεσὼν χαμαὶ προσεκύνησεν καὶ εἶπεν

text_en: and said: Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away: as it has pleased the Lord , so is it done: blessed be the name of the Lord .
text_la: et dixit : Nudus egressus sum de utero matris meæ, et nudus revertar illuc. Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit; sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.
text_pt: E disse: Nu saí do ventre de minha mãe e nu tornarei para lá; o Senhor o deu, e o Senhor o tomou: bendito seja o nome do Senhor.
text_el: αὐτὸς γυμνὸς ἐξῆλθον ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου γυμνὸς καὶ ἀπελεύσομαι ἐκεῖ ὁ κύριος ἔδωκεν ὁ κύριος ἀφείλατο ὡς τῷ κυρίῳ ἔδοξεν οὕτως καὶ ἐγένετο εἴη τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου εὐλογημένον

text_en: In all these things Job sinned not by his lips, nor spoke he any foolish thing against God .
text_la: In omnibus his non peccavit Job labiis suis, neque stultum quid contra Deum locutus est.
text_pt: Em tudo isto Jó não pecou, nem atribuiu a Deus falta alguma.
text_el: ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν τοῖς συμβεβηκόσιν αὐτῷ οὐδὲν ἥμαρτεν Ιωβ ἐναντίον τοῦ κυρίου καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν ἀφροσύνην τῷ θεῷ

text_en: And it came to pass, when on a certain day the sons of God came, and stood before the Lord, and Satan came amongst them, and stood in his sight,
text_la: Factum est autem, cum quadam die venissent filii Dei, et starent coram Domino, venisset quoque Satan inter eos, et staret in conspectu ejus,
text_pt: E, vindo outro dia, em que os filhos de Deus vieram apresentar-se perante o SENHOR, veio também Satanás entre eles, apresentar-se perante o SENHOR.
text_el: ἐγένετο δὲ ὡς ἡ ἡμέρα αὕτη καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ παραστῆναι ἔναντι κυρίου καὶ ὁ διάβολος ἦλθεν ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν παραστῆναι ἐναντίον τοῦ κυρίου

text_en: that the Lord said to Satan : Where do you come from? And he answered, and said: I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it.
text_la: ut diceret Dominus ad Satan : Unde venis? Qui respondens ait : Circuivi terram, et perambulavi eam.
text_pt: Então o Senhor disse a Satanás: Donde vens? E respondeu Satanás ao Senhor, e disse: De rodear a terra, e passear por ela.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ διαβόλῳ πόθεν σὺ ἔρχῃ τότε εἶπεν ὁ διάβολος ἐνώπιον τοῦ κυρίου διαπορευθεὶς τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐμπεριπατήσας τὴν σύμπασαν πάρειμι

text_en: And the Lord said to Satan : Have you considered my servant, Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a man simple and upright, and fearing God , and avoiding evil , and still keeping his innocence? But you have moved me against him, that I should afflict him without cause.
text_la: Et dixit Dominus ad Satan : Numquid considerasti servum meum Job, quod non sit ei similis in terra, vir simplex et rectus, ac timens Deum, et recedens a malo, et adhuc retinens innocentiam? tu autem commovisti me adversus eum, ut affligerem eum frustra.
text_pt: E disse o Senhor a Satanás: Observaste o meu servo Jó? Porque ninguém há na terra semelhante a ele, homem íntegro e reto, temente a Deus e que se desvia do mal, e que ainda retém a sua sinceridade, havendo-me tu incitado contra ele, para o consumir sem causa.
text_el: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος πρὸς τὸν διάβολον προσέσχες οὖν τῷ θεράποντί μου Ιωβ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν κατ' αὐτὸν τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἄνθρωπος ἄκακος ἀληθινός ἄμεμπτος θεοσεβής ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ παντὸς κακοῦ ἔτι δὲ ἔχεται ἀκακίας σὺ δὲ εἶπας τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ διὰ κενῆς ἀπολέσαι

text_en: And Satan answered, and said: Skin for skin; and all that a man has, he will give for his life:
text_la: Cui respondens Satan, ait : Pellem pro pelle, et cuncta quæ habet homo dabit pro anima sua;
text_pt: Então Satanás respondeu ao Senhor, e disse: Pele por pele, e tudo quanto o homem tem dará pela sua vida.
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ ὁ διάβολος εἶπεν τῷ κυρίῳ δέρμα ὑπὲρ δέρματος ὅσα ὑπάρχει ἀνθρώπῳ ὑπὲρ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ ἐκτείσει

text_en: But put forth your hand, and touch his bone and his flesh, and then you shall see that he will bless you to your face.
text_la: alioquin mitte manum tuam, et tange os ejus et carnem, et tunc videbis quod in faciem benedicat tibi.
text_pt: Porém estende a tua mão, e toca-lhe nos ossos, e na carne, e verás se não blasfema contra ti na tua face!
text_el: οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ ἀποστείλας τὴν χεῖρά σου ἅψαι τῶν ὀστῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ τῶν σαρκῶν αὐτοῦ εἰ μὴν εἰς πρόσωπόν σε εὐλογήσει

text_en: And the Lord said to Satan : Behold, he is in your hand, but yet save his life.
text_la: Dixit ergo Dominus ad Satan : Ecce in manu tua est : verumtamen animam illius serva.
text_pt: E disse o Senhor a Satanás: Eis que ele está na tua mão; porém guarda a sua vida.
text_el: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος τῷ διαβόλῳ ἰδοὺ παραδίδωμί σοι αὐτόν μόνον τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ διαφύλαξον

text_en: So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord , and struck Job with a very grievous ulcer, from the sole of the foot even to the top of his head:
text_la: Egressus igitur Satan a facie Domini, percussit Job ulcere pessimo, a planta pedis usque ad verticem ejus;
text_pt: Então saiu Satanás da presença do Senhor, e feriu a Jó de úlceras malignas, desde a planta do pé até ao alto da cabeça.
text_el: ἐξῆλθεν δὲ ὁ διάβολος ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἔπαισεν τὸν Ιωβ ἕλκει πονηρῷ ἀπὸ ποδῶν ἕως κεφαλῆς

text_en: And he took a potsherd and scraped the corrupt matter, sitting on a dunghill.
text_la: qui testa saniem radebat, sedens in sterquilinio.
text_pt: E Jó tomou um caco para se raspar com ele; e estava assentado no meio da cinza.
text_el: καὶ ἔλαβεν ὄστρακον ἵνα τὸν ἰχῶρα ξύῃ καὶ ἐκάθητο ἐπὶ τῆς κοπρίας ἔξω τῆς πόλεως

text_en: And his wife said to him: Do you still continue in your simplicity? bless God and die.
text_la: Dixit autem illi uxor sua : Adhuc tu permanes in simplicitate tua? Benedic Deo, et morere.
text_pt: Então sua mulher lhe disse: Ainda reténs a tua sinceridade? Amaldiçoa a Deus, e morre.
text_el: χρόνου δὲ πολλοῦ προβεβηκότος εἶπεν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ μέχρι τίνος καρτερήσεις λέγων

text_en: And he said to her: You have spoken like one of the foolish women : If we have received good things at the hand of God , why should we not receive evil ? In all these things Job did not sin with his lips.
text_la: Qui ait ad illam : Quasi una de stultis mulieribus locuta es : si bona suscepimus de manu Dei, mala quare non suscipiamus? In omnibus his non peccavit Job labiis suis.
text_pt: Porém ele lhe disse: Como fala qualquer doida, falas tu; receberemos o bem de Deus, e não receberíamos o mal? Em tudo isto não pecou Jó com os seus lábios.
text_el: ὁ δὲ ἐμβλέψας εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὥσπερ μία τῶν ἀφρόνων γυναικῶν ἐλάλησας εἰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἐδεξάμεθα ἐκ χειρὸς κυρίου τὰ κακὰ οὐχ ὑποίσομεν ἐν πᾶσιν τούτοις τοῖς συμβεβηκόσιν αὐτῷ οὐδὲν ἥμαρτεν Ιωβ τοῖς χείλεσιν ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ

text_en: Now when Job's three friends heard all the evil that had befallen him, they came every one from his own place, Eliphaz, the Themanite, and Baldad, the Suhite, and Sophar, the Naamathite. For they had made an appointment to come together and visit him, and comfort him.
text_la: Igitur audientes tres amici Job omne malum quod accidisset ei, venerunt singuli de loco suo, Eliphaz Themanites, et Baldad Suhites, et Sophar Naamathites. Condixerant enim ut pariter venientes visitarent eum, et consolarentur.
text_pt: Ouvindo, pois, três amigos de Jó todo este mal que tinha vindo sobre ele, vieram cada um do seu lugar: Elifaz o temanita, e Bildade o suíta, e Zofar o naamatita; e combinaram condoer-se dele, para o consolarem.
text_el: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ τρεῖς φίλοι αὐτοῦ τὰ κακὰ πάντα τὰ ἐπελθόντα αὐτῷ παρεγένοντο ἕκαστος ἐκ τῆς ἰδίας χώρας πρὸς αὐτόν Ελιφας ὁ Θαιμανων βασιλεύς Βαλδαδ ὁ Σαυχαίων τύραννος Σωφαρ ὁ Μιναίων βασιλεύς καὶ παρεγένοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁμοθυμαδὸν τοῦ παρακαλέσαι καὶ ἐπισκέψασθαι αὐτόν

text_en: And when they had lifted up their eyes afar off, they knew him not, and crying out, they wept, and rending their garments, they sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven .
text_la: Cumque elevassent procul oculos suos, non cognoverunt eum, et exclamantes ploraverunt, scissisque vestibus sparserunt pulverem super caput suum in cælum.
text_pt: E, levantando de longe os seus olhos, não o conheceram; e levantaram a sua voz e choraram, e rasgaram cada um o seu manto, e sobre as suas cabeças lançaram pó ao ar.
text_el: ἰδόντες δὲ αὐτὸν πόρρωθεν οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν καὶ βοήσαντες φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἔκλαυσαν ῥήξαντες ἕκαστος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ στολὴν καὶ καταπασάμενοι γῆν

text_en: And they sat with him on the ground seven day and seven nights and no man spoke to him a word: for they saw that his grief was very great.
text_la: Et sederunt cum eo in terra septem diebus et septem noctibus : et nemo loquebatur ei verbum : videbant enim dolorem esse vehementem.
text_pt: E assentaram-se com ele na terra, sete dias e sete noites; e nenhum lhe dizia palavra alguma, porque viam que a dor era muito grande.
text_el: παρεκάθισαν αὐτῷ ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας καὶ ἑπτὰ νύκτας καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν ἐλάλησεν ἑώρων γὰρ τὴν πληγὴν δεινὴν οὖσαν καὶ μεγάλην σφόδρα

text_en: After this, Job opened his mouth, and cursed his day,
text_la: Post hæc aperuit Job os suum, et maledixit diei suo,
text_pt: Depois disto abriu Jó a sua boca, e amaldiçoou o seu dia.
text_el: μετὰ τοῦτο ἤνοιξεν Ιωβ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ

text_en: and he said:
text_la: et locutus est:
text_pt: E Jó, falando, disse:
text_el: καὶ κατηράσατο τὴν ἡμέραν αὐτοῦ λέγων

text_en: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said: A man child is conceived.
text_la: Pereat dies in qua natus sum, et nox in qua dictum est : Conceptus est homo.
text_pt: Pereça o dia em que nasci, e a noite em que se disse: Foi concebido um homem!
text_el: ἀπόλοιτο ἡ ἡμέρα ἐν ᾗ ἐγεννήθην καὶ ἡ νύξ ἐν ᾗ εἶπαν ἰδοὺ ἄρσεν

text_en: Let that day be turned into darkness, let not God regard it from above, and let not the light shine upon it.
text_la: Dies ille vertatur in tenebras : non requirat eum Deus desuper, et non illustretur lumine.
text_pt: Converta-se aquele dia em trevas; e Deus, lá de cima, não tenha cuidado dele, nem resplandeça sobre ele a luz.
text_el: ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη εἴη σκότος καὶ μὴ ἀναζητήσαι αὐτὴν ὁ κύριος ἄνωθεν μηδὲ ἔλθοι εἰς αὐτὴν φέγγος

text_en: Let darkness, and the shadow of death, cover it, let a mist overspread it, and let it be wrapped up in bitterness.
text_la: Obscurent eum tenebræ et umbra mortis; occupet eum caligo, et involvatur amaritudine.
text_pt: Contaminem-no as trevas e a sombra da morte; habitem sobre ele nuvens; a escuridão do dia o espante!
text_el: ἐκλάβοι δὲ αὐτὴν σκότος καὶ σκιὰ θανάτου ἐπέλθοι ἐπ' αὐτὴν γνόφος

text_en: Let a darksome whirlwind seize upon that night, let it not be counted in the days of the year, nor numbered in the months.
text_la: Noctem illam tenebrosus turbo possideat; non computetur in diebus anni, nec numeretur in mensibus.
text_pt: Quanto àquela noite, dela se apodere a escuridão; e não se regozije ela entre os dias do ano; e não entre no número dos meses!
text_el: καταραθείη ἡ ἡμέρα καὶ ἡ νὺξ ἐκείνη ἀπενέγκαιτο αὐτὴν σκότος μὴ εἴη εἰς ἡμέρας ἐνιαυτοῦ μηδὲ ἀριθμηθείη εἰς ἡμέρας μηνῶν

text_en: Let that night be solitary, and not worthy of praise.
text_la: Sit nox illa solitaria, nec laude digna.
text_pt: Ah! que solitária seja aquela noite, e nela não entre voz de júbilo!
text_el: ἀλλὰ ἡ νὺξ ἐκείνη εἴη ὀδύνη καὶ μὴ ἔλθοι ἐπ' αὐτὴν εὐφροσύνη μηδὲ χαρμονή

text_en: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to raise up a leviathan:
text_la: Maledicant ei qui maledicunt diei, qui parati sunt suscitare Leviathan.
text_pt: Amaldiçoem-na aqueles que amaldiçoam o dia, que estão prontos para suscitar o seu pranto.
text_el: ἀλλὰ καταράσαιτο αὐτὴν ὁ καταρώμενος τὴν ἡμέραν ἐκείνην ὁ μέλλων τὸ μέγα κῆτος χειρώσασθαι

text_en: Let the stars be darkened with the mist thereof: let it expect light, and not see it, nor the rising of the dawning of the day:
text_la: Obtenebrentur stellæ caligine ejus; expectet lucem, et non videat, nec ortum surgentis auroræ.
text_pt: Escureçam-se as estrelas do seu crepúsculo; que espere a luz, e não venha; e não veja as pálpebras da alva;
text_el: σκοτωθείη τὰ ἄστρα τῆς νυκτὸς ἐκείνης ὑπομείναι καὶ εἰς φωτισμὸν μὴ ἔλθοι καὶ μὴ ἴδοι ἑωσφόρον ἀνατέλλοντα

text_en: Because it shut not up the doors of the womb that bore me, nor took away evils from my eyes.
text_la: Quia non conclusit ostia ventris qui portavit me, nec abstulit mala ab oculis meis.
text_pt: Porque não fechou as portas do ventre; nem escondeu dos meus olhos a canseira.
text_el: ὅτι οὐ συνέκλεισεν πύλας γαστρὸς μητρός μου ἀπήλλαξεν γὰρ ἂν πόνον ἀπὸ ὀφθαλμῶν μου

text_en: Why did I not die in the womb? Why did I not perish when I came out of the belly?
text_la: Quare non in vulva mortuus sum? egressus ex utero non statim perii?
text_pt: Por que não morri eu desde a madre? E em saindo do ventre, não expirei?
text_el: διὰ τί γὰρ ἐν κοιλίᾳ οὐκ ἐτελεύτησα ἐκ γαστρὸς δὲ ἐξῆλθον καὶ οὐκ εὐθὺς ἀπωλόμην

text_en: Why received upon the knees? Why suckled at the breasts?
text_la: Quare exceptus genibus? cur lactatus uberibus?
text_pt: Por que me receberam os joelhos? E por que os peitos, para que mamasse?
text_el: ἵνα τί δὲ συνήντησάν μοι γόνατα ἵνα τί δὲ μαστοὺς ἐθήλασα

text_en: For now I should have been asleep and still, and should have rest in my sleep:
text_la: Nunc enim dormiens silerem, et somno meo requiescerem
text_pt: Porque já agora jazeria e repousaria; dormiria, e então haveria repouso para mim.
text_el: νῦν ἂν κοιμηθεὶς ἡσύχασα ὑπνώσας δὲ ἀνεπαυσάμην

text_en: With kings and consuls of the earth, who build themselves solitudes:
text_la: cum regibus et consulibus terræ, qui ædificant sibi solitudines;
text_pt: Com os reis e conselheiros da terra, que para si edificam casas nos lugares assolados,
text_el: μετὰ βασιλέων βουλευτῶν γῆς οἳ ἠγαυριῶντο ἐπὶ ξίφεσιν

text_en: Or with princes, that possess gold, and fill their houses with silver:
text_la: aut cum principibus qui possident aurum, et replent domos suas argento;
text_pt: Ou com os príncipes que possuem ouro, que enchem as suas casas de prata,
text_el: ἢ μετὰ ἀρχόντων ὧν πολὺς ὁ χρυσός οἳ ἔπλησαν τοὺς οἴκους αὐτῶν ἀργυρίου

text_en: Or as a hidden untimely birth, I should not be; or as they that, being conceived, have not seen the light.
text_la: aut sicut abortivum absconditum non subsisterem, vel qui concepti non viderunt lucem.
text_pt: Ou como aborto oculto, não existiria; como as crianças que não viram a luz.
text_el: ἢ ὥσπερ ἔκτρωμα ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ μήτρας μητρὸς ἢ ὥσπερ νήπιοι οἳ οὐκ εἶδον φῶς

text_en: There the wicked cease from tumult, and there the wearied in strength are at rest.
text_la: Ibi impii cessaverunt a tumultu, et ibi requieverunt fessi robore.
text_pt: Ali os maus cessam de perturbar; e ali repousam os cansados.
text_el: ἐκεῖ ἀσεβεῖς ἐξέκαυσαν θυμὸν ὀργῆς ἐκεῖ ἀνεπαύσαντο κατάκοποι τῷ σώματι

text_en: And they sometime bound together without disquiet, have not heard the voice of the oppressor.
text_la: Et quondam vincti pariter sine molestia, non audierunt vocem exactoris.
text_pt: Ali os presos juntamente repousam, e não ouvem a voz do exator.
text_el: ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ οἱ αἰώνιοι οὐκ ἤκουσαν φωνὴν φορολόγου

text_en: The small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master.
text_la: Parvus et magnus ibi sunt, et servus liber a domino suo.
text_pt: Ali está o pequeno e o grande, e o servo livre de seu senhor.
text_el: μικρὸς καὶ μέγας ἐκεῖ ἐστιν καὶ θεράπων οὐ δεδοικὼς τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ

text_en: Why is light given to him that is in misery, and life to them that are in bitterness of soul ?
text_la: Quare misero data est lux, et vita his qui in amaritudine animæ sunt :
text_pt: Por que se dá luz ao miserável, e vida aos amargurados de ânimo?
text_el: ἵνα τί γὰρ δέδοται τοῖς ἐν πικρίᾳ φῶς ζωὴ δὲ ταῖς ἐν ὀδύναις ψυχαῖς

text_en: That look for death, and it comes not, as they that dig for a treasure:
text_la: qui expectant mortem, et non venit, quasi effodientes thesaurum;
text_pt: Que esperam a morte, e ela não vem; e cavam em procura dela mais do que de tesouros ocultos;
text_el: οἳ ὁμείρονται τοῦ θανάτου καὶ οὐ τυγχάνουσιν ἀνορύσσοντες ὥσπερ θησαυρούς

text_en: And they rejoice exceedingly when they have found the grave?
text_la: gaudentque vehementer cum invenerint sepulchrum?
text_pt: Que de alegria saltam, e exultam, achando a sepultura?
text_el: περιχαρεῖς δὲ ἐγένοντο ἐὰν κατατύχωσιν

text_en: To a man whose way is hidden, and God has surrounded him with darkness?
text_la: viro cujus abscondita est via et circumdedit eum Deus tenebris?
text_pt: Por que se dá luz ao homem, cujo caminho é oculto, e a quem Deus o encobriu?
text_el: θάνατος ἀνδρὶ ἀνάπαυμα συνέκλεισεν γὰρ ὁ θεὸς κατ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: Before I eat I sigh: and as overflowing waters, so is my roaring:
text_la: Antequam comedam, suspiro; et tamquam inundantes aquæ, sic rugitus meus :
text_pt: Porque antes do meu pão vem o meu suspiro; e os meus gemidos se derramam como água.
text_el: πρὸ γὰρ τῶν σίτων μου στεναγμός μοι ἥκει δακρύω δὲ ἐγὼ συνεχόμενος φόβῳ

text_en: For the fear which I feared, has come upon me: and that which I was afraid of, has befallen me.
text_la: quia timor quem timebam evenit mihi, et quod verebar accidit.
text_pt: Porque aquilo que temia me sobreveio; e o que receava me aconteceu.
text_el: φόβος γάρ ὃν ἐφρόντισα ἦλθέν μοι καὶ ὃν ἐδεδοίκειν συνήντησέν μοι

text_en: Have I not dissembled? Have I not kept silence? Have I not been quiet? And indignation has come upon me.
text_la: Nonne dissimulavi? nonne silui? nonne quievi? et venit super me indignatio.
text_pt: Nunca estive tranqüilo, nem sosseguei, nem repousei, mas veio sobre mim a perturbação.
text_el: οὔτε εἰρήνευσα οὔτε ἡσύχασα οὔτε ἀνεπαυσάμην ἦλθεν δέ μοι ὀργή

text_en: Then Eliphaz, the Themanite, answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Eliphaz Themanites, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondeu Elifaz o temanita, e disse:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ελιφας ὁ Θαιμανίτης λέγει

text_en: If we begin to speak to you, perhaps you will take it ill; but who can withhold the words he has conceived?
text_la: Si cœperimus loqui tibi, forsitan moleste accipies; sed conceptum sermonem tenere quis poterit?
text_pt: Se intentarmos falar-te, enfadar-te-ás? Mas quem poderia conter as palavras?
text_el: μὴ πολλάκις σοι λελάληται ἐν κόπῳ ἰσχὺν δὲ ῥημάτων σου τίς ὑποίσει

text_en: Behold you have taught many, and you have strengthened the weary hands:
text_la: Ecce docuisti multos, et manus lassas roborasti;
text_pt: Eis que ensinaste a muitos, e tens fortalecido as mãos fracas.
text_el: εἰ γὰρ σὺ ἐνουθέτησας πολλοὺς καὶ χεῖρας ἀσθενοῦς παρεκάλεσας

text_en: Your words have confirmed them that were staggering, and you have strengthened the trembling knees:
text_la: vacillantes confirmaverunt sermones tui, et genua trementia confortasti.
text_pt: As tuas palavras firmaram os que tropeçavam e os joelhos desfalecentes tens fortalecido.
text_el: ἀσθενοῦντάς τε ἐξανέστησας ῥήμασιν γόνασίν τε ἀδυνατοῦσιν θάρσος περιέθηκας

text_en: But now the scourge has come upon you, and you faint: It has touched you, and you are troubled.
text_la: Nunc autem venit super te plaga, et defecisti; tetigit te, et conturbatus es.
text_pt: Mas agora, que se trata de ti, te enfadas; e tocando-te a ti, te perturbas.
text_el: νῦν δὲ ἥκει ἐπὶ σὲ πόνος καὶ ἥψατό σου σὺ δὲ ἐσπούδασας

text_en: Where is your fear, your fortitude , your patience, and the perfection of your ways?
text_la: Ubi est timor tuus, fortitudo tua, patientia tua, et perfectio viarum tuarum?
text_pt: Porventura não é o teu temor de Deus a tua confiança, e a tua esperança a integridade dos teus caminhos?
text_el: πότερον οὐχ ὁ φόβος σού ἐστιν ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ καὶ ἡ ἐλπίς σου καὶ ἡ ἀκακία τῆς ὁδοῦ σου

text_en: Remember, I pray you, who ever perished being innocent? Or when were the just destroyed?
text_la: Recordare, obsecro te, quis umquam innocens periit? aut quando recti deleti sunt?
text_pt: Lembra-te agora qual é o inocente que jamais pereceu? E onde foram os sinceros destruídos?
text_el: μνήσθητι οὖν τίς καθαρὸς ὢν ἀπώλετο ἢ πότε ἀληθινοὶ ὁλόρριζοι ἀπώλοντο

text_en: On the contrary, I have seen those who work iniquity , and sow sorrows, and reap them,
text_la: Quin potius vidi eos qui operantur iniquitatem, et seminant dolores, et metunt eos,
text_pt: Segundo eu tenho visto, os que lavram iniqüidade, e semeiam mal, segam o mesmo.
text_el: καθ' ὃν τρόπον εἶδον τοὺς ἀροτριῶντας τὰ ἄτοπα οἱ δὲ σπείροντες αὐτὰ ὀδύνας θεριοῦσιν ἑαυτοῖς

text_en: perishing by the blast of God , and consumed by the spirit of his wrath .
text_la: flante Deo perisse, et spiritu iræ ejus esse consumptos.
text_pt: Com o hálito de Deus perecem; e com o sopro da sua ira se consomem.
text_el: ἀπὸ προστάγματος κυρίου ἀπολοῦνται ἀπὸ δὲ πνεύματος ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ ἀφανισθήσονται

text_en: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the lioness, and the teeth of the whelps of lions, are broken:
text_la: Rugitus leonis, et vox leænæ, et dentes catulorum leonum contriti sunt.
text_pt: O rugido do leão, e a voz do leão feroz, e os dentes dos leõezinhos se quebram.
text_el: σθένος λέοντος φωνὴ δὲ λεαίνης γαυρίαμα δὲ δρακόντων ἐσβέσθη

text_en: The tiger has perished for want of prey, and the young lions are scattered abroad.
text_la: Tigris periit, eo quod non haberet prædam, et catuli leonis dissipati sunt.
text_pt: Perece o leão velho, porque não tem presa; e os filhos da leoa andam dispersos.
text_el: μυρμηκολέων ὤλετο παρὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βοράν σκύμνοι δὲ λεόντων ἔλιπον ἀλλήλους

text_en: Now there was a word spoken to me in private, and my ears by stealth, as it were, received the veins of its whisper.
text_la: Porro ad me dictum est verbum absconditum, et quasi furtive suscepit auris mea venas susurri ejus.
text_pt: Uma coisa me foi trazida em segredo; e os meus ouvidos perceberam um sussurro dela.
text_el: εἰ δέ τι ῥῆμα ἀληθινὸν ἐγεγόνει ἐν λόγοις σου οὐθὲν ἄν σοι τούτων κακὸν ἀπήντησεν πότερον οὐ δέξεταί μου τὸ οὖς ἐξαίσια παρ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: In the horror of a vision by night, when deep sleep is wont to hold men ,
text_la: In horrore visionis nocturnæ, quando solet sopor occupare homines,
text_pt: Entre pensamentos vindos de visões da noite, quando cai sobre os homens o sono profundo,
text_el: φόβοι δὲ καὶ ἠχὼ νυκτερινή ἐπιπίπτων φόβος ἐπ' ἀνθρώπους

text_en: fear seized upon me, and trembling, and all my bones were affrighted:
text_la: pavor tenuit me, et tremor, et omnia ossa mea perterrita sunt;
text_pt: Sobrevieram-me o espanto e o tremor, e todos os meus ossos estremeceram.
text_el: φρίκη δέ μοι συνήντησεν καὶ τρόμος καὶ μεγάλως μου τὰ ὀστᾶ συνέσεισεν

text_en: And when a spirit passed before me, the hair of my flesh stood up.
text_la: et cum spiritus, me præsente, transiret, inhorruerunt pili carnis meæ.
text_pt: Então um espírito passou por diante de mim; fez-me arrepiar os cabelos da minha carne.
text_el: καὶ πνεῦμα ἐπὶ πρόσωπόν μου ἐπῆλθεν ἔφριξαν δέ μου τρίχες καὶ σάρκες

text_en: There stood one whose countenance I knew not, an image before my eyes, and I heard the voice, as it were, of a gentle wind.
text_la: Stetit quidam, cujus non agnoscebam vultum, imago coram oculis meis, et vocem quasi auræ lenis audivi.
text_pt: Parou ele, porém não conheci a sua feição; um vulto estava diante dos meus olhos; houve silêncio, e ouvi uma voz que dizia:
text_el: ἀνέστην καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνων εἶδον καὶ οὐκ ἦν μορφὴ πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν μου ἀλλ' ἢ αὔραν καὶ φωνὴν ἤκουον

text_en: Shall man be justified in comparison of God , or shall a man be more pure than his maker?
text_la: Numquid homo, Dei comparatione, justificabitur? aut factore suo purior erit vir?
text_pt: Seria porventura o homem mais justo do que Deus? Seria porventura o homem mais puro do que o seu Criador?
text_el: τί γάρ μὴ καθαρὸς ἔσται βροτὸς ἐναντίον κυρίου ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ ἄμεμπτος ἀνήρ

text_en: Behold, they that serve him are not steadfast, and in his angels he found wickedness :
text_la: Ecce qui serviunt ei, non sunt stabiles, et in angelis suis reperit pravitatem;
text_pt: Eis que ele não confia nos seus servos e aos seus anjos atribui loucura;
text_el: εἰ κατὰ παίδων αὐτοῦ οὐ πιστεύει κατὰ δὲ ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ σκολιόν τι ἐπενόησεν

text_en: How much more shall they that dwell in houses of clay, who have an earthly foundation, be consumed as with the moth?
text_la: quanto magis hi qui habitant domos luteas, qui terrenum habent fundamentum, consumentur velut a tinea?
text_pt: Quanto menos àqueles que habitam em casas de lodo, cujo fundamento está no pó, e são esmagados como a traça!
text_el: τοὺς δὲ κατοικοῦντας οἰκίας πηλίνας ἐξ ὧν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ πηλοῦ ἐσμεν ἔπαισεν αὐτοὺς σητὸς τρόπον

text_en: From morning till evening they shall be cut down: and because no one understands, they shall perish for ever.
text_la: De mane usque ad vesperam succidentur; et quia nullus intelligit, in æternum peribunt.
text_pt: Desde a manhã até à tarde são despedaçados; e eternamente perecem sem que disso se faça caso.
text_el: καὶ ἀπὸ πρωίθεν ἕως ἑσπέρας οὐκέτι εἰσίν παρὰ τὸ μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς ἑαυτοῖς βοηθῆσαι ἀπώλοντο

text_en: And they that shall be left, shall be taken away from them: they shall die, and not in wisdom.
text_la: Qui autem reliqui fuerint, auferentur ex eis; morientur, et non in sapientia.
text_pt: Porventura não passa com eles a sua excelência? Morrem, mas sem sabedoria.
text_el: ἐνεφύσησεν γὰρ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐξηράνθησαν ἀπώλοντο παρὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν αὐτοὺς σοφίαν

text_en: Call now, if there be any that will answer you, and turn to some of the saints.
text_la: Voca ergo, si est qui tibi respondeat, et ad aliquem sanctorum convertere.
text_pt: Chama agora; há alguém que te responda? E para qual dos santos te virarás?
text_el: ἐπικάλεσαι δέ εἴ τίς σοι ὑπακούσεται ἢ εἴ τινα ἀγγέλων ἁγίων ὄψῃ

text_en: Anger indeed kills the foolish, and envy slays the little one.
text_la: Vere stultum interficit iracundia, et parvulum occidit invidia.
text_pt: Porque a ira destrói o louco; e o zelo mata o tolo.
text_el: καὶ γὰρ ἄφρονα ἀναιρεῖ ὀργή πεπλανημένον δὲ θανατοῖ ζῆλος

text_en: I have seen a fool with a strong root, and I cursed his beauty immediately.
text_la: Ego vidi stultum firma radice, et maledixi pulchritudini ejus statim.
text_pt: Bem vi eu o louco lançar raízes; porém logo amaldiçoei a sua habitação.
text_el: ἐγὼ δὲ ἑώρακα ἄφρονας ῥίζαν βάλλοντας ἀλλ' εὐθέως ἐβρώθη αὐτῶν ἡ δίαιτα

text_en: His children shall be far from safety, and shall be destroyed in the gate, and there shall be none to deliver them.
text_la: Longe fient filii ejus a salute, et conterentur in porta, et non erit qui eruat.
text_pt: Seus filhos estão longe da salvação; e são despedaçados às portas, e não há quem os livre.
text_el: πόρρω γένοιντο οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ σωτηρίας κολαβρισθείησαν δὲ ἐπὶ θύραις ἡσσόνων καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ ἐξαιρούμενος

text_en: Whose harvest the hungry shall eat, and the armed man shall take him by violence , and the thirsty shall drink up his riches.
text_la: Cujus messem famelicus comedet, et ipsum rapiet armatus, et bibent sitientes divitias ejus.
text_pt: A sua messe, o faminto a devora, e até dentre os espinhos a tira; e o salteador traga a sua fazenda.
text_el: ἃ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι συνήγαγον δίκαιοι ἔδονται αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐκ κακῶν οὐκ ἐξαίρετοι ἔσονται ἐκσιφωνισθείη αὐτῶν ἡ ἰσχύς

text_en: Nothing upon earth is done without a cause, and sorrow does not spring out of the ground.
text_la: Nihil in terra sine causa fit, et de humo non oritur dolor.
text_pt: Porque do pó não procede a aflição, nem da terra brota o trabalho.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ μὴ ἐξέλθῃ ἐκ τῆς γῆς κόπος οὐδὲ ἐξ ὀρέων ἀναβλαστήσει πόνος

text_en: Man is born to labour, and the bird to fly.
text_la: Homo nascitur ad laborem, et avis ad volatum.
text_pt: Mas o homem nasce para a tribulação, como as faíscas se levantam para voar.
text_el: ἀλλὰ ἄνθρωπος γεννᾶται κόπῳ νεοσσοὶ δὲ γυπὸς τὰ ὑψηλὰ πέτονται

text_en: Wherefore I will pray to the Lord , and address my speech to God :
text_la: Quam ob rem ego deprecabor Dominum, et ad Deum ponam eloquium meum :
text_pt: Porém eu buscaria a Deus; e a ele entregaria a minha causa.
text_el: οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ ἐγὼ δεηθήσομαι κυρίου κύριον δὲ τὸν πάντων δεσπότην ἐπικαλέσομαι

text_en: Who does great things, and unsearchable and wonderful things without number:
text_la: qui facit magna et inscrutabilia, et mirabilia absque numero;
text_pt: Ele faz coisas grandes e inescrutáveis, e maravilhas sem número.
text_el: τὸν ποιοῦντα μεγάλα καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστα ἔνδοξά τε καὶ ἐξαίσια ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμός

text_en: Who gives rain upon the face of the earth, and waters all things with waters:
text_la: qui dat pluviam super faciem terræ, et irrigat aquis universa;
text_pt: Ele dá a chuva sobre a terra, e envia águas sobre os campos.
text_el: τὸν διδόντα ὑετὸν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἀποστέλλοντα ὕδωρ ἐπὶ τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανόν

text_en: Who sets up the humble on high, and comforts with health those that mourn.
text_la: qui ponit humiles in sublime, et mœrentes erigit sospitate;
text_pt: Para pôr aos abatidos num lugar alto; e para que os enlutados se exaltem na salvação.
text_el: τὸν ποιοῦντα ταπεινοὺς εἰς ὕψος καὶ ἀπολωλότας ἐξεγείροντα

text_en: Who brings to nought the designs of the malignant, so that their hands cannot accomplish what they had begun:
text_la: qui dissipat cogitationes malignorum, ne possint implere manus eorum quod cœperant;
text_pt: Ele aniquila as imaginações dos astutos, para que as suas mãos não possam levar coisa alguma a efeito.
text_el: διαλλάσσοντα βουλὰς πανούργων καὶ οὐ μὴ ποιήσουσιν αἱ χεῖρες αὐτῶν ἀληθές

text_en: Who catches the wise in their craftiness, and disappoints the counsel of the wicked:
text_la: qui apprehendit sapientes in astutia eorum, et consilium pravorum dissipat.
text_pt: Ele apanha os sábios na sua própria astúcia; e o conselho dos perversos se precipita.
text_el: ὁ καταλαμβάνων σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ φρονήσει βουλὴν δὲ πολυπλόκων ἐξέστησεν

text_en: They shall meet with darkness in the day, and grope at noonday as in the night.
text_la: Per diem incurrent tenebras, et quasi in nocte, sic palpabunt in meridie.
text_pt: Eles de dia encontram as trevas; e ao meio-dia andam às apalpadelas como de noite.
text_el: ἡμέρας συναντήσεται αὐτοῖς σκότος τὸ δὲ μεσημβρινὸν ψηλαφήσαισαν ἴσα νυκτί

text_en: But he shall save the needy from the sword of their mouth, and the poor from the hand of the violent .
text_la: Porro salvum faciet egenum a gladio oris eorum, et de manu violenti pauperem.
text_pt: Porém ao necessitado livra da espada, e da boca deles, e da mão do forte.
text_el: ἀπόλοιντο δὲ ἐν πολέμῳ ἀδύνατος δὲ ἐξέλθοι ἐκ χειρὸς δυνάστου

text_en: And to the needy there shall be hope, but iniquity shall draw in her mouth.
text_la: Et erit egeno spes; iniquitas autem contrahet os suum.
text_pt: Assim há esperança para o pobre; e a iniqüidade tapa a sua boca.
text_el: εἴη δὲ ἀδυνάτῳ ἐλπίς ἀδίκου δὲ στόμα ἐμφραχθείη

text_en: Blessed is the man whom God corrects: refuse not, therefore, the chastising of the Lord .
text_la: Beatus homo qui corripitur a Deo : increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes :
text_pt: Eis que bem-aventurado é o homem a quem Deus repreende; não desprezes, pois, a correção do Todo-Poderoso.
text_el: μακάριος δὲ ἄνθρωπος ὃν ἤλεγξεν ὁ κύριος νουθέτημα δὲ παντοκράτορος μὴ ἀπαναίνου

text_en: For he wounds, and cures: he strikes, and his hands shall heal.
text_la: quia ipse vulnerat, et medetur; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt.
text_pt: Porque ele faz a chaga, e ele mesmo a liga; ele fere, e as suas mãos curam.
text_el: αὐτὸς γὰρ ἀλγεῖν ποιεῖ καὶ πάλιν ἀποκαθίστησιν ἔπαισεν καὶ αἱ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ ἰάσαντο

text_en: In six troubles he shall deliver you, and in the seventh, evil shall not touch you.
text_la: In sex tribulationibus liberabit te, et in septima non tangent te malum.
text_pt: Em seis angústias te livrará; e na sétima o mal não te tocará.
text_el: ἑξάκις ἐξ ἀναγκῶν σε ἐξελεῖται ἐν δὲ τῷ ἑβδόμῳ οὐ μὴ ἅψηταί σου κακόν

text_en: In famine he shall deliver you from death; and in battle, from the hand of the sword.
text_la: In fame eruet te de morte, et in bello de manu gladii.
text_pt: Na fome te livrará da morte; e na guerra, da violência da espada.
text_el: ἐν λιμῷ ῥύσεταί σε ἐκ θανάτου ἐν πολέμῳ δὲ ἐκ χειρὸς σιδήρου λύσει σε

text_en: You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue: and you shall not fear calamity when it comes.
text_la: A flagello linguæ absconderis, et non timebis calamitatem cum venerit.
text_pt: Do açoite da língua estarás encoberto; e não temerás a assolação, quando vier.
text_el: ἀπὸ μάστιγος γλώσσης σε κρύψει καὶ οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇς ἀπὸ κακῶν ἐρχομένων

text_en: In destruction and famine you shall laugh: and you shall not be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
text_la: In vastitate et fame ridebis, et bestias terræ non formidabis.
text_pt: Da assolação e da fome te rirás, e os animais da terra não temerás.
text_el: ἀδίκων καὶ ἀνόμων καταγελάσῃ ἀπὸ δὲ θηρίων ἀγρίων οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇς

text_en: But you shall have a covenant with the stones of the lands, and the beasts of the earth shall be at peace with you.
text_la: Sed cum lapidibus regionum pactum tuum, et bestiæ terræ pacificæ erunt tibi.
text_pt: Porque até com as pedras do campo terás o teu acordo, e as feras do campo serão pacíficas contigo.
text_el: θῆρες γὰρ ἄγριοι εἰρηνεύσουσίν σοι

text_en: And you shall know that your tabernacle is in peace, and visiting your beauty, you shall not sin .
text_la: Et scies quod pacem habeat tabernaculum tuum; et visitans speciem tuam, non peccabis.
text_pt: E saberás que a tua tenda está em paz; e visitarás a tua habitação, e não pecarás.
text_el: εἶτα γνώσῃ ὅτι εἰρηνεύσει σου ὁ οἶκος ἡ δὲ δίαιτα τῆς σκηνῆς σου οὐ μὴ ἁμάρτῃ

text_en: You shall know also that your seed shall be multiplied, and your offspring like the grass of the earth.
text_la: Scies quoque quoniam multiplex erit semen tuum, et progenies tua quasi herba terræ.
text_pt: Também saberás que se multiplicará a tua descendência e a tua posteridade como a erva da terra,
text_el: γνώσῃ δὲ ὅτι πολὺ τὸ σπέρμα σου τὰ δὲ τέκνα σου ἔσται ὥσπερ τὸ παμβότανον τοῦ ἀγροῦ

text_en: You shall enter into the grave in abundance, as a heap of wheat is brought in its season.
text_la: Ingredieris in abundantia sepulchrum, sicut infertur acervus tritici in tempore suo.
text_pt: Na velhice irás à sepultura, como se recolhe o feixe de trigo a seu tempo.
text_el: ἐλεύσῃ δὲ ἐν τάφῳ ὥσπερ σῖτος ὥριμος κατὰ καιρὸν θεριζόμενος ἢ ὥσπερ θιμωνιὰ ἅλωνος καθ' ὥραν συγκομισθεῖσα

text_en: Behold, this is even so, as we have searched out: which you having heard, consider it thoroughly in your mind.
text_la: Ecce hoc, ut investigavimus, ita est : quod auditum, mente pertracta.
text_pt: Eis que isto já o havemos inquirido, e assim é; ouve-o, e medita nisso para teu bem.
text_el: ἰδοὺ ταῦτα οὕτως ἐξιχνιάσαμεν ταῦτά ἐστιν ἃ ἀκηκόαμεν σὺ δὲ γνῶθι σεαυτῷ εἴ τι ἔπραξας

text_en: But Job answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Job, dixit:
text_pt: Então Jó respondeu, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει

text_en: O that my sins , whereby I have deserved wrath , and the calamity that I suffer, were weighed in a balance.
text_la: Utinam appenderentur peccata mea quibus iram merui, et calamitas quam patior, in statera!
text_pt: Oh! se a minha mágoa retamente se pesasse, e a minha miséria juntamente se pusesse numa balança!
text_el: εἰ γάρ τις ἱστῶν στήσαι μου τὴν ὀργήν τὰς δὲ ὀδύνας μου ἄραι ἐν ζυγῷ ὁμοθυμαδόν

text_en: As the sand of the sea, this would appear heavier: therefore, my words are full of sorrow:
text_la: Quasi arena maris hæc gravior appareret; unde et verba mea dolore sunt plena :
text_pt: Porque, na verdade, mais pesada seria, do que a areia dos mares; por isso é que as minhas palavras têm sido engolidas.
text_el: καὶ δὴ ἄμμου παραλίας βαρυτέρα ἔσται ἀλλ' ὡς ἔοικεν τὰ ῥήματά μού ἐστιν φαῦλα

text_en: For the arrows of the Lord are in me, the rage whereof drinks up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord war against me.
text_la: quia sagittæ Domini in me sunt, quarum indignatio ebibit spiritum meum; et terrores Domini militant contra me.
text_pt: Porque as flechas do TodoPoderoso estão em mim, cujo ardente veneno suga o meu espírito; os terrores de Deus se armam contra mim.
text_el: βέλη γὰρ κυρίου ἐν τῷ σώματί μού ἐστιν ὧν ὁ θυμὸς αὐτῶν ἐκπίνει μου τὸ αἷμα ὅταν ἄρξωμαι λαλεῖν κεντοῦσί με

text_en: Will the wild ass bray when he has grass? Or will the ox low when he stands before a full manger?
text_la: Numquid rugiet onager cum habuerit herbam? aut mugiet bos cum ante præsepe plenum steterit?
text_pt: Porventura zurrará o jumento montês junto à relva? Ou mugirá o boi junto ao seu pasto?
text_el: τί γάρ μὴ διὰ κενῆς κεκράξεται ὄνος ἄγριος ἀλλ' ἢ τὰ σῖτα ζητῶν εἰ δὲ καὶ ῥήξει φωνὴν βοῦς ἐπὶ φάτνης ἔχων τὰ βρώματα

text_en: Or can an unsavoury thing be eaten, that is not seasoned with salt ? Or can a man taste that which, when tasted, brings death?
text_la: aut poterit comedi insulsum, quod non est sale conditum? aut potest aliquis gustare quod gustatum affert mortem?
text_pt: Ou comer-se-á sem sal o que é insípido? Ou haverá gosto na clara do ovo?
text_el: εἰ βρωθήσεται ἄρτος ἄνευ ἁλός εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔστιν γεῦμα ἐν ῥήμασιν κενοῖς

text_en: The things which before my soul would not touch, now, through anguish, are my meats.
text_la: Quæ prius nolebat tangere anima mea, nunc, præ angustia, cibi mei sunt.
text_pt: A minha alma recusa tocá-las, pois são para mim como comida repugnante.
text_el: οὐ δύναται γὰρ παύσασθαί μου ἡ ψυχή βρόμον γὰρ ὁρῶ τὰ σῖτά μου ὥσπερ ὀσμὴν λέοντος

text_en: Who will grant that my request may come: and that God may give me what I look for?
text_la: Quis det ut veniat petitio mea, et quod expecto tribuat mihi Deus?
text_pt: Quem dera que se cumprisse o meu desejo, e que Deus me desse o que espero!
text_el: εἰ γὰρ δῴη καὶ ἔλθοι μου ἡ αἴτησις καὶ τὴν ἐλπίδα μου δῴη ὁ κύριος

text_en: And that he that has begun may destroy me, that he may let loose his hand, and cut me off?
text_la: et qui cœpit, ipse me conterat; solvat manum suam, et succidat me?
text_pt: E que Deus quisesse quebrantar-me, e soltasse a sua mão, e me acabasse!
text_el: ἀρξάμενος ὁ κύριος τρωσάτω με εἰς τέλος δὲ μή με ἀνελέτω

text_en: And that this may be my comfort, that afflicting me with sorrow, he spare not, nor I contradict the words of the Holy one.
text_la: Et hæc mihi sit consolatio, ut affligens me dolore, non parcat, nec contradicam sermonibus Sancti.
text_pt: Isto ainda seria a minha consolação, e me refrigeraria no meu tormento, não me poupando ele; porque não ocultei as palavras do Santo.
text_el: εἴη δέ μου πόλις τάφος ἐφ' ἧς ἐπὶ τειχέων ἡλλόμην ἐπ' αὐτῆς οὐ μὴ φείσωμαι οὐ γὰρ ἐψευσάμην ῥήματα ἅγια θεοῦ μου

text_en: For what is my strength, that I can hold out? Or what is my end, that I should keep patience?
text_la: Quæ est enim fortitudo mea, ut sustineam? aut quis finis meus, ut patienter agam?
text_pt: Qual é a minha força, para que eu espere? Ou qual é o meu fim, para que tenha ainda paciência?
text_el: τίς γάρ μου ἡ ἰσχύς ὅτι ὑπομένω ἢ τίς μου ὁ χρόνος ὅτι ἀνέχεταί μου ἡ ψυχή

text_en: My strength is not the strength of stones, nor is my flesh of brass.
text_la: Nec fortitudo lapidum fortitudo mea, nec caro mea ænea est.
text_pt: É porventura a minha força a força da pedra? Ou é de cobre a minha carne?
text_el: μὴ ἰσχὺς λίθων ἡ ἰσχύς μου ἢ αἱ σάρκες μού εἰσιν χάλκειαι

text_en: Behold there is no help for me in myself, and my familiar friends also are departed from me.
text_la: Ecce non est auxilium mihi in me, et necessarii quoque mei recesserunt a me.
text_pt: Está em mim a minha ajuda? Ou desamparou-me a verdadeira sabedoria?
text_el: ἦ οὐκ ἐπ' αὐτῷ ἐπεποίθειν βοήθεια δὲ ἀπ' ἐμοῦ ἄπεστιν

text_en: He that takes away mercy from his friend, forsakes the fear of the Lord .
text_la: Qui tollit ab amico suo misericordiam, timorem Domini derelinquit.
text_pt: Ao que está aflito devia o amigo mostrar compaixão, ainda ao que deixasse o temor do Todo-Poderoso.
text_el: ἀπείπατό με ἔλεος ἐπισκοπὴ δὲ κυρίου ὑπερεῖδέν με

text_en: My brethren have passed by me, as the torrent that passes swiftly in the valleys.
text_la: Fratres mei præterierunt me, sicut torrens qui raptim transit in convallibus.
text_pt: Meus irmãos aleivosamente me trataram, como um ribeiro, como a torrente dos ribeiros que passam,
text_el: οὐ προσεῖδόν με οἱ ἐγγύτατοί μου ὥσπερ χειμάρρους ἐκλείπων ἢ ὥσπερ κῦμα παρῆλθόν με

text_en: They that fear the hoary frost, the snow shall fall upon them.
text_la: Qui timent pruinam, irruet super eos nix.
text_pt: Que estão encobertos com a geada, e neles se esconde a neve,
text_el: οἵτινές με διευλαβοῦντο νῦν ἐπιπεπτώκασίν μοι ὥσπερ χιὼν ἢ κρύσταλλος πεπηγώς

text_en: At the time when they shall be scattered they shall perish: and after it grows hot, they shall be melted out of their place.
text_la: Tempore quo fuerint dissipati, peribunt; et ut incaluerit, solventur de loco suo.
text_pt: No tempo em que se derretem com o calor, se desfazem, e em se aquentando, desaparecem do seu lugar.
text_el: καθὼς τακεῖσα θέρμης γενομένης οὐκ ἐπεγνώσθη ὅπερ ἦν

text_en: The paths of their steps are entangled: they shall walk in vain, and shall perish.
text_la: Involutæ sunt semitæ gressuum eorum; ambulabunt in vacuum, et peribunt.
text_pt: Desviam-se as veredas dos seus caminhos; sobem ao vácuo, e perecem.
text_el: οὕτως κἀγὼ κατελείφθην ὑπὸ πάντων ἀπωλόμην δὲ καὶ ἔξοικος ἐγενόμην

text_en: Consider the paths of Thema, the ways of Saba , and wait a little while.
text_la: Considerate semitas Thema, itinera Saba, et expectate paulisper.
text_pt: Os caminhantes de Tema os vêem; os passageiros de Sabá esperam por eles.
text_el: ἴδετε ὁδοὺς Θαιμανων ἀτραποὺς Σαβων οἱ διορῶντες

text_en: They arc confounded, because I have hoped: they have come also even unto me, and are covered with shame.
text_la: Confusi sunt, quia speravi : venerunt quoque usque ad me, et pudore cooperti sunt.
text_pt: Ficam envergonhados, por terem confiado e, chegando ali, se confundem.
text_el: καὶ αἰσχύνην ὀφειλήσουσιν οἱ ἐπὶ πόλεσιν καὶ χρήμασιν πεποιθότες

text_en: Now you have come: and now, seeing my affliction, you are afraid.
text_la: Nunc venistis; et modo videntes plagam meam, timetis.
text_pt: Agora sois semelhantes a eles; vistes o terror, e temestes.
text_el: ἀτὰρ δὲ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐπέβητέ μοι ἀνελεημόνως ὥστε ἰδόντες τὸ ἐμὸν τραῦμα φοβήθητε

text_en: Did I say: Bring to me, and give me of your substance?
text_la: Numquid dixi : Afferte mihi, et de substantia vestra donate mihi?
text_pt: Acaso disse eu: Dai-me ou oferecei-me presentes de vossos bens?
text_el: τί γάρ μή τι ὑμᾶς ᾔτησα ἢ τῆς παρ' ὑμῶν ἰσχύος ἐπιδέομαι

text_en: Or deliver me from the hand of the enemy, and rescue me out of the hand of the mighty?
text_la: vel : Liberate me de manu hostis, et de manu robustorum eruite me?
text_pt: Ou livrai-me das mãos do opressor? Ou redimi-me das mãos dos tiranos?
text_el: ὥστε σῶσαί με ἐξ ἐχθρῶν ἢ ἐκ χειρὸς δυναστῶν ῥύσασθαί με

text_en: Teach me, and I will hold my peace: and if I have been ignorant of anything, instruct me.
text_la: Docete me, et ego tacebo : et si quid forte ignoravi, instruite me.
text_pt: Ensinai-me, e eu me calarei; e fazei-me entender em que errei.
text_el: διδάξατέ με ἐγὼ δὲ κωφεύσω εἴ τι πεπλάνημαι φράσατέ μοι

text_en: Why have you detracted the words of truth , whereas there is none of you that can reprove me?
text_la: Quare detraxistis sermonibus veritatis, cum e vobis nullus sit qui possit arguere me?
text_pt: Oh! quão fortes são as palavras da boa razão! Mas que é o que censura a vossa argüição?
text_el: ἀλλ' ὡς ἔοικεν φαῦλα ἀληθινοῦ ῥήματα οὐ γὰρ παρ' ὑμῶν ἰσχὺν αἰτοῦμαι

text_en: You dress up speeches only to rebuke, and you utter words to the wind.
text_la: Ad increpandum tantum eloquia concinnatis, et in ventum verba profertis.
text_pt: Porventura buscareis palavras para me repreenderdes, visto que as razões do desesperado são como vento?
text_el: οὐδὲ ὁ ἔλεγχος ὑμῶν ῥήμασίν με παύσει οὐδὲ γὰρ ὑμῶν φθέγμα ῥήματος ἀνέξομαι

text_en: You rush in upon the fatherless, and you endeavour to overthrow your friend.
text_la: Super pupillum irruitis, et subvertere nitimini amicum vestrum.
text_pt: Mas antes lançais sortes sobre o órfão; e cavais uma cova para o amigo.
text_el: πλὴν ὅτι ἐπ' ὀρφανῷ ἐπιπίπτετε ἐνάλλεσθε δὲ ἐπὶ φίλῳ ὑμῶν

text_en: However, finish what you have begun: give ear and see whether I lie.
text_la: Verumtamen quod cœpistis explete : præbete aurem, et videte an mentiar.
text_pt: Agora, pois, se sois servidos, olhai para mim; e vede se minto em vossa presença.
text_el: νυνὶ δὲ εἰσβλέψας εἰς πρόσωπα ὑμῶν οὐ ψεύσομαι

text_en: Answer, I beseech you, without contention: and speaking that which is just , judge.
text_la: Respondete, obsecro, absque contentione; et loquentes id quod justum est, judicate.
text_pt: Voltai, pois, não haja iniqüidade; tornai-vos, digo, que ainda a minha justiça aparecerá nisso.
text_el: καθίσατε δὴ καὶ μὴ εἴη ἄδικον καὶ πάλιν τῷ δικαίῳ συνέρχεσθε

text_en: And you shall not find iniquity in my tongue, neither shall folly sound in my mouth.
text_la: Et non invenietis in lingua mea iniquitatem, nec in faucibus meis stultitia personabit.
text_pt: Há porventura iniqüidade na minha língua? Ou não poderia o meu paladar distinguir coisas iníquas?
text_el: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἐν γλώσσῃ μου ἄδικον ἢ ὁ λάρυγξ μου οὐχὶ σύνεσιν μελετᾷ

text_en: The life of man upon earth is a warfare , and his days are like the days of a hireling.
text_la: Militia est vita hominis super terram, et sicut dies mercenarii dies ejus.
text_pt: Porventura não tem o homem guerra sobre a terra? E não são os seus dias como os dias do jornaleiro?
text_el: πότερον οὐχὶ πειρατήριόν ἐστιν ὁ βίος ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὥσπερ μισθίου αὐθημερινοῦ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ

text_en: As a servant longs for the shade, as the hireling looks for the end of his work;
text_la: Sicut servus desiderat umbram, et sicut mercenarius præstolatur finem operis sui,
text_pt: Como o servo que suspira pela sombra, e como o jornaleiro que espera pela sua paga,
text_el: ἢ ὥσπερ θεράπων δεδοικὼς τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ καὶ τετευχὼς σκιᾶς ἢ ὥσπερ μισθωτὸς ἀναμένων τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ

text_en: so I also have had empty months, and have numbered to myself wearisome nights.
text_la: sic et ego habui menses vacuos, et noctes laboriosas enumeravi mihi.
text_pt: Assim me deram por herança meses de vaidade; e noites de trabalho me prepararam.
text_el: οὕτως κἀγὼ ὑπέμεινα μῆνας κενούς νύκτες δὲ ὀδυνῶν δεδομέναι μοί εἰσιν

text_en: If I lie down to sleep, I shall say: When shall I rise? And again, I shall look for the evening, and shall be filled with sorrows even till darkness.
text_la: Si dormiero, dicam : Quando consurgam? et rursum expectabo vesperam, et replebor doloribus usque ad tenebras.
text_pt: Deitando-me a dormir, então digo: Quando me levantarei? Mas comprida é a noite, e farto-me de me revolver na cama até à alva.
text_el: ἐὰν κοιμηθῶ λέγω πότε ἡμέρα ὡς δ' ἂν ἀναστῶ πάλιν πότε ἑσπέρα πλήρης δὲ γίνομαι ὀδυνῶν ἀπὸ ἑσπέρας ἕως πρωί

text_en: My flesh is clothed with rottenness and the filth of dust; my skin is withered and drawn together.
text_la: Induta est caro mea putredine, et sordibus pulveris cutis mea aruit et contracta est.
text_pt: A minha carne se tem vestido de vermes e de torrões de pó; a minha pele está gretada, e se fez abominável.
text_el: φύρεται δέ μου τὸ σῶμα ἐν σαπρίᾳ σκωλήκων τήκω δὲ βώλακας γῆς ἀπὸ ἰχῶρος ξύων

text_en: My days have passed more swiftly than the web is cut by the weaver, and are consumed without any hope.
text_la: Dies mei velocius transierunt quam a texente tela succiditur, et consumpti sunt absque ulla spe.
text_pt: Os meus dias são mais velozes do que a lançadeira do tecelão, e acabam-se, sem esperança.
text_el: ὁ δὲ βίος μού ἐστιν ἐλαφρότερος λαλιᾶς ἀπόλωλεν δὲ ἐν κενῇ ἐλπίδι

text_en: Remember that my life is but wind, and my eye shall not return to see good things.
text_la: Memento quia ventus est vita mea, et non revertetur oculus meus ut videat bona.
text_pt: Lembra-te de que a minha vida é como o vento; os meus olhos não tornarão a ver o bem.
text_el: μνήσθητι οὖν ὅτι πνεῦμά μου ἡ ζωὴ καὶ οὐκέτι ἐπανελεύσεται ὁ ὀφθαλμός μου ἰδεῖν ἀγαθόν

text_en: Nor shall the sight of man behold me: your eyes are upon me, and I shall be no more.
text_la: Nec aspiciet me visus hominis; oculi tui in me, et non subsistam.
text_pt: Os olhos dos que agora me vêem não me verão mais; os teus olhos estarão sobre mim, porém não serei mais.
text_el: οὐ περιβλέψεταί με ὀφθαλμὸς ὁρῶντός με οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου ἐν ἐμοί καὶ οὐκέτι εἰμὶ

text_en: As a cloud is consumed, and passes away: so he that shall go down to hell shall not come up.
text_la: Sicut consumitur nubes, et pertransit, sic qui descenderit ad inferos, non ascendet.
text_pt: Assim como a nuvem se desfaz e passa, assim aquele que desce à sepultura nunca tornará a subir.
text_el: ὥσπερ νέφος ἀποκαθαρθὲν ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ ἐὰν γὰρ ἄνθρωπος καταβῇ εἰς ᾅδην οὐκέτι μὴ ἀναβῇ

text_en: Nor shall he return any more into his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
text_la: Nec revertetur ultra in domum suam, neque cognoscet eum amplius locus ejus.
text_pt: Nunca mais tornará à sua casa, nem o seu lugar jamais o conhecerá.
text_el: οὐδ' οὐ μὴ ἐπιστρέψῃ ἔτι εἰς τὸν ἴδιον οἶκον οὐδὲ μὴ ἐπιγνῷ αὐτὸν ἔτι ὁ τόπος αὐτοῦ

text_en: Wherefore, I will not spare my month, I will speak in the affliction of my spirit: I will talk with the bitterness of my soul .
text_la: Quapropter et ego non parcam ori meo : loquar in tribulatione spiritus mei; confabulabor cum amaritudine animæ meæ.
text_pt: Por isso não reprimirei a minha boca; falarei na angústia do meu espírito; queixar-me-ei na amargura da minha alma.
text_el: ἀτὰρ οὖν οὐδὲ ἐγὼ φείσομαι τῷ στόματί μου λαλήσω ἐν ἀνάγκῃ ὤν ἀνοίξω πικρίαν ψυχῆς μου συνεχόμενος

text_en: Am I a sea, or a whale, that you have inclosed me in a prison?
text_la: Numquid mare ego sum, aut cetus, quia circumdedisti me carcere?
text_pt: Sou eu porventura o mar, ou a baleia, para que me ponhas uma guarda?
text_el: πότερον θάλασσά εἰμι ἢ δράκων ὅτι κατέταξας ἐπ' ἐμὲ φυλακήν

text_en: If I say: My bed shall comfort me, and I shall be relieved, speaking with myself on my couch:
text_la: Si dixero : Consolabitur me lectulus meus, et relevabor loquens mecum in strato meo :
text_pt: Dizendo eu: Consolar-me-á a minha cama; meu leito aliviará a minha ânsia;
text_el: εἶπα ὅτι παρακαλέσει με ἡ κλίνη μου ἀνοίσω δὲ πρὸς ἐμαυτὸν ἰδίᾳ λόγον τῇ κοίτῃ μου

text_en: You will frighten me with dreams, and terrify me with visions .
text_la: terrebis me per somnia, et per visiones horrore concuties.
text_pt: Então me espantas com sonhos, e com visões me assombras;
text_el: ἐκφοβεῖς με ἐνυπνίοις καὶ ἐν ὁράμασίν με καταπλήσσεις

text_en: So that my soul rather chooses hanging, and my bones death.
text_la: Quam ob rem elegit suspendium anima mea, et mortem ossa mea.
text_pt: Assim a minha alma escolheria antes a estrangulação; e antes a morte do que a vida.
text_el: ἀπαλλάξεις ἀπὸ πνεύματός μου τὴν ψυχήν μου ἀπὸ δὲ θανάτου τὰ ὀστᾶ μου

text_en: I have done with hope, I shall now live no longer: spare me, for my days are nothing.
text_la: Desperavi : nequaquam ultra jam vivam : parce mihi, nihil enim sunt dies mei.
text_pt: A minha vida abomino, pois não viveria para sempre; retira-te de mim; pois vaidade são os meus dias.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ζήσομαι ἵνα μακροθυμήσω ἀπόστα ἀπ' ἐμοῦ κενὸς γάρ μου ὁ βίος

text_en: What is a man , that you should magnify him or why do you set your heart upon him?
text_la: Quid est homo, quia magnificas eum? aut quid apponis erga eum cor tuum?
text_pt: Que é o homem, para que tanto o engrandeças, e ponhas nele o teu coração,
text_el: τί γάρ ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος ὅτι ἐμεγάλυνας αὐτὸν ἢ ὅτι προσέχεις τὸν νοῦν εἰς αὐτὸν

text_en: You visit him early in the morning, and you prove him suddenly.
text_la: Visitas eum diluculo, et subito probas illum.
text_pt: E cada manhã o visites, e cada momento o proves?
text_el: ἢ ἐπισκοπὴν αὐτοῦ ποιήσῃ ἕως τὸ πρωὶ καὶ εἰς ἀνάπαυσιν αὐτὸν κρινεῖς

text_en: How long will you not spare me, nor suffer me to swallow down my spittle?
text_la: Usquequo non parcis mihi, nec dimittis me ut glutiam salivam meam?
text_pt: Até quando não apartarás de mim, nem me largarás, até que engula a minha saliva?
text_el: ἕως τίνος οὐκ ἐᾷς με οὐδὲ προΐῃ με ἕως ἂν καταπίω τὸν πτύελόν μου ἐν ὀδύνῃ

text_en: I have sinned : what shall I do to you, O keeper of men ? Why have you set me opposite to you and am I become burdensome to myself?
text_la: Peccavi; quid faciam tibi, o custos hominum? quare posuisti me contrarium tibi, et factus sum mihimetipsi gravis?
text_pt: Se pequei, que te farei, ó Guarda dos homens? Por que fizeste de mim um alvo para ti, para que a mim mesmo me seja pesado?
text_el: εἰ ἐγὼ ἥμαρτον τί δύναμαί σοι πρᾶξαι ὁ ἐπιστάμενος τὸν νοῦν τῶν ἀνθρώπων διὰ τί ἔθου με κατεντευκτήν σου εἰμὶ δὲ ἐπὶ σοὶ φορτίον

text_en: Why do you not remove my sin , and why do you not take away my iniquity ? Behold now I shall sleep in the dust: and if you seek me in the morning, I shall not be.
text_la: Cur non tollis peccatum meum, et quare non aufers iniquitatem meam? ecce nunc in pulvere dormiam, et si mane me quæsieris, non subsistam.
text_pt: E por que não perdoas a minha transgressão, e não tiras a minha iniqüidade? Porque agora me deitarei no pó, e de madrugada me buscarás, e não existirei mais.
text_el: καὶ διὰ τί οὐκ ἐποιήσω τῆς ἀνομίας μου λήθην καὶ καθαρισμὸν τῆς ἁμαρτίας μου νυνὶ δὲ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσομαι ὀρθρίζων δὲ οὐκέτι εἰμί

text_en: Then Baldad, the Suhite, answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Baldad Suhites, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondendo Bildade o suíta, disse:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Βαλδαδ ὁ Σαυχίτης λέγει

text_en: How long will you speak these things, and how long shall the words of your mouth be like a strong wind?
text_la: Usquequo loqueris talia, et spiritus multiplex sermones oris tui?
text_pt: Até quando falarás tais coisas, e as palavras da tua boca serão como um vento impetuoso?
text_el: μέχρι τίνος λαλήσεις ταῦτα πνεῦμα πολυρῆμον τοῦ στόματός σου

text_en: Does God pervert judgment, or does the Almighty overthrow that which is just ?
text_la: Numquid Deus supplantat judicium? aut Omnipotens subvertit quod justum est?
text_pt: Porventura perverteria Deus o direito? E perverteria o TodoPoderoso a justiça?
text_el: μὴ ὁ κύριος ἀδικήσει κρίνων ἢ ὁ τὰ πάντα ποιήσας ταράξει τὸ δίκαιον

text_en: Although your children have sinned against him, and he has left them in the hand of their iniquity :
text_la: Etiam si filii tui peccaverunt ei, et dimisit eos in manu iniquitatis suæ :
text_pt: Se teus filhos pecaram contra ele, também ele os lançou na mão da sua transgressão.
text_el: εἰ οἱ υἱοί σου ἥμαρτον ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ ἀπέστειλεν ἐν χειρὶ ἀνομίας αὐτῶν

text_en: Yet if you will arise early to God , and will beseech the Almighty:
text_la: tu tamen si diluculo consurrexeris ad Deum, et Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus;
text_pt: Mas, se tu de madrugada buscares a Deus, e ao Todo-Poderoso pedires misericórdia;
text_el: σὺ δὲ ὄρθριζε πρὸς κύριον παντοκράτορα δεόμενος

text_en: If you will walk clean and upright, he will presently awake unto you, and will make the dwelling of your justice peaceable:
text_la: si mundus et rectus incesseris : statim evigilabit ad te, et pacatum reddet habitaculum justitiæ tuæ,
text_pt: Se fores puro e reto, certamente logo despertará por ti, e restaurará a morada da tua justiça.
text_el: εἰ καθαρὸς εἶ καὶ ἀληθινός δεήσεως ἐπακούσεταί σου ἀποκαταστήσει δέ σοι δίαιταν δικαιοσύνης

text_en: In so much, that if your former things were small your latter things would be multiplied exceedingly.
text_la: in tantum ut si priora tua fuerint parva, et novissima tua multiplicentur nimis.
text_pt: O teu princípio, na verdade, terá sido pequeno, porém o teu último estado crescerá em extremo.
text_el: ἔσται οὖν τὰ μὲν πρῶτά σου ὀλίγα τὰ δὲ ἔσχατά σου ἀμύθητα

text_en: For inquire of the former generation , and search diligently into the memory of the fathers:
text_la: Interroga enim generationem pristinam, et diligenter investiga patrum memoriam
text_pt: Pois, eu te peço, pergunta agora às gerações passadas; e prepara-te para a inquirição de seus pais.
text_el: ἐπερώτησον γὰρ γενεὰν πρώτην ἐξιχνίασον δὲ κατὰ γένος πατέρων

text_en: (For we are but of yesterday, and are ignorant that our days upon earth are but a shadow.)
text_la: (hesterni quippe sumus, et ignoramus, quoniam sicut umbra dies nostri sunt super terram),
text_pt: Porque nós somos de ontem, e nada sabemos; porquanto nossos dias sobre a terra são como a sombra.
text_el: χθιζοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν σκιὰ γάρ ἐστιν ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὁ βίος

text_en: And they shall teach you: they shall speak to you, and utter words out of their hearts.
text_la: et ipsi docebunt te, loquentur tibi, et de corde suo proferent eloquia.
text_pt: Porventura não te ensinarão eles, e não te falarão, e do seu coração não tirarão palavras?
text_el: ἦ οὐχ οὗτοί σε διδάξουσιν καὶ ἀναγγελοῦσιν καὶ ἐκ καρδίας ἐξάξουσιν ῥήματα

text_en: Can the rush be green without moisture? Or sedge bush grow without water?
text_la: Numquid vivere potest scirpus absque humore? aut crescere carectum sine aqua?
text_pt: Porventura cresce o junco sem lodo? Ou cresce a espadana sem água?
text_el: μὴ θάλλει πάπυρος ἄνευ ὕδατος ἢ ὑψωθήσεται βούτομον ἄνευ πότου

text_en: When it is yet in flower, and is not plucked u with the hand, it withers before all herbs.
text_la: Cum adhuc sit in flore, nec carpatur manu, ante omnes herbas arescit.
text_pt: Estando ainda no seu verdor, ainda que não cortada, todavia antes de qualquer outra erva se seca.
text_el: ἔτι ὂν ἐπὶ ῥίζης καὶ οὐ μὴ θερισθῇ πρὸ τοῦ πιεῖν πᾶσα βοτάνη οὐχὶ ξηραίνεται

text_en: Even so are the ways of all that forget God , and the hope of the hypocrite shall perish:
text_la: Sic viæ omnium qui obliviscuntur Deum, et spes hypocritæ peribit.
text_pt: Assim são as veredas de todos quantos se esquecem de Deus; e a esperança do hipócrita perecerá.
text_el: οὕτως τοίνυν ἔσται τὰ ἔσχατα πάντων τῶν ἐπιλανθανομένων τοῦ κυρίου ἐλπὶς γὰρ ἀσεβοῦς ἀπολεῖται

text_en: His folly shall not please him, and his trust shall be like the spider's web.
text_la: Non ei placebit vecordia sua, et sicut tela aranearum fiducia ejus.
text_pt: Cuja esperança fica frustrada; e a sua confiança será como a teia de aranha.
text_el: ἀοίκητος γὰρ αὐτοῦ ἔσται ὁ οἶκος ἀράχνη δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀποβήσεται ἡ σκηνή

text_en: He shall lean upon his house, and it shall no stand: he shall prop it up, and it shall not rise:
text_la: Innitetur super domum suam, et non stabit; fulciet eam, et non consurget.
text_pt: Encostar-se-á à sua casa, mas ela não subsistirá; apegar-se-á a ela, mas não ficará em pé.
text_el: ἐὰν ὑπερείσῃ τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ στῇ ἐπιλαβομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ ὑπομείνῃ

text_en: He seems to have moisture before the sun comes; and at his rising, his blossom shall shoot forth.
text_la: Humectus videtur antequam veniat sol, et in ortu suo germen ejus egredietur.
text_pt: Ele é viçoso perante o sol, e os seus renovos saem sobre o seu jardim;
text_el: ὑγρὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὑπὸ ἡλίου καὶ ἐκ σαπρίας αὐτοῦ ὁ ῥάδαμνος αὐτοῦ ἐξελεύσεται

text_en: His roots shall be thick upon a heap of stones; and among the stones he shall abide.
text_la: Super acervum petrarum radices ejus densabuntur, et inter lapides commorabitur.
text_pt: As suas raízes se entrelaçam, junto à fonte; para o pedregal atenta.
text_el: ἐπὶ συναγωγὴν λίθων κοιμᾶται ἐν δὲ μέσῳ χαλίκων ζήσεται

text_en: If one swallow him up out of his place, he shall deny him, and shall say: I know you not.
text_la: Si absorbuerit eum de loco suo, negabit eum, et dicet : Non novi te.
text_pt: Se Deus o consumir do seu lugar, negá-lo-á este, dizendo: Nunca te vi!
text_el: ἐὰν καταπίῃ ὁ τόπος ψεύσεται αὐτόν οὐχ ἑόρακας τοιαῦτα

text_en: For this is the joy of his way, that others may spring again out of the earth.
text_la: Hæc est enim lætitia viæ ejus, ut rursum de terra alii germinentur.
text_pt: Eis que este é a alegria do seu caminho, e outros brotarão do pó.
text_el: ὅτι καταστροφὴ ἀσεβοῦς τοιαύτη ἐκ δὲ γῆς ἄλλον ἀναβλαστήσει

text_en: God will not cast away the simple, nor reach out his hand to the evil doer:
text_la: Deus non projiciet simplicem, nec porriget manum malignis,
text_pt: Eis que Deus não rejeitará ao reto; nem toma pela mão aos malfeitores;
text_el: ὁ γὰρ κύριος οὐ μὴ ἀποποιήσηται τὸν ἄκακον πᾶν δὲ δῶρον ἀσεβοῦς οὐ δέξεται

text_en: Until your mouth be filled with laughter, and your lips with rejoicing.
text_la: donec impleatur risu os tuum, et labia tua jubilo.
text_pt: Até que de riso te encha a boca, e os teus lábios de júbilo.
text_el: ἀληθινῶν δὲ στόμα ἐμπλήσει γέλωτος τὰ δὲ χείλη αὐτῶν ἐξομολογήσεως

text_en: They that hate you, shall be clothed with confusion: and the dwelling of the wicked shall not stand.
text_la: Qui oderunt te induentur confusione, et tabernaculum impiorum non subsistet.
text_pt: Os que te odeiam se vestirão de confusão, e a tenda dos ímpios não existirá mais.
text_el: οἱ δὲ ἐχθροὶ αὐτῶν ἐνδύσονται αἰσχύνην δίαιτα δὲ ἀσεβοῦς οὐκ ἔσται

text_en: And Job answered, and said:
text_la: Et respondens Job, ait:
text_pt: Então Jó respondeu, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει

text_en: Indeed I know it is so, and that man cannot be justified, compared with God .
text_la: Vere scio quod ita sit, et quod non justificetur homo compositus Deo.
text_pt: Na verdade sei que assim é; porque, como se justificaria o homem para com Deus?
text_el: ἐπ' ἀληθείας οἶδα ὅτι οὕτως ἐστίν πῶς γὰρ ἔσται δίκαιος βροτὸς παρὰ κυρίῳ

text_en: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one for a thousand.
text_la: Si voluerit contendere cum eo, non poterit ei respondere unum pro mille.
text_pt: Se quiser contender com ele, nem a uma de mil coisas lhe poderá responder.
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ βούληται κριθῆναι αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ ὑπακούσῃ αὐτῷ ἵνα μὴ ἀντείπῃ πρὸς ἕνα λόγον αὐτοῦ ἐκ χιλίων

text_en: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has resisted him, and has had peace?
text_la: Sapiens corde est, et fortis robore : quis restitit ei, et pacem habuit?
text_pt: Ele é sábio de coração, e forte em poder; quem se endureceu contra ele, e teve paz?
text_el: σοφὸς γάρ ἐστιν διανοίᾳ κραταιός τε καὶ μέγας τίς σκληρὸς γενόμενος ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ ὑπέμεινεν

text_en: Who has removed mountains, and they whom he overthrew in his wrath , knew it not.
text_la: Qui transtulit montes, et nescierunt hi quos subvertit in furore suo.
text_pt: Ele é o que remove os montes, sem que o saibam, e o que os transtorna no seu furor.
text_el: ὁ παλαιῶν ὄρη καὶ οὐκ οἴδασιν ὁ καταστρέφων αὐτὰ ὀργῇ

text_en: Who shakes the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.
text_la: Qui commovet terram de loco suo, et columnæ ejus concutiuntur.
text_pt: O que sacode a terra do seu lugar, e as suas colunas estremecem.
text_el: ὁ σείων τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανὸν ἐκ θεμελίων οἱ δὲ στῦλοι αὐτῆς σαλεύονται

text_en: Who commands the sun, and it rises not: and shuts up the stars, as it were, under a seal:
text_la: Qui præcipit soli, et non oritur, et stellas claudit quasi sub signaculo.
text_pt: O que fala ao sol, e ele não nasce, e sela as estrelas.
text_el: ὁ λέγων τῷ ἡλίῳ καὶ οὐκ ἀνατέλλει κατὰ δὲ ἄστρων κατασφραγίζει

text_en: Who alone spreads out the heavens , and walks upon the waves of the sea,
text_la: Qui extendit cælos solus, et graditur super fluctus maris.
text_pt: O que sozinho estende os céus, e anda sobre os altos do mar.
text_el: ὁ τανύσας τὸν οὐρανὸν μόνος καὶ περιπατῶν ὡς ἐπ' ἐδάφους ἐπὶ θαλάσσης

text_en: who makes Arcturus, and Orion , and Hyades , and the inner parts of the south .
text_la: Qui facit Arcturum et Oriona, et Hyadas et interiora austri.
text_pt: O que fez a Ursa, o Órion, e o Sete-estrelo, e as recâmaras do sul.
text_el: ὁ ποιῶν Πλειάδα καὶ ἕσπερον καὶ ἀρκτοῦρον καὶ ταμίεια νότου

text_en: Who does things great and incomprehensible, and wonderful, of which there is no number.
text_la: Qui facit magna, et incomprehensibilia, et mirabilia, quorum non est numerus.
text_pt: O que faz coisas grandes e inescrutáveis; e maravilhas sem número.
text_el: ὁ ποιῶν μεγάλα καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστα ἔνδοξά τε καὶ ἐξαίσια ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμός

text_en: If he come to me, I shall not see him: if he depart, I shall not understand.
text_la: Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum; si abierit, non intelligam.
text_pt: Eis que ele passa por diante de mim, e não o vejo; e torna a passar perante mim, e não o sinto.
text_el: ἐὰν ὑπερβῇ με οὐ μὴ ἴδω καὶ ἐὰν παρέλθῃ με οὐδ' ὧς ἔγνων

text_en: If he examine on a sudden, who shall answer him? Or who can say: Why do you so?
text_la: Si repente interroget, quis respondebit ei? vel quis dicere potest : Cur ita facis?
text_pt: Eis que arrebata a presa; quem lha fará restituir? Quem lhe dirá: Que é o que fazes?
text_el: ἐὰν ἀπαλλάξῃ τίς ἀποστρέψει ἢ τίς ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ τί ἐποίησας

text_en: God , whose wrath no man can resist, and under whom they stoop that bear up the world.
text_la: Deus, cujus iræ nemo resistere potest, et sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem.
text_pt: Deus não revogará a sua ira; debaixo dele se encurvam os auxiliadores soberbos.
text_el: αὐτὸς γὰρ ἀπέστραπται ὀργήν ὑπ' αὐτοῦ ἐκάμφθησαν κήτη τὰ ὑπ' οὐρανόν

text_en: What am I then, that I should answer him, and have words with him?
text_la: Quantus ergo sum ego, ut respondeam ei, et loquar verbis meis cum eo?
text_pt: Quanto menos lhe responderia eu, ou escolheria diante dele as minhas palavras!
text_el: ἐὰν δέ μου ὑπακούσηται ἦ διακρινεῖ τὰ ῥήματά μου

text_en: I, who although I should have any just thing, would not answer, but would make supplication to my judge.
text_la: qui etiam si habuero quippiam justum, non respondebo : sed meum judicem deprecabor.
text_pt: Porque, ainda que eu fosse justo, não lhe responderia; antes ao meu Juiz pediria misericórdia.
text_el: ἐάν τε γὰρ ὦ δίκαιος οὐκ εἰσακούσεταί μου τοῦ κρίματος αὐτοῦ δεηθήσομαι

text_en: And if he should hear me when I call, I should not believe that he had heard my voice.
text_la: Et cum invocantem exaudierit me, non credo quod audierit vocem meam.
text_pt: Ainda que chamasse, e ele me respondesse, nem por isso creria que desse ouvidos à minha voz.
text_el: ἐάν τε καλέσω καὶ ὑπακούσῃ οὐ πιστεύω ὅτι εἰσακήκοέν μου

text_en: For he shall crush me in a whirlwind, and multiply my wounds even without cause.
text_la: In turbine enim conteret me, et multiplicabit vulnera mea, etiam sine causa.
text_pt: Porque me quebranta com uma tempestade, e multiplica as minhas chagas sem causa.
text_el: μὴ γνόφῳ με ἐκτρίψῃ πολλὰ δέ μου τὰ συντρίμματα πεποίηκεν διὰ κενῆς

text_en: He allows not my spirit to rest, and he fills me with bitterness.
text_la: Non concedit requiescere spiritum meum, et implet me amaritudinibus.
text_pt: Não me permite respirar, antes me farta de amarguras.
text_el: οὐκ ἐᾷ γάρ με ἀναπνεῦσαι ἐνέπλησεν δέ με πικρίας

text_en: If strength be demanded, he is most strong: if equity of judgment, no man dare bear witness for me.
text_la: Si fortitudo quæritur, robustissimus est; si æquitas judicii, nemo audet pro me testimonium dicere.
text_pt: Quanto às forças, eis que ele é o forte; e, quanto ao juízo, quem me citará com ele?
text_el: ὅτι μὲν γὰρ ἰσχύι κρατεῖ τίς οὖν κρίματι αὐτοῦ ἀντιστήσεται

text_en: If I would justify myself, my own mouth shall condemn me: if I would show myself innocent, he shall prove me wicked .
text_la: Si justificare me voluero, os meum condemnabit me; si innocentem ostendero, pravum me comprobabit.
text_pt: Se eu me justificar, a minha boca me condenará; se for perfeito, então ela me declarará perverso.
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ ὦ δίκαιος τὸ στόμα μου ἀσεβήσει ἐάν τε ὦ ἄμεμπτος σκολιὸς ἀποβήσομαι

text_en: Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of, and I shall be weary of my life.
