text_la: Etiam si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea, et tædebit me vitæ meæ.
text_pt: Se for perfeito, não estimo a minha alma; desprezo a minha vida.
text_el: εἴτε γὰρ ἠσέβησα οὐκ οἶδα τῇ ψυχῇ πλὴν ὅτι ἀφαιρεῖταί μου ἡ ζωή

text_en: One thing there is that I have spoken, both the innocent and the wicked he consumes.
text_la: Unum est quod locutus sum : et innocentem et impium ipse consumit.
text_pt: A coisa é esta; por isso eu digo que ele consome ao perfeito e ao ímpio.
text_el: διὸ εἶπον μέγαν καὶ δυνάστην ἀπολλύει ὀργή

text_en: If he scourge, let him kill at once, and not laugh at the pains of the innocent.
text_la: Si flagellat, occidat semel, et non de pœnis innocentum rideat.
text_pt: Quando o açoite mata de repente, então ele zomba da prova dos inocentes.
text_el: ὅτι φαῦλοι ἐν θανάτῳ ἐξαισίῳ ἀλλὰ δίκαιοι καταγελῶνται

text_en: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked, he covers the face of the judges thereof: and if it be not he, who is it then?
text_la: Terra data est in manus impii; vultum judicum ejus operit. Quod si non ille est, quis ergo est?
text_pt: A terra é entregue nas mãos do ímpio; ele cobre o rosto dos juízes; se não é ele, quem é, logo?
text_el: παραδέδονται γὰρ εἰς χεῖρας ἀσεβοῦς πρόσωπα κριτῶν αὐτῆς συγκαλύπτει εἰ δὲ μὴ αὐτός τίς ἐστιν

text_en: My days have been swifter than a post: they have fled away and have not seen good .
text_la: Dies mei velociores fuerunt cursore; fugerunt, et non viderunt bonum.
text_pt: E os meus dias são mais velozes do que um correio; fugiram, e não viram o bem.
text_el: ὁ δὲ βίος μού ἐστιν ἐλαφρότερος δρομέως ἀπέδρασαν καὶ οὐκ εἴδοσαν

text_en: They have passed by as ships carrying fruits, as an eagle flying to the prey.
text_la: Pertransierunt quasi naves poma portantes; sicut aquila volans ad escam.
text_pt: Passam como navios veleiros; como águia que se lança à comida.
text_el: ἦ καὶ ἔστιν ναυσὶν ἴχνος ὁδοῦ ἢ ἀετοῦ πετομένου ζητοῦντος βοράν

text_en: If I say: I will not speak so: I change my face, and am tormented with sorrow.
text_la: Cum dixero : Nequaquam ita loquar : commuto faciem meam, et dolore torqueor.
text_pt: Se eu disser: Eu me esquecerei da minha queixa, e mudarei o meu aspecto e tomarei alento,
text_el: ἐάν τε γὰρ εἴπω ἐπιλήσομαι λαλῶν συγκύψας τῷ προσώπῳ στενάξω

text_en: I feared all my works, knowing that you did not spare the offender.
text_la: Verebar omnia opera mea, sciens quod non parceres delinquenti.
text_pt: Receio todas as minhas dores, porque bem sei que não me terás por inocente.
text_el: σείομαι πᾶσιν τοῖς μέλεσιν οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἀθῷόν με ἐάσεις

text_en: But if so also I am wicked , why have I laboured in vain?
text_la: Si autem et sic impius sum, quare frustra laboravi?
text_pt: E, sendo eu ímpio, por que trabalharei em vão?
text_el: ἐπειδὴ δέ εἰμι ἀσεβής διὰ τί οὐκ ἀπέθανον

text_en: If I be washed, as it were, with snow waters, and my hands shall shine ever 80. clean:
text_la: Si lotus fuero quasi aquis nivis, et fulserint velut mundissimæ manus meæ,
text_pt: Ainda que me lave com água de neve, e purifique as minhas mãos com sabão,
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀπολούσωμαι χιόνι καὶ ἀποκαθάρωμαι χερσὶν καθαραῖς

text_en: Yet you shall plunge me in filth, and my garments shall abhor me.
text_la: tamen sordibus intinges me, et abominabuntur me vestimenta mea.
text_pt: Ainda me submergirás no fosso, e as minhas próprias vestes me abominarão.
text_el: ἱκανῶς ἐν ῥύπῳ με ἔβαψας ἐβδελύξατο δέ με ἡ στολή

text_en: For I shall not answer a man that is like myself: nor one that may be heard with me equally in judgment.
text_la: Neque enim viro qui similis mei est, respondebo; nec qui mecum in judicio ex æquo possit audiri.
text_pt: Porque ele não é homem, como eu, a quem eu responda, vindo juntamente a juízo.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ εἶ ἄνθρωπος κατ' ἐμέ ᾧ ἀντικρινοῦμαι ἵνα ἔλθωμεν ὁμοθυμαδὸν εἰς κρίσιν

text_en: There is none that may be able to reprove both, and to put his hand between both.
text_la: Non est qui utrumque valeat arguere, et ponere manum suam in ambobus.
text_pt: Não há entre nós árbitro que ponha a mão sobre nós ambos.
text_el: εἴθε ἦν ὁ μεσίτης ἡμῶν καὶ ἐλέγχων καὶ διακούων ἀνὰ μέσον ἀμφοτέρων

text_en: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me.
text_la: Auferat a me virgam suam, et pavor ejus non me terreat.
text_pt: Tire ele a sua vara de cima de mim, e não me amedronte o seu terror.
text_el: ἀπαλλαξάτω ἀπ' ἐμοῦ τὴν ῥάβδον ὁ δὲ φόβος αὐτοῦ μή με στροβείτω

text_en: I will speak, and will not fear him: for I cannot answer while I am in fear.
text_la: Loquar, et non timebo eum; neque enim possum metuens respondere.
text_pt: Então falarei, e não o temerei; porque não sou assim em mim mesmo.
text_el: καὶ οὐ μὴ φοβηθῶ ἀλλὰ λαλήσω οὐ γὰρ οὕτω συνεπίσταμαι

text_en: My soul is weary of my life, I will let go my speech against myself, I will speak in the bitterness of my soul .
text_la: Tædet animam meam vitæ meæ; dimittam adversum me eloquium meum : loquar in amaritudine animæ meæ.
text_pt: A minha alma tem tédio da minha vida; darei livre curso à minha queixa, falarei na amargura da minha alma.
text_el: κάμνων τῇ ψυχῇ μου στένων ἐπαφήσω ἐπ' αὐτὸν τὰ ῥήματά μου λαλήσω πικρίᾳ ψυχῆς μου συνεχόμενος

text_en: I will say to God : Do not condemn me: tell me why you judge me so?
text_la: Dicam Deo : Noli me condemnare; indica mihi cur me ita judices.
text_pt: Direi a Deus: Não me condenes; faze-me saber por que contendes comigo.
text_el: καὶ ἐρῶ πρὸς κύριον μή με ἀσεβεῖν δίδασκε καὶ διὰ τί με οὕτως ἔκρινας

text_en: Does it seem good to you that you should calumniate me, and oppress me, the work of your own hands, and help the counsel of the wicked?
text_la: Numquid bonum tibi videtur, si calumnieris me, et opprimas me opus manuum tuarum, et consilium impiorum adjuves?
text_pt: Parece-te bem que me oprimas, que rejeites o trabalho das tuas mãos e resplandeças sobre o conselho dos ímpios?
text_el: ἦ καλόν σοι ἐὰν ἀδικήσω ὅτι ἀπείπω ἔργα χειρῶν σου βουλῇ δὲ ἀσεβῶν προσέσχες

text_en: Have you eyes of flesh: or, shall you see as man sees?
text_la: Numquid oculi carnei tibi sunt? aut sicut videt homo, et tu videbis?
text_pt: Tens tu porventura olhos de carne? Vês tu como vê o homem?
text_el: ἦ ὥσπερ βροτὸς ὁρᾷ καθορᾷς ἢ καθὼς ὁρᾷ ἄνθρωπος βλέψῃ

text_en: Are your days as the days of man , and are your years as the times of men :
text_la: Numquid sicut dies hominis dies tui, et anni tui sicut humana sunt tempora,
text_pt: São os teus dias como os dias do homem? Ou são os teus anos como os anos de um homem,
text_el: ἦ ὁ βίος σου ἀνθρώπινός ἐστιν ἢ τὰ ἔτη σου ἀνδρός

text_en: That you should inquire after my iniquity , and search after my sin ?
text_la: ut quæras iniquitatem meam, et peccatum meum scruteris,
text_pt: Para te informares da minha iniqüidade, e averiguares o meu pecado?
text_el: ὅτι ἀνεζήτησας τὴν ἀνομίαν μου καὶ τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου ἐξιχνίασας

text_en: And should know that I have done no wicked thing, whereas there is no man that can deliver out of your hand?
text_la: et scias quia nihil impium fecerim, cum sit nemo qui de manu tua possit eruere?
text_pt: Bem sabes tu que eu não sou iníquo; todavia ninguém há que me livre da tua mão.
text_el: οἶδας γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἠσέβησα ἀλλὰ τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν σου ἐξαιρούμενος

text_en: Your hands have made me, and fashioned me wholly round about, and do you thus cast me down headlong on a sudden?
text_la: Manus tuæ fecerunt me, et plasmaverunt me totum in circuitu : et sic repente præcipitas me?
text_pt: As tuas mãos me fizeram e me formaram completamente; contudo me consomes.
text_el: αἱ χεῖρές σου ἔπλασάν με καὶ ἐποίησάν με μετὰ ταῦτα μεταβαλών με ἔπαισας

text_en: Remember, I beseech you, that you have made me as the clay, and you will bring me into dust.
text_la: Memento, quæso, quod sicut lutum feceris me, et in pulverem reduces me.
text_pt: Peço-te que te lembres de que como barro me formaste e me farás voltar ao pó.
text_el: μνήσθητι ὅτι πηλόν με ἔπλασας εἰς δὲ γῆν με πάλιν ἀποστρέφεις

text_en: Have you not milked me as milk, and curdled me like cheese?
text_la: Nonne sicut lac mulsisti me, et sicut caseum me coagulasti?
text_pt: Porventura não me vazaste como leite, e como queijo não me coalhaste?
text_el: ἦ οὐχ ὥσπερ γάλα με ἤμελξας ἐτύρωσας δέ με ἴσα τυρῷ

text_en: You have clothed me with skin and flesh: you have put me together with bones and sinews:
text_la: Pelle et carnibus vestisti me; ossibus et nervis compegisti me.
text_pt: De pele e carne me vestiste, e de ossos e nervos me teceste.
text_el: δέρμα καὶ κρέας με ἐνέδυσας ὀστέοις δὲ καὶ νεύροις με ἐνεῖρας

text_en: You have granted me life and mercy, and your visitation has preserved my spirit.
text_la: Vitam et misericordiam tribuisti mihi, et visitatio tua custodivit spiritum meum.
text_pt: Vida e misericórdia me concedeste; e o teu cuidado guardou o meu espírito.
text_el: ζωὴν δὲ καὶ ἔλεος ἔθου παρ' ἐμοί ἡ δὲ ἐπισκοπή σου ἐφύλαξέν μου τὸ πνεῦμα

text_en: Although you conceal these things in your heart, yet I know that you remember all things.
text_la: Licet hæc celes in corde tuo, tamen scio quia universorum memineris.
text_pt: Porém estas coisas as ocultaste no teu coração; bem sei eu que isto esteve contigo.
text_el: ταῦτα ἔχων ἐν σεαυτῷ οἶδα ὅτι πάντα δύνασαι ἀδυνατεῖ δέ σοι οὐθέν

text_en: If I have sinned , and you have spared me for an hour: why do you not suffer me to be clean from my iniquity ?
text_la: Si peccavi, et ad horam pepercisti mihi, cur ab iniquitate mea mundum me esse non pateris?
text_pt: Se eu pecar, tu me observas; e da minha iniqüidade não me escusarás.
text_el: ἐάν τε γὰρ ἁμάρτω φυλάσσεις με ἀπὸ δὲ ἀνομίας οὐκ ἀθῷόν με πεποίηκας

text_en: And if I be wicked , woe unto me: and if just , I shall not lift up my head, being filled with affliction and misery.
text_la: Et si impius fuero, væ mihi est; et si justus, non levabo caput, saturatus afflictione et miseria.
text_pt: Se for ímpio, ai de mim! E se for justo, não levantarei a minha cabeça; farto estou da minha ignomínia; e vê qual é a minha aflição,
text_el: ἐάν τε γὰρ ἀσεβὴς ὦ οἴμμοι ἐάν τε ὦ δίκαιος οὐ δύναμαι ἀνακύψαι πλήρης γὰρ ἀτιμίας εἰμί

text_en: And for pride you will take me as a lioness, and returning, you torment me wonderfully.
text_la: Et propter superbiam quasi leænam capies me, reversusque mirabiliter me crucias.
text_pt: Porque se vai crescendo; tu me caças como a um leão feroz; tornas a fazer maravilhas para comigo.
text_el: ἀγρεύομαι γὰρ ὥσπερ λέων εἰς σφαγήν πάλιν δὲ μεταβαλὼν δεινῶς με ὀλέκεις

text_en: You renew your witnesses against me, and multiply your wrath upon me, and pains war against me.
text_la: Instauras testes tuos contra me, et multiplicas iram tuam adversum me, et pœnæ militant in me.
text_pt: Tu renovas contra mim as tuas testemunhas, e multiplicas contra mim a tua ira; reveses e combate estão comigo.
text_el: ἐπανακαινίζων ἐπ' ἐμὲ τὴν ἔτασίν μου ὀργῇ δὲ μεγάλῃ μοι ἐχρήσω ἐπήγαγες δὲ ἐπ' ἐμὲ πειρατήρια

text_en: Why did you bring me forth out of the womb? O that I had been consumed, that eye might not see me!
text_la: Quare de vulva eduxisti me? qui utinam consumptus essem, ne oculus me videret.
text_pt: Por que, pois, me tiraste da madre? Ah! se então tivera expirado, e olho nenhum me visse!
text_el: ἵνα τί οὖν ἐκ κοιλίας με ἐξήγαγες καὶ οὐκ ἀπέθανον ὀφθαλμὸς δέ με οὐκ εἶδεν

text_en: I should have been as if I had not been, carried from the womb to the grave.
text_la: Fuissem quasi non essem, de utero translatus ad tumulum.
text_pt: Então eu teria sido como se nunca fora; e desde o ventre seria levado à sepultura!
text_el: καὶ ὥσπερ οὐκ ὢν ἐγενόμην διὰ τί γὰρ ἐκ γαστρὸς εἰς μνῆμα οὐκ ἀπηλλάγην

text_en: Shall not the fewness of my days be ended shortly? Suffer me, therefore, that I may lament my sorrow a little:
text_la: Numquid non paucitas dierum meorum finietur brevi? dimitte ergo me, ut plangam paululum dolorem meum,
text_pt: Porventura não são poucos os meus dias? Cessa, pois, e deixa-me, para que por um pouco eu tome alento.
text_el: ἦ οὐκ ὀλίγος ἐστὶν ὁ χρόνος τοῦ βίου μου ἔασόν με ἀναπαύσασθαι μικρὸν

text_en: Before I go and return no more, to a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death:
text_la: antequam vadam, et non revertar, ad terram tenebrosam, et opertam mortis caligine :
text_pt: Antes que eu vá para o lugar de que não voltarei, à terra da escuridão e da sombra da morte;
text_el: πρὸ τοῦ με πορευθῆναι ὅθεν οὐκ ἀναστρέψω εἰς γῆν σκοτεινὴν καὶ γνοφεράν

text_en: A land of misery and darkness, where the shadow of death, and no order, but everlasting horror dwells.
text_la: terram miseriæ et tenebrarum, ubi umbra mortis et nullus ordo, sed sempiternus horror inhabitat.
text_pt: Terra escuríssima, como a própria escuridão, terra da sombra da morte e sem ordem alguma, e onde a luz é como a escuridão.
text_el: εἰς γῆν σκότους αἰωνίου οὗ οὐκ ἔστιν φέγγος οὐδὲ ὁρᾶν ζωὴν βροτῶν

text_en: Then Sophar the Naamathite answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Sophar Naamathites, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondeu Zofar, o naamatita, e disse:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Σωφαρ ὁ Μιναῖος λέγει

text_en: Shall not he that speaks much, hear also? Or shall a man full of talk be justified?
text_la: Numquid qui multa loquitur, non et audiet? aut vir verbosus justificabitur?
text_pt: Porventura não se dará resposta à multidão de palavras? E o homem falador será justificado?
text_el: ὁ τὰ πολλὰ λέγων καὶ ἀντακούσεται ἢ καὶ ὁ εὔλαλος οἴεται εἶναι δίκαιος εὐλογημένος γεννητὸς γυναικὸς ὀλιγόβιος

text_en: Shall men hold their peace to you only? And when you have mocked others, shall no man confute you?
text_la: Tibi soli tacebunt homines? et cum ceteros irriseris, a nullo confutaberis?
text_pt: Às tuas mentiras se hão de calar os homens? E zombarás tu sem que ninguém te envergonhe?
text_el: μὴ πολὺς ἐν ῥήμασιν γίνου οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἀντικρινόμενός σοι

text_en: For you have said: My word is pure, and I am clean in your sight.
text_la: Dixisti enim : Purus est sermo meus, et mundus sum in conspectu tuo.
text_pt: Pois dizes: A minha doutrina é pura, e limpo sou aos teus olhos.
text_el: μὴ γὰρ λέγε ὅτι καθαρός εἰμι τοῖς ἔργοις καὶ ἄμεμπτος ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ

text_en: And I wish that God would speak with you, and would open his lips to you,
text_la: Atque utinam Deus loqueretur tecum, et aperiret labia sua tibi,
text_pt: Mas na verdade, quem dera que Deus falasse e abrisse os seus lábios contra ti!
text_el: ἀλλὰ πῶς ἂν ὁ κύριος λαλήσαι πρὸς σέ καὶ ἀνοίξει χείλη αὐτοῦ μετὰ σοῦ

text_en: that he might show you the secrets of wisdom, and that his law is manifold, and you might understand that he exacts much less of you, than your iniquity deserves.
text_la: ut ostenderet tibi secreta sapientiæ, et quod multiplex esset lex ejus : et intelligeres quod multo minora exigaris ab eo quam meretur iniquitas tua!
text_pt: E te fizesse saber os segredos da sabedoria, que é multíplice em eficácia; sabe, pois, que Deus exige de ti menos do que merece a tua iniqüidade.
text_el: εἶτα ἀναγγελεῖ σοι δύναμιν σοφίας ὅτι διπλοῦς ἔσται τῶν κατὰ σέ καὶ τότε γνώσῃ ὅτι ἄξιά σοι ἀπέβη ἀπὸ κυρίου ὧν ἡμάρτηκας

text_en: Peradventure you will comprehend the steps of God , and will find out the Almighty perfectly?
text_la: Forsitan vestigia Dei comprehendes, et usque ad perfectum Omnipotentem reperies?
text_pt: Porventura alcançarás os caminhos de Deus, ou chegarás à perfeição do Todo-Poderoso?
text_el: ἦ ἴχνος κυρίου εὑρήσεις ἢ εἰς τὰ ἔσχατα ἀφίκου ἃ ἐποίησεν ὁ παντοκράτωρ

text_en: He is higher than heaven , and what will you do? He is deeper than hell, and how will you know?
text_la: Excelsior cælo est, et quid facies? profundior inferno, et unde cognosces?
text_pt: Como as alturas dos céus é a sua sabedoria; que poderás tu fazer? É mais profunda do que o inferno, que poderás tu saber?
text_el: ὑψηλὸς ὁ οὐρανός καὶ τί ποιήσεις βαθύτερα δὲ τῶν ἐν ᾅδου τί οἶδας

text_en: The measure of him is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
text_la: Longior terra mensura ejus, et latior mari.
text_pt: Mais comprida é a sua medida do que a terra, e mais larga do que o mar.
text_el: ἢ μακρότερα μέτρου γῆς ἢ εὔρους θαλάσσης

text_en: If he shall overturn all things, or shall press them together, who shall contradict him?
text_la: Si subverterit omnia, vel in unum coarctaverit, quis contradicet ei?
text_pt: Se ele passar, aprisionar, ou chamar a juízo, quem o impedirá?
text_el: ἐὰν δὲ καταστρέψῃ τὰ πάντα τίς ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ τί ἐποίησας

text_en: For he knows the vanity of men , and when he sees iniquity , does he not consider it?
text_la: Ipse enim novit hominum vanitatem; et videns iniquitatem, nonne considerat?
text_pt: Porque ele conhece aos homens vãos, e vê o vício; e não o terá em consideração?
text_el: αὐτὸς γὰρ οἶδεν ἔργα ἀνόμων ἰδὼν δὲ ἄτοπα οὐ παρόψεται

text_en: A vain man is lifted up into pride , and thinks himself born free like a wild ass' colt.
text_la: Vir vanus in superbiam erigitur, et tamquam pullum onagri se liberum natum putat.
text_pt: Mas o homem vão é falto de entendimento; sim, o homem nasce como a cria do jumento montês.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος δὲ ἄλλως νήχεται λόγοις βροτὸς δὲ γεννητὸς γυναικὸς ἴσα ὄνῳ ἐρημίτῃ

text_en: But you have hardened your heart, and have spread your hands to him.
text_la: Tu autem firmasti cor tuum, et expandisti ad eum manus tuas.
text_pt: Se tu preparares o teu coração, e estenderes as tuas mãos para ele;
text_el: εἰ γὰρ σὺ καθαρὰν ἔθου τὴν καρδίαν σου ὑπτιάζεις δὲ χεῖρας πρὸς αὐτόν

text_en: If you will put away from you the iniquity that is in your hand, and let not injustice remain in your tabernacle:
text_la: Si iniquitatem quæ est in manu tua abstuleris a te, et non manserit in tabernaculo tuo injustitia,
text_pt: Se há iniqüidade na tua mão, lança-a para longe de ti e não deixes habitar a injustiça nas tuas tendas.
text_el: εἰ ἄνομόν τί ἐστιν ἐν χερσίν σου πόρρω ποίησον αὐτὸ ἀπὸ σοῦ ἀδικία δὲ ἐν διαίτῃ σου μὴ αὐλισθήτω

text_en: Then may you lift up your face without spot, and you shall be steadfast, and shall not fear.
text_la: tunc levare poteris faciem tuam absque macula; et eris stabilis, et non timebis.
text_pt: Porque então o teu rosto levantarás sem mácula; e estarás firme, e não temerás.
text_el: οὕτως γὰρ ἀναλάμψει σου τὸ πρόσωπον ὥσπερ ὕδωρ καθαρόν ἐκδύσῃ δὲ ῥύπον καὶ οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇς

text_en: You shall also forget misery, and remember it only as waters that are passed away.
text_la: Miseriæ quoque oblivisceris, et quasi aquarum quæ præterierunt recordaberis.
text_pt: Porque te esquecerás do cansaço, e lembrar-te-ás dele como das águas que já passaram.
text_el: καὶ τὸν κόπον ἐπιλήσῃ ὥσπερ κῦμα παρελθὸν καὶ οὐ πτοηθήσῃ

text_en: And brightness like that of the noonday, shall arise to you at evening: and when you shall think yourself consumed, you shall rise as the day star .
text_la: Et quasi meridianus fulgor consurget tibi ad vesperam; et cum te consumptum putaveris, orieris ut lucifer.
text_pt: E a tua vida mais clara se levantará do que o meio-dia; ainda que haja trevas, será como a manhã.
text_el: ἡ δὲ εὐχή σου ὥσπερ ἑωσφόρος ἐκ δὲ μεσημβρίας ἀνατελεῖ σοι ζωή

text_en: And you shall have confidence, hope being set before you, and being buried you shall sleep secure.
text_la: Et habebis fiduciam, proposita tibi spe : et defossus securus dormies.
text_pt: E terás confiança, porque haverá esperança; olharás em volta e repousarás seguro.
text_el: πεποιθώς τε ἔσῃ ὅτι ἔστιν σοι ἐλπίς ἐκ δὲ μερίμνης καὶ φροντίδος ἀναφανεῖταί σοι εἰρήνη

text_en: You shall rest, and there shall be none to make you afraid: and many shall entreat your face.
text_la: Requiesces, et non erit qui te exterreat; et deprecabuntur faciem tuam plurimi.
text_pt: E deitar-te-ás, e ninguém te espantará; muitos suplicarão o teu favor.
text_el: ἡσυχάσεις γάρ καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ πολεμῶν σε μεταβαλόμενοι δὲ πολλοί σου δεηθήσονται

text_en: But the eyes of the wicked shall decay, and the way to escape shall fail them, and their hope the abomination of the soul .
text_la: Oculi autem impiorum deficient, et effugium peribit ab eis : et spes illorum abominatio animæ.
text_pt: Porém os olhos dos ímpios desfalecerão, e perecerá o seu refúgio; e a sua esperança será o expirar da alma.
text_el: σωτηρία δὲ αὐτοὺς ἀπολείψει ἡ γὰρ ἐλπὶς αὐτῶν ἀπώλεια ὀφθαλμοὶ δὲ ἀσεβῶν τακήσονται

text_en: Then Job answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Job, dixit:
text_pt: Então Jó respondeu, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει

text_en: Are you then men alone, and shall wisdom die with you?
text_la: Ergo vos estis soli homines, et vobiscum morietur sapientia?
text_pt: Na verdade, vós sois o povo, e convosco morrerá a sabedoria.
text_el: εἶτα ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἄνθρωποι ἦ μεθ' ὑμῶν τελευτήσει σοφία

text_en: I also have a heart as well as you: for who is ignorant of these things, which you know?
text_la: Et mihi est cor sicut et vobis, nec inferior vestri sum; quis enim hæc quæ nostis ignorat?
text_pt: Também eu tenho entendimento como vós, e não vos sou inferior; e quem não sabe tais coisas como essas?
text_el: κἀμοὶ μὲν καρδία καθ' ὑμᾶς ἐστιν

text_en: He that is mocked by his friends as I, shall call upon God and he will hear him: for the simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn.
text_la: Qui deridetur ab amico suo, sicut ego, invocabit Deum, et exaudiet eum : deridetur enim justi simplicitas.
text_pt: Eu sou motivo de riso para os meus amigos; eu, que invoco a Deus, e ele me responde; o justo e perfeito serve de zombaria.
text_el: δίκαιος γὰρ ἀνὴρ καὶ ἄμεμπτος ἐγενήθη εἰς χλεύασμα

text_en: The lamp despised in the thoughts of the rich, is ready for the time appointed.
text_la: Lampas contempta apud cogitationes divitum parata ad tempus statutum.
text_pt: Tocha desprezível é, na opinião do que está descansado, aquele que está pronto a vacilar com os pés.
text_el: εἰς χρόνον γὰρ τακτὸν ἡτοίμαστο πεσεῖν ὑπὸ ἄλλους οἴκους τε αὐτοῦ ἐκπορθεῖσθαι ὑπὸ ἀνόμων

text_en: The tabernacles of robbers abound, and they provoke God boldly; whereas it is he that has given all into their hands:
text_la: Abundant tabernacula prædonum, et audacter provocant Deum, cum ipse dederit omnia in manus eorum.
text_pt: As tendas dos assoladores têm descanso, e os que provocam a Deus estão seguros; nas suas mãos Deus lhes põe tudo.
text_el: οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ μηδεὶς πεποιθέτω πονηρὸς ὢν ἀθῷος ἔσεσθαι ὅσοι παροργίζουσιν τὸν κύριον ὡς οὐχὶ καὶ ἔτασις αὐτῶν ἔσται

text_en: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach you: and the birds of the air, and they shall tell you.
text_la: Nimirum interroga jumenta, et docebunt te; et volatilia cæli, et indicabunt tibi.
text_pt: Mas, pergunta agora às alimárias, e cada uma delas te ensinará; e às aves dos céus, e elas te farão saber;
text_el: ἀλλὰ δὴ ἐπερώτησον τετράποδα ἐάν σοι εἴπωσιν πετεινὰ δὲ οὐρανοῦ ἐάν σοι ἀπαγγείλωσιν

text_en: Speak to the earth, and it shall answer you: and the fishes of the sea shall tell.
text_la: Loquere terræ, et respondebit tibi, et narrabunt pisces maris.
text_pt: Ou fala com a terra, e ela te ensinará; até os peixes do mar te contarão.
text_el: ἐκδιήγησαι δὲ γῇ ἐάν σοι φράσῃ καὶ ἐξηγήσονταί σοι οἱ ἰχθύες τῆς θαλάσσης

text_en: Who is ignorant that the hand of the Lord has made all these things?
text_la: Quis ignorat quod omnia hæc manus Domini fecerit?
text_pt: Quem não entende, por todas estas coisas, que a mão do Senhor fez isto?
text_el: τίς οὐκ ἔγνω ἐν πᾶσι τούτοις ὅτι χεὶρ κυρίου ἐποίησεν ταῦτα

text_en: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the spirit of all flesh of man .
text_la: In cujus manu anima omnis viventis, et spiritus universæ carnis hominis.
text_pt: Na sua mão está a alma de tudo quanto vive, e o espírito de toda a carne humana.
text_el: εἰ μὴ ἐν χειρὶ αὐτοῦ ψυχὴ πάντων τῶν ζώντων καὶ πνεῦμα παντὸς ἀνθρώπου

text_en: Does not the ear discern words, and the palate of him that eats, the taste?
text_la: Nonne auris verba dijudicat? et fauces comedentis, saporem?
text_pt: Porventura o ouvido não provará as palavras, como o paladar prova as comidas?
text_el: οὖς μὲν γὰρ ῥήματα διακρίνει λάρυγξ δὲ σῖτα γεύεται

text_en: In the ancient is wisdom, and in length of days prudence.
text_la: In antiquis est sapientia, et in multo tempore prudentia.
text_pt: Com os idosos está a sabedoria, e na longevidade o entendimento.
text_el: ἐν πολλῷ χρόνῳ σοφία ἐν δὲ πολλῷ βίῳ ἐπιστήμη

text_en: With him is wisdom and strength, he has counsel and understanding.
text_la: Apud ipsum est sapientia et fortitudo; ipse habet consilium et intelligentiam.
text_pt: Com ele está a sabedoria e a força; conselho e entendimento tem.
text_el: παρ' αὐτῷ σοφία καὶ δύναμις αὐτῷ βουλὴ καὶ σύνεσις

text_en: If he pull down, there is no man that can build up: if he shut up a man , there is none that can open.
text_la: Si destruxerit, nemo est qui ædificet; si incluserit hominem, nullus est qui aperiat.
text_pt: Eis que ele derruba, e ninguém há que edifique; prende um homem, e ninguém há que o solte.
text_el: ἐὰν καταβάλῃ τίς οἰκοδομήσει ἐὰν κλείσῃ κατὰ ἀνθρώπων τίς ἀνοίξει

text_en: If he withhold the waters, all things shall be dried up: and if he send them out, they shall overturn the earth.
text_la: Si continuerit aquas, omnia siccabuntur; et si emiserit eas, subvertent terram.
text_pt: Eis que ele retém as águas, e elas secam; e solta-as, e elas transtornam a terra.
text_el: ἐὰν κωλύσῃ τὸ ὥδωρ ξηρανεῖ τὴν γῆν ἐὰν δὲ ἐπαφῇ ἀπώλεσεν αὐτὴν καταστρέψας

text_en: With him is strength and wisdom: he knows both the deceivers, and him that is deceived.
text_la: Apud ipsum est fortitudo et sapientia; ipse novit et decipientem, et eum qui decipitur.
text_pt: Com ele está a força e a sabedoria; seu é o que erra e o que o faz errar.
text_el: παρ' αὐτῷ κράτος καὶ ἰσχύς αὐτῷ ἐπιστήμη καὶ σύνεσις

text_en: He brings counsellors to a foolish end, and judges to insensibility.
text_la: Adducit consiliarios in stultum finem, et judices in stuporem.
text_pt: Aos conselheiros leva despojados, e aos juízes faz desvairar.
text_el: διάγων βουλευτὰς αἰχμαλώτους κριτὰς δὲ γῆς ἐξέστησεν

text_en: He loosens the belt of kings, and girds their loins with a cord.
text_la: Balteum regum dissolvit, et præcingit fune renes eorum.
text_pt: Solta a autoridade dos reis, e ata o cinto aos seus lombos.
text_el: καθιζάνων βασιλεῖς ἐπὶ θρόνους καὶ περιέδησεν ζώνῃ ὀσφύας αὐτῶν

text_en: He leads away priests without glory , and overthrows nobles.
text_la: Ducit sacerdotes inglorios, et optimates supplantat :
text_pt: Aos sacerdotes leva despojados, aos poderosos transtorna.
text_el: ἐξαποστέλλων ἱερεῖς αἰχμαλώτους δυνάστας δὲ γῆς κατέστρεψεν

text_en: He changes the speech of the true speakers, and takes away the doctrine of the aged.
text_la: commutans labium veracium, et doctrinam senum auferens.
text_pt: Aos acreditados tira a fala, e tira o entendimento aos anciãos.
text_el: διαλλάσσων χείλη πιστῶν σύνεσιν δὲ πρεσβυτέρων ἔγνω

text_en: He pours contempt upon princes, and relieves them that were oppressed.
text_la: Effundit despectionem super principes, eos qui oppressi fuerant relevans.
text_pt: Derrama desprezo sobre os príncipes, e afrouxa o cinto dos fortes.
text_el: ἐκχέων ἀτιμίαν ἐπ' ἄρχοντας ταπεινοὺς δὲ ἰάσατο

text_en: He discovers deep things out of darkness, and brings up to light the shadow of death.
text_la: Qui revelat profunda de tenebris, et producit in lucem umbram mortis.
text_pt: Das trevas descobre coisas profundas, e traz à luz a sombra da morte.
text_el: ἀνακαλύπτων βαθέα ἐκ σκότους ἐξήγαγεν δὲ εἰς φῶς σκιὰν θανάτου

text_en: He multiplies nations, and destroys them, and restores them again after they were overthrown.
text_la: Qui multiplicat gentes, et perdit eas, et subversas in integrum restituit.
text_pt: Multiplica as nações e as faz perecer; dispersa as nações, e de novo as reconduz.
text_el: πλανῶν ἔθνη καὶ ἀπολλύων αὐτά καταστρωννύων ἔθνη καὶ καθοδηγῶν αὐτά

text_en: He changes the heart of the princes of the people of the earth, and deceives them that they walk in vain where there is no way.
text_la: Qui immutat cor principum populi terræ, et decipit eos ut frustra incedant per invium :
text_pt: Tira o entendimento aos chefes dos povos da terra, e os faz vaguear pelos desertos, sem caminho.
text_el: διαλλάσσων καρδίας ἀρχόντων γῆς ἐπλάνησεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ὁδῷ ᾗ οὐκ ᾔδεισαν

text_en: They shall grope as in the dark, and not in the light, and he shall make them stagger like men that are drunk.
text_la: palpabunt quasi in tenebris, et non in luce, et errare eos faciet quasi ebrios.
text_pt: Nas trevas andam às apalpadelas, sem terem luz, e os faz desatinar como ébrios.
text_el: ψηλαφήσαισαν σκότος καὶ μὴ φῶς πλανηθείησαν δὲ ὥσπερ ὁ μεθύων

text_en: Behold my eye has seen all these things, and my ear has heard them, and I have understood them all.
text_la: Ecce omnia hæc vidit oculus meus, et audivit auris mea, et intellexi singula.
text_pt: Eis que tudo isto viram os meus olhos, e os meus ouvidos o ouviram e entenderam.
text_el: ἰδοὺ ταῦτα ἑώρακέν μου ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς καὶ ἀκήκοέν μου τὸ οὖς

text_en: According to your knowledge I also know: neither am I inferior to you.
text_la: Secundum scientiam vestram et ego novi : nec inferior vestri sum.
text_pt: Como vós o sabeis, também eu o sei; não vos sou inferior.
text_el: καὶ οἶδα ὅσα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε καὶ οὐκ ἀσυνετώτερός εἰμι ὑμῶν

text_en: But yet I will speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God .
text_la: Sed tamen ad Omnipotentem loquar, et disputare cum Deo cupio :
text_pt: Mas eu falarei ao Todo-Poderoso, e quero defender-me perante Deus.
text_el: οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλ' ἐγὼ πρὸς κύριον λαλήσω ἐλέγξω δὲ ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ ἐὰν βούληται

text_en: Having first shown that you are forgers of lies, and maintainers of perverse opinions.
text_la: prius vos ostendens fabricatores mendacii, et cultores perversorum dogmatum.
text_pt: Vós, porém, sois inventores de mentiras, e vós todos médicos que não valem nada.
text_el: ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε ἰατροὶ ἄδικοι καὶ ἰαταὶ κακῶν πάντες

text_en: And I wish you would hold your peace, that you might be thought to be wise men .
text_la: Atque utinam taceretis, ut putaremini esse sapientes.
text_pt: Quem dera que vos calásseis de todo, pois isso seria a vossa sabedoria.
text_el: εἴη δὲ ὑμῖν κωφεῦσαι καὶ ἀποβήσεται ὑμῖν εἰς σοφίαν

text_en: Hear therefore my reproof, and attend to the judgment of my lips.
text_la: Audite ergo correptionem meam, et judicium labiorum meorum attendite.
text_pt: Ouvi agora a minha defesa, e escutai os argumentos dos meus lábios.
text_el: ἀκούσατε ἔλεγχον στόματός μου κρίσιν δὲ χειλέων μου προσέχετε

text_en: Hath God any need of your lie, that you should speak deceitfully for him?
text_la: Numquid Deus indiget vestro mendacio, ut pro illo loquamini dolos?
text_pt: Porventura por Deus falareis perversidade e por ele falareis mentiras?
text_el: πότερον οὐκ ἔναντι κυρίου λαλεῖτε ἔναντι δὲ αὐτοῦ φθέγγεσθε δόλον

text_en: Do you accept this person, and do you endeavour to judge for God ?
text_la: numquid faciem ejus accipitis, et pro Deo judicare nitimini?
text_pt: Fareis acepção da sua pessoa? Contendereis por Deus?
text_el: ἦ ὑποστελεῖσθε ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτοὶ κριταὶ γένεσθε

text_en: Or shall it please him, from whom nothing can be concealed? Or shall he be deceived as a man , with your deceitful dealings?
text_la: aut placebit ei quem celare nihil potest? aut decipietur, ut homo, vestris fraudulentiis?
text_pt: Ser-vos-ia bom, se ele vos esquadrinhasse? Ou zombareis dele, como se zomba de algum homem?
text_el: καλόν γε ἐὰν ἐξιχνιάσῃ ὑμᾶς εἰ γὰρ τὰ πάντα ποιοῦντες προστεθήσεσθε αὐτῷ

text_en: He shall reprove you, because in secret you accept his person.
text_la: Ipse vos arguet, quoniam in abscondito faciem ejus accipitis.
text_pt: Certamente vos repreenderá, se em oculto fizerdes acepção de pessoas.
text_el: οὐθὲν ἧττον ἐλέγξει ὑμᾶς εἰ δὲ καὶ κρυφῇ πρόσωπα θαυμάσετε

text_en: As soon as he shall move himself, he shall trouble you: and his dread shall fall upon you.
text_la: Statim ut se commoverit, turbabit vos, et terror ejus irruet super vos.
text_pt: Porventura não vos espantará a sua alteza, e não cairá sobre vós o seu terror?
text_el: πότερον οὐχὶ δεινὰ αὐτοῦ στροβήσει ὑμᾶς φόβος δὲ παρ' αὐτοῦ ἐπιπεσεῖται ὑμῖν

text_en: Your remembrance shall be compared to ashes, and your necks shall be brought to clay.
text_la: Memoria vestra comparabitur cineri, et redigentur in lutum cervices vestræ.
text_pt: As vossas memórias são como provérbios de cinza; as vossas defesas como defesas de lodo.
text_el: ἀποβήσεται δὲ ὑμῶν τὸ ἀγαυρίαμα ἴσα σποδῷ τὸ δὲ σῶμα πήλινον

text_en: Hold your peace a little while, that I may speak whatsoever my mind shall suggest to me.
text_la: Tacete paulisper, ut loquar quodcumque mihi mens suggesserit.
text_pt: Calai-vos perante mim, e falarei eu, e venha sobre mim o que vier.
text_el: κωφεύσατε ἵνα λαλήσω καὶ ἀναπαύσωμαι θυμοῦ

text_en: Why do I tear my flesh with my teeth, and carry my soul in my hands?
text_la: Quare lacero carnes meas dentibus meis, et animam meam porto in manibus meis?
text_pt: Por que razão tomarei eu a minha carne com os meus dentes, e porei a minha vida na minha mão?
text_el: ἀναλαβὼν τὰς σάρκας μου τοῖς ὀδοῦσιν ψυχὴν δέ μου θήσω ἐν χειρί

text_en: Although he should kill me, I will trust in him: but yet I will reprove my ways in his sight.
text_la: Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo : verumtamen vias meas in conspectu ejus arguam.
text_pt: Ainda que ele me mate, nele esperarei; contudo os meus caminhos defenderei diante dele.
text_el: ἐάν με χειρώσηται ὁ δυνάστης ἐπεὶ καὶ ἦρκται ἦ μὴν λαλήσω καὶ ἐλέγξω ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ

text_en: And he shall be my saviour: for no hypocrite shall come before his presence.
text_la: Et ipse erit salvator meus : non enim veniet in conspectu ejus omnis hypocrita.
text_pt: Também ele será a minha salvação; porém o hipócrita não virá perante ele.
text_el: καὶ τοῦτό μοι ἀποβήσεται εἰς σωτηρίαν οὐ γὰρ ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ δόλος εἰσελεύσεται

text_en: Hear my speech, and receive with your ears hidden truths.
text_la: Audite sermonem meum, et ænigmata percipite auribus vestris.
text_pt: Ouvi com atenção as minhas palavras, e com os vossos ouvidos a minha declaração.
text_el: ἀκούσατε ἀκούσατε τὰ ῥήματά μου ἀναγγελῶ γὰρ ὑμῶν ἀκουόντων

text_en: If I shall be judged, I know that I shall be found just .
text_la: Si fuero judicatus, scio quod justus inveniar.
text_pt: Eis que já tenho ordenado a minha causa, e sei que serei achado justo.
text_el: ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐγγύς εἰμι τοῦ κρίματός μου οἶδα ἐγὼ ὅτι δίκαιος ἀναφανοῦμαι

text_en: Who is he that will plead against me? Let him come: why am I consumed holding my peace?
text_la: Quis est qui judicetur mecum? veniat : quare tacens consumor?
text_pt: Quem é o que contenderá comigo? Se eu agora me calasse, renderia o espírito.
text_el: τίς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ κριθησόμενός μοι ὅτι νῦν κωφεύσω καὶ ἐκλείψω

text_en: Two things only do not to me, and then from your face I shall not be hid:
text_la: Duo tantum ne facias mihi, et tunc a facie tua non abscondar :
text_pt: Duas coisas somente não faças para comigo; então não me esconderei do teu rosto:
text_el: δυεῖν δέ μοι χρήσῃ τότε ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου σου οὐ κρυβήσομαι

text_en: Withdraw your hand far from me, and let not your dread terrify me.
text_la: manum tuam longe fac a me, et formido tua non me terreat.
text_pt: Desvia a tua mão para longe, de mim, e não me espante o teu terror.
text_el: τὴν χεῖρα ἀπ' ἐμοῦ ἀπέχου καὶ ὁ φόβος σου μή με καταπλησσέτω

text_en: Call me, and I will answer you: or else I will speak, and you answer me.
text_la: Voca me, et ego respondebo tibi : aut certe loquar, et tu responde mihi.
text_pt: Chama, pois, e eu responderei; ou eu falarei, e tu me responderás.
text_el: εἶτα καλέσεις ἐγὼ δέ σοι ὑπακούσομαι ἢ λαλήσεις ἐγὼ δέ σοι δώσω ἀνταπόκρισιν

text_en: How many are my iniquities and sins ? make me know my crimes and offenses.
text_la: Quantas habeo iniquitates et peccata? scelera mea et delicta ostende mihi.
text_pt: Quantas culpas e pecados tenho eu? Notifica-me a minha transgressão e o meu pecado.
text_el: πόσαι εἰσὶν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι μου καὶ αἱ ἀνομίαι μου δίδαξόν με τίνες εἰσίν

text_en: Why do you hide your face, and think me your enemy?
text_la: Cur faciem tuam abscondis, et arbitraris me inimicum tuum?
text_pt: Por que escondes o teu rosto, e me tens por teu inimigo?
text_el: διὰ τί ἀπ' ἐμοῦ κρύπτῃ ἥγησαι δέ με ὑπεναντίον σοι

text_en: Against a leaf, that is carried away with the wind, you show your power, and you pursue a dry straw.
text_la: Contra folium, quod vento rapitur, ostendis potentiam tuam, et stipulam siccam persequeris :
text_pt: Porventura acossarás uma folha arrebatada pelo vento? E perseguirás o restolho seco?
text_el: ἦ ὡς φύλλον κινούμενον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου εὐλαβηθήσῃ ἢ ὡς χόρτῳ φερομένῳ ὑπὸ πνεύματος ἀντίκεισαί μοι

text_en: For you write bitter things against me, and will consume me for the sins of my youth.
text_la: scribis enim contra me amaritudines, et consumere me vis peccatis adolescentiæ meæ.
text_pt: Por que escreves contra mim coisas amargas e me fazes herdar as culpas da minha mocidade?
text_el: ὅτι κατέγραψας κατ' ἐμοῦ κακά περιέθηκας δέ μοι νεότητος ἁμαρτίας

text_en: You have put my feet in the stocks, and have observed all my paths, and have considered the steps of my feet:
text_la: Posuisti in nervo pedem meum, et observasti omnes semitas meas, et vestigia pedum meorum considerasti :
text_pt: Também pões os meus pés no tronco, e observas todos os meus caminhos, e marcas os sinais dos meus pés.
text_el: ἔθου δέ μου τὸν πόδα ἐν κωλύματι ἐφύλαξας δέ μου πάντα τὰ ἔργα εἰς δὲ ῥίζας τῶν ποδῶν μου ἀφίκου

text_en: Who am to be consumed as rottenness, and as a garment that is motheaten.
text_la: qui quasi putredo consumendus sum, et quasi vestimentum quod comeditur a tinea.
text_pt: E ele me consome como a podridão, e como a roupa, à qual rói a traça.
text_el: ὃ παλαιοῦται ἴσα ἀσκῷ ἢ ὥσπερ ἱμάτιον σητόβρωτον

text_en: Man born of a woman , living for a short time, is filled with many miseries.
text_la: Homo natus de muliere, brevi vivens tempore, repletur multis miseriis.
text_pt: O homem, nascido da mulher, é de poucos dias e farto de inquietação.
text_el: βροτὸς γὰρ γεννητὸς γυναικὸς ὀλιγόβιος καὶ πλήρης ὀργῆς

text_en: Who comes forth like a flower, and is destroyed, and flees as a shadow, and never continues in the same state.
text_la: Qui quasi flos egreditur et conteritur, et fugit velut umbra, et numquam in eodem statu permanet.
text_pt: Sai como a flor, e murcha; foge também como a sombra, e não permanece.
text_el: ἢ ὥσπερ ἄνθος ἀνθῆσαν ἐξέπεσεν ἀπέδρα δὲ ὥσπερ σκιὰ καὶ οὐ μὴ στῇ

text_en: And do you think it meet to open your eyes upon such an one, and to bring him into judgment with you?
text_la: Et dignum ducis super hujuscemodi aperire oculos tuos, et adducere eum tecum in judicium?
text_pt: E sobre este tal abres os teus olhos, e a mim me fazes entrar no juízo contigo.
text_el: οὐχὶ καὶ τούτου λόγον ἐποιήσω καὶ τοῦτον ἐποίησας εἰσελθεῖν ἐν κρίματι ἐνώπιόν σου

text_en: Who can make him clean that is conceived of unclean seed? Is it not you who only is?
text_la: Quis potest facere mundum de immundo conceptum semine? nonne tu qui solus es?
text_pt: Quem do imundo tirará o puro? Ninguém.
text_el: τίς γὰρ καθαρὸς ἔσται ἀπὸ ῥύπου ἀλλ' οὐθείς

text_en: The days of man are short, and the number of his months is with you: you have appointed his bounds which cannot be passed.
text_la: Breves dies hominis sunt : numerus mensium ejus apud te est : constituisti terminos ejus, qui præteriri non poterunt.
text_pt: Visto que os seus dias estão determinados, contigo está o número dos seus meses; e tu lhe puseste limites, e não passará além deles.
text_el: ἐὰν καὶ μία ἡμέρα ὁ βίος αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀριθμητοὶ δὲ μῆνες αὐτοῦ παρὰ σοί εἰς χρόνον ἔθου καὶ οὐ μὴ ὑπερβῇ

text_en: Depart a little from him, that he may rest until his wished for day come, as that of the hireling.
text_la: Recede paululum ab eo, ut quiescat, donec optata veniat, sicut mercenarii, dies ejus.
text_pt: Desvia-te dele, para que tenha repouso, até que, como o jornaleiro, tenha contentamento no seu dia.
text_el: ἀπόστα ἀπ' αὐτοῦ ἵνα ἡσυχάσῃ καὶ εὐδοκήσῃ τὸν βίον ὥσπερ ὁ μισθωτός

text_en: A tree has hope: if it be cut, it growth green again, and the boughs thereof sprout.
text_la: Lignum habet spem : si præcisum fuerit, rursum virescit, et rami ejus pullulant.
text_pt: Porque há esperança para a árvore que, se for cortada, ainda se renovará, e não cessarão os seus renovos.
text_el: ἔστιν γὰρ δένδρῳ ἐλπίς ἐὰν γὰρ ἐκκοπῇ ἔτι ἐπανθήσει καὶ ὁ ῥάδαμνος αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ ἐκλίπῃ

text_en: If its roots be old in the earth, and its stock be dead in the dust:
text_la: Si senuerit in terra radix ejus, et in pulvere emortuus fuerit truncus illius,
text_pt: Se envelhecer na terra a sua raiz, e o seu tronco morrer no pó,
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ γηράσῃ ἐν γῇ ἡ ῥίζα αὐτοῦ ἐν δὲ πέτρᾳ τελευτήσῃ τὸ στέλεχος αὐτοῦ

text_en: At the scent of water, it shall spring, and bring forth leaves, as when it was first planted.
text_la: ad odorem aquæ germinabit, et faciet comam, quasi cum primum plantatum est.
text_pt: Ao cheiro das águas brotará, e dará ramos como uma planta.
text_el: ἀπὸ ὀσμῆς ὕδατος ἀνθήσει ποιήσει δὲ θερισμὸν ὥσπερ νεόφυτον

text_en: But man when he shall be dead, and stripped and consumed, I pray you where is he?
text_la: Homo vero cum mortuus fuerit, et nudatus, atque consumptus, ubi, quæso, est?
text_pt: Porém, morto o homem, é consumido; sim, rendendo o homem o espírito, então onde está ele?
text_el: ἀνὴρ δὲ τελευτήσας ᾤχετο πεσὼν δὲ βροτὸς οὐκέτι ἔστιν

text_en: As if the waters should depart out of the sea, and an emptied river should be dried up;
text_la: Quomodo si recedant aquæ de mari, et fluvius vacuefactus arescat :
text_pt: Como as águas se retiram do mar, e o rio se esgota, e fica seco,
text_el: χρόνῳ γὰρ σπανίζεται θάλασσα ποταμὸς δὲ ἐρημωθεὶς ἐξηράνθη

text_en: so man when he is fallen asleep shall not rise again ; till the heavens be broken, he shall not awake, nor rise up out of his sleep.
text_la: sic homo, cum dormierit, non resurget : donec atteratur cælum, non evigilabit, nec consurget de somno suo.
text_pt: Assim o homem se deita, e não se levanta; até que não haja mais céus, não acordará nem despertará de seu sono.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος δὲ κοιμηθεὶς οὐ μὴ ἀναστῇ ἕως ἂν ὁ οὐρανὸς οὐ μὴ συρραφῇ καὶ οὐκ ἐξυπνισθήσονται ἐξ ὕπνου αὐτῶν

text_en: Who will grant me this, that you may protect me in hell, and hide me till your wrath pass, and appoint me a time when you will remember me?
text_la: Quis mihi hoc tribuat, ut in inferno protegas me, et abscondas me donec pertranseat furor tuus, et constituas mihi tempus in quo recorderis mei?
text_pt: Quem dera que me escondesses na sepultura, e me ocultasses até que a tua ira se fosse; e me pusesses um limite, e te lembrasses de mim!
text_el: εἰ γὰρ ὄφελον ἐν ᾅδῃ με ἐφύλαξας ἔκρυψας δέ με ἕως ἂν παύσηταί σου ἡ ὀργὴ καὶ τάξῃ μοι χρόνον ἐν ᾧ μνείαν μου ποιήσῃ

text_en: Shall man that is dead, do you think, live again? All the days in which I am now in warfare , I expect until my change come.
text_la: Putasne mortuus homo rursum vivat? cunctis diebus quibus nunc milito, expecto donec veniat immutatio mea.
text_pt: Morrendo o homem, porventura tornará a viver? Todos os dias de meu combate esperaria, até que viesse a minha mudança.
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀποθάνῃ ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται συντελέσας ἡμέρας τοῦ βίου αὐτοῦ ὑπομενῶ ἕως ἂν πάλιν γένωμαι

text_en: You shall call me, and I will answer you: to the work of your hands you shall reach out your right hand.
text_la: Vocabis me, et ego respondebo tibi : operi manuum tuarum porriges dexteram.
text_pt: Chamar-me-ias, e eu te responderia, e terias afeto à obra de tuas mãos.
text_el: εἶτα καλέσεις ἐγὼ δέ σοι ὑπακούσομαι τὰ δὲ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν σου μὴ ἀποποιοῦ

text_en: You indeed have numbered my steps, but spare my sins .
text_la: Tu quidem gressus meos dinumerasti : sed parce peccatis meis.
text_pt: Mas agora contas os meus passos; porventura não vigias sobre o meu pecado?
text_el: ἠρίθμησας δέ μου τὰ ἐπιτηδεύματα καὶ οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ σε οὐδὲν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν μου

text_en: You have sealed up my offences as it were in a bag, but have cured my iniquity .
text_la: Signasti quasi in sacculo delicta mea, sed curasti iniquitatem meam.
text_pt: A minha transgressão está selada num saco, e amontoas as minhas iniqüidades.
text_el: ἐσφράγισας δέ μου τὰς ἀνομίας ἐν βαλλαντίῳ ἐπεσημήνω δέ εἴ τι ἄκων παρέβην

text_en: A mountain falling comes to nought, and a rock is removed out of its place.
text_la: Mons cadens defluit, et saxum transfertur de loco suo :
text_pt: E, na verdade, caindo a montanha, desfaz-se; e a rocha se remove do seu lugar.
text_el: καὶ πλὴν ὄρος πῖπτον διαπεσεῖται καὶ πέτρα παλαιωθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτῆς

text_en: Waters wear away the stones, and with inundation the ground by little and little is washed away: so in like manner you shall destroy man .
text_la: lapides excavant aquæ, et alluvione paulatim terra consumitur : et hominem ergo similiter perdes.
text_pt: As águas gastam as pedras, as cheias afogam o pó da terra; e tu fazes perecer a esperança do homem;
text_el: λίθους ἐλέαναν ὕδατα καὶ κατέκλυσεν ὕδατα ὕπτια τοῦ χώματος τῆς γῆς καὶ ὑπομονὴν ἀνθρώπου ἀπώλεσας

text_en: You have strengthened him for a little while, that he may pass away for ever: you shall change his face, and shall send him away.
text_la: Roborasti eum paululum, ut in perpetuum transiret : immutabis faciem ejus, et emittes eum.
text_pt: Tu para sempre prevaleces contra ele, e ele passa; mudas o seu rosto, e o despedes.
text_el: ὦσας αὐτὸν εἰς τέλος καὶ ᾤχετο ἐπέστησας αὐτῷ τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ ἐξαπέστειλας

text_en: Whether his children come to honour or dishonour, he shall not understand.
text_la: Sive nobiles fuerint filii ejus, sive ignobiles, non intelliget.
text_pt: Os seus filhos recebem honra, sem que ele o saiba; são humilhados, sem que ele o perceba;
text_el: πολλῶν δὲ γενομένων τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ οὐκ οἶδεν ἐὰν δὲ ὀλίγοι γένωνται οὐκ ἐπίσταται

text_en: But yet his flesh, while he shall live, shall have pain, and his soul shall mourn over him.
text_la: Attamen caro ejus, dum vivet, dolebit, et anima illius super semetipso lugebit.
text_pt: Mas a sua carne nele tem dores, e a sua alma nele lamenta.
text_el: ἀλλ' ἢ αἱ σάρκες αὐτοῦ ἤλγησαν ἡ δὲ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπένθησεν

text_en: And Eliphaz the Themanite, answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Eliphaz Themanites, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondeu Elifaz o temanita, e disse:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ελιφας ὁ Θαιμανίτης λέγει

text_en: Will a wise man answer as if he were speaking in the wind, and fill his stomach with burning heat?
text_la: Numquid sapiens respondebit quasi in ventum loquens, et implebit ardore stomachum suum?
text_pt: Porventura proferirá o sábio và sabedoria? E encherá do vento oriental o seu ventre,
text_el: πότερον σοφὸς ἀπόκρισιν δώσει συνέσεως πνεύματος καὶ ἐνέπλησεν πόνον γαστρὸς

text_en: You reprove him by words, who is not equal to you, and you speak that which is not good for you.
text_la: Arguis verbis eum qui non est æqualis tibi, et loqueris quod tibi non expedit.
text_pt: Argüindo com palavras que de nada servem, e com razões, de que nada aproveita?
text_el: ἐλέγχων ἐν ῥήμασιν οἷς οὐ δεῖ ἐν λόγοις οἷς οὐδὲν ὄφελος

text_en: As much as is in you, you have made void fear, and have taken away prayers from before God .
text_la: Quantum in te est, evacuasti timorem, et tulisti preces coram Deo.
text_pt: E tu tens feito vão o temor, e diminuis os rogos diante de Deus.
text_el: οὐ καὶ σὺ ἀπεποιήσω φόβον συνετελέσω δὲ ῥήματα τοιαῦτα ἔναντι τοῦ κυρίου

text_en: For your iniquity has taught your mouth, and you imitate the tongue of blasphemers .
text_la: Docuit enim iniquitas tua os tuum, et imitaris linguam blasphemantium.
text_pt: Porque a tua boca declara a tua iniqüidade; e tu escolhes a língua dos astutos.
text_el: ἔνοχος εἶ ῥήμασιν στόματός σου οὐδὲ διέκρινας ῥήματα δυναστῶν

text_en: Your own mouth shall condemn you, and not I: and your own lips shall answer you.
text_la: Condemnabit te os tuum, et non ego : et labia tua respondebunt tibi.
text_pt: A tua boca te condena, e não eu, e os teus lábios testificam contra ti.
text_el: ἐλέγξαι σε τὸ σὸν στόμα καὶ μὴ ἐγώ τὰ δὲ χείλη σου καταμαρτυρήσουσίν σου

text_en: Are you the first man that was born, or were you made before the hills?
text_la: Numquid primus homo tu natus es, et ante colles formatus?
text_pt: És tu porventura o primeiro homem que nasceu? Ou foste formado antes dos outeiros?
text_el: τί γάρ μὴ πρῶτος ἀνθρώπων ἐγενήθης ἢ πρὸ θινῶν ἐπάγης

text_en: Have you heard God's counsel, and shall his wisdom be inferior to you?
text_la: numquid consilium Dei audisti, et inferior te erit ejus sapientia?
text_pt: Ou ouviste o secreto conselho de Deus e a ti só limitaste a sabedoria?
text_el: ἦ σύνταγμα κυρίου ἀκήκοας εἰς δὲ σὲ ἀφίκετο σοφία

text_en: What do you know that we are ignorant of? What do you understand that we know not?
text_la: Quid nosti quod ignoremus? quid intelligis quod nesciamus?
text_pt: Que sabes tu, que nós não saibamos? Que entendes, que não haja em nós?
text_el: τί γὰρ οἶδας ὃ οὐκ οἴδαμεν ἢ τί συνίεις ὃ οὐχὶ καὶ ἡμεῖς

text_en: There are with us also aged and ancient men , much elder than your fathers.
text_la: Et senes et antiqui sunt in nobis, multo vetustiores quam patres tui.
text_pt: Também há entre nós encanecidos e idosos, muito mais idosos do que teu pai.
text_el: καί γε πρεσβύτης καί γε παλαιὸς ἐν ἡμῖν βαρύτερος τοῦ πατρός σου ἡμέραις

text_en: Is it a great matter that God should comfort you? But your wicked words hinder this.
text_la: Numquid grande est ut consoletur te Deus? sed verba tua prava hoc prohibent.
text_pt: Porventura fazes pouco caso das consolações de Deus, e da suave palavra que te dirigimos?
text_el: ὀλίγα ὧν ἡμάρτηκας μεμαστίγωσαι μεγάλως ὑπερβαλλόντως λελάληκας

text_en: Why does your heart elevate you, and why do you stare with your eyes, as if they were thinking great things?
text_la: Quid te elevat cor tuum, et quasi magna cogitans attonitos habes oculos?
text_pt: Por que te arrebata o teu coração, e por que piscam os teus olhos?
text_el: τί ἐτόλμησεν ἡ καρδία σου ἢ τί ἐπήνεγκαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου

text_en: Why does your spirit swell against God , to utter such words out of your mouth?
text_la: Quid tumet contra Deum spiritus tuus, ut proferas de ore tuo hujuscemodi sermones?
text_pt: Para virares contra Deus o teu espírito, e deixares sair tais palavras da tua boca?
text_el: ὅτι θυμὸν ἔρρηξας ἔναντι κυρίου ἐξήγαγες δὲ ἐκ στόματος ῥήματα τοιαῦτα

text_en: What is man that he should be without spot, and he that is born of a woman that he should appear just ?
text_la: Quid est homo ut immaculatus sit, et ut justus appareat natus de muliere?
text_pt: Que é o homem, para que seja puro? E o que nasce da mulher, para ser justo?
text_el: τίς γὰρ ὢν βροτός ὅτι ἔσται ἄμεμπτος ἢ ὡς ἐσόμενος δίκαιος γεννητὸς γυναικός

text_en: Behold among his saints none is unchangeable, and the heavens are not pure in his sight.
text_la: Ecce inter sanctos ejus nemo immutabilis, et cæli non sunt mundi in conspectu ejus.
text_pt: Eis que ele não confia nos seus santos, e nem os céus são puros aos seus olhos.
text_el: εἰ κατὰ ἁγίων οὐ πιστεύει οὐρανὸς δὲ οὐ καθαρὸς ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ

text_en: How much more is man abominable, and unprofitable, who drinks iniquity like water?
text_la: Quanto magis abominabilis et inutilis homo, qui bibit quasi aquam iniquitatem?
text_pt: Quanto mais abominável e corrupto é o homem que bebe a iniqüidade como a água?
text_el: ἔα δὲ ἐβδελυγμένος καὶ ἀκάθαρτος ἀνὴρ πίνων ἀδικίας ἴσα ποτῷ

text_en: I will show you, hear me: and I will tell you what I have seen.
text_la: Ostendam tibi : audi me : quod vidi, narrabo tibi.
text_pt: Escuta-me, mostrar-te-ei; e o que tenho visto te contarei
text_el: ἀναγγελῶ δέ σοι ἄκουέ μου ἃ δὴ ἑώρακα ἀναγγελῶ σοι

text_en: Wise men confess and hide not their fathers.
text_la: Sapientes confitentur, et non abscondunt patres suos :
text_pt: (O que os sábios anunciaram, ouvindo-o de seus pais, e o não ocultaram;
text_el: ἃ σοφοὶ ἐροῦσιν καὶ οὐκ ἔκρυψαν πατέρας αὐτῶν

text_en: To whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger has passed among them.
text_la: quibus solis data est terra, et non transivit alienus per eos.
text_pt: Aos quais somente se dera a terra, e nenhum estranho passou por entre eles):
text_el: αὐτοῖς μόνοις ἐδόθη ἡ γῆ καὶ οὐκ ἐπῆλθεν ἀλλογενὴς ἐπ' αὐτούς

text_en: The wicked man is proud all his days, and the number of the years of his tyranny is uncertain.
text_la: Cunctis diebus suis impius superbit, et numerus annorum incertus est tyrannidis ejus.
text_pt: Todos os dias o ímpio é atormentado, e se reserva, para o tirano, um certo número de anos.
text_el: πᾶς ὁ βίος ἀσεβοῦς ἐν φροντίδι ἔτη δὲ ἀριθμητὰ δεδομένα δυνάστῃ

text_en: The sound of dread is always in his ears: and when there is peace, he always suspects treason.
text_la: Sonitus terroris semper in auribus illius : et cum pax sit, ille semper insidias suspicatur.
text_pt: O sonido dos horrores está nos seus ouvidos; até na paz lhe sobrevém o assolador.
text_el: ὁ δὲ φόβος αὐτοῦ ἐν ὠσὶν αὐτοῦ ὅταν δοκῇ ἤδη εἰρηνεύειν ἥξει αὐτοῦ ἡ καταστροφή

text_en: He believes not that he may return from darkness to light, looking round about for the sword on every side.
text_la: Non credit quod reverti possit de tenebris ad lucem, circumspectans undique gladium.
text_pt: Não crê que tornará das trevas, mas que o espera a espada.
text_el: μὴ πιστευέτω ἀποστραφῆναι ἀπὸ σκότους ἐντέταλται γὰρ ἤδη εἰς χεῖρας σιδήρου

text_en: When he moves himself to seek bread, he knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
text_la: Cum se moverit ad quærendum panem, novit quod paratus sit in manu ejus tenebrarum dies.
text_pt: Anda vagueando por pão, dizendo: Onde está? Bem sabe que já o dia das trevas lhe está preparado, à mão.
text_el: κατατέτακται δὲ εἰς σῖτα γυψίν οἶδεν δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὅτι μένει εἰς πτῶμα ἡμέρα δὲ αὐτὸν σκοτεινὴ στροβήσει

text_en: Tribulation shall terrify him, and distress shall surround him, as a king that is prepared for the battle.
text_la: Terrebit eum tribulatio, et angustia vallabit eum, sicut regem qui præparatur ad prælium.
text_pt: Assombram-no a angústia e a tribulação; prevalecem contra ele, como o rei preparado para a peleja;
text_el: ἀνάγκη δὲ καὶ θλῖψις αὐτὸν καθέξει ὥσπερ στρατηγὸς πρωτοστάτης πίπτων

text_en: For he has stretched out his hand against God , and has strengthened himself against the Almighty.
text_la: Tetendit enim adversus Deum manum suam, et contra Omnipotentem roboratus est.
text_pt: Porque estendeu a sua mão contra Deus, e contra o Todo-Poderoso se embraveceu.
text_el: ὅτι ἦρκεν χεῖρας ἐναντίον τοῦ κυρίου ἔναντι δὲ κυρίου παντοκράτορος ἐτραχηλίασεν

text_en: He has run against him with his neck raised up, and is armed with a fat neck.
text_la: Cucurrit adversus eum erecto collo, et pingui cervice armatus est.
text_pt: Arremete contra ele com a dura cerviz, e contra os pontos grossos dos seus escudos.
text_el: ἔδραμεν δὲ ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ ὕβρει ἐν πάχει νώτου ἀσπίδος αὐτοῦ

text_en: Fatness has covered his face, and the fat hangs down on his sides.
text_la: Operuit faciem ejus crassitudo, et de lateribus ejus arvina dependet.
text_pt: Porquanto cobriu o seu rosto com a sua gordura, e criou gordura nas ilhargas.
text_el: ὅτι ἐκάλυψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἐν στέατι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐποίησεν περιστόμιον ἐπὶ τῶν μηρίων

text_en: He has dwelt in desolate cities, and in desert houses that are reduced into heaps.
text_la: Habitavit in civitatibus desolatis, et in domibus desertis, quæ in tumulos sunt redactæ.
text_pt: E habitou em cidades assoladas, em casas em que ninguém morava, que estavam a ponto de fazer-se montões de ruínas.
text_el: αὐλισθείη δὲ πόλεις ἐρήμους εἰσέλθοι δὲ εἰς οἴκους ἀοικήτους ἃ δὲ ἐκεῖνοι ἡτοίμασαν ἄλλοι ἀποίσονται

text_en: He shall not be enriched, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he push his root in the earth.
text_la: Non ditabitur, nec perseverabit substantia ejus, nec mittet in terra radicem suam.
text_pt: Não se enriquecerá, nem subsistirá a sua fazenda, nem se estenderão pela terra as suas possessões.
text_el: οὔτε μὴ πλουτισθῇ οὔτε μὴ μείνῃ αὐτοῦ τὰ ὑπάρχοντα οὐ μὴ βάλῃ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν σκιὰν

text_en: He shall not depart out of darkness: the flame shall dry up his branches, and he shall be taken away by the breath of his own mouth.
text_la: Non recedet de tenebris : ramos ejus arefaciet flamma, et auferetur spiritu oris sui.
text_pt: Não escapará das trevas; a chama do fogo secará os seus renovos, e ao sopro da sua boca desaparecerá.
text_el: οὐδὲ μὴ ἐκφύγῃ τὸ σκότος τὸν βλαστὸν αὐτοῦ μαράναι ἄνεμος ἐκπέσοι δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ ἄνθος

text_en: He shall not believe , being vainly deceived by error, that he may be redeemed with any price.
text_la: Non credet, frustra errore deceptus, quod aliquo pretio redimendus sit.
text_pt: Não confie, pois, na vaidade, enganando-se a si mesmo, porque a vaidade será a sua recompensa.
text_el: μὴ πιστευέτω ὅτι ὑπομενεῖ κενὰ γὰρ ἀποβήσεται αὐτῷ

text_en: Before his days be full he shall perish: and his hands shall wither away.
text_la: Antequam dies ejus impleantur peribit, et manus ejus arescent.
text_pt: Antes do seu dia ela se consumará; e o seu ramo não reverdecerá.
text_el: ἡ τομὴ αὐτοῦ πρὸ ὥρας φθαρήσεται καὶ ὁ ῥάδαμνος αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ πυκάσῃ

text_en: He shall be blasted as a vine when its grapes are in the first flower, and as an olive tree that casts its flower.
text_la: Lædetur quasi vinea in primo flore botrus ejus, et quasi oliva projiciens florem suum.
text_pt: Sacudirá as suas uvas verdes, como as da vide, e deixará cair a sua flor como a oliveira,
text_el: τρυγηθείη δὲ ὥσπερ ὄμφαξ πρὸ ὥρας ἐκπέσοι δὲ ὡς ἄνθος ἐλαίας

text_en: For the congregation of the hypocrite is barren, and fire shall devour their tabernacles, who love to take bribes .
text_la: Congregatio enim hypocritæ sterilis, et ignis devorabit tabernacula eorum qui munera libenter accipiunt.
text_pt: Porque a congregação dos hipócritas se fará estéril, e o fogo consumirá as tendas do suborno.
text_el: μαρτύριον γὰρ ἀσεβοῦς θάνατος πῦρ δὲ καύσει οἴκους δωροδεκτῶν

text_en: He has conceived sorrow, and has brought forth iniquity , and his womb prepares deceits.
text_la: Concepit dolorem, et peperit iniquitatem, et uterus ejus præparat dolos.
text_pt: Concebem a malícia, e dão à luz a iniqüidade, e o seu ventre prepara enganos.
text_el: ἐν γαστρὶ δὲ λήμψεται ὀδύνας ἀποβήσεται δὲ αὐτῷ κενά ἡ δὲ κοιλία αὐτοῦ ὑποίσει δόλον

text_en: Then Job answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Job, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondeu Jó, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει

text_en: I have often heard such things as these: you are all troublesome comforters.
text_la: Audivi frequenter talia : consolatores onerosi omnes vos estis.
text_pt: Tenho ouvido muitas coisas como estas; todos vós sois consoladores molestos.
text_el: ἀκήκοα τοιαῦτα πολλά παρακλήτορες κακῶν πάντες

text_en: Shall windy words have no end? Or is it any trouble to you to speak?
text_la: Numquid habebunt finem verba ventosa? aut aliquid tibi molestum est, si loquaris?
text_pt: Porventura não terão fim essas palavras de vento? Ou o que te irrita, para assim responderes?
text_el: τί γάρ μὴ τάξις ἐστὶν ῥήμασιν πνεύματος ἢ τί παρενοχλήσει σοι ὅτι ἀποκρίνῃ

text_en: I also could speak like you: and would God your soul were for my soul .
text_la: Poteram et ego similia vestri loqui, atque utinam esset anima vestra pro anima mea :
text_pt: Falaria eu também como vós falais, se a vossa alma estivesse em lugar da minha alma, ou amontoaria palavras contra vós, e menearia contra vós a minha cabeça?
text_el: κἀγὼ καθ' ὑμᾶς λαλήσω εἰ ὑπέκειτό γε ἡ ψυχὴ ὑμῶν ἀντὶ τῆς ἐμῆς εἶτ' ἐναλοῦμαι ὑμῖν ῥήμασιν κινήσω δὲ καθ' ὑμῶν κεφαλήν

text_en: I would comfort you also with words, and would wag my head over you.
text_la: consolarer et ego vos sermonibus, et moverem caput meum super vos;
text_pt: Antes vos fortaleceria com a minha boca, e a consolação dos meus lábios abrandaria a vossa dor.
text_el: εἴη δὲ ἰσχὺς ἐν τῷ στόματί μου κίνησιν δὲ χειλέων οὐ φείσομαι

text_en: I would strengthen you with my mouth, and would move my lips, as sparing you.
text_la: roborarem vos ore meo, et moverem labia mea, quasi parcens vobis.
text_pt: Se eu falar, a minha dor não cessa, e, calando-me eu, qual é o meu alívio?
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ λαλήσω οὐκ ἀλγήσω τὸ τραῦμα ἐὰν δὲ καὶ σιωπήσω τί ἔλαττον τρωθήσομαι

text_en: But what shall I do? If I speak, my pain will not rest: and if I hold my peace, it will not depart from me.
text_la: Sed quid agam? Si locutus fuero, non quiescet dolor meus, et si tacuero, non recedet a me.
text_pt: Na verdade, agora tu me tens fatigado; tu assolaste toda a minha companhia,

text_en: But now my sorrow has oppressed me, and all my limbs are brought to nothing.
text_la: Nunc autem oppressit me dolor meus, et in nihilum redacti sunt omnes artus mei.
text_pt: Testemunha disto é que já me fizeste enrugado, e a minha magreza já se levanta contra mim, e no meu rosto testifica contra mim.
text_el: νῦν δὲ κατάκοπόν με πεποίηκεν μωρόν σεσηπότα

text_en: My wrinkles bear witness against me, and a false speaker rises up against my face, contradicting me.
text_la: Rugæ meæ testimonium dicunt contra me, et suscitatur falsiloquus adversus faciem meam, contradicens mihi.
text_pt: Na sua ira me despedaçou, e ele me perseguiu; rangeu os seus dentes contra mim; aguça o meu adversário os seus olhos contra mim.
text_el: καὶ ἐπελάβου μου εἰς μαρτύριον ἐγενήθη καὶ ἀνέστη ἐν ἐμοὶ τὸ ψεῦδός μου κατὰ πρόσωπόν μου ἀνταπεκρίθη

text_en: He has gathered together his fury against me, and threatening me he has gnashed with his teeth upon me: my enemy has beheld me with terrible eyes.
text_la: Collegit furorem suum in me, et comminans mihi, infremuit contra me dentibus suis : hostis meus terribilibus oculis me intuitus est.
text_pt: Abrem a sua boca contra mim; com desprezo me feriram nos queixos, e contra mim se ajuntam todos.
text_el: ὀργῇ χρησάμενος κατέβαλέν με ἔβρυξεν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τοὺς ὀδόντας βέλη πειρατῶν αὐτοῦ ἐπ' ἐμοὶ ἔπεσεν

text_en: They have opened their mouths upon me, and reproaching me they have struck me on the cheek, they are filled with my pains.
text_la: Aperuerunt super me ora sua, et exprobrantes percusserunt maxillam meam : satiati sunt pœnis meis.
text_pt: Entrega-me Deus ao perverso, e nas mãos dos ímpios me faz cair.
text_el: ἀκίσιν ὀφθαλμῶν ἐνήλατο ὀξεῖ ἔπαισέν με εἰς σιαγόνα ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ κατέδραμον ἐπ' ἐμοί

text_en: God has shut me up with the unjust man , and has delivered me into the hands of the wicked.
text_la: Conclusit me Deus apud iniquum, et manibus impiorum me tradidit.
text_pt: Descansado estava eu, porém ele me quebrantou; e pegou-me pela cerviz, e me despedaçou; também me pôs por seu alvo.
text_el: παρέδωκεν γάρ με ὁ κύριος εἰς χεῖρας ἀδίκου ἐπὶ δὲ ἀσεβέσιν ἔρριψέν με

text_en: I that was formerly so wealthy, am all on a sudden broken to pieces: he has taken me by my neck, he has broken me, and has set me up to be his mark.
text_la: Ego ille quondam opulentus, repente contritus sum : tenuit cervicem meam, confregit me, et posuit me sibi quasi in signum.
text_pt: Cercam-me os seus flecheiros; atravessa-me os rins, e não me poupa, e o meu fel derrama sobre a terra,
text_el: εἰρηνεύοντα διεσκέδασέν με λαβών με τῆς κόμης διέτιλεν κατέστησέν με ὥσπερ σκοπόν

text_en: He has compassed me round about with his lances, he has wounded my loins, he has not spared, and has poured out my bowels on the earth,
text_la: Circumdedit me lanceis suis; convulneravit lumbos meos : non pepercit, et effudit in terra viscera mea.
text_pt: Fere-me com ferimento sobre ferimento; arremete contra mim como um valente.
text_el: ἐκύκλωσάν με λόγχαις βάλλοντες εἰς νεφρούς μου οὐ φειδόμενοι ἐξέχεαν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν χολήν μου

text_en: he has torn me with wound upon wound, he has rushed in upon me like a giant.
text_la: Concidit me vulnere super vulnus : irruit in me quasi gigas.
text_pt: Cosi sobre a minha pele o cilício, e revolvi a minha cabeça no pó.
text_el: κατέβαλόν με πτῶμα ἐπὶ πτώματι ἔδραμον πρός με δυνάμενοι

text_en: I have sowed sackcloth upon my skin, and have covered my flesh with ashes.
text_la: Saccum consui super cutem meam, et operui cinere carnem meam.
text_pt: O meu rosto está todo avermelhado de chorar, e sobre as minhas pálpebras está a sombra da morte:
text_el: σάκκον ἔρραψα ἐπὶ βύρσης μου τὸ δὲ σθένος μου ἐν γῇ ἐσβέσθη

text_en: My face is swollen with weeping, and my eyelids are dim.
text_la: Facies mea intumuit a fletu, et palpebræ meæ caligaverunt.
text_pt: Apesar de não haver violência nas minhas mãos, e de ser pura a minha oração.
text_el: ἡ γαστήρ μου συγκέκαυται ἀπὸ κλαυθμοῦ ἐπὶ δὲ βλεφάροις μου σκιά

text_en: These things have I suffered without the iniquity of my hand, when I offered pure prayers to God .
text_la: Hæc passus sum absque iniquitate manus meæ, cum haberem mundas ad Deum preces.
text_pt: Ah! terra, não cubras o meu sangue e não haja lugar para ocultar o meu clamor!
text_el: ἄδικον δὲ οὐδὲν ἦν ἐν χερσίν μου εὐχὴ δέ μου καθαρά

text_en: O earth, cover not my blood, neither let my cry find a hiding place in you.
text_la: Terra, ne operias sanguinem meum, neque inveniat in te locum latendi clamor meus :
text_pt: Eis que também agora a minha testemunha está no céu, e nas alturas o meu testemunho está.
text_el: γῆ μὴ ἐπικαλύψῃς ἐφ' αἵματι τῆς σαρκός μου μηδὲ εἴη τόπος τῇ κραυγῇ μου

text_en: For behold my witness is in heaven , and he that knows my conscience is on high.
text_la: ecce enim in cælo testis meus, et conscius meus in excelsis.
text_pt: Os meus amigos são os que zombam de mim; os meus olhos se desfazem em lágrimas diante de Deus.
text_el: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὁ μάρτυς μου ὁ δὲ συνίστωρ μου ἐν ὑψίστοις

text_en: My friends are full of words: my eye pours out tears to God .
text_la: Verbosi amici mei : ad Deum stillat oculus meus :
text_pt: Ah! se alguém pudesse contender com Deus pelo homem, como o homem pelo seu próximo!
text_el: ἀφίκοιτό μου ἡ δέησις πρὸς κύριον ἔναντι δὲ αὐτοῦ στάζοι μου ὁ ὀφθαλμός

text_en: And O that a man might so be judged with God , as the son of man is judged with his companion!
text_la: atque utinam sic judicaretur vir cum Deo, quomodo judicatur filius hominis cum collega suo.
text_pt: Porque decorridos poucos anos, eu seguirei o caminho por onde não tornarei.
text_el: εἴη δὲ ἔλεγχος ἀνδρὶ ἔναντι κυρίου καὶ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου τῷ πλησίον αὐτοῦ

text_en: For behold short years pass away, and I am walking in a path by which I shall not return.
text_la: Ecce enim breves anni transeunt, et semitam per quam non revertar ambulo.
text_el: ἔτη δὲ ἀριθμητὰ ἥκασιν ὁδῷ δέ ᾗ οὐκ ἐπαναστραφήσομαι πορεύσομαι

text_en: My spirit shall be wasted, my days shall be shortened and only the grave remains for me.
text_la: Spiritus meus attenuabitur; dies mei breviabuntur : et solum mihi superest sepulchrum.
text_pt: O meu espírito se vai consumindo, os meus dias se vão apagando, e só tenho perante mim a sepultura.
text_el: ὀλέκομαι πνεύματι φερόμενος δέομαι δὲ ταφῆς καὶ οὐ τυγχάνω

text_en: I have not sinned , and my eye abides in bitterness.
text_la: Non peccavi, et in amaritudinibus moratur oculus meus.
text_pt: Deveras estou cercado de zombadores, e os meus olhos contemplam as suas provocações.
text_el: λίσσομαι κάμνων καὶ τί ποιήσας

text_en: Deliver me, O Lord , and set me beside you, and let any man's hand fight against me.
text_la: Libera me, Domine, et pone me juxta te, et cujusvis manus pugnet contra me.
text_pt: Promete agora, e dá-me um fiador para contigo; quem há que me dê a mão?
text_el: ἔκλεψαν δέ μου τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ἀλλότριοι τίς ἐστιν οὗτος τῇ χειρί μου συνδεθήτω

text_en: You have set their heart far from understanding, therefore they shall not be exalted.
text_la: Cor eorum longe fecisti a disciplina : propterea non exaltabuntur.
text_pt: Porque aos seus corações encobriste o entendimento, por isso não os exaltarás.
text_el: ὅτι καρδίαν αὐτῶν ἔκρυψας ἀπὸ φρονήσεως διὰ τοῦτο οὐ μὴ ὑψώσῃς αὐτούς

text_en: He promises a prey to his companions, and the eyes of his children shall fail.
text_la: Prædam pollicetur sociis, et oculi filiorum ejus deficient.
text_pt: O que denuncia os seus amigos, a fim de serem despojados, também os olhos de seus filhos desfalecerão.
text_el: τῇ μερίδι ἀναγγελεῖ κακίας ὀφθαλμοὶ δέ μου ἐφ' υἱοῖς ἐτάκησαν

text_en: He has made me as it were a byword of the people, and I am an example before them.
text_la: Posuit me quasi in proverbium vulgi, et exemplum sum coram eis.
text_pt: Porém a mim me pôs por um provérbio dos povos, de modo que me tornei uma abominação para eles.
text_el: ἔθου δέ με θρύλημα ἐν ἔθνεσιν γέλως δὲ αὐτοῖς ἀπέβην

text_en: My eye is dim through indignation, and my limbs are brought as it were to nothing.
text_la: Caligavit ab indignatione oculus meus, et membra mea quasi in nihilum redacta sunt.
text_pt: Pelo que já se escureceram de mágoa os meus olhos, e já todos os meus membros são como a sombra.
text_el: πεπώρωνται γὰρ ἀπὸ ὀργῆς οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου πεπολιόρκημαι μεγάλως ὑπὸ πάντων

text_en: The just shall be astonished at this, and the innocent shall be raised up against the hypocrite .
text_la: Stupebunt justi super hoc, et innocens contra hypocritam suscitabitur.
text_pt: Os retos pasmarão disto, e o inocente se levantará contra o hipócrita.
text_el: θαῦμα ἔσχεν ἀληθινοὺς ἐπὶ τούτῳ δίκαιος δὲ ἐπὶ παρανόμῳ ἐπανασταίη

text_en: And the just man shall hold on his way, and he that has clean hands shall be stronger and stronger.
text_la: Et tenebit justus viam suam, et mundis manibus addet fortitudinem.
text_pt: E o justo seguirá o seu caminho firmemente, e o puro de mãos irá crescendo em força.
text_el: σχοίη δὲ πιστὸς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ὁδόν καθαρὸς δὲ χεῖρας ἀναλάβοι θάρσος

text_en: Wherefore be you all converted, and come, and I shall not find among you any wise man .
text_la: Igitur omnes vos convertimini, et venite, et non inveniam in vobis ullum sapientem.
text_pt: Mas, na verdade, tornai todos vós e vinde; porque sábio nenhum acharei entre vós.
text_el: οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ πάντες ἐρείδετε καὶ δεῦτε δή οὐ γὰρ εὑρίσκω ἐν ὑμῖν ἀληθές

text_en: My days have passed away, my thoughts are dissipated, tormenting my heart.
text_la: Dies mei transierunt; cogitationes meæ dissipatæ sunt, torquentes cor meum.
text_pt: Os meus dias passaram, e malograram os meus propósitos, as aspirações do meu coração.
text_el: αἱ ἡμέραι μου παρῆλθον ἐν βρόμῳ ἐρράγη δὲ τὰ ἄρθρα τῆς καρδίας μου

text_en: They have turned night into day, and after darkness I hope for light again.
text_la: Noctem verterunt in diem, et rursum post tenebras spero lucem.
text_pt: Trocaram a noite em dia; a luz está perto do fim, por causa das trevas.
text_el: νύκτα εἰς ἡμέραν ἔθηκαν φῶς ἐγγὺς ἀπὸ προσώπου σκότους

text_en: If I wait hell is my house, and I have made my bed in darkness.
text_la: Si sustinuero, infernus domus mea est, et in tenebris stravi lectulum meum.
text_pt: Se eu esperar, a sepultura será a minha casa; nas trevas estenderei a minha cama.
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ ὑπομείνω ᾅδης μου ὁ οἶκος ἐν δὲ γνόφῳ ἔστρωταί μου ἡ στρωμνή

text_en: I have said to rottenness: You are my father; to worms, my mother and my sister.
text_la: Putredini dixi : Pater meus es; Mater mea, et soror mea, vermibus.
text_pt: À corrupção clamo: Tu és meu pai; e aos vermes: Vós sois minha mãe e minha irmã.
text_el: θάνατον ἐπεκαλεσάμην πατέρα μου εἶναι μητέρα δέ μου καὶ ἀδελφὴν σαπρίαν

text_en: Where is now then my expectation, and who considers my patience?
text_la: Ubi est ergo nunc præstolatio mea? et patientiam meam quis considerat?
text_pt: Onde, pois, estaria agora a minha esperança? Sim, a minha esperança, quem a poderá ver?
text_el: ποῦ οὖν μου ἔτι ἐστὶν ἡ ἐλπίς ἦ τὰ ἀγαθά μου ὄψομαι

text_en: All that I have shall go down into the deepest pit : do you think that there at least I shall have rest?
text_la: In profundissimum infernum descendent omnia mea : putasne saltem ibi erit requies mihi?
text_pt: As barras da sepultura descerão quando juntamente no pó teremos descanso.
text_el: ἦ μετ' ἐμοῦ εἰς ᾅδην καταβήσονται ἢ ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπὶ χώματος καταβησόμεθα

text_en: Then Baldad the Suhite answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Baldad Suhites, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondeu Bildade, o suíta, e disse:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Βαλδαδ ὁ Σαυχίτης λέγει

text_en: How long will you throw out words? understand first, and so let us speak.
text_la: Usque ad quem finem verba jactabitis? intelligite prius, et sic loquamur.
text_pt: Até quando poreis fim às palavras? Considerai bem, e então falaremos.
text_el: μέχρι τίνος οὐ παύσῃ ἐπίσχες ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ λαλήσωμεν

text_en: Why are we reputed as beasts, and counted vile before you?
text_la: Quare reputati sumus ut jumenta, et sorduimus coram vobis?
text_pt: Por que somos tratados como animais, e como imundos aos vossos olhos?
text_el: διὰ τί ὥσπερ τετράποδα σεσιωπήκαμεν ἐναντίον σου

text_en: You that destroy your soul in your fury, shall the earth be forsaken for you, and shall rocks be removed out of their place?
text_la: Qui perdis animam tuam in furore tuo, numquid propter te derelinquetur terra, et transferentur rupes de loco suo?
text_pt: Oh tu, que despedaças a tua alma na tua ira, será a terra deixada por tua causa? Remover-se-ão as rochas do seu lugar?
text_el: κέχρηταί σοι ὀργή τί γάρ ἐὰν σὺ ἀποθάνῃς ἀοίκητος ἡ ὑπ' οὐρανόν ἢ καταστραφήσεται ὄρη ἐκ θεμελίων

text_en: Shall not the light of the wicked be extinguished, and the flame of his fire not shine?
text_la: Nonne lux impii extinguetur, nec splendebit flamma ignis ejus?
text_pt: Na verdade, a luz dos ímpios se apagará, e a chama do seu fogo não resplandecerá.
text_el: καὶ φῶς ἀσεβῶν σβεσθήσεται καὶ οὐκ ἀποβήσεται αὐτῶν ἡ φλόξ

text_en: The light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and the lamp that is over him, shall be put out.
text_la: Lux obtenebrescet in tabernaculo illius, et lucerna quæ super eum est extinguetur.
text_pt: A luz se escurecerá nas suas tendas, e a sua lâmpada sobre ele se apagará.
text_el: τὸ φῶς αὐτοῦ σκότος ἐν διαίτῃ ὁ δὲ λύχνος ἐπ' αὐτῷ σβεσθήσεται

text_en: The step of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down headlong.
text_la: Arctabuntur gressus virtutis ejus, et præcipitabit eum consilium suum.
text_pt: Os seus passos firmes se estreitarão, e o seu próprio conselho o derrubará.
text_el: θηρεύσαισαν ἐλάχιστοι τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ σφάλαι δὲ αὐτοῦ ἡ βουλή

text_en: For he has thrust his feet into a net, and walks in its meshes.
text_la: Immisit enim in rete pedes suos, et in maculis ejus ambulat.
text_pt: Porque por seus próprios pés é lançado na rede, e andará nos fios enredados.
text_el: ἐμβέβληται δὲ ὁ ποὺς αὐτοῦ ἐν παγίδι ἐν δικτύῳ ἑλιχθείη

text_en: The sole of his foot shall be held in a snare, and thirst shall burn against him.
text_la: Tenebitur planta illius laqueo, et exardescet contra eum sitis.
text_pt: O laço o apanhará pelo calcanhar, e a armadilha o prenderá.
text_el: ἔλθοισαν δὲ ἐπ' αὐτὸν παγίδες κατισχύσει ἐπ' αὐτὸν διψῶντας

text_en: A gin is hidden for him in the earth, and his trap upon the path.
text_la: Abscondita est in terra pedica ejus, et decipula illius super semitam.
text_pt: Está escondida debaixo da terra uma corda, e uma armadilha na vereda.
text_el: κέκρυπται ἐν τῇ γῇ σχοινίον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ σύλλημψις αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τρίβων

text_en: Fears shall terrify him on every side, and shall entangle his feet.
text_la: Undique terrebunt eum formidines, et involvent pedes ejus.
text_pt: Os assombros o espantarão de todos os lados, e o perseguirão a cada passo.
text_el: κύκλῳ ὀλέσαισαν αὐτὸν ὀδύναι πολλοὶ δὲ περὶ πόδας αὐτοῦ ἔλθοισαν ἐν λιμῷ στενῷ

text_en: Let his strength be wasted with famine, and let hunger invade his ribs.
text_la: Attenuetur fame robur ejus, et inedia invadat costas illius.
text_pt: Será faminto o seu vigor, e a destruição está pronta ao seu lado.
text_el: πτῶμα δὲ αὐτῷ ἡτοίμασται ἐξαίσιον

text_en: Let it devour the beauty of his skin, let the firstborn death consume his arms.
text_la: Devoret pulchritudinem cutis ejus; consumat brachia illius primogenita mors.
text_pt: Serão devorados os membros do seu corpo; sim, o primogênito da morte devorará os seus membros.
text_el: βρωθείησαν αὐτοῦ κλῶνες ποδῶν κατέδεται δὲ τὰ ὡραῖα αὐτοῦ θάνατος

text_en: Let his confidence be rooted out of his tabernacle, and let destruction tread upon him like a king.
text_la: Avellatur de tabernaculo suo fiducia ejus, et calcet super eum, quasi rex, interitus.
text_pt: A sua confiança será arrancada da sua tenda, onde está confiado, e isto o fará caminhar para o rei dos terrores.
text_el: ἐκραγείη δὲ ἐκ διαίτης αὐτοῦ ἴασις σχοίη δὲ αὐτὸν ἀνάγκη αἰτίᾳ βασιλικῇ

text_en: Let the companions of him that is not, dwell in his tabernacle, let brimstone be sprinkled in his tent.
text_la: Habitent in tabernaculo illius socii ejus qui non est; aspergatur in tabernaculo ejus sulphur.
text_pt: Morará na sua mesma tenda, o que não lhe pertence; espalhar-se-á enxofre sobre a sua habitação.
text_el: κατασκηνώσει ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ αὐτοῦ ἐν νυκτὶ αὐτοῦ κατασπαρήσονται τὰ εὐπρεπῆ αὐτοῦ θείῳ

text_en: Let his roots be dried up beneath, and his harvest destroyed above.
text_la: Deorsum radices ejus siccentur : sursum autem atteratur messis ejus.
text_pt: Por baixo se secarão as suas raízes e por cima serão cortados os seus ramos.
text_el: ὑποκάτωθεν αἱ ῥίζαι αὐτοῦ ξηρανθήσονται καὶ ἐπάνωθεν ἐπιπεσεῖται θερισμὸς αὐτοῦ

text_en: Let the memory of him perish from the earth, and let not his name be renowned in the streets.
text_la: Memoria illius pereat de terra, et non celebretur nomen ejus in plateis.
text_pt: A sua memória perecerá da terra, e pelas praças não terá nome.
text_el: τὸ μνημόσυνον αὐτοῦ ἀπόλοιτο ἐκ γῆς καὶ ὑπάρχει ὄνομα αὐτῷ ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐξωτέρω

text_en: He shall drive him out of light into darkness, and shall remove him out of the world.
text_la: Expellet eum de luce in tenebras, et de orbe transferet eum.
text_pt: Da luz o lançarão nas trevas, e afugentá-lo-ão do mundo.
text_el: ἀπώσειεν αὐτὸν ἐκ φωτὸς εἰς σκότος

text_en: His seed shall not subsist, nor his offspring among his people, nor any remnants in his country.
text_la: Non erit semen ejus, neque progenies in populo suo, nec ullæ reliquiæ in regionibus ejus.
text_pt: Não terá filho nem neto entre o seu povo, e nem quem lhe suceda nas suas moradas.
text_el: οὐκ ἔσται ἐπίγνωστος ἐν λαῷ αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ σεσῳσμένος ἐν τῇ ὑπ' οὐρανὸν ὁ οἶκος αὐτοῦ ἀλλ' ἐν τοῖς αὐτοῦ ζήσονται ἕτεροι

text_en: They that come after him shall be astonished at his day, and horror shall fall upon them that went before.
text_la: In die ejus stupebunt novissimi, et primos invadet horror.
text_pt: Do seu dia se espantarão os do ocidente, assim como se espantam os do oriente.
text_el: ἐπ' αὐτῷ ἐστέναξαν ἔσχατοι πρώτους δὲ ἔσχεν θαῦμα

text_en: These then are the tabernacles of the wicked, and this the place of him that knows not God .
text_la: Hæc sunt ergo tabernacula iniqui, et iste locus ejus qui ignorat Deum.
text_pt: Tais são, na verdade, as moradas do perverso, e este é o lugar do que não conhece a Deus.
text_el: οὗτοί εἰσιν οἶκοι ἀδίκων οὗτος δὲ ὁ τόπος τῶν μὴ εἰδότων τὸν κύριον

text_en: Then Job answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Job, dixit:
text_pt: Respondeu, porém, Jó, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει

text_en: How long do you afflict my soul , and break me in pieces with words?
text_la: Usquequo affligitis animam meam, et atteritis me sermonibus?
text_pt: Até quando afligireis a minha alma, e me quebrantareis com palavras?
text_el: ἕως τίνος ἔγκοπον ποιήσετε ψυχήν μου καὶ καθαιρεῖτε με λόγοις

text_en: Behold, these ten times you confound me, and are not ashamed to oppress me.
text_la: En decies confunditis me, et non erubescitis opprimentes me.
text_pt: Já dez vezes me vituperastes; não tendes vergonha de injuriar-me.
text_el: γνῶτε μόνον ὅτι ὁ κύριος ἐποίησέ με οὕτως καταλαλεῖτέ μου οὐκ αἰσχυνόμενοί με ἐπίκεισθέ μοι
