text_en: For if I have been ignorant , my ignorance shall be with me.
text_la: Nempe etsi ignoravi, mecum erit ignorantia mea.
text_pt: Embora haja eu, na verdade, errado, comigo ficará o meu erro.
text_el: ναὶ δὴ ἐπ' ἀληθείας ἐγὼ ἐπλανήθην παρ' ἐμοὶ δὲ αὐλίζεται πλάνος

text_en: But you set yourselves up against me, and reprove me with my reproaches.
text_la: At vos contra me erigimini, et arguitis me opprobriis meis.
text_pt: Se deveras vos quereis engrandecer contra mim, e argüir-me pelo meu opróbrio,
text_el: ἔα δὲ ὅτι ἐπ' ἐμοὶ μεγαλύνεσθε ἐνάλλεσθε δέ μοι ὀνείδει

text_en: At least now understand, that God has not afflicted me with an equal judgment, and compassed me with his scourges.
text_la: Saltem nunc intelligite quia Deus non æquo judicio afflixerit me, et flagellis suis me cinxerit.
text_pt: Sabei agora que Deus é o que me transtornou, e com a sua rede me cercou.
text_el: γνῶτε οὖν ὅτι ὁ κύριός ἐστιν ὁ ταράξας ὀχύρωμα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπ' ἐμὲ ὕψωσεν

text_en: Behold I shall cry suffering violence , and no one will hear: I shall cry aloud, and there is none to judge.
text_la: Ecce clamabo, vim patiens, et nemo audiet; vociferabor, et non est qui judicet.
text_pt: Eis que clamo: Violência! Porém não sou ouvido. Grito: Socorro! Porém não há justiça.
text_el: ἰδοὺ γελῶ ὀνείδει καὶ οὐ λαλήσω κεκράξομαι καὶ οὐδαμοῦ κρίμα

text_en: He has hedged in my path round about, and I cannot pass, and in my way he has set darkness.
text_la: Semitam meam circumsepsit, et transire non possum : et in calle meo tenebras posuit.
text_pt: O meu caminho ele entrincheirou, e já não posso passar, e nas minhas veredas pôs trevas.
text_el: κύκλῳ περιῳκοδόμημαι καὶ οὐ μὴ διαβῶ ἐπὶ πρόσωπόν μου σκότος ἔθετο

text_en: He has stripped me of my glory , and has taken the crown from my head.
text_la: Spoliavit me gloria mea, et abstulit coronam de capite meo.
text_pt: Da minha honra me despojou; e tirou-me a coroa da minha cabeça.
text_el: τὴν δὲ δόξαν ἀπ' ἐμοῦ ἐξέδυσεν ἀφεῖλεν δὲ στέφανον ἀπὸ κεφαλῆς μου

text_en: He has destroyed me on every side, and I am lost, and he has taken away my hope, as from a tree that is plucked up.
text_la: Destruxit me undique, et pereo : et quasi evulsæ arbori abstulit spem meam.
text_pt: Quebrou-me de todos os lados, e eu me vou; e arrancou a minha esperança, como a uma árvore.
text_el: διέσπασέν με κύκλῳ καὶ ᾠχόμην ἐξέκοψεν δὲ ὥσπερ δένδρον τὴν ἐλπίδα μου

text_en: His wrath is kindled against me, and he has counted me as his enemy.
text_la: Iratus est contra me furor ejus, et sic me habuit quasi hostem suum.
text_pt: E fez inflamar contra mim a sua ira, e me reputou para consigo, como a seus inimigos.
text_el: δεινῶς δέ μοι ὀργῇ ἐχρήσατο ἡγήσατο δέ με ὥσπερ ἐχθρόν

text_en: His troops have come together, and have made themselves a way by me, and have besieged my tabernacle round about.
text_la: Simul venerunt latrones ejus, et fecerunt sibi viam per me, et obsederunt in gyro tabernaculum meum.
text_pt: Juntas vieram as suas tropas, e prepararam contra mim o seu caminho, e se acamparam ao redor da minha tenda.
text_el: ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ ἦλθον τὰ πειρατήρια αὐτοῦ ἐπ' ἐμοὶ ταῖς ὁδοῖς μου ἐκύκλωσάν με ἐγκάθετοι

text_en: He has put my brethren far from me, and my acquaintance like strangers have departed from me.
text_la: Fratres meos longe fecit a me, et noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me.
text_pt: pôs longe de mim a meus irmãos, e os que me conhecem, como estranhos se apartaram de mim.
text_el: ἀπ' ἐμοῦ δὲ ἀδελφοί μου ἀπέστησαν ἔγνωσαν ἀλλοτρίους ἢ ἐμέ φίλοι δέ μου ἀνελεήμονες γεγόνασιν

text_en: My kinsmen have forsaken me, and they that knew me, have forgotten me.
text_la: Dereliquerunt me propinqui mei, et qui me noverant obliti sunt mei.
text_pt: Os meus parentes me deixaram, e os meus conhecidos se esqueceram de mim.
text_el: οὐ προσεποιήσαντό με οἱ ἐγγύτατοί μου καὶ οἱ εἰδότες μου τὸ ὄνομα ἐπελάθοντό μου

text_en: They that dwell in my house, and my maidservants have counted me as a stranger, and I have been like an alien in their eyes.
text_la: Inquilini domus meæ et ancillæ meæ sicut alienum habuerunt me, et quasi peregrinus fui in oculis eorum.
text_pt: Os meus domésticos e as minhas servas me reputaram como um estranho, e vim a ser um estrangeiro aos seus olhos.
text_el: γείτονες οἰκίας θεράπαιναί τέ μου ἀλλογενὴς ἤμην ἐναντίον αὐτῶν

text_en: I called my servant, and he gave me no answer, I entreated him with my own mouth.
text_la: Servum meum vocavi, et non respondit : ore proprio deprecabar illum.
text_pt: Chamei a meu criado, e ele não me respondeu; cheguei a suplicar-lhe com a minha própria boca.
text_el: θεράποντά μου ἐκάλεσα καὶ οὐχ ὑπήκουσεν στόμα δέ μου ἐδέετο

text_en: My wife has abhorred my breath, and I entreated the children of my womb.
text_la: Halitum meum exhorruit uxor mea, et orabam filios uteri mei.
text_pt: O meu hálito se fez estranho à minha mulher; tanto que supliquei o interesse dos filhos do meu corpo.
text_el: καὶ ἱκέτευον τὴν γυναῖκά μου προσεκαλούμην δὲ κολακεύων υἱοὺς παλλακίδων μου

text_en: Even fools despised me, and when I had gone from them, they spoke against me.
text_la: Stulti quoque despiciebant me : et cum ab eis recessissem, detrahebant mihi.
text_pt: Até os pequeninos me desprezam, e, levantando-me eu, falam contra mim.
text_el: οἱ δὲ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνά με ἀπεποιήσαντο ὅταν ἀναστῶ κατ' ἐμοῦ λαλοῦσιν

text_en: They that were sometime my counsellors, have abhorred me: and he whom I loved most is turned against me.
text_la: Abominati sunt me quondam consiliarii mei, et quem maxime diligebam, aversatus est me.
text_pt: Todos os homens da minha confidência me abominam, e até os que eu amava se tornaram contra mim.
text_el: ἐβδελύξαντο δέ με οἱ εἰδότες με οὓς δὴ ἠγαπήκειν ἐπανέστησάν μοι

text_en: The flesh being consumed, my bone has cleaved to my skin, and nothing but lips are left about my teeth.
text_la: Pelli meæ, consumptis carnibus, adhæsit os meum, et derelicta sunt tantummodo labia circa dentes meos.
text_pt: Os meus ossos se apegaram à minha pele e à minha carne, e escapei só com a pele dos meus dentes.
text_el: ἐν δέρματί μου ἐσάπησαν αἱ σάρκες μου τὰ δὲ ὀστᾶ μου ἐν ὀδοῦσιν ἔχεται

text_en: Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends, because the hand of the Lord has touched me.
text_la: Miseremini mei, miseremini mei saltem vos, amici mei, quia manus Domini tetigit me.
text_pt: Compadecei-vos de mim, amigos meus, compadecei-vos de mim, porque a mão de Deus me tocou.
text_el: ἐλεήσατέ με ἐλεήσατέ με ὦ φίλοι χεὶρ γὰρ κυρίου ἡ ἁψαμένη μού ἐστιν

text_en: Why do you persecute me as God , and glut yourselves with my flesh?
text_la: Quare persequimini me sicut Deus, et carnibus meis saturamini?
text_pt: Por que me perseguis assim como Deus, e da minha carne não vos fartais?
text_el: διὰ τί δέ με διώκετε ὥσπερ καὶ ὁ κύριος ἀπὸ δὲ σαρκῶν μου οὐκ ἐμπίπλασθε

text_en: Who will grant me that my words may be written? Who will grant me that they may be marked down in a book?
text_la: Quis mihi tribuat ut scribantur sermones mei? quis mihi det ut exarentur in libro
text_pt: Quem me dera agora, que as minhas palavras fossem escritas! Quem me dera, fossem gravadas num livro!
text_el: τίς γὰρ ἂν δῴη γραφῆναι τὰ ῥήματά μου τεθῆναι δὲ αὐτὰ ἐν βιβλίῳ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

text_en: With an iron pen and in a plate of lead, or else be graven with an instrument in flint stone?
text_la: stylo ferreo et plumbi lamina, vel celte sculpantur in silice?
text_pt: E que, com pena de ferro, e com chumbo, para sempre fossem esculpidas na rocha.
text_el: ἐν γραφείῳ σιδηρῷ καὶ μολίβῳ ἢ ἐν πέτραις ἐγγλυφῆναι

text_en: For I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth.
text_la: Scio enim quod redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum :
text_pt: Porque eu sei que o meu Redentor vive, e que por fim se levantará sobre a terra.
text_el: οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι ἀέναός ἐστιν ὁ ἐκλύειν με μέλλων ἐπὶ γῆς

text_en: And I shall be clothed again with my skin, and in my flesh I shall see my God .
text_la: et rursum circumdabor pelle mea, et in carne mea videbo Deum meum :
text_pt: E depois de consumida a minha pele, contudo ainda em minha carne verei a Deus,
text_el: ἀναστήσαι τὸ δέρμα μου τὸ ἀνατλῶν ταῦτα παρὰ γὰρ κυρίου ταῦτά μοι συνετελέσθη

text_en: Whom I myself shall see, and my eyes shall behold, and not another: this my hope is laid up in my bosom.
text_la: quem visurus sum ego ipse, et oculi mei conspecturi sunt, et non alius : reposita est hæc spes mea in sinu meo.
text_pt: Vê-lo-ei, por mim mesmo, e os meus olhos, e não outros o contemplarão; e por isso os meus rins se consomem no meu interior.
text_el: ἃ ἐγὼ ἐμαυτῷ συνεπίσταμαι ἃ ὁ ὀφθαλμός μου ἑόρακεν καὶ οὐκ ἄλλος πάντα δέ μοι συντετέλεσται ἐν κόλπῳ

text_en: Why then do you say now: Let us persecute him, and let us find occasion of word against him?
text_la: Quare ergo nunc dicitis : Persequamur eum, et radicem verbi inveniamus contra eum?
text_pt: Na verdade, que devíeis dizer: Por que o perseguimos? Pois a raiz da acusação se acha em mim.
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐρεῖτε τί ἐροῦμεν ἔναντι αὐτοῦ καὶ ῥίζαν λόγου εὑρήσομεν ἐν αὐτῷ

text_en: Flee then from the face of the sword, for the sword is the revenger of iniquities : and know that there is a judgment.
text_la: Fugite ergo a facie gladii, quoniam ultor iniquitatum gladius est : et scitote esse judicium.
text_pt: Temei vós mesmos a espada; porque o furor traz os castigos da espada, para saberdes que há um juízo.
text_el: εὐλαβήθητε δὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀπὸ ἐπικαλύμματος θυμὸς γὰρ ἐπ' ἀνόμους ἐπελεύσεται καὶ τότε γνώσονται ποῦ ἐστιν αὐτῶν ἡ ὕλη

text_en: Then Sophar the Naamathite answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Sophar Naamathites, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondeu Zofar, o naamatita, e disse:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Σωφαρ ὁ Μιναῖος λέγει

text_en: Therefore various thoughts succeed one another in me, and my mind is hurried away to different things.
text_la: Idcirco cogitationes meæ variæ succedunt sibi, et mens in diversa rapitur.
text_pt: Visto que os meus pensamentos me fazem responder, eu me apresso.
text_el: οὐχ οὕτως ὑπελάμβανον ἀντερεῖν σε ταῦτα καὶ οὐχὶ συνίετε μᾶλλον ἢ καὶ ἐγώ

text_en: The doctrine with which you reprove me, I will hear, and the spirit of my understanding shall answer for me.
text_la: Doctrinam qua me arguis audiam, et spiritus intelligentiæ meæ respondebit mihi.
text_pt: Eu ouvi a repreensão, que me envergonha, mas o espírito do meu entendimento responderá por mim.
text_el: παιδείαν ἐντροπῆς μου ἀκούσομαι καὶ πνεῦμα ἐκ τῆς συνέσεως ἀποκρίνεταί μοι

text_en: This I know from the beginning, since man was placed upon the earth,
text_la: Hoc scio a principio, ex quo positus est homo super terram,
text_pt: Porventura não sabes tu que desde a antiguidade, desde que o homem foi posto sobre a terra,
text_el: μὴ ταῦτα ἔγνως ἀπὸ τοῦ ἔτι ἀφ' οὗ ἐτέθη ἄνθρωπος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

text_en: that the praise of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment.
text_la: quod laus impiorum brevis sit, et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti.
text_pt: O júbilo dos ímpios é breve, e a alegria dos hipócritas momentânea?
text_el: εὐφροσύνη γὰρ ἀσεβῶν πτῶμα ἐξαίσιον χαρμονὴ δὲ παρανόμων ἀπώλεια

text_en: If his pride mount up even to heaven , and his head touch the clouds:
text_la: Si ascenderit usque ad cælum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit,
text_pt: Ainda que a sua altivez suba até ao céu, e a sua cabeça chegue até às nuvens.
text_el: ἐὰν ἀναβῇ εἰς οὐρανὸν αὐτοῦ τὰ δῶρα ἡ δὲ θυσία αὐτοῦ νεφῶν ἅψηται

text_en: In the end he shall be destroyed like a dunghill, and they that had seen him, shall say: Where is he?
text_la: quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur, et qui eum viderant, dicent : Ubi est?
text_pt: Contudo, como o seu próprio esterco, perecerá para sempre; e os que o viam dirão: Onde está?
text_el: ὅταν γὰρ δοκῇ ἤδη κατεστηρίχθαι τότε εἰς τέλος ἀπολεῖται οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐροῦσιν ποῦ ἐστιν

text_en: As a dream that flees away he shall not be found, he shall pass as a vision of the night:
text_la: Velut somnium avolans non invenietur : transiet sicut visio nocturna.
text_pt: Como um sonho voará, e não será achado, e será afugentado como uma visão da noite.
text_el: ὥσπερ ἐνύπνιον ἐκπετασθὲν οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἔπτη δὲ ὥσπερ φάσμα νυκτερινόν

text_en: The eyes that had seen him, shall see him no more, neither shall his place any more behold him.
text_la: Oculus qui eum viderat non videbit, neque ultra intuebitur eum locus suus.
text_pt: O olho, que já o viu, jamais o verá, nem o seu lugar o verá mais.
text_el: ὀφθαλμὸς παρέβλεψεν καὶ οὐ προσθήσει καὶ οὐκέτι προσνοήσει αὐτὸν ὁ τόπος αὐτοῦ

text_en: His children shall be oppressed with want, and his hands shall render to him his sorrow.
text_la: Filii ejus atterentur egestate, et manus illius reddent ei dolorem suum.
text_pt: Os seus filhos procurarão agradar aos pobres, e as suas mãos restituirão os seus bens.
text_el: τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ ὀλέσαισαν ἥττονες αἱ δὲ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ πυρσεύσαισαν ὀδύνας

text_en: His bones shall be filled with the vices of his youth, and they shall sleep with him in the dust.
text_la: Ossa ejus implebuntur vitiis adolescentiæ ejus, et cum eo in pulvere dormient.
text_pt: Os seus ossos estão cheios do vigor da sua mocidade, mas este se deitará com ele no pó.
text_el: ὀστᾶ αὐτοῦ ἐνεπλήσθησαν νεότητος αὐτοῦ καὶ μετ' αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ χώματος κοιμηθήσεται

text_en: For when evil shall be sweet in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue.
text_la: Cum enim dulce fuerit in ore ejus malum, abscondet illud sub lingua sua.
text_pt: Ainda que o mal lhe seja doce na boca, e ele o esconda debaixo da sua língua,
text_el: ἐὰν γλυκανθῇ ἐν στόματι αὐτοῦ κακία κρύψει αὐτὴν ὑπὸ τὴν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ

text_en: He will spare it, and not leave it, and will hide it in his throat.
text_la: Parcet illi, et non derelinquet illud, et celabit in gutture suo.
text_pt: E o guarde, e não o deixe, antes o retenha no seu paladar,
text_el: οὐ φείσεται αὐτῆς καὶ οὐκ ἐγκαταλείψει αὐτὴν καὶ συνέξει αὐτὴν ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ λάρυγγος αὐτοῦ

text_en: His bread in his belly shall be turned into the gall of asps within him,
text_la: Panis ejus in utero illius vertetur in fel aspidum intrinsecus.
text_pt: Contudo a sua comida se mudará nas suas entranhas; fel de áspides será interiormente.
text_el: καὶ οὐ μὴ δυνηθῇ βοηθῆσαι ἑαυτῷ χολὴ ἀσπίδος ἐν γαστρὶ αὐτοῦ

text_en: the riches which he has swallowed, he shall vomit up, and God shall draw them out of his belly.
text_la: Divitias quas devoravit evomet, et de ventre illius extrahet eas Deus.
text_pt: Engoliu riquezas, porém vomitá-las-á; do seu ventre Deus as lançará.
text_el: πλοῦτος ἀδίκως συναγόμενος ἐξεμεσθήσεται ἐξ οἰκίας αὐτοῦ ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἄγγελος

text_en: He shall suck the head of asps, and the viper's tongue shall kill him.
text_la: Caput aspidum suget, et occidet eum lingua viperæ.
text_pt: Veneno de áspides sorverá; língua de víbora o matará.
text_el: θυμὸν δὲ δρακόντων θηλάσειεν ἀνέλοι δὲ αὐτὸν γλῶσσα ὄφεως

text_en: Let him not see the streams of the river, the brooks of honey and of butter.
text_la: (Non videat rivulos fluminis, torrentes mellis et butyri.)
text_pt: Não verá as correntes, os rios e os ribeiros de mel e manteiga.
text_el: μὴ ἴδοι ἄμελξιν νομάδων μηδὲ νομὰς μέλιτος καὶ βουτύρου

text_en: He shall be punished for all that he did, and yet shall not be consumed: according to the multitude of his devices so also shall he suffer.
text_la: Luet quæ fecit omnia, nec tamen consumetur : juxta multitudinem adinventionum suarum, sic et sustinebit.
text_pt: Restituirá o seu trabalho, e não o engolirá; conforme ao poder de sua mudança, e não saltará de gozo.
text_el: εἰς κενὰ καὶ μάταια ἐκοπίασεν πλοῦτον ἐξ οὗ οὐ γεύσεται ὥσπερ στρίφνος ἀμάσητος ἀκατάποτος

text_en: Because he broke in and stripped the poor: he has violently taken away a house which he did not build.
text_la: Quoniam confringens nudavit pauperes : domum rapuit, et non ædificavit eam.
text_pt: Porquanto oprimiu e desamparou os pobres, e roubou a casa que não edificou.
text_el: πολλῶν γὰρ ἀδυνάτων οἴκους ἔθλασεν δίαιταν δὲ ἥρπασεν καὶ οὐκ ἔστησεν

text_en: And yet his belly was not filled: and when he has the things he coveted , he shall not be able to possess them.
text_la: Nec est satiatus venter ejus : et cum habuerit quæ concupierat, possidere non poterit.
text_pt: Porquanto não sentiu sossego no seu ventre; nada salvará das coisas por ele desejadas.
text_el: οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ σωτηρία τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ αὐτοῦ οὐ σωθήσεται

text_en: There was nothing left of his meat, and therefore nothing shall continue of his goods:
text_la: Non remansit de cibo ejus, et propterea nihil permanebit de bonis ejus.
text_pt: Nada lhe sobejará do que coma; por isso as suas riquezas não durarão.
text_el: οὐκ ἔστιν ὑπόλειμμα τοῖς βρώμασιν αὐτοῦ διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀνθήσει αὐτοῦ τὰ ἀγαθά

text_en: When he shall be filled, he shall be straitened, he shall burn, and every sorrow shall fall upon him.
text_la: Cum satiatus fuerit, arctabitur : æstuabit, et omnis dolor irruet super eum.
text_pt: Sendo plena a sua abastança, estará angustiado; toda a força da miséria virá sobre ele.
text_el: ὅταν δὲ δοκῇ ἤδη πεπληρῶσθαι θλιβήσεται πᾶσα δὲ ἀνάγκη ἐπ' αὐτὸν ἐπελεύσεται

text_en: May his belly be filled, that God may send forth the wrath of his indignation upon him, and rain down his war upon him.
text_la: Utinam impleatur venter ejus, ut emittat in eum iram furoris sui, et pluat super illum bellum suum.
text_pt: Mesmo estando ele a encher a sua barriga, Deus mandará sobre ele o ardor da sua ira, e a fará chover sobre ele quando for comer.
text_el: εἴ πως πληρώσαι γαστέρα αὐτοῦ ἐπαποστείλαι ἐπ' αὐτὸν θυμὸν ὀργῆς νίψαι ἐπ' αὐτὸν ὀδύνας

text_en: He shall flee from weapons of iron, and shall fall upon a bow of brass.
text_la: Fugiet arma ferrea, et irruet in arcum æreum.
text_pt: Ainda que fuja das armas de ferro, o arco de bronze o atravessará.
text_el: καὶ οὐ μὴ σωθῇ ἐκ χειρὸς σιδήρου τρώσαι αὐτὸν τόξον χάλκειον

text_en: The sword is drawn out, and comes forth from its scabbard, and glitters in his bitterness: the terrible ones shall go and come upon him.
text_la: Eductus, et egrediens de vagina sua, et fulgurans in amaritudine sua : vadent et venient super eum horribiles.
text_pt: Desembainhará a espada que sairá do seu corpo, e resplandecendo virá do seu fel; e haverá sobre ele assombros.
text_el: διεξέλθοι δὲ διὰ σώματος αὐτοῦ βέλος ἀστραπαὶ δὲ ἐν διαίταις αὐτοῦ περιπατήσαισαν ἐπ' αὐτῷ φόβοι

text_en: All darkness is hid in his secret places: a fire that is not kindled shall devour him, he shall be afflicted when left in his tabernacle.
text_la: Omnes tenebræ absconditæ sunt in occultis ejus; devorabit eum ignis qui non succenditur : affligetur relictus in tabernaculo suo.
text_pt: Toda a escuridão se ocultará nos seus esconderijos; um fogo não assoprado o consumirá, irá mal com o que ficar na sua tenda.
text_el: πᾶν δὲ σκότος αὐτῷ ὑπομείναι κατέδεται αὐτὸν πῦρ ἄκαυστον κακώσαι δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπήλυτος τὸν οἶκον

text_en: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity , and the earth shall rise up against him.
text_la: Revelabunt cæli iniquitatem ejus, et terra consurget adversus eum.
text_pt: Os céus manifestarão a sua iniqüidade; e a terra se levantará contra ele.
text_el: ἀνακαλύψαι δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ οὐρανὸς τὰς ἀνομίας γῆ δὲ ἐπανασταίη αὐτῷ

text_en: The offspring of his house shall be exposed, he shall be pulled down in the day of God's wrath .
text_la: Apertum erit germen domus illius : detrahetur in die furoris Dei.
text_pt: As riquezas de sua casa serão transportadas; no dia da sua ira todas se derramarão.
text_el: ἑλκύσαι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεια εἰς τέλος ἡμέρα ὀργῆς ἐπέλθοι αὐτῷ

text_en: This is the portion of a wicked man from God , and the inheritance of his doings from the Lord .
text_la: Hæc est pars hominis impii a Deo, et hæreditas verborum ejus a Domino.
text_pt: Esta, da parte de Deus, é a porção do homem ímpio; esta é a herança que Deus lhe decretou.
text_el: αὕτη ἡ μερὶς ἀνθρώπου ἀσεβοῦς παρὰ κυρίου καὶ κτῆμα ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ παρὰ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου

text_en: Then Job answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Job, dixit:
text_pt: Respondeu, porém, Jó, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει

text_en: Hear, I beseech you, my words, and do penance .
text_la: Audite, quæso, sermones meos, et agite pœnitentiam.
text_pt: Ouvi atentamente as minhas razões; e isto vos sirva de consolação.
text_el: ἀκούσατε ἀκούσατέ μου τῶν λόγων ἵνα μὴ ᾖ μοι παρ' ὑμῶν αὕτη ἡ παράκλησις

text_en: Suffer me, and I will speak, and after, if you please, laugh at my words.
text_la: Sustinete me, et ego loquar : et post mea, si videbitur, verba, ridete.
text_pt: Sofrei-me, e eu falarei; e havendo eu falado, zombai.
text_el: ἄρατέ με ἐγὼ δὲ λαλήσω εἶτ' οὐ καταγελάσετέ μου

text_en: Is my debate against man , that I should not have just reason to be troubled?
text_la: Numquid contra hominem disputatio mea est, ut merito non debeam contristari?
text_pt: Porventura eu me queixo de algum homem? Porém, ainda que assim fosse, por que não se angustiaria o meu espírito?
text_el: τί γάρ μὴ ἀνθρώπου μου ἡ ἔλεγξις ἢ διὰ τί οὐ θυμωθήσομαι

text_en: Hearken to me and be astonished, and lay your finger on your mouth.
text_la: Attendite me et obstupescite, et superponite digitum ori vestro.
text_pt: Olhai para mim, e pasmai; e ponde a mão sobre a boca.
text_el: εἰσβλέψαντες εἰς ἐμὲ θαυμάσατε χεῖρα θέντες ἐπὶ σιαγόνι

text_en: As for me, when I remember, I am afraid, and trembling takes hold on my flesh.
text_la: Et ego, quando recordatus fuero, pertimesco, et concutit carnem meam tremor.
text_pt: Porque, quando me lembro disto me perturbo, e a minha carne é sobressaltada de horror.
text_el: ἐάν τε γὰρ μνησθῶ ἐσπούδακα ἔχουσιν δέ μου τὰς σάρκας ὀδύναι

text_en: Why then do the wicked live, are they advanced, and strengthened with riches?
text_la: Quare ergo impii vivunt, sublevati sunt, confortatique divitiis?
text_pt: Por que razão vivem os ímpios, envelhecem, e ainda se robustecem em poder?
text_el: διὰ τί ἀσεβεῖς ζῶσιν πεπαλαίωνται δὲ καὶ ἐν πλούτῳ

text_en: Their seed continues before them, a multitude of kinsmen, and of children's children in their sight.
text_la: Semen eorum permanet coram eis : propinquorum turba et nepotum in conspectu eorum.
text_pt: A sua descendência se estabelece com eles perante a sua face; e os seus renovos perante os seus olhos.
text_el: ὁ σπόρος αὐτῶν κατὰ ψυχήν τὰ δὲ τέκνα αὐτῶν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς

text_en: Their houses are secure and peaceable, and the rod of God is not upon them.
text_la: Domus eorum securæ sunt et pacatæ, et non est virga Dei super illos.
text_pt: As suas casas têm paz, sem temor; e a vara de Deus não está sobre eles.
text_el: οἱ οἶκοι αὐτῶν εὐθηνοῦσιν φόβος δὲ οὐδαμοῦ μάστιξ δὲ παρὰ κυρίου οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπ' αὐτοῖς

text_en: Their cattle have conceived, and failed not: their cow has calved, and is not deprived of her fruit.
text_la: Bos eorum concepit, et non abortivit : vacca peperit, et non est privata fœtu suo.
text_pt: O seu touro gera, e não falha; pare a sua vaca, e não aborta.
text_el: ἡ βοῦς αὐτῶν οὐκ ὠμοτόκησεν διεσώθη δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα καὶ οὐκ ἔσφαλεν

text_en: Their little ones go out like a flock, and their children dance and play .
text_la: Egrediuntur quasi greges parvuli eorum, et infantes eorum exultant lusibus.
text_pt: Fazem sair as suas crianças, como a um rebanho, e seus filhos andam saltando.
text_el: μένουσιν δὲ ὡς πρόβατα αἰώνια τὰ δὲ παιδία αὐτῶν προσπαίζουσιν

text_en: They take the timbrel, and the harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.
text_la: Tenent tympanum et citharam, et gaudent ad sonitum organi.
text_pt: Levantam a voz, ao som do tamboril e da harpa, e alegram-se ao som do órgão.
text_el: ἀναλαβόντες ψαλτήριον καὶ κιθάραν καὶ εὐφραίνονται φωνῇ ψαλμοῦ

text_en: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment they go down to hell.
text_la: Ducunt in bonis dies suos, et in puncto ad inferna descendunt.
text_pt: Na prosperidade gastam os seus dias, e num momento descem à sepultura.
text_el: συνετέλεσαν δὲ ἐν ἀγαθοῖς τὸν βίον αὐτῶν ἐν δὲ ἀναπαύσει ᾅδου ἐκοιμήθησαν

text_en: Who have said to God : Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of your ways.
text_la: Qui dixerunt Deo : Recede a nobis, et scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus.
text_pt: E, todavia, dizem a Deus: Retira-te de nós; porque não desejamos ter conhecimento dos teus caminhos.
text_el: λέγει δὲ κυρίῳ ἀπόστα ἀπ' ἐμοῦ ὁδούς σου εἰδέναι οὐ βούλομαι

text_en: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? And what does it profit us if we pray to him?
text_la: Quis est Omnipotens, ut serviamus ei? et quid nobis prodest si oraverimus illum?
text_pt: Quem é o Todo-Poderoso, para que nós o sirvamos? E que nos aproveitará que lhe façamos orações?
text_el: τί ἱκανός ὅτι δουλεύσομεν αὐτῷ καὶ τίς ὠφέλεια ὅτι ἀπαντήσομεν αὐτῷ

text_en: Yet because their good things are not in their hand, may the counsel of the wicked be far from me.
text_la: Verumtamen quia non sunt in manu eorum bona sua, consilium impiorum longe sit a me.
text_pt: Vede, porém, que a prosperidade não está nas mãos deles; esteja longe de mim o conselho dos ímpios!
text_el: ἐν χερσὶν γὰρ ἦν αὐτῶν τὰ ἀγαθά ἔργα δὲ ἀσεβῶν οὐκ ἐφορᾷ

text_en: How often shall the lamp of the wicked be put out, and a deluge come upon them, and he shall distribute the sorrows of his wrath ?
text_la: Quoties lucerna impiorum extinguetur, et superveniet eis inundatio, et dolores dividet furoris sui?
text_pt: Quantas vezes sucede que se apaga a lâmpada dos ímpios, e lhes sobrevém a sua destruição? E Deus na sua ira lhes reparte dores!
text_el: οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀσεβῶν λύχνος σβεσθήσεται ἐπελεύσεται δὲ αὐτοῖς ἡ καταστροφή ὠδῖνες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἕξουσιν ἀπὸ ὀργῆς

text_en: They shall be as chaff before the face of the wind, and as ashes which the whirlwind scatters.
text_la: Erunt sicut paleæ ante faciem venti, et sicut favilla quam turbo dispergit.
text_pt: Porque são como a palha diante do vento, e como a pragana, que arrebata o redemoinho.
text_el: ἔσονται δὲ ὥσπερ ἄχυρα πρὸ ἀνέμου ἢ ὥσπερ κονιορτός ὃν ὑφείλατο λαῖλαψ

text_en: God shall lay up the sorrow of the father for his children: and when he shall repay, then shall he know.
text_la: Deus servabit filiis illius dolorem patris, et cum reddiderit, tunc sciet.
text_pt: Deus guarda a sua violência para seus filhos, e dá-lhe o pago, para que o conheça.
text_el: ἐκλίποι υἱοὺς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ ἀνταποδώσει πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ γνώσεται

text_en: His eyes shall see his own destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
text_la: Videbunt oculi ejus interfectionem suam, et de furore Omnipotentis bibet.
text_pt: Seus olhos verão a sua ruína, e ele beberá do furor do Todo-Poderoso.
text_el: ἴδοισαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ σφαγήν ἀπὸ δὲ κυρίου μὴ διασωθείη

text_en: For what is it to him what befalls his house after him: and if the number of his months be diminished by one half?
text_la: Quid enim ad eum pertinet de domo sua post se, et si numerus mensium ejus dimidietur?
text_pt: Por que, que prazer teria na sua casa, depois de morto, cortando-se-lhe o número dos seus meses?
text_el: ὅτι τί θέλημα αὐτοῦ ἐν οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ μετ' αὐτόν καὶ ἀριθμοὶ μηνῶν αὐτοῦ διῃρέθησαν

text_en: Shall any one teach God knowledge, who judges those that are high?
text_la: Numquid Deus docebit quispiam scientiam, qui excelsos judicat?
text_pt: Porventura a Deus se ensinaria ciência, a ele que julga os excelsos?
text_el: πότερον οὐχὶ ὁ κύριός ἐστιν ὁ διδάσκων σύνεσιν καὶ ἐπιστήμην αὐτὸς δὲ φόνους διακρινεῖ

text_en: One man dies strong, and hale, rich and happy .
text_la: Iste moritur robustus et sanus, dives et felix :
text_pt: Um morre na força da sua plenitude, estando inteiramente sossegado e tranqüilo.
text_el: οὗτος ἀποθανεῖται ἐν κράτει ἁπλοσύνης αὐτοῦ ὅλος δὲ εὐπαθῶν καὶ εὐθηνῶν

text_en: His bowels are full of fat, and his bones are moistened with marrow.
text_la: viscera ejus plena sunt adipe, et medullis ossa illius irrigantur :
text_pt: Com seus baldes cheios de leite, e a medula dos seus ossos umedecida.
text_el: τὰ δὲ ἔγκατα αὐτοῦ πλήρη στέατος μυελὸς δὲ αὐτοῦ διαχεῖται

text_en: But another dies in bitterness of soul without any riches:
text_la: alius vero moritur in amaritudine animæ absque ullis opibus :
text_pt: E outro, ao contrário, morre na amargura do seu coração, não havendo provado do bem.
text_el: ὁ δὲ τελευτᾷ ὑπὸ πικρίας ψυχῆς οὐ φαγὼν οὐδὲν ἀγαθόν

text_en: And yet they shall sleep together in the dust, and worms shall cover them.
text_la: et tamen simul in pulvere dormient, et vermes operient eos.
text_pt: Juntamente jazem no pó, e os vermes os cobrem.
text_el: ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ ἐπὶ γῆς κοιμῶνται σαπρία δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐκάλυψεν

text_en: Surely I know your thoughts, and your unjust judgments against me.
text_la: Certe novi cogitationes vestras, et sententias contra me iniquas.
text_pt: Eis que conheço bem os vossos pensamentos; e os maus intentos com que injustamente me fazeis violência.
text_el: ὥστε οἶδα ὑμᾶς ὅτι τόλμῃ ἐπίκεισθέ μοι

text_en: For you say: Where is the house of the prince? And where are the dwelling places of the wicked?
text_la: Dicitis enim : Ubi est domus principis? et ubi tabernacula impiorum?
text_pt: Porque direis: Onde está a casa do príncipe, e onde a tenda em que moravam os ímpios?
text_el: ὅτι ἐρεῖτε ποῦ ἐστιν οἶκος ἄρχοντος καὶ ποῦ ἐστιν ἡ σκέπη τῶν σκηνωμάτων τῶν ἀσεβῶν

text_en: Ask any one of them that go by the way, and you shall perceive that he knows these same things.
text_la: Interrogate quemlibet de viatoribus, et hæc eadem illum intelligere cognoscetis :
text_pt: Porventura não perguntastes aos que passam pelo caminho, e não conheceis os seus sinais,
text_el: ἐρωτήσατε παραπορευομένους ὁδόν καὶ τὰ σημεῖα αὐτῶν οὐκ ἀπαλλοτριώσετε

text_en: Because the wicked man is reserved to the day of destruction, and he shall be brought to the day of wrath .
text_la: quia in diem perditionis servatur malus, et ad diem furoris ducetur.
text_pt: Que o mau é preservado para o dia da destruição; e arrebatado no dia do furor?
text_el: ὅτι εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπωλείας κουφίζεται ὁ πονηρός εἰς ἡμέραν ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ ἀπαχθήσονται

text_en: Who shall reprove his way to his face? And who shall repay him what he has done?
text_la: Quis arguet coram eo viam ejus? et quæ fecit, quis reddet illi?
text_pt: Quem acusará diante dele o seu caminho, e quem lhe dará o pago do que faz?
text_el: τίς ἀπαγγελεῖ ἐπὶ προσώπου αὐτοῦ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἐποίησεν τίς ἀνταποδώσει αὐτῷ

text_en: He shall be brought to the graves, and shall watch in the heap of the dead.
text_la: Ipse ad sepulchra ducetur, et in congerie mortuorum vigilabit.
text_pt: Finalmente é levado à sepultura, e vigiam-lhe o túmulo.
text_el: καὶ αὐτὸς εἰς τάφους ἀπηνέχθη καὶ ἐπὶ σορῷ ἠγρύπνησεν

text_en: He has been acceptable to the gravel of Cocytus, and he shall draw every man after him, and there are innumerable before him.
text_la: Dulcis fuit glareis Cocyti, et post se omnem hominem trahet, et ante se innumerabiles.
text_pt: Os torrões do vale lhe são doces, e o seguirão todos os homens; e adiante dele foram inumeráveis.
text_el: ἐγλυκάνθησαν αὐτῷ χάλικες χειμάρρου καὶ ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ἀπελεύσεται καὶ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ ἀναρίθμητοι

text_en: How then do you comfort me in vain, whereas your answer is shown to be repugnant to truth ?
text_la: Quomodo igitur consolamini me frustra, cum responsio vestra repugnare ostensa sit veritati?
text_pt: Como, pois, me consolais com vaidade? Pois nas vossas respostas ainda resta a transgressão.
text_el: πῶς δὲ παρακαλεῖτέ με κενά τὸ δὲ ἐμὲ καταπαύσασθαι ἀφ' ὑμῶν οὐδέν

text_en: Then Eliphaz the Themanite answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Eliphaz Themanites, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondeu Elifaz, o temanita, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ελιφας ὁ Θαιμανίτης λέγει

text_en: Can man be compared with God , even though he were of perfect knowledge?
text_la: Numquid Deo potest comparari homo, etiam cum perfectæ fuerit scientiæ?
text_pt: Porventura será o homem de algum proveito a Deus? Antes a si mesmo o prudente será proveitoso.
text_el: πότερον οὐχὶ ὁ κύριός ἐστιν ὁ διδάσκων σύνεσιν καὶ ἐπιστήμην

text_en: What does it profit God if you be just ? Or what do you give him if your way be unspotted?
text_la: Quid prodest Deo, si justus fueris? aut quid ei confers, si immaculata fuerit via tua?
text_pt: Ou tem o Todo-Poderoso prazer em que tu sejas justo, ou algum lucro em que tu faças perfeitos os teus caminhos?
text_el: τί γὰρ μέλει τῷ κυρίῳ ἐὰν σὺ ἦσθα τοῖς ἔργοις ἄμεμπτος ἢ ὠφέλεια ὅτι ἁπλώσῃς τὴν ὁδόν σου

text_en: Shall he reprove you for fear, and come with you into judgment:
text_la: Numquid timens arguet te, et veniet tecum in judicium,
text_pt: Ou te repreende, pelo temor que tem de ti, ou entra contigo em juízo?
text_el: ἦ λόγον σου ποιούμενος ἐλέγξει σε καὶ συνεισελεύσεταί σοι εἰς κρίσιν

text_en: And not for your manifold wickedness and your infinite iniquities ?
text_la: et non propter malitiam tuam plurimam, et infinitas iniquitates tuas?
text_pt: Porventura não é grande a tua malícia, e sem termo as tuas iniqüidades?
text_el: πότερον οὐχ ἡ κακία σού ἐστιν πολλή ἀναρίθμητοι δέ σού εἰσιν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι

text_en: For you have taken away the pledge of your brethren without cause, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
text_la: Abstulisti enim pignus fratrum tuorum sine causa, et nudos spoliasti vestibus.
text_pt: Porque sem causa penhoraste a teus irmãos, e aos nus despojaste as vestes.
text_el: ἠνεχύραζες δὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου διὰ κενῆς ἀμφίασιν δὲ γυμνῶν ἀφείλου

text_en: You have not given water to the weary, you have withdrawn bread from the hungry.
text_la: Aquam lasso non dedisti, et esurienti subtraxisti panem.
text_pt: Não deste ao cansado água a beber, e ao faminto retiveste o pão.
text_el: οὐδὲ ὕδωρ διψῶντας ἐπότισας ἀλλὰ πεινώντων ἐστέρησας ψωμόν

text_en: In the strength of your arm you possessed the land, and being the most mighty you hold it.
text_la: In fortitudine brachii tui possidebas terram, et potentissimus obtinebas eam.
text_pt: Mas para o poderoso era a terra, e o homem tido em respeito habitava nela.
text_el: ἐθαύμασας δέ τινων πρόσωπον ᾤκισας δὲ τοὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

text_en: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless you have broken in pieces.
text_la: Viduas dimisisti vacuas, et lacertos pupillorum comminuisti.
text_pt: As viúvas despediste vazias, e os braços dos órfãos foram quebrados.
text_el: χήρας δὲ ἐξαπέστειλας κενάς ὀρφανοὺς δὲ ἐκάκωσας

text_en: Therefore are you surrounded with shares, and sudden fear troubles you.
text_la: Propterea circumdatus es laqueis, et conturbat te formido subita.
text_pt: Por isso é que estás cercado de laços, e te perturba um pavor repentino,
text_el: τοιγαροῦν ἐκύκλωσάν σε παγίδες καὶ ἐσπούδασέν σε πόλεμος ἐξαίσιος

text_en: And did you think that you should not see darkness, and that you should not be covered with the violence of overflowing waters?
text_la: Et putabas te tenebras non visurum, et impetu aquarum inundantium non oppressum iri?
text_pt: Ou trevas em que nada vês, e a abundância de águas que te cobre.
text_el: τὸ φῶς σοι σκότος ἀπέβη κοιμηθέντα δὲ ὕδωρ σε ἐκάλυψεν

text_en: Do you not think that God is higher than heaven , and is elevated above the height of the stars?
text_la: an non cogitas quod Deus excelsior cælo sit, et super stellarum verticem sublimetur?
text_pt: Porventura Deus não está na altura dos céus? Olha para a altura das estrelas; quão elevadas estão.
text_el: μὴ οὐχὶ ὁ τὰ ὑψηλὰ ναίων ἐφορᾷ τοὺς δὲ ὕβρει φερομένους ἐταπείνωσεν

text_en: And you say: What does God know? And he judges as it were through a mist.
text_la: Et dicis : Quid enim novit Deus? et quasi per caliginem judicat.
text_pt: E dizes: que sabe Deus? Porventura julgará ele através da escuridão?
text_el: καὶ εἶπας τί ἔγνω ὁ ἰσχυρός ἦ κατὰ τοῦ γνόφου κρινεῖ

text_en: The clouds are his covert, and he does not consider our things, and he walks about the poles of heaven .
text_la: Nubes latibulum ejus, nec nostra considerat, et circa cardines cæli perambulat.
text_pt: As nuvens são esconderijo para ele, para que não veja; e passeia pelo circuito dos céus.
text_el: νέφη ἀποκρυφὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐχ ὁραθήσεται καὶ γῦρον οὐρανοῦ διαπορεύσεται

text_en: Do you desire to keep the path of ages, which wicked men have trodden?
text_la: Numquid semitam sæculorum custodire cupis, quam calcaverunt viri iniqui,
text_pt: Porventura queres guardar a vereda antiga, que pisaram os homens iníquos?
text_el: μὴ τρίβον αἰώνιον φυλάξεις ἣν ἐπάτησαν ἄνδρες ἄδικοι

text_en: Who were taken away before their time, and a flood has overthrown their foundation.
text_la: qui sublati sunt ante tempus suum, et fluvius subvertit fundamentum eorum?
text_pt: Eles foram arrebatados antes do seu tempo; sobre o seu fundamento um dilúvio se derramou.
text_el: οἳ συνελήμφθησαν ἄωροι ποταμὸς ἐπιρρέων οἱ θεμέλιοι αὐτῶν

text_en: Who said to God : Depart from us: and looked upon the Almighty as if he could do nothing:
text_la: Qui dicebant Deo : Recede a nobis : et quasi nihil posset facere Omnipotens, æstimabant eum,
text_pt: Diziam a Deus: Retira-te de nós. E: Que foi que o Todo-Poderoso nos fez?
text_el: οἱ λέγοντες κύριος τί ποιήσει ἡμῖν ἢ τί ἐπάξεται ἡμῖν ὁ παντοκράτωρ

text_en: Whereas he had filled their houses with good things: whose way of thinking be far from me.
text_la: cum ille implesset domos eorum bonis : quorum sententia procul sit a me.
text_pt: Contudo ele encheu de bens as suas casas; mas o conselho dos ímpios esteja longe de mim.
text_el: ὃς δὲ ἐνέπλησεν τοὺς οἴκους αὐτῶν ἀγαθῶν βουλὴ δὲ ἀσεβῶν πόρρω ἀπ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: The just shall see, and shall rejoice, and the innocent shall laugh them to scorn.
text_la: Videbunt justi, et lætabuntur, et innocens subsannabit eos :
text_pt: Os justos o vêem, e se alegram, e o inocente escarnece deles.
text_el: ἰδόντες δίκαιοι ἐγέλασαν ἄμεμπτος δὲ ἐμυκτήρισεν

text_en: Is not their exaltation cut down, and has not fire devoured the remnants of them?
text_la: nonne succisa est erectio eorum? et reliquias eorum devoravit ignis?
text_pt: Porquanto o nosso adversário não foi destruído, mas o fogo consumiu o que restou deles.
text_el: εἰ μὴ ἠφανίσθη ἡ ὑπόστασις αὐτῶν καὶ τὸ κατάλειμμα αὐτῶν καταφάγεται πῦρ

text_en: Submit yourself then to him, and be at peace: and thereby you shall have the best fruits.
text_la: Acquiesce igitur ei, et habeto pacem, et per hæc habebis fructus optimos.
text_pt: Apega-te, pois, a ele, e tem paz, e assim te sobrevirá o bem.
text_el: γενοῦ δὴ σκληρός ἐὰν ὑπομείνῃς εἶτ' ὁ καρπός σου ἔσται ἐν ἀγαθοῖς

text_en: Receive the law of his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.
text_la: Suscipe ex ore illius legem, et pone sermones ejus in corde tuo.
text_pt: Aceita, peço-te, a lei da sua boca, e põe as suas palavras no teu coração.
text_el: ἔκλαβε δὲ ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐξηγορίαν καὶ ἀνάλαβε τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ ἐν καρδίᾳ σου

text_en: If you will return to the Almighty, you shall be built up, and shall put away iniquity far from your tabernacle.
text_la: Si reversus fueris ad Omnipotentem, ædificaberis, et longe facies iniquitatem a tabernaculo tuo.
text_pt: Se te voltares ao Todo-Poderoso, serás edificado; se afastares a iniqüidade da tua tenda,
text_el: ἐὰν δὲ ἐπιστραφῇς καὶ ταπεινώσῃς σεαυτὸν ἔναντι κυρίου πόρρω ἐποίησας ἀπὸ διαίτης σου τὸ ἄδικον

text_en: He shall give for earth flint, and for flint torrents of gold.
text_la: Dabit pro terra silicem, et pro silice torrentes aureos.
text_pt: E deitares o teu tesouro no pó, e o ouro de Ofir nas pedras dos ribeiros,
text_el: θήσῃ ἐπὶ χώματι ἐν πέτρᾳ καὶ ὡς πέτρᾳ χειμάρρους Ωφιρ

text_en: And the Almighty shall be against your enemies, and silver shall be heaped together for you.
text_la: Eritque Omnipotens contra hostes tuos, et argentum coacervabitur tibi.
text_pt: Então o Todo-Poderoso será o teu tesouro, e a tua prata acumulada.
text_el: ἔσται οὖν σου ὁ παντοκράτωρ βοηθὸς ἀπὸ ἐχθρῶν καθαρὸν δὲ ἀποδώσει σε ὥσπερ ἀργύριον πεπυρωμένον

text_en: Then shall you abound in delights in the Almighty, and shall lift up your face to God .
text_la: Tunc super Omnipotentem deliciis afflues, et elevabis ad Deum faciem tuam.
text_pt: Porque então te deleitarás no Todo-Poderoso, e levantarás o teu rosto para Deus.
text_el: εἶτα παρρησιασθήσῃ ἔναντι κυρίου ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἱλαρῶς

text_en: You shall pray to him, and he will hear you, and you shall pay vows .
text_la: Rogabis eum, et exaudiet te, et vota tua reddes.
text_pt: Orarás a ele, e ele te ouvirá, e pagarás os teus votos.
text_el: εὐξαμένου δέ σου πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰσακούσεταί σου δώσει δέ σοι ἀποδοῦναι τὰς εὐχάς

text_en: You shall decree a thing, and it shall come to you, and light shall shine in your ways.
text_la: Decernes rem, et veniet tibi, et in viis tuis splendebit lumen.
text_pt: Determinarás tu algum negócio, e ser-te-á firme, e a luz brilhará em teus caminhos.
text_el: ἀποκαταστήσει δέ σοι δίαιταν δικαιοσύνης ἐπὶ δὲ ὁδοῖς σου ἔσται φέγγος

text_en: For he that has been humbled , shall be in glory : and he that shall bow down his eyes, he shall be saved.
text_la: Qui enim humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria, et qui inclinaverit oculos, ipse salvabitur.
text_pt: Quando te abaterem, então tu dirás: Haja exaltação! E Deus salvará ao humilde.
text_el: ὅτι ἐταπείνωσεν αὐτόν καὶ ἐρεῖς ὑπερηφανεύσατο καὶ κύφοντα ὀφθαλμοῖς σώσει

text_en: The innocent shall be saved, and he shall be saved by the cleanness of his hands.
text_la: Salvabitur innocens : salvabitur autem in munditia manuum suarum.
text_pt: E livrará até ao que não é inocente; porque será libertado pela pureza de tuas mãos.
text_el: ῥύσεται ἀθῷον καὶ διασώθητι ἐν καθαραῖς χερσίν σου

text_en: Then Job answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Job, ait:
text_pt: Respondeu, porém, Jó, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει

text_en: Now also my words are in bitterness, and the hand of my scourge is more grievous than my mourning.
text_la: Nunc quoque in amaritudine est sermo meus, et manus plagæ meæ aggravata est super gemitum meum.
text_pt: Ainda hoje a minha queixa está em amargura; a minha mão pesa sobre meu gemido.
text_el: καὶ δὴ οἶδα ὅτι ἐκ χειρός μου ἡ ἔλεγξίς ἐστιν καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ βαρεῖα γέγονεν ἐπ' ἐμῷ στεναγμῷ

text_en: Who will grant me that I might know and find him, and come even to his throne?
text_la: Quis mihi tribuat ut cognoscam et inveniam illum, et veniam usque ad solium ejus?
text_pt: Ah, se eu soubesse onde o poderia achar! Então me chegaria ao seu tribunal.
text_el: τίς δ' ἄρα γνοίη ὅτι εὕροιμι αὐτὸν καὶ ἔλθοιμι εἰς τέλος

text_en: I would set judgment before him, and would fill my mouth with complaints.
text_la: Ponam coram eo judicium, et os meum replebo increpationibus :
text_pt: Exporia ante ele a minha causa, e a minha boca encheria de argumentos.
text_el: εἴποιμι δὲ ἐμαυτοῦ κρίμα τὸ δὲ στόμα μου ἐμπλήσαιμι ἐλέγχων

text_en: That I might know the words that he would answer me, and understand what he would say to me.
text_la: ut sciam verba quæ mihi respondeat, et intelligam quid loquatur mihi.
text_pt: Saberia as palavras com que ele me responderia, e entenderia o que me dissesse.
text_el: γνῴην δὲ ῥήματα ἅ μοι ἐρεῖ αἰσθοίμην δὲ τίνα μοι ἀπαγγελεῖ

text_en: I would not that he should contend with me with much strength, nor overwhelm me with the weight of his greatness.
text_la: Nolo multa fortitudine contendat mecum, nec magnitudinis suæ mole me premat.
text_pt: Porventura segundo a grandeza de seu poder contenderia comigo? Não: ele antes me atenderia.
text_el: καὶ εἰ ἐν πολλῇ ἰσχύι ἐπελεύσεταί μοι εἶτα ἐν ἀπειλῇ μοι οὐ χρήσεται

text_en: Let him propose equity against me, and let my judgment come to victory.
text_la: Proponat æquitatem contra me, et perveniat ad victoriam judicium meum.
text_pt: Ali o reto pleitearia com ele, e eu me livraria para sempre do meu Juiz.
text_el: ἀλήθεια γὰρ καὶ ἔλεγχος παρ' αὐτοῦ ἐξαγάγοι δὲ εἰς τέλος τὸ κρίμα μου

text_en: But if I go to the east, he appears not; if to the west, I shall not understand him.
text_la: Si ad orientem iero, non apparet; si ad occidentem, non intelligam eum.
text_pt: Eis que se me adianto, ali não está; se torno para trás, não o percebo.
text_el: εἰς γὰρ πρῶτα πορεύσομαι καὶ οὐκέτι εἰμί τὰ δὲ ἐπ' ἐσχάτοις τί οἶδα

text_en: If to the left hand, what shall I do? I shall not take hold on him: if I turn myself to the right hand, I shall not see him.
text_la: Si ad sinistram, quid agam? non apprehendam eum; si me vertam ad dexteram, non videbo illum.
text_pt: Se opera à esquerda, não o vejo; se se encobre à direita, não o diviso.
text_el: ἀριστερὰ ποιήσαντος αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐ κατέσχον περιβαλεῖ δεξιά καὶ οὐκ ὄψομαι

text_en: But he knows my way, and has tried me as gold that passes through the fire:
text_la: Ipse vero scit viam meam, et probavit me quasi aurum quod per ignem transit.
text_pt: Porém ele sabe o meu caminho; provando-me ele, sairei como o ouro.
text_el: οἶδεν γὰρ ἤδη ὁδόν μου διέκρινεν δέ με ὥσπερ τὸ χρυσίον

text_en: My foot has followed his steps, I have kept his way, and have not declined from it.
text_la: Vestigia ejus secutus est pes meus : viam ejus custodivi, et non declinavi ex ea.
text_pt: Nas suas pisadas os meus pés se afirmaram; guardei o seu caminho, e não me desviei dele.
text_el: ἐξελεύσομαι δὲ ἐν ἐντάλμασιν αὐτοῦ ὁδοὺς γὰρ αὐτοῦ ἐφύλαξα καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐκκλίνω

text_en: I have not departed from the commandments of his lips, and the words of his mouth I have hid in my bosom.
text_la: A mandatis labiorum ejus non recessi, et in sinu meo abscondi verba oris ejus.
text_pt: Do preceito de seus lábios nunca me apartei, e as palavras da sua boca guardei mais do que a minha porção.
text_el: ἀπὸ ἐνταλμάτων αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐ μὴ παρέλθω ἐν δὲ κόλπῳ μου ἔκρυψα ῥήματα αὐτοῦ

text_en: For he is alone, and no man can turn away his thought: and whatsoever his soul has desired, that has he done.
text_la: Ipse enim solus est, et nemo avertere potest cogitationem ejus : et anima ejus quodcumque voluit, hoc fecit.
text_pt: Mas, se ele resolveu alguma coisa, quem então o desviará? O que a sua alma quiser, isso fará.
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς ἔκρινεν οὕτως τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἀντειπὼν αὐτῷ ὃ γὰρ αὐτὸς ἠθέλησεν καὶ ἐποίησεν

text_en: And when he shall have fulfilled his will in me, many other like things are also at hand with him.
text_la: Cum expleverit in me voluntatem suam, et alia multa similia præsto sunt ei.
text_pt: Porque cumprirá o que está ordenado a meu respeito, e muitas coisas como estas ainda tem consigo.
text_el: διὰ τοῦτο ἐπ' αὐτῷ ἐσπούδακα νουθετούμενος δὲ ἐφρόντισα αὐτοῦ

text_en: And therefore I am troubled at his presence, and when I consider him I am made pensive with fear.
text_la: Et idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor.
text_pt: Por isso me perturbo perante ele, e quando isto considero, temo-me dele.
text_el: ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ κατασπουδασθῶ κατανοήσω καὶ πτοηθήσομαι ἐξ αὐτοῦ

text_en: God has softened my heart, and the Almighty has troubled me.
text_la: Deus mollivit cor meum, et Omnipotens conturbavit me.
text_pt: Porque Deus macerou o meu coração, e o Todo-Poderoso me perturbou.
text_el: κύριος δὲ ἐμαλάκυνεν τὴν καρδίαν μου ὁ δὲ παντοκράτωρ ἐσπούδασέν με

text_en: For I have not perished because of the darkness that hangs over me, neither has the mist covered my face.
text_la: Non enim perii propter imminentes tenebras, nec faciem meam operuit caligo.
text_pt: Porquanto não fui desarraigado por causa das trevas, e nem encobriu o meu rosto com a escuridão.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ ᾔδειν ὅτι ἐπελεύσεταί μοι σκότος πρὸ προσώπου δέ μου ἐκάλυψεν γνόφος

text_en: Times are not hid from the Almighty: but they that know him, know not his days.
text_la: Ab Omnipotente non sunt abscondita tempora : qui autem noverunt eum, ignorant dies illius.
text_pt: Visto que do Todo-Poderoso não se encobriram os tempos, por que, os que o conhecem, não vêem os seus dias?
text_el: διὰ τί δὲ κύριον ἔλαθον ὧραι

text_en: Some have removed landmarks, have taken away flocks by force, and fed them.
text_la: Alii terminos transtulerunt; diripuerunt greges, et paverunt eos.
text_pt: Até os limites removem; roubam os rebanhos, e os apascentam.
text_el: ἀσεβεῖς δὲ ὅριον ὑπερέβησαν ποίμνιον σὺν ποιμένι ἁρπάσαντες

text_en: They have driven away the ass of the fatherless, and have taken away the widow's ox for a pledge.
text_la: Asinum pupillorum abegerunt, et abstulerunt pro pignore bovem viduæ.
text_pt: Do órfão levam o jumento; tomam em penhor o boi da viúva.
text_el: ὑποζύγιον ὀρφανῶν ἀπήγαγον καὶ βοῦν χήρας ἠνεχύρασαν

text_en: They have overturned the way of the poor, and have oppressed together the meek of the earth.
text_la: Subverterunt pauperum viam, et oppresserunt pariter mansuetos terræ.
text_pt: Desviam do caminho os necessitados; e os pobres da terra juntos se escondem.
text_el: ἐξέκλιναν ἀδυνάτους ἐξ ὁδοῦ δικαίας ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐκρύβησαν πραεῖς γῆς

text_en: Others like wild asses in the desert go forth to their work: by watching for a prey they get bread for their children.
text_la: Alii quasi onagri in deserto egrediuntur ad opus suum : vigilantes ad prædam, præparant panem liberis.
text_pt: Eis que, como jumentos monteses no deserto, saem à sua obra, madrugando para a presa; a campina dá mantimento a eles e aos seus filhos.
text_el: ἀπέβησαν δὲ ὥσπερ ὄνοι ἐν ἀγρῷ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ ἐξελθόντες τὴν ἑαυτῶν πρᾶξιν ἡδύνθη αὐτῷ ἄρτος εἰς νεωτέρους

text_en: They reap the field that is not their own, and gather the vintage of his vineyard whom by violence they have oppressed.
text_la: Agrum non suum demetunt, et vineam ejus, quem vi oppresserint, vindemiant.
text_pt: No campo segam o seu pasto, e vindimam a vinha do ímpio.
text_el: ἀγρὸν πρὸ ὥρας οὐκ αὐτῶν ὄντα ἐθέρισαν ἀδύνατοι δὲ ἀμπελῶνας ἀσεβῶν ἀμισθὶ καὶ ἀσιτὶ ἠργάσαντο

text_en: They send men away naked, taking away their clothes who have no covering in the cold:
text_la: Nudos dimittunt homines, indumenta tollentes, quibus non est operimentum in frigore :
text_pt: Ao nu fazem passar a noite sem roupa, não tendo ele coberta contra o frio.
text_el: γυμνοὺς πολλοὺς ἐκοίμισαν ἄνευ ἱματίων ἀμφίασιν δὲ ψυχῆς αὐτῶν ἀφείλαντο

text_en: Who are wet, with the showers of the mountains, and having no covering embrace the stones.
text_la: quos imbres montium rigant, et non habentes velamen, amplexantur lapides.
text_pt: Pelas chuvas das montanhas são molhados e, não tendo refúgio, abraçam-se com as rochas.
text_el: ἀπὸ ψεκάδων ὀρέων ὑγραίνονται παρὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν αὐτοὺς σκέπην πέτραν περιεβάλοντο

text_en: They have violently robbed the fatherless, and stripped the poor common people.
text_la: Vim fecerunt deprædantes pupillos, et vulgum pauperem spoliaverunt.
text_pt: Ao orfãozinho arrancam dos peitos, e tomam o penhor do pobre.
text_el: ἥρπασαν ὀρφανὸν ἀπὸ μαστοῦ ἐκπεπτωκότα δὲ ἐταπείνωσαν

text_en: From the naked and them that go without clothing, and from the hungry they have taken away the ears of corn.
text_la: Nudis et incedentibus absque vestitu, et esurientibus tulerunt spicas.
text_pt: Fazem com que os nus vão sem roupa e aos famintos tiram as espigas.
text_el: γυμνοὺς δὲ ἐκοίμισαν ἀδίκως πεινώντων δὲ τὸν ψωμὸν ἀφείλαντο

text_en: They have taken their rest at noon among the stores of them, who after having trodden the winepresses suffer thirst.
text_la: Inter acervos eorum meridiati sunt, qui calcatis torcularibus sitiunt.
text_pt: Dentro das suas paredes espremem o azeite; pisam os lagares, e ainda têm sede.
text_el: ἐν στενοῖς ἀδίκως ἐνήδρευσαν ὁδὸν δὲ δικαίαν οὐκ ᾔδεισαν

text_en: Out of the cities they have made men to groan, and the soul of the wounded has cried out, and God does not suffer it to pass unrevenged.
text_la: De civitatibus fecerunt viros gemere, et anima vulneratorum clamavit : et Deus inultum abire non patitur.
text_pt: Desde as cidades gemem os homens, e a alma dos feridos exclama, e contudo Deus lho não imputa como loucura.
text_el: οἳ ἐκ πόλεως καὶ οἴκων ἰδίων ἐξεβάλλοντο ψυχὴ δὲ νηπίων ἐστέναξεν μέγα αὐτὸς δὲ διὰ τί τούτων ἐπισκοπὴν οὐ πεποίηται

text_en: They have been rebellious to the light, they have not known his ways, neither have they returned by his paths.
text_la: Ipsi fuerunt rebelles lumini : nescierunt vias ejus, nec reversi sunt per semitas ejus.
text_pt: Eles estão entre os que se opõem à luz; não conhecem os seus caminhos, e não permanecem nas suas veredas.
text_el: ἐπὶ γῆς ὄντων αὐτῶν καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν ὁδὸν δὲ δικαιοσύνης οὐκ ᾔδεισαν οὐδὲ ἀτραποὺς αὐτῆς ἐπορεύθησαν

text_en: The murderer rises at the very break of day, he kills the needy, and the poor man : but in the night he will be as a thief.
text_la: Mane primo consurgit homicida; interficit egenum et pauperem : per noctem vero erit quasi fur.
text_pt: De madrugada se levanta o homicida, mata o pobre e necessitado, e de noite é como o ladrão.
text_el: γνοὺς δὲ αὐτῶν τὰ ἔργα παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς εἰς σκότος καὶ νυκτὸς ἔσται ὡς κλέπτης

text_en: The eye of the adulterer observes darkness, saying: No eye shall see me: and he will cover his face.
text_la: Oculus adulteri observat caliginem, dicens : Non me videbit oculus : et operiet vultum suum.
text_pt: Assim como o olho do adúltero aguarda o crepúsculo, dizendo: Não me verá olho nenhum; e oculta o rosto,
text_el: καὶ ὀφθαλμὸς μοιχοῦ ἐφύλαξεν σκότος λέγων οὐ προσνοήσει με ὀφθαλμός καὶ ἀποκρυβὴν προσώπου ἔθετο

text_en: He digs through houses in the dark, as in the day they had appointed for themselves, and they have not known the light.
text_la: Perfodit in tenebris domos, sicut in die condixerant sibi, et ignoraverunt lucem.
text_pt: Nas trevas minam as casas, que de dia se marcaram; não conhecem a luz.
text_el: διώρυξεν ἐν σκότει οἰκίας ἡμέρας ἐσφράγισαν ἑαυτούς οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν φῶς

text_en: If the morning suddenly appear, it is to them the shadow of death: and they walk in darkness as if it were in light.
text_la: Si subito apparuerit aurora, arbitrantur umbram mortis : et sic in tenebris quasi in luce ambulant.
text_pt: Porque a manhã para todos eles é como sombra de morte; pois, sendo conhecidos, sentem os pavores da sombra da morte.
text_el: ὅτι ὁμοθυμαδὸν τὸ πρωὶ αὐτοῖς σκιὰ θανάτου ὅτι ἐπιγνώσεται ταραχὰς σκιᾶς θανάτου

text_en: He is light upon the face of the water: cursed be his portion on the earth, let him not walk by the way of the vineyards.
text_la: Levis est super faciem aquæ : maledicta sit pars ejus in terra, nec ambulet per viam vinearum.
text_pt: É ligeiro sobre a superfície das águas; maldita é a sua parte sobre a terra; não volta pelo caminho das vinhas.
text_el: ἐλαφρός ἐστιν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ὕδατος καταραθείη ἡ μερὶς αὐτῶν ἐπὶ γῆς

text_en: Let him pass from the snow waters to excessive heat, and his sin even to hell.
text_la: Ad nimium calorem transeat ab aquis nivium, et usque ad inferos peccatum illius.
text_pt: A secura e o calor desfazem as águas da neve; assim desfará a sepultura aos que pecaram.
text_el: ἀναφανείη δὲ τὰ φυτὰ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ γῆς ξηρά ἀγκαλίδα γὰρ ὀρφανῶν ἥρπασαν

text_en: Let mercy forget him: may worms be his sweetness: let him be remembered no more, but be broken in pieces as an unfruitful tree.
text_la: Obliviscatur ejus misericordia; dulcedo illius vermes : non sit in recordatione, sed conteratur quasi lignum infructuosum.
text_pt: A madre se esquecerá dele, os vermes o comerão gostosamente; nunca mais haverá lembrança dele; e a iniqüidade se quebrará como uma árvore.
text_el: εἶτ' ἀνεμνήσθη αὐτοῦ ἡ ἁμαρτία ὥσπερ δὲ ὁμίχλη δρόσου ἀφανὴς ἐγένετο ἀποδοθείη δὲ αὐτῷ ἃ ἔπραξεν συντριβείη δὲ πᾶς ἄδικος ἴσα ξύλῳ ἀνιάτῳ

text_en: For he has fed the barren that bears not, and to the widow he has done no good .
text_la: Pavit enim sterilem quæ non parit, et viduæ bene non fecit.
text_pt: Aflige à estéril que não dá à luz, e à viúva não faz bem.
text_el: στεῖραν γὰρ οὐκ εὖ ἐποίησεν καὶ γύναιον οὐκ ἠλέησεν

text_en: He has pulled down the strong by his might: and when he stands up, he shall not trust to his life.
text_la: Detraxit fortes in fortitudine sua, et cum steterit, non credet vitæ suæ.
text_pt: Até aos poderosos arrasta com a sua força; se ele se levanta, não há vida segura.
text_el: θυμῷ δὲ κατέστρεψεν ἀδυνάτους ἀναστὰς τοιγαροῦν οὐ μὴ πιστεύσῃ κατὰ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ ζωῆς

text_en: God has given him place for penance , and he abuses it unto pride : but his eyes are upon his ways.
text_la: Dedit ei Deus locum pœnitentiæ, et ille abutitur eo in superbiam : oculi autem ejus sunt in viis illius.
text_pt: Se Deus lhes dá descanso, estribam-se nisso; seus olhos porém estão nos caminhos deles.
text_el: μαλακισθεὶς μὴ ἐλπιζέτω ὑγιασθῆναι ἀλλὰ πεσεῖται νόσῳ

text_en: They are lifted up for a little while and shall not stand, and shall be brought down as all things, and shall be taken away, and as the tops of the ears of corn they shall be broken.
text_la: Elevati sunt ad modicum, et non subsistent : et humiliabuntur sicut omnia, et auferentur, et sicut summitates spicarum conterentur.
text_pt: Por um pouco se exaltam, e logo desaparecem; são abatidos, encerrados como todos os demais; e cortados como as cabeças das espigas.
text_el: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐκάκωσεν τὸ ὕψωμα αὐτοῦ ἐμαράνθη δὲ ὥσπερ μολόχη ἐν καύματι ἢ ὥσπερ στάχυς ἀπὸ καλάμης αὐτόματος ἀποπεσών

text_en: And if it be not so, who can convince me that I have lied, and set my words before God ?
text_la: Quod si non est ita, quis me potest arguere esse mentitum, et ponere ante Deum verba mea?
text_pt: Se agora não é assim, quem me desmentirá e desfará as minhas razões?
text_el: εἰ δὲ μή τίς ἐστιν ὁ φάμενος ψευδῆ με λέγειν καὶ θήσει εἰς οὐδὲν τὰ ῥήματά μου

text_en: Then Baldad the Suhite answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Baldad Suhites, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondeu Bildade, o suíta, e disse:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Βαλδαδ ὁ Σαυχίτης λέγει

text_en: Power and terror are with him, who makes peace in his high places.
text_la: Potestas et terror apud eum est, qui facit concordiam in sublimibus suis.
text_pt: Com ele estão domínio e temor; ele faz paz nas suas alturas.
text_el: τί γὰρ προοίμιον ἢ φόβος παρ' αὐτοῦ ὁ ποιῶν τὴν σύμπασαν ἐν ὑψίστῳ

text_en: Is there any numbering of his soldiers? And upon whom shall not his light arise?
text_la: Numquid est numerus militum ejus? et super quem non surget lumen illius?
text_pt: Porventura têm número as suas tropas? E sobre quem não se levanta a sua luz?
text_el: μὴ γάρ τις ὑπολάβοι ὅτι ἔστιν παρέλκυσις πειραταῖς ἐπὶ τίνας δὲ οὐκ ἐπελεύσεται ἔνεδρα παρ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: Can man be justified compared with God, or he that is born of a woman appear clean?
text_la: Numquid justificari potest homo comparatus Deo? aut apparere mundus natus de muliere?
text_pt: Como, pois, seria justo o homem para com Deus, e como seria puro aquele que nasce de mulher?
text_el: πῶς γὰρ ἔσται δίκαιος βροτὸς ἔναντι κυρίου ἢ τίς ἂν ἀποκαθαρίσαι ἑαυτὸν γεννητὸς γυναικός

text_en: Behold even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in his sight.
text_la: Ecce luna etiam non splendet, et stellæ non sunt mundæ in conspectu ejus :
text_pt: Eis que até a lua não resplandece, e as estrelas não são puras aos seus olhos.
text_el: εἰ σελήνῃ συντάσσει καὶ οὐκ ἐπιφαύσκει ἄστρα δὲ οὐ καθαρὰ ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ

text_en: How much less man that is rottenness and the son of man who is a worm?
text_la: quanto magis homo putredo, et filius hominis vermis?
text_pt: E quanto menos o homem, que é um verme, e o filho do homem, que é um vermezinho!
text_el: ἔα δέ ἄνθρωπος σαπρία καὶ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου σκώληξ

text_en: Then Job answered, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Job dixit:
text_pt: Jó, porém, respondeu, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει

text_en: Whose helper are you? Is it of him that is weak? And do you hold up the arm of him that has no strength?
text_la: Cujus adjutor es? numquid imbecillis? et sustentas brachium ejus qui non est fortis?
text_pt: Como ajudaste aquele que não tinha força, e sustentaste o braço que não tinha vigor?
text_el: τίνι πρόσκεισαι ἢ τίνι μέλλεις βοηθεῖν πότερον οὐχ ᾧ πολλὴ ἰσχὺς καὶ ᾧ βραχίων κραταιός ἐστιν

text_en: To whom have you given counsel? Perhaps to him that has no wisdom, and you have shown your very great prudence.
text_la: Cui dedisti consilium? forsitan illi qui non habet sapientiam : et prudentiam tuam ostendisti plurimam.
text_pt: Como aconselhaste aquele que não tinha sabedoria, e plenamente fizeste saber a causa, assim como era?
text_el: τίνι συμβεβούλευσαι οὐχ ᾧ πᾶσα σοφία ἢ τίνι ἐπακολουθήσεις οὐχ ᾧ μεγίστη δύναμις

text_en: Whom have you desired to teach? Was it not him that made life?
text_la: Quem docere voluisti? nonne eum qui fecit spiramentum?
text_pt: A quem proferiste palavras, e de quem é o espírito que saiu de ti?
text_el: τίνι ἀνήγγειλας ῥήματα πνοὴ δὲ τίνος ἐστὶν ἡ ἐξελθοῦσα ἐκ σοῦ

text_en: Behold the giants groan under the waters, and they that dwell with them.
text_la: Ecce gigantes gemunt sub aquis, et qui habitant cum eis.
text_pt: Os mortos tremem debaixo das águas, com os seus moradores.
text_el: μὴ γίγαντες μαιωθήσονται ὑποκάτωθεν ὕδατος καὶ τῶν γειτόνων αὐτοῦ

text_en: Hell is naked before him, and there is no covering for destruction .
text_la: Nudus est infernus coram illo, et nullum est operimentum perditioni.
text_pt: O inferno está nu perante ele, e não há coberta para a perdição.
text_el: γυμνὸς ὁ ᾅδης ἐπώπιον αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν περιβόλαιον τῇ ἀπωλείᾳ

text_en: He stretched out the north over the empty space, and hangs the earth upon nothing.
text_la: Qui extendit aquilonem super vacuum, et appendit terram super nihilum.
text_pt: O norte estende sobre o vazio; e suspende a terra sobre o nada.
text_el: ἐκτείνων βορέαν ἐπ' οὐδέν κρεμάζων γῆν ἐπὶ οὐδενός

text_en: He binds up the waters in his clouds, so that they break not out and fall down together.
text_la: Qui ligat aquas in nubibus suis, ut non erumpant pariter deorsum.
text_pt: Prende as águas nas suas nuvens, todavia a nuvem não se rasga debaixo delas.
text_el: δεσμεύων ὕδωρ ἐν νεφέλαις αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐρράγη νέφος ὑποκάτω αὐτοῦ

text_en: He withholds the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud over it.
text_la: Qui tenet vultum solii sui, et expandit super illud nebulam suam.
text_pt: Encobre a face do seu trono, e sobre ele estende a sua nuvem.
text_el: ὁ κρατῶν πρόσωπον θρόνου ἐκπετάζων ἐπ' αὐτὸν νέφος αὐτοῦ

text_en: He has set bounds about the waters, till light and darkness come to an end.
text_la: Terminum circumdedit aquis, usque dum finiantur lux et tenebræ.
text_pt: Marcou um limite sobre a superfície das águas em redor, até aos confins da luz e das trevas.
text_el: πρόσταγμα ἐγύρωσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ὕδατος μέχρι συντελείας φωτὸς μετὰ σκότους

text_en: The pillars of heaven tremble, and dread at his beck.
text_la: Columnæ cæli contremiscunt, et pavent ad nutum ejus.
text_pt: As colunas do céu tremem, e se espantam da sua ameaça.
text_el: στῦλοι οὐρανοῦ ἐπετάσθησαν καὶ ἐξέστησαν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐπιτιμήσεως αὐτοῦ

text_en: By his power the seas are suddenly gathered together, and his wisdom has struck the proud one.
text_la: In fortitudine illius repente maria congregata sunt, et prudentia ejus percussit superbum.
text_pt: Com a sua força fende o mar, e com o seu entendimento abate a soberba.
text_el: ἰσχύι κατέπαυσεν τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπιστήμῃ δὲ ἔτρωσε τὸ κῆτος

text_en: His spirit has adorned the heavens , and his obstetric hand brought forth the winding serpent .
text_la: Spiritus ejus ornavit cælos, et obstetricante manu ejus, eductus est coluber tortuosus.
text_pt: Pelo seu Espírito ornou os céus; a sua mão formou a serpente enroscadiça.
text_el: κλεῖθρα δὲ οὐρανοῦ δεδοίκασιν αὐτόν προστάγματι δὲ ἐθανάτωσεν δράκοντα ἀποστάτην

text_en: Lo, these things are said in part of his ways: and seeing we have heard scarce a little drop of his word, who shall be able to behold the thunder of his greatness?
text_la: Ecce hæc ex parte dicta sunt viarum ejus : et cum vix parvam stillam sermonis ejus audierimus, quis poterit tonitruum magnitudinis illius intueri?
text_pt: Eis que isto são apenas as orlas dos seus caminhos; e quão pouco é o que temos ouvido dele! Quem, pois, entenderia o trovão do seu poder?
text_el: ἰδοὺ ταῦτα μέρη ὁδοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ ἰκμάδα λόγου ἀκουσόμεθα ἐν αὐτῷ σθένος δὲ βροντῆς αὐτοῦ τίς οἶδεν ὁπότε ποιήσει

text_en: Job also added, taking up his parable , and said:
text_la: Addidit quoque Job, assumens parabolam suam, et dixit:
text_pt: E prosseguindo Jó em seu discurso, disse:
text_el: ἔτι δὲ προσθεὶς Ιωβ εἶπεν τῷ προοιμίῳ

text_en: As God lives, who has taken away my judgment, and the Almighty, who has brought my soul to bitterness,
text_la: Vivit Deus, qui abstulit judicium meum, et Omnipotens, qui ad amaritudinem adduxit animam meam.
text_pt: Vive Deus, que desviou a minha causa, e o Todo-Poderoso, que amargurou a minha alma.
text_el: ζῇ κύριος ὃς οὕτω με κέκρικεν καὶ ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὁ πικράνας μου τὴν ψυχήν

text_en: as long as breath remains in me, and the spirit of God in my nostrils,
text_la: Quia donec superest halitus in me, et spiritus Dei in naribus meis,
text_pt: Que, enquanto em mim houver alento, e o sopro de Deus nas minhas narinas,
text_el: ἦ μὴν ἔτι τῆς πνοῆς μου ἐνούσης πνεῦμα δὲ θεῖον τὸ περιόν μοι ἐν ῥισίν

text_en: my lips shall not speak iniquity , neither shall my tongue contrive lying.
text_la: non loquentur labia mea iniquitatem, nec lingua mea meditabitur mendacium.
text_pt: Não falarão os meus lábios iniqüidade, nem a minha língua pronunciará engano.
text_el: μὴ λαλήσειν τὰ χείλη μου ἄνομα οὐδὲ ἡ ψυχή μου μελετήσει ἄδικα

text_en: God forbid that I should judge you to be just : till I die I will not depart from my innocence.
text_la: Absit a me ut justos vos esse judicem : donec deficiam, non recedam ab innocentia mea.
text_pt: Longe de mim que eu vos justifique; até que eu expire, nunca apartarei de mim a minha integridade.
text_el: μή μοι εἴη δικαίους ὑμᾶς ἀποφῆναι ἕως ἂν ἀποθάνω οὐ γὰρ ἀπαλλάξω μου τὴν ἀκακίαν

text_en: My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake: for my heart does not reprehend me in all my life.
text_la: Justificationem meam, quam cœpi tenere, non deseram : neque enim reprehendit me cor meum in omni vita mea.
text_pt: À minha justiça me apegarei e não a largarei; não me reprovará o meu coração em toda a minha vida.
text_el: δικαιοσύνῃ δὲ προσέχων οὐ μὴ προῶμαι οὐ γὰρ σύνοιδα ἐμαυτῷ ἄτοπα πράξας

text_en: Let my enemy be as the ungodly, and my adversary as the wicked one .
text_la: Sit ut impius, inimicus meus, et adversarius meus quasi iniquus.
text_pt: Seja como o ímpio o meu inimigo, e como o perverso o que se levantar contra mim.
text_el: οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ εἴησαν οἱ ἐχθροί μου ὥσπερ ἡ καταστροφὴ τῶν ἀσεβῶν καὶ οἱ ἐπ' ἐμὲ ἐπανιστανόμενοι ὥσπερ ἡ ἀπώλεια τῶν παρανόμων

text_en: For what is the hope of the hypocrite if through covetousness he take by violence , and God deliver not his soul ?
text_la: Quæ est enim spes hypocritæ, si avare rapiat, et non liberet Deus animam ejus?
text_pt: Porque qual será a esperança do hipócrita, havendo sido avaro, quando Deus lhe arrancar a sua alma?
text_el: καὶ τίς γάρ ἐστιν ἐλπὶς ἀσεβεῖ ὅτι ἐπέχει πεποιθὼς ἐπὶ κύριον ἆρα σωθήσεται

text_en: Will God hear his cry, when distress shall come upon him?
text_la: Numquid Deus audiet clamorem ejus, cum venerit super eum angustia?
text_pt: Porventura Deus ouvirá o seu clamor, sobrevindo-lhe a tribulação?
text_el: ἦ τὴν δέησιν αὐτοῦ εἰσακούσεται κύριος ἢ ἐπελθούσης αὐτῷ ἀνάγκης

text_en: Or can he delight himself in the Almighty , and call upon God at all times?
text_la: aut poterit in Omnipotente delectari, et invocare Deum omni tempore?
text_pt: Deleitar-se-á no TodoPoderoso, ou invocará a Deus em todo o tempo?
text_el: μὴ ἔχει τινὰ παρρησίαν ἔναντι αὐτοῦ ἢ ὡς ἐπικαλεσαμένου αὐτοῦ εἰσακούσεται αὐτοῦ

text_en: I will teach you by the hand of God , what the Almighty has, and I will not conceal it.
text_la: Docebo vos per manum Dei quæ Omnipotens habeat, nec abscondam.
text_pt: Ensinar-vos-ei acerca da mão de Deus, e não vos encobrirei o que está com o Todo-Poderoso.
text_el: ἀλλὰ δὴ ἀναγγελῶ ὑμῖν τί ἐστιν ἐν χειρὶ κυρίου ἅ ἐστιν παρὰ παντοκράτορι οὐ ψεύσομαι

text_en: Behold you all know it, and why do you speak vain things without cause?
text_la: Ecce vos omnes nostis : et quid sine causa vana loquimini?
text_pt: Eis que todos vós já o vistes; por que, pois, vos desvaneceis na vossa vaidade?
text_el: ἰδοὺ δὴ πάντες οἴδατε ὅτι κενὰ κενοῖς ἐπιβάλλετε

text_en: This is the portion of a wicked man with God , and the inheritance of the violent , which they shall receive of the Almighty.
text_la: Hæc est pars hominis impii apud Deum, et hæreditas violentorum, quam ob Omnipotente suscipient.
text_pt: Esta, pois, é a porção do homem ímpio da parte de Deus, e a herança, que os tiranos receberão do Todo-Poderoso.
text_el: αὕτη ἡ μερὶς ἀνθρώπου ἀσεβοῦς παρὰ κυρίου κτῆμα δὲ δυναστῶν ἐλεύσεται παρὰ παντοκράτορος ἐπ' αὐτούς

text_en: If his sons be multiplied, they shall be for the sword, and his grandsons shall not be filled with bread.
text_la: Si multiplicati fuerint filii ejus, in gladio erunt, et nepotes ejus non saturabuntur pane :
text_pt: Se os seus filhos se multiplicarem, será para a espada, e a sua prole não se fartará de pão.
text_el: ἐὰν δὲ πολλοὶ γένωνται οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς σφαγὴν ἔσονται ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἀνδρωθῶσιν προσαιτήσουσιν

text_en: They that shall remain of him, shall be buried in death, and his widows shall not weep.
text_la: qui reliqui fuerint ex eo sepelientur in interitu, et viduæ illius non plorabunt.
text_pt: Os que ficarem dele na morte serão enterrados, e as suas viúvas não chorarão.
text_el: οἱ δὲ περιόντες αὐτοῦ ἐν θανάτῳ τελευτήσουσιν χήρας δὲ αὐτῶν οὐθεὶς ἐλεήσει

text_en: If he shall heap together silver as earth, and prepare raiment as clay,
text_la: Si comportaverit quasi terram argentum, et sicut lutum præparaverit vestimenta :
text_pt: Se amontoar prata como pó, e aparelhar roupas como lodo,
text_el: ἐὰν συναγάγῃ ὥσπερ γῆν ἀργύριον ἴσα δὲ πηλῷ ἑτοιμάσῃ χρυσίον

text_en: he shall prepare indeed, but the just man shall be clothed with it: and the innocent shall divide the silver.
text_la: præparabit quidem, sed justus vestietur illis, et argentum innocens dividet.
text_pt: Ele as aparelhará, porém o justo as vestirá, e o inocente repartirá a prata.
text_el: ταῦτα πάντα δίκαιοι περιποιήσονται τὰ δὲ χρήματα αὐτοῦ ἀληθινοὶ καθέξουσιν

text_en: He has built his house as a moth, and as a keeper he has made a booth.
text_la: Ædificavit sicut tinea domum suam, et sicut custos fecit umbraculum.
text_pt: E edificará a sua casa como a traça, e como o guarda que faz a cabana.
text_el: ἀπέβη δὲ ὁ οἶκος αὐτοῦ ὥσπερ σῆτες καὶ ὥσπερ ἀράχνη

text_en: The rich man when he shall sleep shall take away nothing with him: he shall open his eyes and find nothing.
text_la: Dives, cum dormierit, nihil secum auferet : aperiet oculos suos, et nihil inveniet.
text_pt: Rico se deita, e não será recolhido; abre os seus olhos, e nada terá.
text_el: πλούσιος κοιμηθεὶς καὶ οὐ προσθήσει ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ διήνοιξεν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν

text_en: Poverty like water shall take hold on him, a tempest shall oppress him in the night:
text_la: Apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia : nocte opprimet eum tempestas.
text_pt: Pavores se apoderam dele como águas; de noite o arrebata a tempestade.
text_el: συνήντησαν αὐτῷ ὥσπερ ὕδωρ αἱ ὀδύναι νυκτὶ δὲ ὑφείλατο αὐτὸν γνόφος

text_en: A burning wind shall take him up, and carry him away, and as a whirlwind shall snatch him from his place.
text_la: Tollet eum ventus urens, et auferet, et velut turbo rapiet eum de loco suo.
text_pt: O vento oriental leva-o, e ele se vai, e varre-o com ímpeto do seu lugar.
text_el: ἀναλήμψεται αὐτὸν καύσων καὶ ἀπελεύσεται καὶ λικμήσει αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτοῦ

text_en: And he shall cast upon him, and shall not spare: out of his hand he would willingly flee.
text_la: Et mittet super eum, et non parcet : de manu ejus fugiens fugiet.
text_pt: E Deus lançará isto sobre ele, e não lhe poupará; irá fugindo da sua mão.
text_el: καὶ ἐπιρρίψει ἐπ' αὐτὸν καὶ οὐ φείσεται ἐκ χειρὸς αὐτοῦ φυγῇ φεύξεται

text_en: He shall clasp his hands upon him, and shall hiss at him, beholding his place.
text_la: Stringet super eum manus suas, et sibilabit super illum, intuens locum ejus.
text_pt: Cada um baterá palmas contra ele e assobiará tirando-o do seu lugar.
text_el: κροτήσει ἐπ' αὐτοῦ χεῖρας αὐτοῦ καὶ συριεῖ αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτοῦ

text_en: Silver has beginnings of its veins, and gold has a place wherein it is melted.
text_la: Habet argentum venarum suarum principia, et auro locus est in quo conflatur.
text_pt: Na verdade, há veios de onde se extrai a prata, e lugar onde se refina o ouro.
text_el: ἔστιν γὰρ ἀργυρίῳ τόπος ὅθεν γίνεται τόπος δὲ χρυσίῳ ὅθεν διηθεῖται

text_en: Iron is taken out of the earth, and stone melted with heat is turned into brass.
text_la: Ferrum de terra tollitur, et lapis solutus calore in æs vertitur.
text_pt: O ferro tira-se da terra, e da pedra se funde o cobre.
text_el: σίδηρος μὲν γὰρ ἐκ γῆς γίνεται χαλκὸς δὲ ἴσα λίθῳ λατομεῖται

text_en: He has set a time for darkness, and the end of all things he considers, the stone also that is in the dark and the shadow of death.
text_la: Tempus posuit tenebris, et universorum finem ipse considerat : lapidem quoque caliginis et umbram mortis.
text_pt: Ele põe fim às trevas, e toda a extremidade ele esquadrinha, a pedra da escuridão e a da sombra da morte.
text_el: τάξιν ἔθετο σκότει καὶ πᾶν πέρας αὐτὸς ἐξακριβάζεται λίθος σκοτία καὶ σκιὰ θανάτου

text_en: The flood divides from the people that are on their journey, those whom the food of the needy man has forgotten, and who cannot be come at.
text_la: Dividit torrens a populo peregrinante eos quos oblitus est pes egentis hominis, et invios.
text_pt: Abre um poço de mina longe dos homens, em lugares esquecidos do pé; ficando pendentes longe dos homens, oscilam de um lado para outro.
text_el: διακοπὴ χειμάρρου ἀπὸ κονίας οἱ δὲ ἐπιλανθανόμενοι ὁδὸν δικαίαν ἠσθένησαν ἐκ βροτῶν

text_en: The land, out of which bread grew in its place, has been overturned with fire.
text_la: Terra de qua oriebatur panis, in loco suo igni subversa est.
text_pt: Da terra procede o pão, mas por baixo é revolvida como por fogo.
text_el: γῆ ἐξ αὐτῆς ἐξελεύσεται ἄρτος ὑποκάτω αὐτῆς ἐστράφη ὡσεὶ πῦρ

text_en: The stones of it are the place of sapphires, and the clods of it are gold.
text_la: Locus sapphiri lapides ejus, et glebæ illius aurum.
text_pt: As suas pedras são o lugar da safira, e tem pó de ouro.
text_el: τόπος σαπφείρου οἱ λίθοι αὐτῆς καὶ χῶμα χρυσίον αὐτῷ

text_en: The bird has not known the path, neither has the eye of the vulture beheld it.
text_la: Semitam ignoravit avis, nec intuitus est eam oculus vulturis.
text_pt: Essa vereda a ave de rapina a ignora, e não a viram os olhos da gralha.
text_el: τρίβος οὐκ ἔγνω αὐτὴν πετεινόν καὶ οὐ παρέβλεψεν αὐτὴν ὀφθαλμὸς γυπός

text_en: The children of the merchants have not trodden it, neither has the lioness passed by it.
text_la: Non calcaverunt eam filii institorum, nec pertransivit per eam leæna.
text_pt: Nunca a pisaram filhos de animais altivos, nem o feroz leão passou por ela.
text_el: οὐκ ἐπάτησαν αὐτὴν υἱοὶ ἀλαζόνων οὐ παρῆλθεν ἐπ' αὐτῆς λέων

text_en: He has stretched forth his hand to the flint, he has overturned mountains from the roots.
text_la: Ad silicem extendit manum suam : subvertit a radicibus montes.
text_pt: Ele estende a sua mão contra o rochedo, e revolve os montes desde as suas raízes.
text_el: ἐν ἀκροτόμῳ ἐξέτεινεν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ κατέστρεψεν δὲ ἐκ ῥιζῶν ὄρη

text_en: In the rocks he has cut out rivers, and his eye has seen every precious thing.
text_la: In petris rivos excidit, et omne pretiosum vidit oculus ejus.
text_pt: Dos rochedos faz sair rios, e o seu olho vê tudo o que há de precioso.
text_el: δίνας δὲ ποταμῶν ἔρρηξεν πᾶν δὲ ἔντιμον εἶδέν μου ὁ ὀφθαλμός

text_en: The depths also of rivers he has searched, and hidden things he has brought forth to light.
text_la: Profunda quoque fluviorum scrutatus est, et abscondita in lucem produxit.
text_pt: Os rios tapa, e nem uma gota sai deles, e tira à luz o que estava escondido.
text_el: βάθη δὲ ποταμῶν ἀνεκάλυψεν ἔδειξεν δὲ ἑαυτοῦ δύναμιν εἰς φῶς

text_en: But where is wisdom to be found, and where is the place of understanding?
text_la: Sapientia vero ubi invenitur? et quis est locus intelligentiæ?
text_pt: Porém onde se achará a sabedoria, e onde está o lugar da inteligência?
text_el: ἡ δὲ σοφία πόθεν εὑρέθη ποῖος δὲ τόπος ἐστὶν τῆς ἐπιστήμης

text_en: Man knows not the price thereof, neither is it found in the land of them that live in delights.
text_la: Nescit homo pretium ejus, nec invenitur in terra suaviter viventium.
text_pt: O homem não conhece o seu valor, e nem ela se acha na terra dos viventes.
text_el: οὐκ οἶδεν βροτὸς ὁδὸν αὐτῆς οὐδὲ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἐν ἀνθρώποις

text_en: The depth says: It is not in me: and the sea says: It is not with me.
text_la: Abyssus dicit : Non est in me, et mare loquitur : Non est mecum.
text_pt: O abismo diz: Não está em mim; e o mar diz: Ela não está comigo.
text_el: ἄβυσσος εἶπεν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἐμοί καὶ θάλασσα εἶπεν οὐκ ἔστιν μετ' ἐμοῦ

text_en: The finest gold shall not purchase it, neither shall silver be weighed in exchange for it.
text_la: Non dabitur aurum obrizum pro ea, nec appendetur argentum in commutatione ejus.
text_pt: Não se dará por ela ouro fino, nem se pesará prata em troca dela.
text_el: οὐ δώσει συγκλεισμὸν ἀντ' αὐτῆς καὶ οὐ σταθήσεται ἀργύριον ἀντάλλαγμα αὐτῆς

text_en: It shall not be compared with the dyed colours of India, or with the most precious stone sardonyx, or the sapphire.
text_la: Non conferetur tinctis Indiæ coloribus, nec lapidi sardonycho pretiosissimo vel sapphiro.
text_pt: Nem se pode comprar por ouro fino de Ofir, nem pelo precioso ônix, nem pela safira.
text_el: καὶ οὐ συμβασταχθήσεται χρυσίῳ Ωφιρ ἐν ὄνυχι τιμίῳ καὶ σαπφείρῳ

text_en: Gold or crystal cannot equal it, neither shall any vessels of gold be changed for it.
text_la: Non adæquabitur ei aurum vel vitrum, nec commutabuntur pro ea vasa auri.
text_pt: Com ela não se pode comparar o ouro nem o cristal; nem se trocará por jóia de ouro fino.
text_el: οὐκ ἰσωθήσεται αὐτῇ χρυσίον καὶ ὕαλος καὶ τὸ ἄλλαγμα αὐτῆς σκεύη χρυσᾶ

text_en: High and eminent things shall not be mentioned in comparison of it: but wisdom is drawn out of secret places.
text_la: Excelsa et eminentia non memorabuntur comparatione ejus : trahitur autem sapientia de occultis.
text_pt: Não se fará menção de coral nem de pérolas; porque o valor da sabedoria é melhor que o dos rubis.
text_el: μετέωρα καὶ γαβις οὐ μνησθήσεται καὶ ἕλκυσον σοφίαν ὑπὲρ τὰ ἐσώτατα

text_en: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not be equal to it, neither shall it be compared to the cleanest dyeing.
text_la: Non adæquabitur ei topazius de Æthiopia, nec tincturæ mundissimæ componetur.
text_pt: Não se lhe igualará o topázio da Etiópia, nem se pode avaliar por ouro puro.
text_el: οὐκ ἰσωθήσεται αὐτῇ τοπάζιον Αἰθιοπίας χρυσίῳ καθαρῷ οὐ συμβασταχθήσεται

text_en: Whence then comes wisdom? And where is the place of understanding?
text_la: Unde ergo sapientia venit? et quis est locus intelligentiæ?
text_pt: Donde, pois, vem a sabedoria, e onde está o lugar da inteligência?
text_el: ἡ δὲ σοφία πόθεν εὑρέθη ποῖος δὲ τόπος ἐστὶν τῆς συνέσεως

text_en: It is hid from the eyes of all living, and the fowls of the air know it not.
text_la: Abscondita est ab oculis omnium viventium : volucres quoque cæli latet.
text_pt: Pois está encoberta aos olhos de todo o vivente, e oculta às aves do céu.
text_el: λέληθεν πάντα ἄνθρωπον καὶ ἀπὸ πετεινῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐκρύβη

text_en: Destruction and death have said: With our ears we have heard the fame thereof.
text_la: Perditio et mors dixerunt : Auribus nostris audivimus famam ejus.
text_pt: A perdição e a morte dizem: Ouvimos com os nossos ouvidos a sua fama.
text_el: ἡ ἀπώλεια καὶ ὁ θάνατος εἶπαν ἀκηκόαμεν δὲ αὐτῆς τὸ κλέος

text_en: God understands the way of it, and he knows the place thereof.
text_la: Deus intelligit viam ejus, et ipse novit locum illius.
