text_pt: Deus entende o seu caminho, e ele sabe o seu lugar.
text_el: ὁ θεὸς εὖ συνέστησεν αὐτῆς τὴν ὁδόν αὐτὸς δὲ οἶδεν τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς

text_en: For he beholds the ends of the world: and looks on all things that are under heaven .
text_la: Ipse enim fines mundi intuetur, et omnia quæ sub cælo sunt respicit.
text_pt: Porque ele vê as extremidades da terra; e vê tudo o que há debaixo dos céus.
text_el: αὐτὸς γὰρ τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανὸν πᾶσαν ἐφορᾷ εἰδὼς τὰ ἐν τῇ γῇ πάντα ἃ ἐποίησεν

text_en: Who made a weight for the winds, and weighed the waters by measure.
text_la: Qui fecit ventis pondus, et aquas appendit in mensura.
text_pt: Quando deu peso ao vento, e tomou a medida das águas;
text_el: ἀνέμων σταθμὸν ὕδατός τε μέτρα

text_en: When he gave a law for the rain, and a way for the sounding storms.
text_la: Quando ponebat pluviis legem, et viam procellis sonantibus :
text_pt: Quando prescreveu leis para a chuva e caminho para o relâmpago dos trovões;
text_el: ὅτε ἐποίησεν οὕτως ὑετὸν ἠρίθμησεν καὶ ὁδὸν ἐν τινάγματι φωνάς

text_en: Then he saw it, and declared, and prepared, and searched it.
text_la: tunc vidit illam et enarravit, et præparavit, et investigavit.
text_pt: Então a viu e relatou; estabeleceu-a, e também a esquadrinhou.
text_el: τότε εἶδεν αὐτὴν καὶ ἐξηγήσατο αὐτήν ἑτοιμάσας ἐξιχνίασεν

text_en: And he said to man : Behold the fear of the Lord , that is wisdom: and to depart from evil , is understanding.
text_la: Et dixit homini : Ecce timor Domini, ipsa est sapientia; et recedere a malo, intelligentia.
text_pt: E disse ao homem: Eis que o temor do Senhor é a sabedoria, e apartar-se do mal é a inteligência.
text_el: εἶπεν δὲ ἀνθρώπῳ ἰδοὺ ἡ θεοσέβειά ἐστιν σοφία τὸ δὲ ἀπέχεσθαι ἀπὸ κακῶν ἐστιν ἐπιστήμη

text_en: Job also added, taking up his parable , and said:
text_la: Addidit quoque Job, assumens parabolam suam, et dixit:
text_pt: E prosseguiu Jó no seu discurso, dizendo:
text_el: ἔτι δὲ προσθεὶς Ιωβ εἶπεν τῷ προοιμίῳ

text_en: Who will grant me, that I might be according to the months past, according to the days in which God kept me?
text_la: Quis mihi tribuat ut sim juxta menses pristinos, secundum dies quibus Deus custodiebat me?
text_pt: Ah! quem me dera ser como eu fui nos meses passados, como nos dias em que Deus me guardava!
text_el: τίς ἄν με θείη κατὰ μῆνα ἔμπροσθεν ἡμερῶν ὧν με ὁ θεὸς ἐφύλαξεν

text_en: When his lamp shined over my head, and I walked by his light in darkness?
text_la: Quando splendebat lucerna ejus super caput meum, et ad lumen ejus ambulabam in tenebris :
text_pt: Quando fazia resplandecer a sua lâmpada sobre a minha cabeça e quando eu pela sua luz caminhava pelas trevas.
text_el: ὡς ὅτε ηὔγει ὁ λύχνος αὐτοῦ ὑπὲρ κεφαλῆς μου ὅτε τῷ φωτὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπορευόμην ἐν σκότει

text_en: As I was in the days of my youth, when God was secretly in my tabernacle?
text_la: sicut fui in diebus adolescentiæ meæ, quando secreto Deus erat in tabernaculo meo :
text_pt: Como fui nos dias da minha mocidade, quando o segredo de Deus estava sobre a minha tenda;
text_el: ὅτε ἤμην ἐπιβρίθων ὁδοῖς ὅτε ὁ θεὸς ἐπισκοπὴν ἐποιεῖτο τοῦ οἴκου μου

text_en: When the Almighty was with me: and my servants round about me?
text_la: quando erat Omnipotens mecum, et in circuitu meo pueri mei :
text_pt: Quando o Todo-Poderoso ainda estava comigo, e os meus filhos em redor de mim.
text_el: ὅτε ἤμην ὑλώδης λίαν κύκλῳ δέ μου οἱ παῖδες

text_en: When I washed my feet with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil?
text_la: quando lavabam pedes meos butyro, et petra fundebat mihi rivos olei :
text_pt: Quando lavava os meus passos na manteiga, e da rocha me corriam ribeiros de azeite;
text_el: ὅτε ἐχέοντό μου αἱ ὁδοὶ βουτύρῳ τὰ δὲ ὄρη μου ἐχέοντο γάλακτι

text_en: When I went out to the gate of the city, and in the street they prepared me a chair?
text_la: quando procedebam ad portam civitatis, et in platea parabant cathedram mihi.
text_pt: Quando eu saía para a porta da cidade, e na rua fazia preparar a minha cadeira,
text_el: ὅτε ἐξεπορευόμην ὄρθριος ἐν πόλει ἐν δὲ πλατείαις ἐτίθετό μου ὁ δίφρος

text_en: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the old men rose up and stood.
text_la: Videbant me juvenes, et abscondebantur : et senes assurgentes stabant.
text_pt: Os moços me viam, e se escondiam, e até os idosos se levantavam e se punham em pé;
text_el: ἰδόντες με νεανίσκοι ἐκρύβησαν πρεσβῦται δὲ πάντες ἔστησαν

text_en: The princes ceased to speak, and laid the finger on their mouth.
text_la: Principes cessabant loqui, et digitum superponebant ori suo.
text_pt: Os príncipes continham as suas palavras, e punham a mão sobre a sua boca;
text_el: ἁδροὶ δὲ ἐπαύσαντο λαλοῦντες δάκτυλον ἐπιθέντες ἐπὶ στόματι

text_en: The rulers held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to their throat.
text_la: Vocem suam cohibebant duces, et lingua eorum gutturi suo adhærebat.
text_pt: A voz dos nobres se calava, e a sua língua apegava-se ao seu paladar.
text_el: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐμακάρισάν με καὶ γλῶσσα αὐτῶν τῷ λάρυγγι αὐτῶν ἐκολλήθη

text_en: The ear that heard me blessed me, and the eye that saw me gave witness to me:
text_la: Auris audiens beatificabat me, et oculus videns testimonium reddebat mihi :
text_pt: Ouvindo-me algum ouvido, me tinha por bem-aventurado; vendo-me algum olho, dava testemunho de mim;
text_el: ὅτι οὖς ἤκουσεν καὶ ἐμακάρισέν με ὀφθαλμὸς δὲ ἰδών με ἐξέκλινεν

text_en: Because I had delivered the poor man that cried out; and the fatherless, that had no helper.
text_la: eo quod liberassem pauperem vociferantem, et pupillum cui non esset adjutor.
text_pt: Porque eu livrava o miserável, que clamava, como também o órfão que não tinha quem o socorresse.
text_el: διέσωσα γὰρ πτωχὸν ἐκ χειρὸς δυνάστου καὶ ὀρφανῷ ᾧ οὐκ ἦν βοηθός ἐβοήθησα

text_en: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me, and I comforted the heart of the widow.
text_la: Benedictio perituri super me veniebat, et cor viduæ consolatus sum.
text_pt: A bênção do que ia perecendo vinha sobre mim, e eu fazia que rejubilasse o coração da viúva.
text_el: εὐλογία ἀπολλυμένου ἐπ' ἐμὲ ἔλθοι στόμα δὲ χήρας με εὐλόγησεν

text_en: I was clad with justice : and I clothed myself with my judgment, as with a robe and a diadem.
text_la: Justitia indutus sum, et vestivi me, sicut vestimento et diademate, judicio meo.
text_pt: Vestia-me da justiça, e ela me servia de vestimenta; como manto e diadema era a minha justiça.
text_el: δικαιοσύνην δὲ ἐνεδεδύκειν ἠμφιασάμην δὲ κρίμα ἴσα διπλοΐδι

text_en: I was an eye to the blind, and a foot to the lame.
text_la: Oculus fui cæco, et pes claudo.
text_pt: Eu me fazia de olhos para o cego, e de pés para o coxo.
text_el: ὀφθαλμὸς ἤμην τυφλῶν ποὺς δὲ χωλῶν

text_en: I was the father of the poor: and the cause which I knew not, I searched out most diligently.
text_la: Pater eram pauperum, et causam quam nesciebam diligentissime investigabam.
text_pt: Dos necessitados era pai, e as causas de que eu não tinha conhecimento inquiria com diligência.
text_el: ἐγὼ ἤμην πατὴρ ἀδυνάτων δίκην δέ ἣν οὐκ ᾔδειν ἐξιχνίασα

text_en: I broke the jaws of the wicked man , and out of his teeth I took away the prey.
text_la: Conterebam molas iniqui, et de dentibus illius auferebam prædam.
text_pt: E quebrava os queixos do perverso, e dos seus dentes tirava a presa.
text_el: συνέτριψα δὲ μύλας ἀδίκων ἐκ δὲ μέσου τῶν ὀδόντων αὐτῶν ἅρπαγμα ἐξέσπασα

text_en: And I said: I shall die in my nest, and as a palm tree shall multiply my days.
text_la: Dicebamque : In nidulo meo moriar, et sicut palma multiplicabo dies.
text_pt: E dizia: No meu ninho expirarei, e multiplicarei os meus dias como a areia.
text_el: εἶπα δέ ἡ ἡλικία μου γηράσει ὥσπερ στέλεχος φοίνικος πολὺν χρόνον βιώσω

text_en: My root is opened beside the waters, and dew shall continue in my harvest.
text_la: Radix mea aperta est secus aquas, et ros morabitur in messione mea.
text_pt: A minha raiz se estendia junto às águas, e o orvalho permanecia sobre os meus ramos;
text_el: ἡ ῥίζα μου διήνοικται ἐπὶ ὕδατος καὶ δρόσος αὐλισθήσεται ἐν τῷ θερισμῷ μου

text_en: My glory shall always be renewed, and my bow in my hand shall be repaired.
text_la: Gloria mea semper innovabitur, et arcus meus in manu mea instaurabitur.
text_pt: A minha honra se renovava em mim, e o meu arco se reforçava na minha mão.
text_el: ἡ δόξα μου καινὴ μετ' ἐμοῦ καὶ τὸ τόξον μου ἐν χειρὶ αὐτοῦ πορεύσεται

text_en: They that heard me, waited for my sentence, and being attentive held their peace at my counsel.
text_la: Qui me audiebant, expectabant sententiam, et intenti tacebant ad consilium meum.
text_pt: Ouviam-me e esperavam, e em silêncio atendiam ao meu conselho.
text_el: ἐμοῦ ἀκούσαντες προσέσχον ἐσιώπησαν δὲ ἐπὶ τῇ ἐμῇ βουλῇ

text_en: To my words they dared add nothing, and my speech dropped upon them.
text_la: Verbis meis addere nihil audebant, et super illos stillabat eloquium meum.
text_pt: Havendo eu falado, não replicavam, e minhas razões destilavam sobre eles;
text_el: ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ἐμῷ ῥήματι οὐ προσέθεντο περιχαρεῖς δὲ ἐγίνοντο ὁπόταν αὐτοῖς ἐλάλουν

text_en: They waited for me as for rain, and they opened their mouth as for a latter shower.
text_la: Expectabant me sicut pluviam, et os suum aperiebant quasi ad imbrem serotinum.
text_pt: Porque me esperavam, como à chuva; e abriam a sua boca, como à chuva tardia.
text_el: ὥσπερ γῆ διψῶσα προσδεχομένη τὸν ὑετόν οὕτως οὗτοι τὴν ἐμὴν λαλιάν

text_en: If at any time I laughed on them, they believed not, and the light of my countenance fell not on earth.
text_la: Siquando ridebam ad eos, non credebant : et lux vultus mei non cadebat in terram.
text_pt: Se eu ria para eles, não o criam, e a luz do meu rosto não faziam abater;
text_el: ἐὰν γελάσω πρὸς αὐτούς οὐ μὴ πιστεύσωσιν καὶ φῶς τοῦ προσώπου μου οὐκ ἀπέπιπτεν

text_en: If I had a mind to go to them, I sat first, and when I sat as a king, with his army standing about him, yet I was a comforter of them that mourned.
text_la: Si voluissem ire ad eos, sedebam primus : cumque sederem quasi rex, circumstante exercitu, eram tamen mœrentium consolator.
text_pt: Eu escolhia o seu caminho, assentava-me como chefe, e habitava como rei entre as suas tropas; como aquele que consola os que pranteiam.
text_el: ἐξελεξάμην ὁδὸν αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκάθισα ἄρχων καὶ κατεσκήνουν ὡσεὶ βασιλεὺς ἐν μονοζώνοις ὃν τρόπον παθεινοὺς παρακαλῶν

text_en: But now the younger in time scorn me, whose fathers I would not have set with the dogs of my flock:
text_la: Nunc autem derident me juniores tempore, quorum non dignabar patres ponere cum canibus gregis mei :
text_pt: Agora, porém, se riem de mim os de menos idade do que eu, cujos pais eu teria desdenhado de pôr com os cães do meu rebanho.
text_el: νυνὶ δὲ κατεγέλασάν μου ἐλάχιστοι νῦν νουθετοῦσίν με ἐν μέρει ὧν ἐξουδένουν πατέρας αὐτῶν οὓς οὐχ ἡγησάμην εἶναι ἀξίους κυνῶν τῶν ἐμῶν νομάδων

text_en: The strength of whose hands was to me as nothing, and they were thought unworthy of life itself.
text_la: quorum virtus manuum mihi erat pro nihilo, et vita ipsa putabantur indigni :
text_pt: De que também me serviria a força das mãos daqueles, cujo vigor se tinha esgotado?
text_el: καί γε ἰσχὺς χειρῶν αὐτῶν ἵνα τί μοι ἐπ' αὐτοὺς ἀπώλετο συντέλεια

text_en: Barren with want and hunger, who gnawed in the wilderness , disfigured with calamity and misery.
text_la: egestate et fame steriles, qui rodebant in solitudine, squallentes calamitate et miseria.
text_pt: De míngua e fome se debilitaram; e recolhiam-se para os lugares secos, tenebrosos, assolados e desertos.
text_el: ἐν ἐνδείᾳ καὶ λιμῷ ἄγονος οἱ φεύγοντες ἄνυδρον ἐχθὲς συνοχὴν καὶ ταλαιπωρίαν

text_en: And they ate grass, and barks of trees, and the root of junipers was their food.
text_la: Et mandebant herbas, et arborum cortices, et radix juniperorum erat cibus eorum :
text_pt: Apanhavam malvas junto aos arbustos, e o seu mantimento eram as raízes dos zimbros.
text_el: οἱ περικλῶντες ἅλιμα ἐπὶ ἠχοῦντι οἵτινες ἅλιμα ἦν αὐτῶν τὰ σῖτα ἄτιμοι δὲ καὶ πεφαυλισμένοι ἐνδεεῖς παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ οἳ καὶ ῥίζας ξύλων ἐμασῶντο ὑπὸ λιμοῦ μεγάλου

text_en: Who snatched up these things out of the valleys, and when they had found any of them, they ran to them with a cry.
text_la: qui de convallibus ista rapientes, cum singula reperissent, ad ea cum clamore currebant.
text_pt: Do meio dos homens eram expulsos, e gritavam contra eles, como contra o ladrão;
text_el: ἐπανέστησάν μοι κλέπται

text_en: They dwelt in the desert places of torrents, and in caves of earth, or upon the gravel.
text_la: In desertis habitabant torrentium, et in cavernis terræ, vel super glaream :
text_pt: Para habitarem nos barrancos dos vales, e nas cavernas da terra e das rochas.
text_el: ὧν οἱ οἶκοι αὐτῶν ἦσαν τρῶγλαι πετρῶν

text_en: They pleased themselves among these kind of things, and counted it delightful to be under the briers.
text_la: qui inter hujuscemodi lætabantur, et esse sub sentibus delicias computabant :
text_pt: Bramavam entre os arbustos, e ajuntavam-se debaixo das urtigas.
text_el: ἀνὰ μέσον εὐήχων βοήσονται οἳ ὑπὸ φρύγανα ἄγρια διῃτῶντο

text_en: The children of foolish and base men , and not appearing at all upon the earth.
text_la: filii stultorum et ignobilium, et in terra penitus non parentes.
text_pt: Eram filhos de doidos, e filhos de gente sem nome, e da terra foram expulsos.
text_el: ἀφρόνων υἱοὶ καὶ ἀτίμων ὄνομα καὶ κλέος ἐσβεσμένον ἀπὸ γῆς

text_en: Now I am turned into their song, and have become their byword.
text_la: Nunc in eorum canticum versus sum, et factus sum eis in proverbium.
text_pt: Agora, porém, sou a sua canção, e lhes sirvo de provérbio.
text_el: νυνὶ δὲ κιθάρα ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτῶν καὶ ἐμὲ θρύλημα ἔχουσιν

text_en: They abhor me, and flee far from me, and are not afraid to spit in my face.
text_la: Abominantur me, et longe fugiunt a me, et faciem meam conspuere non verentur.
text_pt: Abominam-me, e fogem para longe de mim, e no meu rosto não se privam de cuspir.
text_el: ἐβδελύξαντο δέ με ἀποστάντες μακράν ἀπὸ δὲ προσώπου μου οὐκ ἐφείσαντο πτύελον

text_en: For he has opened his quiver, and has afflicted me, and has put a bridle into my mouth.
text_la: Pharetram enim suam aperuit, et afflixit me, et frenum posuit in os meum.
text_pt: Porque Deus desatou a sua corda, e me oprimiu, por isso sacudiram de si o freio perante o meu rosto.
text_el: ἀνοίξας γὰρ φαρέτραν αὐτοῦ ἐκάκωσέν με καὶ χαλινὸν τοῦ προσώπου μου ἐξαπέστειλαν

text_en: At the right hand of my rising, my calamities forthwith arose: they have overthrown my feet, and have overwhelmed me with their paths as with waves.
text_la: Ad dexteram orientis calamitates meæ illico surrexerunt : pedes meos subverterunt, et oppresserunt quasi fluctibus semitis suis.
text_pt: À direita se levantam os moços; empurram os meus pés, e preparam contra mim os seus caminhos de destruição.
text_el: ἐπὶ δεξιῶν βλαστοῦ ἐπανέστησαν πόδα αὐτῶν ἐξέτειναν καὶ ὡδοποίησαν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τρίβους ἀπωλείας αὐτῶν

text_en: They have destroyed my ways, they have lain in wait against me, and they have prevailed, and there was none to help.
text_la: Dissipaverunt itinera mea; insidiati sunt mihi, et prævaluerunt : et non fuit qui ferret auxilium.
text_pt: Desbaratam-me o caminho; promovem a minha miséria; contra eles não há ajudador.
text_el: ἐξετρίβησαν τρίβοι μου ἐξέδυσεν γάρ μου τὴν στολήν

text_en: They have rushed in upon me, as when a wall is broken, and a gate opened, and have rolled themselves down to my miseries.
text_la: Quasi rupto muro, et aperta janua, irruerunt super me, et ad meas miserias devoluti sunt.
text_pt: Vêm contra mim como por uma grande brecha, e revolvem-se entre a assolação.
text_el: βέλεσιν αὐτοῦ κατηκόντισέν με κέχρηταί μοι ὡς βούλεται ἐν ὀδύναις πέφυρμαι

text_en: I am brought to nothing: as a wind you have taken away my desire: and my prosperity has passed away like a cloud.
text_la: Redactus sum in nihilum : abstulisti quasi ventus desiderium meum, et velut nubes pertransiit salus mea.
text_pt: Sobrevieram-me pavores; como vento perseguem a minha honra, e como nuvem passou a minha felicidade.
text_el: ἐπιστρέφονται δέ μου αἱ ὀδύναι ᾤχετό μου ἡ ἐλπὶς ὥσπερ πνεῦμα καὶ ὥσπερ νέφος ἡ σωτηρία μου

text_en: And now my soul fades within myself, and the days of affliction possess me.
text_la: Nunc autem in memetipso marcescit anima mea, et possident me dies afflictionis.
text_pt: E agora derrama-se em mim a minha alma; os dias da aflição se apoderaram de mim.
text_el: καὶ νῦν ἐπ' ἐμὲ ἐκχυθήσεται ἡ ψυχή μου ἔχουσιν δέ με ἡμέραι ὀδυνῶν

text_en: In the night my bone is pierced with sorrows: and they that feed upon me, do not sleep.
text_la: Nocte os meum perforatur doloribus, et qui me comedunt, non dormiunt.
text_pt: De noite se me traspassam os meus ossos, e os meus nervos não descansam.
text_el: νυκτὶ δέ μου τὰ ὀστᾶ συγκέκαυται τὰ δὲ νεῦρά μου διαλέλυται

text_en: With the multitude of them my garment is consumed, and they have girded me about, as with the collar of my coat.
text_la: In multitudine eorum consumitur vestimentum meum, et quasi capito tunicæ succinxerunt me.
text_pt: Pela grandeza do meu mal está desfigurada a minha veste, que, como a gola da minha túnica, me cinge.
text_el: ἐν πολλῇ ἰσχύι ἐπελάβετό μου τῆς στολῆς ὥσπερ τὸ περιστόμιον τοῦ χιτῶνός μου περιέσχεν με

text_en: I am compared to dirt, and am likened to embers and ashes.
text_la: Comparatus sum luto, et assimilatus sum favillæ et cineri.
text_pt: Lançou-me na lama, e fiquei semelhante ao pó e à cinza.
text_el: ἥγησαι δέ με ἴσα πηλῷ ἐν γῇ καὶ σποδῷ μου ἡ μερίς

text_en: I cry to you, and you hear me not: I stand up, and you do not regard me.
text_la: Clamo ad te, et non exaudis me : sto, et non respicis me.
text_pt: Clamo a ti, porém, tu não me respondes; estou em pé, porém, para mim não atentas.
text_el: κέκραγα δὲ πρὸς σὲ καὶ οὐκ εἰσακούεις μου ἔστησαν καὶ κατενόησάν με

text_en: You are changed to be cruel toward me, and in the hardness of your hand you are against me.
text_la: Mutatus es mihi in crudelem, et in duritia manus tuæ adversaris mihi.
text_pt: Tornaste-te cruel contra mim; com a força da tua mão resistes violentamente.
text_el: ἐπέβης δέ μοι ἀνελεημόνως χειρὶ κραταιᾷ με ἐμαστίγωσας

text_en: You have lifted me up, and set me as it were upon the wind, and you have mightily dashed me.
text_la: Elevasti me, et quasi super ventum ponens; elisisti me valide.
text_pt: Levantas-me sobre o vento, fazes-me cavalgar sobre ele, e derretes-me o ser.
text_el: ἔταξας δέ με ἐν ὀδύναις καὶ ἀπέρριψάς με ἀπὸ σωτηρίας

text_en: I know that you will deliver me to death, where a house is appointed for every one that lives.
text_la: Scio quia morti trades me, ubi constituta est domus omni viventi.
text_pt: Porque eu sei que me levarás à morte e à casa do ajuntamento determinada a todos os viventes.
text_el: οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι θάνατός με ἐκτρίψει οἰκία γὰρ παντὶ θνητῷ γῆ

text_en: But yet you stretch not forth your hand to their consumption: and if they shall fall down you will save.
text_la: Verumtamen non ad consumptionem eorum emittis manum tuam : et si corruerint, ipse salvabis.
text_pt: Porém não estenderá a mão para o túmulo, ainda que eles clamem na sua destruição.
text_el: εἰ γὰρ ὄφελον δυναίμην ἐμαυτὸν χειρώσασθαι ἢ δεηθείς γε ἑτέρου καὶ ποιήσει μοι τοῦτο

text_en: I wept heretofore for him that was afflicted, and my soul had compassion on the poor.
text_la: Flebam quondam super eo qui afflictus erat, et compatiebatur anima mea pauperi.
text_pt: Porventura não chorei sobre aquele que estava aflito, ou não se angustiou a minha alma pelo necessitado?
text_el: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐπὶ παντὶ ἀδυνάτῳ ἔκλαυσα ἐστέναξα δὲ ἰδὼν ἄνδρα ἐν ἀνάγκαις

text_en: I expected good things, and evils have come upon me: I waited for light, and darkness broke out.
text_la: Expectabam bona, et venerunt mihi mala : præstolabar lucem, et eruperunt tenebræ.
text_pt: Todavia aguardando eu o bem, então me veio o mal, esperando eu a luz, veio a escuridão.
text_el: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐπέχων ἀγαθοῖς ἰδοὺ συνήντησάν μοι μᾶλλον ἡμέραι κακῶν

text_en: My inner parts have boiled without any rest, the days of affliction have prevented me.
text_la: Interiora mea efferbuerunt absque ulla requie : prævenerunt me dies afflictionis.
text_pt: As minhas entranhas fervem e não estão quietas; os dias da aflição me surpreendem.
text_el: ἡ κοιλία μου ἐξέζεσεν καὶ οὐ σιωπήσεται προέφθασάν με ἡμέραι πτωχείας

text_en: I went mourning without indignation; I rose up, and cried in the crowd.
text_la: Mœrens incedebam sine furore; consurgens, in turba clamabam.
text_pt: Denegrido ando, porém não do sol; levantando-me na congregação, clamo por socorro.
text_el: στένων πεπόρευμαι ἄνευ φιμοῦ ἕστηκα δὲ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ κεκραγώς

text_en: I was the brother of dragons, and companion of ostriches.
text_la: Frater fui draconum, et socius struthionum.
text_pt: Irmão me fiz dos chacais, e companheiro dos avestruzes.
text_el: ἀδελφὸς γέγονα σειρήνων ἑταῖρος δὲ στρουθῶν

text_en: My skin has become black upon me, and my bones are dried up with heat.
text_la: Cutis mea denigrata est super me, et ossa mea aruerunt præ caumate.
text_pt: Enegreceu-se a minha pele sobre mim, e os meus ossos estão queimados do calor.
text_el: τὸ δὲ δέρμα μου ἐσκότωται μεγάλως τὰ δὲ ὀστᾶ μου ἀπὸ καύματος

text_en: My harp is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of those that weep.
text_la: Versa est in luctum cithara mea, et organum meum in vocem flentium.
text_pt: A minha harpa se tornou em luto, e o meu órgão em voz dos que choram.
text_el: ἀπέβη δὲ εἰς πάθος μου ἡ κιθάρα ὁ δὲ ψαλμός μου εἰς κλαυθμὸν ἐμοί

text_en: I made a covenant with my eyes, that I would not so much as think upon a virgin.
text_la: Pepigi fœdus cum oculis meis, ut ne cogitarem quidem de virgine.
text_pt: Fiz aliança com os meus olhos; como, pois, os fixaria numa virgem?
text_el: διαθήκην ἐθέμην τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς μου καὶ οὐ συνήσω ἐπὶ παρθένον

text_en: For what part should God from above have in me, and what inheritance the Almighty from on high?
text_la: Quam enim partem haberet in me Deus desuper, et hæreditatem Omnipotens de excelsis?
text_pt: Que porção teria eu do Deus lá de cima, ou que herança do TodoPoderoso desde as alturas?
text_el: καὶ τί ἐμέρισεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπάνωθεν καὶ κληρονομία ἱκανοῦ ἐξ ὑψίστων

text_en: Is not destruction to the wicked, and aversion to them that work iniquity ?
text_la: Numquid non perditio est iniquo, et alienatio operantibus injustitiam?
text_pt: Porventura não é a perdição para o perverso, o desastre para os que praticam iniqüidade?
text_el: οὐχὶ ἀπώλεια τῷ ἀδίκῳ καὶ ἀπαλλοτρίωσις τοῖς ποιοῦσιν ἀνομίαν

text_en: Does not he consider my ways, and number all my steps?
text_la: Nonne ipse considerat vias meas, et cunctos gressus meos dinumerat?
text_pt: Ou não vê ele os meus caminhos, e não conta todos os meus passos?
text_el: οὐχὶ αὐτὸς ὄψεται ὁδόν μου καὶ πάντα τὰ διαβήματά μου ἐξαριθμήσεται

text_en: If I have walked in vanity, and my foot has made haste to deceit:
text_la: Si ambulavi in vanitate, et festinavit in dolo pes meus,
text_pt: Se andei com falsidade, e se o meu pé se apressou para o engano
text_el: εἰ δὲ ἤμην πεπορευμένος μετὰ γελοιαστῶν εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐσπούδασεν ὁ πούς μου εἰς δόλον

text_en: Let him weigh me in a just balance, and let God know my simplicity.
text_la: appendat me in statera justa, et sciat Deus simplicitatem meam.
text_pt: (Pese-me em balanças fiéis, e saberá Deus a minha sinceridade),
text_el: ἱσταίη με ἄρα ἐν ζυγῷ δικαίῳ οἶδεν δὲ ὁ κύριος τὴν ἀκακίαν μου

text_en: If my step has turned out of the way, and if my heart has followed my eyes, and if a spot has cleaved to my hands:
text_la: Si declinavit gressus meus de via, et si secutum est oculos meos cor meum, et si manibus meis adhæsit macula,
text_pt: Se os meus passos se desviaram do caminho, e se o meu coração segue os meus olhos, e se às minhas mãos se apegou qualquer coisa,
text_el: εἰ ἐξέκλινεν ὁ πούς μου ἐκ τῆς ὁδοῦ εἰ δὲ καὶ τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ ἐπηκολούθησεν ἡ καρδία μου εἰ δὲ καὶ ταῖς χερσίν μου ἡψάμην δώρων

text_en: Then let me sow and let another reap: and let my offspring be rooted out.
text_la: seram, et alius comedat, et progenies mea eradicetur.
text_pt: Então semeie eu e outro coma, e seja a minha descendência arrancada até à raiz.
text_el: σπείραιμι ἄρα καὶ ἄλλοι φάγοισαν ἄρριζος δὲ γενοίμην ἐπὶ γῆς

text_en: If my heart has been deceived upon a woman , and if I have laid wait at my friend's door:
text_la: Si deceptum est cor meum super muliere, et si ad ostium amici mei insidiatus sum,
text_pt: Se o meu coração se deixou seduzir por uma mulher, ou se eu armei traições à porta do meu próximo,
text_el: εἰ ἐξηκολούθησεν ἡ καρδία μου γυναικὶ ἀνδρὸς ἑτέρου εἰ καὶ ἐγκάθετος ἐγενόμην ἐπὶ θύραις αὐτῆς

text_en: Let my wife be the harlot of another, and let other men lie with her.
text_la: scortum alterius sit uxor mea, et super illam incurventur alii.
text_pt: Então moa minha mulher para outro, e outros se encurvem sobre ela,
text_el: ἀρέσαι ἄρα καὶ ἡ γυνή μου ἑτέρῳ τὰ δὲ νήπιά μου ταπεινωθείη

text_en: For this is a heinous crime, and a most grievous iniquity .
text_la: Hoc enim nefas est, et iniquitas maxima.
text_pt: Porque é uma infâmia, e é delito pertencente aos juízes.
text_el: θυμὸς γὰρ ὀργῆς ἀκατάσχετος τὸ μιᾶναι ἀνδρὸς γυναῖκα

text_en: It is a fire that devours even to destruction , and roots up all things that spring.
text_la: Ignis est usque ad perditionem devorans, et omnia eradicans genimina.
text_pt: Porque é fogo que consome até à perdição, e desarraigaria toda a minha renda.
text_el: πῦρ γάρ ἐστιν καιόμενον ἐπὶ πάντων τῶν μερῶν οὗ δ' ἂν ἐπέλθῃ ἐκ ῥιζῶν ἀπώλεσεν

text_en: If I have despised to abide judgment with my manservant, or my maidservant, when they had any controversy against me:
text_la: Si contempsi subire judicium cum servo meo et ancilla mea, cum disceptarent adversum me :
text_pt: Se desprezei o direito do meu servo ou da minha serva, quando eles contendiam comigo;
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐφαύλισα κρίμα θεράποντός μου ἢ θεραπαίνης κρινομένων αὐτῶν πρός με

text_en: For what shall I do when God shall rise to judge? And when he shall examine, what shall I answer him?
text_la: quid enim faciam cum surrexerit ad judicandum Deus? et cum quæsierit, quid respondebo illi?
text_pt: Então que faria eu quando Deus se levantasse? E, inquirindo a causa, que lhe responderia?
text_el: τί γὰρ ποιήσω ἐὰν ἔτασίν μου ποιήσηται ὁ κύριος ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἐπισκοπήν τίνα ἀπόκρισιν ποιήσομαι

text_en: Did not he that made me in the womb make him also: and did not one and the same form me in the womb?
text_la: Numquid non in utero fecit me, qui et illum operatus est, et formavit me in vulva unus?
text_pt: Aquele que me formou no ventre não o fez também a ele? Ou não nos formou do mesmo modo na madre?
text_el: πότερον οὐχ ὡς καὶ ἐγὼ ἐγενόμην ἐν γαστρί καὶ ἐκεῖνοι γεγόνασιν γεγόναμεν δὲ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ κοιλίᾳ

text_en: If I have denied to the poor what they desired, and have made the eyes of the widow wait:
text_la: Si negavi quod volebant pauperibus, et oculos viduæ expectare feci;
text_pt: Se retive o que os pobres desejavam, ou fiz desfalecer os olhos da viúva,
text_el: ἀδύνατοι δὲ χρείαν ἥν ποτ' εἶχον οὐκ ἀπέτυχον χήρας δὲ τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν οὐκ ἐξέτηξα

text_en: If I have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten thereof:
text_la: si comedi buccellam meam solus, et non comedit pupillus ex ea
text_pt: Ou se, sozinho comi o meu bocado, e o órfão não comeu dele
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ τὸν ψωμόν μου ἔφαγον μόνος καὶ οὐχὶ ὀρφανῷ μετέδωκα

text_en: (For from my infancy mercy grew up with me: and it came out with me from my mother's womb):
text_la: (quia ab infantia mea crevit mecum miseratio, et de utero matris meæ egressa est mecum);
text_pt: (Porque desde a minha mocidade cresceu comigo como com seu pai, e fui o guia da viúva desde o ventre de minha mãe),
text_el: ὅτι ἐκ νεότητός μου ἐξέτρεφον ὡς πατὴρ καὶ ἐκ γαστρὸς μητρός μου ὡδήγησα

text_en: If I have despised him that was perishing for want of clothing, and the poor man that had no covering:
text_la: si despexi pereuntem, eo quod non habuerit indumentum, et absque operimento pauperem;
text_pt: Se alguém vi perecer por falta de roupa, e ao necessitado por não ter coberta,
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὑπερεῖδον γυμνὸν ἀπολλύμενον καὶ οὐκ ἠμφίασα

text_en: If his sides have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep:
text_la: si non benedixerunt mihi latera ejus, et de velleribus ovium mearum calefactus est;
text_pt: Se os seus lombos não me abençoaram, se ele não se aquentava com as peles dos meus cordeiros,
text_el: ἀδύνατοι δὲ εἰ μὴ εὐλόγησάν με ἀπὸ δὲ κουρᾶς ἀμνῶν μου ἐθερμάνθησαν οἱ ὦμοι αὐτῶν

text_en: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, even when I saw myself superior in the gate:
text_la: si levavi super pupillum manum meam, etiam cum viderem me in porta superiorem :
text_pt: Se eu levantei a minha mão contra o órfão, porquanto na porta via a minha ajuda,
text_el: εἰ ἐπῆρα ὀρφανῷ χεῖρα πεποιθὼς ὅτι πολλή μοι βοήθεια περίεστιν

text_en: Let my shoulder fall from its joint, and let my arm with its bones be broken.
text_la: humerus meus a junctura sua cadat, et brachium meum cum suis ossibus confringatur.
text_pt: Então caia do ombro a minha espádua, e separe-se o meu braço do osso.
text_el: ἀποσταίη ἄρα ὁ ὦμός μου ἀπὸ τῆς κλειδός ὁ δὲ βραχίων μου ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀγκῶνός μου συντριβείη

text_en: For I have always feared God as waves swelling over me, and his weight I was unable to bear.
text_la: Semper enim quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum, et pondus ejus ferre non potui.
text_pt: Porque o castigo de Deus era para mim um assombro, e eu não podia suportar a sua grandeza.
text_el: φόβος γὰρ κυρίου συνέσχεν με καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ λήμματος αὐτοῦ οὐχ ὑποίσω

text_en: If I have thought gold my strength, and have said to fine gold: My confidence:
text_la: Si putavi aurum robur meum, et obrizo dixi : Fiducia mea;
text_pt: Se no ouro pus a minha esperança, ou disse ao ouro fino: Tu és a minha confiança;
text_el: εἰ ἔταξα χρυσίον ἰσχύν μου εἰ δὲ καὶ λίθῳ πολυτελεῖ ἐπεποίθησα

text_en: If I have rejoiced over my great riches, and because my hand had gotten much.
text_la: si lætatus sum super multis divitiis meis, et quia plurima reperit manus mea;
text_pt: Se me alegrei de que era muita a minha riqueza, e de que a minha mão tinha alcançado muito;
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ εὐφράνθην πολλοῦ πλούτου μοι γενομένου εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐπ' ἀναριθμήτοις ἐθέμην χεῖρά μου

text_en: If I beheld the sun when it shined and the moon going in brightness:
text_la: si vidi solem cum fulgeret, et lunam incedentem clare,
text_pt: Se olhei para o sol, quando resplandecia, ou para a lua, caminhando gloriosa,
text_el: ἦ οὐχ ὁρῶ μὲν ἥλιον τὸν ἐπιφαύσκοντα ἐκλείποντα σελήνην δὲ φθίνουσαν οὐ γὰρ ἐπ' αὐτοῖς ἐστιν

text_en: And my heart in secret has rejoiced, and I have kissed my hand with, my mouth:
text_la: et lætatum est in abscondito cor meum, et osculatus sum manum meam ore meo :
text_pt: E o meu coração se deixou enganar em oculto, e a minha boca beijou a minha mão,
text_el: καὶ εἰ ἠπατήθη λάθρᾳ ἡ καρδία μου εἰ δὲ καὶ χεῖρά μου ἐπιθεὶς ἐπὶ στόματί μου ἐφίλησα

text_en: Which is a very great iniquity , and a denial against the most high God .
text_la: quæ est iniquitas maxima, et negatio contra Deum altissimum.
text_pt: Também isto seria delito à punição de juízes; pois assim negaria a Deus que está lá em cima.
text_el: καὶ τοῦτό μοι ἄρα ἀνομία ἡ μεγίστη λογισθείη ὅτι ἐψευσάμην ἐναντίον κυρίου τοῦ ὑψίστου

text_en: If I have been glad at the downfall of him that hated me, and have rejoiced that evil had found him.
text_la: Si gavisus sum ad ruinam ejus qui me oderat, et exsultavi quod invenisset eum malum :
text_pt: Se me alegrei da desgraça do que me tem ódio, e se exultei quando o mal o atingiu
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐπιχαρὴς ἐγενόμην πτώματι ἐχθρῶν μου καὶ εἶπεν ἡ καρδία μου εὖγε

text_en: For I have not given my mouth to sin , by wishing a curse to his soul .
text_la: non enim dedi ad peccandum guttur meum, ut expeterem maledicens animam ejus.
text_pt: (Também não deixei pecar a minha boca, desejando a sua morte com maldição);
text_el: ἀκούσαι ἄρα τὸ οὖς μου τὴν κατάραν μου θρυληθείην δὲ ἄρα ὑπὸ λαοῦ μου κακούμενος

text_en: If the men of my tabernacle have not said: Who will give us of his flesh that we may be filled?
text_la: Si non dixerunt viri tabernaculi mei : Quis det de carnibus ejus, ut saturemur?
text_pt: Se a gente da minha tenda não disse: Ah! quem nos dará da sua carne? Nunca nos fartaríamos dela.
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ πολλάκις εἶπον αἱ θεράπαιναί μου τίς ἂν δῴη ἡμῖν τῶν σαρκῶν αὐτοῦ πλησθῆναι λίαν μου χρηστοῦ ὄντος

text_en: The stranger did not stay without, my door was open to the traveller.
text_la: foris non mansit peregrinus : ostium meum viatori patuit.
text_pt: O estrangeiro não passava a noite na rua; as minhas portas abria ao viandante.
text_el: ἔξω δὲ οὐκ ηὐλίζετο ξένος ἡ δὲ θύρα μου παντὶ ἐλθόντι ἀνέῳκτο

text_en: If as a man I have hid my sin , and have concealed my iniquity in my bosom.
text_la: Si abscondi quasi homo peccatum meum, et celavi in sinu meo iniquitatem meam;
text_pt: Se, como Adão, encobri as minhas transgressões, ocultando o meu delito no meu seio;
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἁμαρτὼν ἀκουσίως ἔκρυψα τὴν ἁμαρτίαν μου

text_en: If I have been afraid at a very great multitude, and the contempt of kinsmen has terrified me: and have not rather held my peace, and not gone out of the door.
text_la: si expavi ad multitudinem nimiam, et despectio propinquorum terruit me : et non magis tacui, nec egressus sum ostium.
text_pt: Porque eu temia a grande multidão, e o desprezo das famílias me apavorava, e eu me calei, e não saí da porta;
text_el: οὐ γὰρ διετράπην πολυοχλίαν πλήθους τοῦ μὴ ἐξαγορεῦσαι ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν εἰ δὲ καὶ εἴασα ἀδύνατον ἐξελθεῖν θύραν μου κόλπῳ κενῷ

text_en: Who would grant me a hearing, that the Almighty may hear my desire: and that he himself that judges would write a book,
text_la: Quis mihi tribuat auditorem, ut desiderium meum audiat Omnipotens, et librum scribat ipse qui judicat,
text_pt: Ah! quem me dera um que me ouvisse! Eis que o meu desejo é que o Todo-Poderoso me responda, e que o meu adversário escreva um livro.
text_el: τίς δῴη ἀκούοντά μου χεῖρα δὲ κυρίου εἰ μὴ ἐδεδοίκειν συγγραφὴν δέ ἣν εἶχον κατά τινος

text_en: that I may carry it on my shoulder, and put it about me as a crown?
text_la: ut in humero meo portem illum, et circumdem illum quasi coronam mihi?
text_pt: Por certo que o levaria sobre o meu ombro, sobre mim o ataria por coroa.
text_el: ἐπ' ὤμοις ἂν περιθέμενος στέφανον ἀνεγίνωσκον

text_en: At every step of mine I would pronounce it, and offer it as to a prince.
text_la: Per singulos gradus meos pronuntiabo illum, et quasi principi offeram eum.
text_pt: O número dos meus passos lhe mostraria; como príncipe me chegaria a ele.
text_el: καὶ εἰ μὴ ῥήξας αὐτὴν ἀπέδωκα οὐθὲν λαβὼν παρὰ χρεοφειλέτου

text_en: If my land cry against me, and with it the furrows thereof mourn:
text_la: Si adversum me terra mea clamat, et cum ipsa sulci ejus deflent :
text_pt: Se a minha terra clamar contra mim, e se os seus sulcos juntamente chorarem,
text_el: εἰ ἐπ' ἐμοί ποτε ἡ γῆ ἐστέναξεν εἰ δὲ καὶ οἱ αὔλακες αὐτῆς ἔκλαυσαν ὁμοθυμαδόν

text_en: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, and have afflicted the son of the tillers thereof:
text_la: si fructus ejus comedi absque pecunia, et animam agricolarum ejus afflixi :
text_pt: Se comi os seus frutos sem dinheiro, e sufoquei a alma dos seus donos,
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ τὴν ἰσχὺν αὐτῆς ἔφαγον μόνος ἄνευ τιμῆς εἰ δὲ καὶ ψυχὴν κυρίου τῆς γῆς ἐκβαλὼν ἐλύπησα

text_en: Let thistles grow up to me instead of wheat, and thorns instead of barley.
text_la: pro frumento oriatur mihi tribulus, et pro hordeo spina.
text_pt: Por trigo me produza cardos, e por cevada joio. Acabaram-se as palavras de Jó.
text_el: ἀντὶ πυροῦ ἄρα ἐξέλθοι μοι κνίδη ἀντὶ δὲ κριθῆς βάτος

text_en: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he seemed just to himself.
text_la: Omiserunt autem tres viri isti respondere Job, eo quod justus sibi videretur.
text_pt: Então aqueles três homens cessaram de responder a Jó; porque era justo aos seus próprios olhos.
text_el: ἡσύχασαν δὲ καὶ οἱ τρεῖς φίλοι αὐτοῦ ἔτι ἀντειπεῖν Ιωβ ἦν γὰρ Ιωβ δίκαιος ἐναντίον αὐτῶν

text_en: And Eliu the son of Barachel the Buzite of the kindred of Ram, was angry and was moved to indignation: now he was angry against Job, because he said he was just before God .
text_la: Et iratus indignatusque est Eliu filius Barachel Buzites, de cognatione Ram : iratus est autem adversum Job, eo quod justum se esse diceret coram Deo.
text_pt: E acendeu-se a ira de Eliú, filho de Baraquel, o buzita, da família de Rão; contra Jó se acendeu a sua ira, porque se justificava a si mesmo, mais do que a Deus.
text_el: ὠργίσθη δὲ Ελιους ὁ τοῦ Βαραχιηλ ὁ Βουζίτης ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας Ραμ τῆς Αυσίτιδος χώρας ὠργίσθη δὲ τῷ Ιωβ σφόδρα διότι ἀπέφηνεν ἑαυτὸν δίκαιον ἐναντίον κυρίου

text_en: And he was angry with his friends, because they had not found a reasonable answer, but only had condemned Job.
text_la: Porro adversum amicos ejus indignatus est, eo quod non invenissent responsionem rationabilem, sed tantummodo condemnassent Job.
text_pt: Também a sua ira se acendeu contra os seus três amigos, porque, não achando que responder, todavia condenavam a Jó.
text_el: καὶ κατὰ τῶν τριῶν δὲ φίλων ὠργίσθη σφόδρα διότι οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν ἀποκριθῆναι ἀντίθετα Ιωβ καὶ ἔθεντο αὐτὸν εἶναι ἀσεβῆ

text_en: So Eliu waited while Job was speaking because they were his elders that were speaking.
text_la: Igitur Eliu expectavit Job loquentem, eo quod seniores essent qui loquebantur.
text_pt: Eliú, porém, esperou para falar a Jó, porquanto tinham mais idade do que ele.
text_el: Ελιους δὲ ὑπέμεινεν δοῦναι ἀπόκρισιν Ιωβ ὅτι πρεσβύτεροι αὐτοῦ εἰσιν ἡμέραις

text_en: But when he saw that the three were not able to answer, he was exceedingly angry .
text_la: Cum autem vidisset quod tres respondere non potuissent, iratus est vehementer.
text_pt: Vendo, pois, Eliú que já não havia resposta na boca daqueles três homens, a sua ira se acendeu.
text_el: καὶ εἶδεν Ελιους ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἀπόκρισις ἐν στόματι τῶν τριῶν ἀνδρῶν καὶ ἐθυμώθη ὀργὴ αὐτοῦ

text_en: Then Eliu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, and said: I am younger in days, and you are more ancient, therefore hanging down my head, I was afraid to show you my opinion.
text_la: Respondensque Eliu filius Barachel Buzites, dixit : Junior sum tempore, vos autem antiquiores : idcirco, demisso capite, veritus sum vobis indicare meam sententiam.
text_pt: E respondeu Eliú, filho de Baraquel, o buzita, dizendo: Eu sou de menos idade, e vós sois idosos; receei-me e temi de vos declarar a minha opinião.
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ελιους ὁ τοῦ Βαραχιηλ ὁ Βουζίτης εἶπεν νεώτερος μέν εἰμι τῷ χρόνῳ ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε πρεσβύτεροι διὸ ἡσύχασα φοβηθεὶς τοῦ ὑμῖν ἀναγγεῖλαι τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ ἐπιστήμην

text_en: For I hoped that greater age would speak, and that a multitude of years would teach wisdom.
text_la: Sperabam enim quod ætas prolixior loqueretur, et annorum multitudo doceret sapientiam.
text_pt: Dizia eu: Falem os dias, e a multidão dos anos ensine a sabedoria.
text_el: εἶπα δὲ ὅτι ὁ χρόνος ἐστὶν ὁ λαλῶν ἐν πολλοῖς δὲ ἔτεσιν οἴδασιν σοφίαν

text_en: But, as I see, there is a spirit in men , and the inspiration of the Almighty gives understanding.
text_la: Sed, ut video, spiritus est in hominibus, et inspiratio Omnipotentis dat intelligentiam.
text_pt: Na verdade, há um espírito no homem, e a inspiração do TodoPoderoso o faz entendido.
text_el: ἀλλὰ πνεῦμά ἐστιν ἐν βροτοῖς πνοὴ δὲ παντοκράτορός ἐστιν ἡ διδάσκουσα

text_en: They that are aged are not the wise men , neither do the ancients understand judgment.
text_la: Non sunt longævi sapientes, nec senes intelligunt judicium.
text_pt: Os grandes não são os sábios, nem os velhos entendem o que é direito.
text_el: οὐχ οἱ πολυχρόνιοί εἰσιν σοφοί οὐδ' οἱ γέροντες οἴδασιν κρίμα

text_en: Therefore I will speak: Hearken to me, I also will show you my wisdom.
text_la: Ideo dicam : Audite me : ostendam vobis etiam ego meam sapientiam.
text_pt: Assim digo: Dai-me ouvidos, e também eu declararei a minha opinião.
text_el: διὸ εἶπα ἀκούσατέ μου καὶ ἀναγγελῶ ὑμῖν ἃ οἶδα

text_en: For I have waited for your words, I have given ear to your wisdom, as long as you were disputing in words.
text_la: Expectavi enim sermones vestros; audivi prudentiam vestram, donec disceptaremini sermonibus;
text_pt: Eis que aguardei as vossas palavras, e dei ouvidos às vossas considerações, até que buscásseis razões.
text_el: ἐνωτίζεσθέ μου τὰ ῥήματα ἐρῶ γὰρ ὑμῶν ἀκουόντων ἄχρι οὗ ἐτάσητε λόγους

text_en: And as long as I thought you said some thing, I considered: but, as I see, there is none of you that can convince Job, and answer his words.
text_la: et donec putabam vos aliquid dicere, considerabam : sed, ut video, non est qui possit arguere Job, et respondere ex vobis sermonibus ejus.
text_pt: Atentando, pois, para vós, eis que nenhum de vós há que possa convencer a Jó, nem que responda às suas razões;
text_el: καὶ μέχρι ὑμῶν συνήσω καὶ ἰδοὺ οὐκ ἦν τῷ Ιωβ ἐλέγχων ἀνταποκρινόμενος ῥήματα αὐτοῦ ἐξ ὑμῶν

text_en: Lest you should say: We have found wisdom, God has cast him down, not man .
text_la: Ne forte dicatis : Invenimus sapientiam : Deus projecit eum, non homo.
text_pt: Para que não digais: Achamos a sabedoria; Deus o derrubou, e não homem algum.
text_el: ἵνα μὴ εἴπητε εὕρομεν σοφίαν κυρίῳ προσθέμενοι

text_en: He has spoken nothing to me, and I will not answer him according to your words.
text_la: Nihil locutus est mihi : et ego non secundum sermones vestros respondebo illi.
text_pt: Ora ele não dirigiu contra mim palavra alguma, nem lhe responderei com as vossas palavras.
text_el: ἀνθρώπῳ δὲ ἐπετρέψατε λαλῆσαι τοιαῦτα ῥήματα

text_en: They were afraid, and answered no more, and they left off speaking.
text_la: Extimuerunt, nec responderunt ultra, abstuleruntque a se eloquia.
text_pt: Estão pasmados, não respondem mais, faltam-lhes as palavras.
text_el: ἐπτοήθησαν οὐκ ἀπεκρίθησαν ἔτι ἐπαλαίωσαν ἐξ αὐτῶν λόγους

text_en: Therefore because I have waited, and they have not spoken: they stood, and answered no more:
text_la: Quoniam igitur expectavi, et non sunt locuti : steterunt, nec ultra responderunt :
text_pt: Esperei, pois, mas não falam; porque já pararam, e não respondem mais.
text_el: ὑπέμεινα οὐ γὰρ ἐλάλησαν ὅτι ἔστησαν οὐκ ἀπεκρίθησαν

text_en: I also will answer my part, and will show my knowledge.
text_la: respondebo et ego partem meam, et ostendam scientiam meam.
text_pt: Também eu responderei pela minha parte; também eu declararei a minha opinião.
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ελιους λέγει

text_en: For I am full of matter to speak of, and the spirit of my bowels straitens me.
text_la: Plenus sum enim sermonibus, et coarctat me spiritus uteri mei.
text_pt: Porque estou cheio de palavras; o meu espírito me constrange.
text_el: πάλιν λαλήσω πλήρης γάρ εἰμι ῥημάτων ὀλέκει γάρ με τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς γαστρός

text_en: Behold, my belly is as new wine which wants vent, which bursts the new vessels.
text_la: En venter meus quasi mustum absque spiraculo, quod lagunculas novas disrumpit.
text_pt: Eis que dentro de mim sou como o mosto, sem respiradouro, prestes a arrebentar, como odres novos.
text_el: ἡ δὲ γαστήρ μου ὥσπερ ἀσκὸς γλεύκους ζέων δεδεμένος ἢ ὥσπερ φυσητὴρ χαλκέως ἐρρηγώς

text_en: I will speak and take breath a little: I will open my lips, and will answer.
text_la: Loquar, et respirabo paululum : aperiam labia mea, et respondebo.
text_pt: Falarei, para que ache alívio; abrirei os meus lábios, e responderei.
text_el: λαλήσω ἵνα ἀναπαύσωμαι ἀνοίξας τὰ χείλη

text_en: I will not accept the person of man , and I will not level God with man .
text_la: Non accipiam personam viri, et Deum homini non æquabo.
text_pt: Que não faça eu acepção de pessoas, nem use de palavras lisonjeiras com o homem!
text_el: ἄνθρωπον γὰρ οὐ μὴ αἰσχυνθῶ ἀλλὰ μὴν οὐδὲ βροτὸν οὐ μὴ ἐντραπῶ

text_en: For I know not how long I shall continue, and whether after a while my Maker may take me away.
text_la: Nescio enim quamdiu subsistam, et si post modicum tollat me factor meus.
text_pt: Porque não sei usar de lisonjas; em breve me levaria o meu Criador.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ ἐπίσταμαι θαυμάσαι πρόσωπον εἰ δὲ μή καὶ ἐμὲ σῆτες ἔδονται

text_en: Hear therefore, O Job, my speeches, and hearken to all my words.
text_la: Audi igitur, Job, eloquia mea, et omnes sermones meos ausculta.
text_pt: Assim, na verdade, ó Jó, ouve as minhas razões, e dá ouvidos a todas as minhas palavras.
text_el: οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ ἄκουσον Ιωβ τὰ ῥήματά μου καὶ λαλιὰν ἐνωτίζου μου

text_en: Behold now I have opened my mouth, let my tongue speak within my jaws.
text_la: Ecce aperui os meum : loquatur lingua mea in faucibus meis.
text_pt: Eis que já abri a minha boca; já falou a minha língua debaixo do meu paladar.
text_el: ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἤνοιξα τὸ στόμα μου καὶ ἐλάλησεν ἡ γλῶσσά μου

text_en: My words are from my upright heart, and my lips shall speak a pure sentence.
text_la: Simplici corde meo sermones mei, et sententiam puram labia mea loquentur.
text_pt: As minhas razões provam a sinceridade do meu coração, e os meus lábios proferem o puro saber.
text_el: καθαρά μου ἡ καρδία ῥήμασιν σύνεσις δὲ χειλέων μου καθαρὰ νοήσει

text_en: The spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life.
text_la: Spiritus Dei fecit me, et spiraculum Omnipotentis vivificavit me.
text_pt: O Espírito de Deus me fez; e a inspiração do Todo-Poderoso me deu vida.
text_el: πνεῦμα θεῖον τὸ ποιῆσάν με πνοὴ δὲ παντοκράτορος ἡ διδάσκουσά με

text_en: If you can, answer me, and stand up against my face.
text_la: Si potes, responde mihi, et adversus faciem meam consiste.
text_pt: Se podes, responde-me, põe em ordem as tuas razões diante de mim, e apresenta-te.
text_el: ἐὰν δύνῃ δός μοι ἀπόκρισιν πρὸς ταῦτα ὑπόμεινον στῆθι κατ' ἐμὲ καὶ ἐγὼ κατὰ σέ

text_en: Behold God has made me as well as you, and of the same clay I also was formed.
text_la: Ecce, et me sicut et te fecit Deus, et de eodem luto ego quoque formatus sum.
text_pt: Eis que vim de Deus, como tu; do barro também eu fui formado.
text_el: ἐκ πηλοῦ διήρτισαι σὺ ὡς καὶ ἐγώ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ διηρτίσμεθα

text_en: But yet let not my wonder terrify you, and let not my eloquence be burdensome to you.
text_la: Verumtamen miraculum meum non te terreat, et eloquentia mea non sit tibi gravis.
text_pt: Eis que não te perturbará o meu terror, nem será pesada sobre ti a minha mão.
text_el: οὐχ ὁ φόβος μού σε στροβήσει οὐδὲ ἡ χείρ μου βαρεῖα ἔσται ἐπὶ σοί

text_en: Now you have said in my hearing, and I have heard the voice of your words:
text_la: Dixisti ergo in auribus meis, et vocem verborum tuorum audivi :
text_pt: Na verdade tu falaste aos meus ouvidos; e eu ouvi a voz das tuas palavras. Dizias:
text_el: πλὴν εἶπας ἐν ὠσίν μου φωνὴν ῥημάτων σου ἀκήκοα

text_en: I am clean, and without sin : I am unspotted, and there is no iniquity in me.
text_la: Mundus sum ego, et absque delicto : immaculatus, et non est iniquitas in me.
text_pt: Limpo estou, sem transgressão; puro sou, e não tenho iniqüidade.
text_el: διότι λέγεις καθαρός εἰμι οὐχ ἁμαρτών ἄμεμπτος δέ εἰμι οὐ γὰρ ἠνόμησα

text_en: Because he has found complaints against me, therefore he has counted me for his enemy.
text_la: Quia querelas in me reperit, ideo arbitratus est me inimicum sibi.
text_pt: Eis que procura pretexto contra mim, e me considera como seu inimigo.
text_el: μέμψιν δὲ κατ' ἐμοῦ εὗρεν ἥγηται δέ με ὥσπερ ὑπεναντίον

text_en: He has put my feet in the stocks, he has observed all my paths.
text_la: Posuit in nervo pedes meos; custodivit omnes semitas meas.
text_pt: Põe no tronco os meus pés, e observa todas as minhas veredas.
text_el: ἔθετο δὲ ἐν ξύλῳ τὸν πόδα μου ἐφύλαξεν δέ μου πάσας τὰς ὁδούς

text_en: Now this is the thing in which you are not justified: I will answer you, that God is greater than man .
text_la: Hoc est ergo in quo non es justificatus : respondebo tibi, quia major sit Deus homine.
text_pt: Eis que nisso não tens razão; eu te respondo; porque maior é Deus do que o homem.
text_el: πῶς γὰρ λέγεις δίκαιός εἰμι καὶ οὐκ ἐπακήκοέν μου αἰώνιος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἐπάνω βροτῶν

text_en: Do you strive against him, because he has not answered you to all words?
text_la: Adversus eum contendis, quod non ad omnia verba responderit tibi?
text_pt: Por que razão contendes com ele, sendo que não responde acerca de todos os seus feitos?
text_el: λέγεις δέ διὰ τί τῆς δίκης μου οὐκ ἐπακήκοεν πᾶν ῥῆμα

text_en: God speaks once, and repeats not the selfsame thing the second time.
text_la: Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo idipsum non repetit.
text_pt: Antes Deus fala uma e duas vezes; porém ninguém atenta para isso.
text_el: ἐν γὰρ τῷ ἅπαξ λαλήσαι ὁ κύριος ἐν δὲ τῷ δευτέρῳ ἐνύπνιον

text_en: By a dream in a vision by night, when deep sleep falls upon men , and they are sleeping in their beds:
text_la: Per somnium, in visione nocturna, quando irruit sopor super homines, et dormiunt in lectulo,
text_pt: Em sonho ou em visão noturna, quando cai sono profundo sobre os homens, e adormecem na cama.
text_el: ἢ ἐν μελέτῃ νυκτερινῇ ὡς ὅταν ἐπιπίπτῃ δεινὸς φόβος ἐπ' ἀνθρώπους ἐπὶ νυσταγμάτων ἐπὶ κοίτης

text_en: Then he opens the ears of men , and teaching instructs them in what they are to learn.
text_la: tunc aperit aures virorum, et erudiens eos instruit disciplina,
text_pt: Então o revela ao ouvido dos homens, e lhes sela a sua instrução,
text_el: τότε ἀνακαλύπτει νοῦν ἀνθρώπων ἐν εἴδεσιν φόβου τοιούτοις αὐτοὺς ἐξεφόβησεν

text_en: That he may withdraw a man from the things he is doing, and may deliver him from pride .
text_la: ut avertat hominem ab his quæ facit, et liberet eum de superbia,
text_pt: Para apartar o homem daquilo que faz, e esconder do homem a soberba.
text_el: ἀποστρέψαι ἄνθρωπον ἐξ ἀδικίας τὸ δὲ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ πτώματος ἐρρύσατο

text_en: Rescuing his soul from corruption: and his life from passing to the sword.
text_la: eruens animam ejus a corruptione, et vitam illius ut non transeat in gladium.
text_pt: Para desviar a sua alma da cova, e a sua vida de passar pela espada.
text_el: ἐφείσατο δὲ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ θανάτου καὶ μὴ πεσεῖν αὐτὸν ἐν πολέμῳ

text_en: He rebukes also by sorrow in the bed, and he makes all his bones to wither.
text_la: Increpat quoque per dolorem in lectulo, et omnia ossa ejus marcescere facit.
text_pt: Também na sua cama é castigado com dores; e com incessante contenda nos seus ossos;
text_el: πάλιν δὲ ἤλεγξεν αὐτὸν ἐν μαλακίᾳ ἐπὶ κοίτης καὶ πλῆθος ὀστῶν αὐτοῦ ἐνάρκησεν

text_en: Bread becomes abominable to him in his life, and to his soul the meat which before he desired.
text_la: Abominabilis ei fit in vita sua panis, et animæ illius cibus ante desiderabilis.
text_pt: De modo que a sua vida abomina até o pão, e a sua alma a comida apetecível.
text_el: πᾶν δὲ βρωτὸν σίτου οὐ μὴ δύνηται προσδέξασθαι καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ βρῶσιν ἐπιθυμήσει

text_en: His flesh shall be consumed away, and his bones that were covered shall be made bare.
text_la: Tabescet caro ejus, et ossa, quæ tecta fuerant, nudabuntur.
text_pt: Desaparece a sua carne a olhos vistos, e os seus ossos, que não se viam, agora aparecem.
text_el: ἕως ἂν σαπῶσιν αὐτοῦ αἱ σάρκες καὶ ἀποδείξῃ τὰ ὀστᾶ αὐτοῦ κενά

text_en: His soul has drawn near to corruption, and his life to the destroyers.
text_la: Appropinquavit corruptioni anima ejus, et vita illius mortiferis.
text_pt: E a sua alma se vai chegando à cova, e a sua vida aos que trazem a morte.
text_el: ἤγγισεν δὲ εἰς θάνατον ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἡ δὲ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν ᾅδῃ

text_en: If there shall be an angel speaking for him, one among thousands, to declare man's uprightness,
text_la: Si fuerit pro eo angelus loquens, unus de millibus, ut annuntiet hominis æquitatem,
text_pt: Se com ele, pois, houver um mensageiro, um intérprete, um entre milhares, para declarar ao homem a sua retidão,
text_el: ἐὰν ὦσιν χίλιοι ἄγγελοι θανατηφόροι εἷς αὐτῶν οὐ μὴ τρώσῃ αὐτόν ἐὰν νοήσῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ ἐπιστραφῆναι ἐπὶ κύριον ἀναγγείλῃ δὲ ἀνθρώπῳ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ μέμψιν τὴν δὲ ἄνοιαν αὐτοῦ δείξῃ

text_en: he shall have mercy on him, and shall say: Deliver him, that he may not go down to corruption: I have found wherein I may be merciful to him.
text_la: miserebitur ejus, et dicet : Libera eum, ut non descendat in corruptionem : inveni in quo ei propitier.
text_pt: Então terá misericórdia dele, e lhe dirá: Livra-o, para que não desça à cova; já achei resgate.
text_el: ἀνθέξεται τοῦ μὴ πεσεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς θάνατον ἀνανεώσει δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ σῶμα ὥσπερ ἀλοιφὴν ἐπὶ τοίχου τὰ δὲ ὀστᾶ αὐτοῦ ἐμπλήσει μυελοῦ

text_en: His flesh is consumed with punishments, let him return to the days of his youth.
text_la: Consumpta est caro ejus a suppliciis : revertatur ad dies adolescentiæ suæ.
text_pt: Sua carne se reverdecerá mais do que era na mocidade, e tornará aos dias da sua juventude.
text_el: ἁπαλυνεῖ δὲ αὐτοῦ τὰς σάρκας ὥσπερ νηπίου ἀποκαταστήσει δὲ αὐτὸν ἀνδρωθέντα ἐν ἀνθρώποις

text_en: He shall pray to God , and he will be gracious to him: and he shall see his face with joy , and he will render to man his justice .
text_la: Deprecabitur Deum, et placabilis ei erit : et videbit faciem ejus in jubilo, et reddet homini justitiam suam.
text_pt: Deveras orará a Deus, o qual se agradará dele, e verá a sua face com júbilo, e restituirá ao homem a sua justiça.
text_el: εὐξάμενος δὲ πρὸς κύριον καὶ δεκτὰ αὐτῷ ἔσται εἰσελεύσεται δὲ προσώπῳ καθαρῷ σὺν ἐξηγορίᾳ ἀποδώσει δὲ ἀνθρώποις δικαιοσύνην

text_en: He shall look upon men , and shall say: I have sinned , and indeed I have offended, and I have not received what I have deserved.
text_la: Respiciet homines, et dicet : Peccavi, et vere deliqui, et ut eram dignus, non recepi.
text_pt: Olhará para os homens, e dirá: Pequei, e perverti o direito, o que de nada me aproveitou.
text_el: εἶτα τότε ἀπομέμψεται ἄνθρωπος αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ λέγων οἷα συνετέλουν καὶ οὐκ ἄξια ἤτασέν με ὧν ἥμαρτον

text_en: He has delivered his soul from going into destruction, that it may live and see the light.
text_la: Liberavit animam suam, ne pergeret in interitum, sed vivens lucem videret.
text_pt: Porém Deus livrou a minha alma de ir para a cova, e a minha vida verá a luz.
text_el: σῶσον ψυχήν μου τοῦ μὴ ἐλθεῖν εἰς διαφθοράν καὶ ἡ ζωή μου φῶς ὄψεται

text_en: Behold, all these things God works three times within every one.
text_la: Ecce hæc omnia operatur Deus tribus vicibus per singulos,
text_pt: Eis que tudo isto é obra de Deus, duas e três vezes para com o homem,
text_el: ἰδοὺ πάντα ταῦτα ἐργᾶται ὁ ἰσχυρὸς ὁδοὺς τρεῖς μετὰ ἀνδρός

text_en: That he may withdraw their souls from corruption, and enlighten them with the light of the living.
text_la: ut revocet animas eorum a corruptione, et illuminet luce viventium.
text_pt: Para desviar a sua alma da perdição, e o iluminar com a luz dos viventes.
text_el: ἀλλ' ἐρρύσατο τὴν ψυχήν μου ἐκ θανάτου ἵνα ἡ ζωή μου ἐν φωτὶ αἰνῇ αὐτόν

text_en: Attend, Job, and hearken to me, and hold your peace, whilst I speak.
text_la: Attende, Job, et audi me : et tace, dum ego loquor.
text_pt: Escuta, pois, ó Jó, ouve-me; cala-te, e eu falarei.
text_el: ἐνωτίζου Ιωβ καὶ ἄκουέ μου κώφευσον καὶ ἐγώ εἰμι λαλήσω

text_en: But if you have anything to say, answer me, speak: for I would have you to appear just .
text_la: Si autem habes quod loquaris, responde mihi : loquere, volo enim te apparere justum.
text_pt: Se tens alguma coisa que dizer, responde-me; fala, porque desejo justificar-te.
text_el: εἰ εἰσὶν λόγοι ἀποκρίθητί μοι λάλησον θέλω γὰρ δικαιωθῆναί σε

text_en: And if you have not, hear me: hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.
text_la: Quod si non habes, audi me : tace, et docebo te sapientiam.
text_pt: Se não, escuta-me tu; cala-te, e ensinar-te-ei a sabedoria.
text_el: εἰ μή σὺ ἄκουσόν μου κώφευσον καὶ διδάξω σε σοφίαν

text_en: And Eliu continued his discourse, and said:
text_la: Pronuntians itaque Eliu, etiam hæc locutus est:
text_pt: Respondeu mais Eliú, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ελιους λέγει

text_en: Hear, wise men , my words, and you learned, hearken to me:
text_la: Audite, sapientes, verba mea : et eruditi, auscultate me.
text_pt: Ouvi, vós, sábios, as minhas razões; e vós, entendidos, inclinai os ouvidos para mim.
text_el: ἀκούσατέ μου σοφοί ἐπιστάμενοι ἐνωτίζεσθε τὸ καλόν

text_en: For the ear tries words, and the mouth discerns meats by the taste.
text_la: Auris enim verba probat, et guttur escas gustu dijudicat.
text_pt: Porque o ouvido prova as palavras, como o paladar experimenta a comida.
text_el: ὅτι οὖς λόγους δοκιμάζει καὶ λάρυγξ γεύεται βρῶσιν

text_en: Let us choose to us judgment, and let us see among ourselves what is the best.
text_la: Judicium eligamus nobis, et inter nos videamus quid sit melius.
text_pt: O que é direito escolhamos para nós; e conheçamos entre nós o que é bom.
text_el: κρίσιν ἑλώμεθα ἑαυτοῖς γνῶμεν ἀνὰ μέσον ἑαυτῶν ὅ τι καλόν

text_en: For Job has said: I am just , and God has overthrown my judgment.
text_la: Quia dixit Job : Justus sum, et Deus subvertit judicium meum.
text_pt: Porque Jó disse: Sou justo, e Deus tirou o meu direito.
text_el: ὅτι εἴρηκεν Ιωβ δίκαιός εἰμι ὁ κύριος ἀπήλλαξέν μου τὸ κρίμα

text_en: For in judging me there is a lie: my arrow is violent without any sin .
text_la: In judicando enim me mendacium est : violenta sagitta mea absque ullo peccato.
text_pt: Apesar do meu direito sou considerado mentiroso; a minha ferida é incurável, embora eu esteja sem transgressão.
text_el: ἐψεύσατο δὲ τῷ κρίματί μου βίαιον τὸ βέλος μου ἄνευ ἀδικίας

text_en: What man is there like Job, who drinks up scorning like water?
text_la: Quis est vir ut est Job, qui bibit subsannationem quasi aquam :
text_pt: Que homem há como Jó, que bebe a zombaria como água?
text_el: τίς ἀνὴρ ὥσπερ Ιωβ πίνων μυκτηρισμὸν ὥσπερ ὕδωρ

text_en: Who goes in company with them that work iniquity , and walks with wicked men ?
text_la: qui graditur cum operantibus iniquitatem, et ambulat cum viris impiis?
text_pt: E caminha em companhia dos que praticam a iniqüidade, e anda com homens ímpios?
text_el: οὐχ ἁμαρτὼν οὐδὲ ἀσεβήσας ἢ ὁδοῦ κοινωνήσας μετὰ ποιούντων τὰ ἄνομα τοῦ πορευθῆναι μετὰ ἀσεβῶν

text_en: For he has said: Man shall not please God , although he run with him.
text_la: Dixit enim : Non placebit vir Deo, etiam si cucurrerit cum eo.
text_pt: Porque disse: De nada aproveita ao homem o comprazer-se em Deus.
text_el: μὴ γὰρ εἴπῃς ὅτι οὐκ ἔσται ἐπισκοπὴ ἀνδρός καὶ ἐπισκοπὴ αὐτῷ παρὰ κυρίου

text_en: Therefore, you men of understanding, hear me: far from God be wickedness , and iniquity from the Almighty.
text_la: Ideo, viri cordati, audite me : absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas.
text_pt: Portanto vós, homens de entendimento, escutai-me: Longe de Deus esteja o praticar a maldade e do Todo-Poderoso o cometer a perversidade!
text_el: διό συνετοὶ καρδίας ἀκούσατέ μου μή μοι εἴη ἔναντι κυρίου ἀσεβῆσαι καὶ ἔναντι παντοκράτορος ταράξαι τὸ δίκαιον

text_en: For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward them.
text_la: Opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet eis.
text_pt: Porque, segundo a obra do homem, ele lhe paga; e faz a cada um segundo o seu caminho.
text_el: ἀλλὰ ἀποδιδοῖ ἀνθρώπῳ καθὰ ποιεῖ ἕκαστος αὐτῶν καὶ ἐν τρίβῳ ἀνδρὸς εὑρήσει αὐτόν

text_en: For in very deed God will not condemn without cause, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.
text_la: Vere enim Deus non condemnabit frustra, nec Omnipotens subvertet judicium.
text_pt: Também, na verdade, Deus não procede impiamente; nem o Todo-Poderoso perverte o juízo.
text_el: οἴῃ δὲ τὸν κύριον ἄτοπα ποιήσειν ἢ ὁ παντοκράτωρ ταράξει κρίσιν

text_en: What other has he appointed over the earth? Or whom has he set over the world which he made?
text_la: Quem constituit alium super terram? aut quem posuit super orbem quem fabricatus est?
text_pt: Quem lhe entregou o governo da terra? E quem fez todo o mundo?
text_el: ὃς ἐποίησεν τὴν γῆν τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανὸν καὶ τὰ ἐνόντα πάντα

text_en: If he turn his heart to him, he shall draw his spirit and breath unto himself.
text_la: Si direxerit ad eum cor suum, spiritum illius et flatum ad se trahet.
text_pt: Se ele pusesse o seu coração contra o homem, e recolhesse para si o seu espírito e o seu fôlego,
text_el: εἰ γὰρ βούλοιτο συνέχειν καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα παρ' αὐτῷ κατασχεῖν

text_en: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall return into ashes.
text_la: Deficiet omnis caro simul, et homo in cinerem revertetur.
text_pt: Toda a carne juntamente expiraria, e o homem voltaria para o pó.
text_el: τελευτήσει πᾶσα σὰρξ ὁμοθυμαδόν πᾶς δὲ βροτὸς εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσεται ὅθεν καὶ ἐπλάσθη

text_en: If then you have understanding, hear what is said, and hearken to the voice of my words.
text_la: Si habes ergo intellectum, audi quod dicitur, et ausculta vocem eloquii mei :
text_pt: Se, pois, há em ti entendimento, ouve isto; inclina os ouvidos ao som da minha palavra.
text_el: εἰ δὲ μὴ νουθετῇ ἄκουε ταῦτα ἐνωτίζου φωνὴν ῥημάτων

text_en: Can he be healed that loves not judgment? And how do you so far condemn him that is just ?
text_la: numquid qui non amat judicium sanari potest? et quomodo tu eum qui justus est in tantum condemnas?
text_pt: Porventura o que odiasse o direito se firmaria? E tu condenarias aquele que é justo e poderoso?
text_el: ἰδὲ σὺ τὸν μισοῦντα ἄνομα καὶ τὸν ὀλλύντα τοὺς πονηροὺς ὄντα αἰώνιον δίκαιον

text_en: Who says to the king: You are an apostate: who calls rulers ungodly:
text_la: Qui dicit regi : Apostata; qui vocat duces impios;
text_pt: Ou dir-se-á a um rei: Oh! Vil? Ou aos príncipes: Oh! ímpios?
text_el: ἀσεβὴς ὁ λέγων βασιλεῖ παρανομεῖς ἀσεβέστατε τοῖς ἄρχουσιν

text_en: Who accepts not the persons of princes: nor has regarded the tyrant, when he contended against the poor man : for all are the work of his hands.
text_la: qui non accipit personas principum, nec cognovit tyrannum cum disceptaret contra pauperem : opus enim manuum ejus sunt universi.
text_pt: Quanto menos àquele, que não faz acepção das pessoas de príncipes, nem estima o rico mais do que o pobre; porque todos são obras de suas mãos.
text_el: ὃς οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη πρόσωπον ἐντίμου οὐδὲ οἶδεν τιμὴν θέσθαι ἁδροῖς θαυμασθῆναι πρόσωπα αὐτῶν

text_en: They shall suddenly die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and they shall pass, and take away the violent without hand.
text_la: Subito morientur, et in media nocte turbabuntur populi : et pertransibunt, et auferent violentum absque manu.
text_pt: Eles num momento morrem; e até à meia-noite os povos são perturbados, e passam, e os poderosos serão tomados não por mão humana.
text_el: κενὰ δὲ αὐτοῖς ἀποβήσεται τὸ κεκραγέναι καὶ δεῖσθαι ἀνδρός ἐχρήσαντο γὰρ παρανόμως ἐκκλινομένων ἀδυνάτων

text_en: For his eyes are upon the ways of men , and he considers all their steps.
text_la: Oculi enim ejus super vias hominum, et omnes gressus eorum considerat.
text_pt: Porque os seus olhos estão sobre os caminhos de cada um, e ele vê todos os seus passos.
text_el: αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁρατής ἐστιν ἔργων ἀνθρώπων λέληθεν δὲ αὐτὸν οὐδὲν ὧν πράσσουσιν

text_en: There is no darkness, and there is no shadow of death, where they may be hid who work iniquity .
text_la: Non sunt tenebræ, et non est umbra mortis, ut abscondantur ibi qui operantur iniquitatem,
text_pt: Não há trevas nem sombra de morte, onde se escondam os que praticam a iniqüidade.
text_el: οὐδὲ ἔσται τόπος τοῦ κρυβῆναι τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὰ ἄνομα

text_en: For it is no longer in the power of man to enter into judgment with God .
text_la: neque enim ultra in hominis potestate est, ut veniat ad Deum in judicium.
text_pt: Porque Deus não sobrecarrega o homem mais do que é justo, para o fazer ir a juízo diante dele.
text_el: ὅτι οὐκ ἐπ' ἄνδρα θήσει ἔτι ὁ γὰρ κύριος πάντας ἐφορᾷ

text_en: He shall break in pieces many and innumerable, and shall make others to stand in their stead.
text_la: Conteret multos, et innumerabiles, et stare faciet alios pro eis.
text_pt: Quebranta aos fortes, sem que se possa inquirir, e põe outros em seu lugar.
text_el: ὁ καταλαμβάνων ἀνεξιχνίαστα ἔνδοξά τε καὶ ἐξαίσια ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμός

text_en: For he knows their works: and therefore he shall bring night on them, and they shall be destroyed.
text_la: Novit enim opera eorum, et idcirco inducet noctem, et conterentur.
text_pt: Ele conhece, pois, as suas obras; de noite os transtorna, e ficam moídos.
text_el: ὁ γνωρίζων αὐτῶν τὰ ἔργα καὶ στρέψει νύκτα καὶ ταπεινωθήσονται

text_en: He has struck them, as being wicked , in open sight.
text_la: Quasi impios percussit eos in loco videntium:
text_pt: Ele os bate como ímpios que são, à vista dos espectadores;
text_el: ἔσβεσεν δὲ ἀσεβεῖς ὁρατοὶ δὲ ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ

text_en: Who as it were on purpose have revolted from him, and would not understand all his ways:
text_la: qui quasi de industria recesserunt ab eo, et omnes vias ejus intelligere noluerunt :
text_pt: Porquanto se desviaram dele, e não compreenderam nenhum de seus caminhos,
text_el: ὅτι ἐξέκλιναν ἐκ νόμου θεοῦ δικαιώματα δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν

text_en: So that they caused the cry of the needy to come to him, and he heard the voice of the poor.
text_la: ut pervenire facerent ad eum clamorem egeni, et audiret vocem pauperum.
text_pt: De sorte que o clamor do pobre subisse até ele, e que ouvisse o clamor dos aflitos.
text_el: τοῦ ἐπαγαγεῖν ἐπ' αὐτὸν κραυγὴν πένητος καὶ κραυγὴν πτωχῶν εἰσακούσεται

text_en: For when he grants peace, who is there that can condemn? When he hides his countenance, who is there that can behold him, whether it regard nations, or all men ?
text_la: Ipso enim concedente pacem, quis est qui condemnet? ex quo absconderit vultum, quis est qui contempletur eum, et super gentes, et super omnes homines?
text_pt: Se ele aquietar, quem então inquietará? Se encobrir o rosto, quem então o poderá contemplar? Seja isto para com um povo, seja para com um homem só,
text_el: καὶ αὐτὸς ἡσυχίαν παρέξει καὶ τίς καταδικάσεται καὶ κρύψει πρόσωπον καὶ τίς ὄψεται αὐτόν καὶ κατὰ ἔθνους καὶ κατὰ ἀνθρώπου ὁμοῦ

text_en: Who makes a man that is a hypocrite to reign for the sins of the people?
text_la: Qui regnare facit hominem hypocritam propter peccata populi.
text_pt: Para que o homem hipócrita nunca mais reine, e não haja laços no povo.
text_el: βασιλεύων ἄνθρωπον ὑποκριτὴν ἀπὸ δυσκολίας λαοῦ

text_en: Seeing then I have spoken of God , I will not hinder you in your turn.
text_la: Quia ergo ego locutus sum ad Deum, te quoque non prohibebo.
text_pt: Na verdade, quem a Deus disse: Suportei castigo, não ofenderei mais.
text_el: ὅτι πρὸς τὸν ἰσχυρὸν ὁ λέγων εἴληφα οὐκ ἐνεχυράσω

text_en: If I have erred, teach me: if I have spoken iniquity , I will add no more.
text_la: Si erravi, tu doce me; si iniquitatem locutus sum, ultra non addam.
text_pt: O que não vejo, ensina-me tu; se fiz alguma maldade, nunca mais a hei de fazer?
text_el: ἄνευ ἐμαυτοῦ ὄψομαι σὺ δεῖξόν μοι εἰ ἀδικίαν ἠργασάμην οὐ μὴ προσθήσω

text_en: Does God require it of you, because it has displeased you? For you began to speak, and not I: but if you know anything better, speak.
text_la: Numquid a te Deus expetit eam, quia displicuit tibi? tu enim cœpisti loqui, et non ego : quod si quid nosti melius, loquere.
text_pt: Virá de ti como há de ser a recompensa, para que tu a rejeites? Faze tu, pois, e não eu, a escolha; fala logo o que sabes.
text_el: μὴ παρὰ σοῦ ἀποτείσει αὐτήν ὅτι ἀπώσῃ ὅτι σὺ ἐκλέξῃ καὶ οὐκ ἐγώ καὶ τί ἔγνως λάλησον

text_en: Let men of understanding speak to me, and let a wise man hearken to me.
text_la: Viri intelligentes loquantur mihi, et vir sapiens audiat me.
text_pt: Os homens de entendimento dirão comigo, e o homem sábio que me ouvir:
text_el: διὸ συνετοὶ καρδίας ἐροῦσιν ταῦτα ἀνὴρ δὲ σοφὸς ἀκήκοέν μου τὸ ῥῆμα

text_en: But Job has spoken foolishly, and his words sound not discipline.
text_la: Job autem stulte locutus est, et verba illius non sonant disciplinam.
text_pt: Jó falou sem conhecimento; e às suas palavras falta prudência.
text_el: Ιωβ δὲ οὐκ ἐν συνέσει ἐλάλησεν τὰ δὲ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐν ἐπιστήμῃ

text_en: My father, let Job be tried even to the end: cease not from the man of iniquity .
text_la: Pater mi, probetur Job usque ad finem : ne desinas ab homine iniquitatis :
text_pt: Pai meu! Provado seja Jó até ao fim, pelas suas respostas próprias de homens malignos.
text_el: οὐ μὴν δὲ ἀλλὰ μάθε Ιωβ μὴ δῷς ἔτι ἀνταπόκρισιν ὥσπερ οἱ ἄφρονες

text_en: Because he adds blasphemy upon his sins , let him be tied fast in the mean time amongst us: and then let him provoke God to judgment with his speeches.
text_la: quia addit super peccata sua blasphemiam, inter nos interim constringatur : et tunc ad judicium provocet sermonibus suis Deum.
text_pt: Porque ao seu pecado acrescenta a transgressão; entre nós bate palmas, e multiplica contra Deus as suas palavras.
text_el: ἵνα μὴ προσθῶμεν ἐφ' ἁμαρτίαις ἡμῶν ἀνομία δὲ ἐφ' ἡμῖν λογισθήσεται πολλὰ λαλούντων ῥήματα ἐναντίον τοῦ κυρίου

text_en: Moreover Eliu spoke these words:
text_la: Igitur Eliu hæc rursum locutus est:
text_pt: Respondeu mais Eliú, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ελιους λέγει

text_en: Does your thought seem right to you, that you should say: I am more just than God ?
text_la: Numquid æqua tibi videtur tua cogitatio, ut diceres : Justior sum Deo?
text_pt: Tens por direito dizeres: Maior é a minha justiça do que a de Deus?
text_el: τί τοῦτο ἡγήσω ἐν κρίσει σὺ τίς εἶ ὅτι εἶπας δίκαιός εἰμι ἔναντι κυρίου

text_en: For you said: That which is right does not please you: or what will it profit you if I sin ?
text_la: Dixisti enim : Non tibi placet quod rectum est : vel quid tibi proderit, si ego peccavero?
text_pt: Porque disseste: De que me serviria? Que proveito tiraria mais do que do meu pecado?
text_el: ἢ ἐρεῖς τί ποιήσω ἁμαρτών

text_en: Therefore I will answer your words, and your friends with you.
text_la: Itaque ego respondebo sermonibus tuis, et amicis tuis tecum.
text_pt: Eu te darei resposta, a ti e aos teus amigos contigo.
text_el: ἐγὼ σοὶ δώσω ἀπόκρισιν καὶ τοῖς τρισὶν φίλοις σου

text_en: Look up to heaven and see, and behold the sky, that it is higher than you.
text_la: Suspice cælum, et intuere : et contemplare æthera quod altior te sit.
text_pt: Atenta para os céus, e vê; e contempla as mais altas nuvens, que são mais altas do que tu.
text_el: ἀνάβλεψον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἰδέ κατάμαθε δὲ νέφη ὡς ὑψηλὰ ἀπὸ σοῦ

text_en: If you sin , what shall you hurt him? And if your iniquities be multiplied, what shall you do against him?
text_la: Si peccaveris, quid ei nocebis? et si multiplicatæ fuerint iniquitates tuæ, quid facies contra eum?
text_pt: Se pecares, que efetuarás contra ele? Se as tuas transgressões se multiplicarem, que lhe farás?
text_el: εἰ ἥμαρτες τί πράξεις εἰ δὲ καὶ πολλὰ ἠνόμησας τί δύνασαι ποιῆσαι

text_en: And if you do justly , what shall you give him, or what shall he receive of your hand?
text_la: Porro si juste egeris, quid donabis ei? aut quid de manu tua accipiet?
text_pt: Se fores justo, que lhe darás, ou que receberá ele da tua mão?
text_el: ἐπεὶ δὲ οὖν δίκαιος εἶ τί δώσεις αὐτῷ ἢ τί ἐκ χειρός σου λήμψεται

text_en: Your wickedness may hurt a man that is like you: and your justice may help the son of man .
text_la: Homini qui similis tui est, nocebit impietas tua : et filium hominis adjuvabit justitia tua.
text_pt: A tua impiedade faria mal a outro tal como tu; e a tua justiça aproveitaria ao filho do homem.
text_el: ἀνδρὶ τῷ ὁμοίῳ σου ἡ ἀσέβειά σου καὶ υἱῷ ἀνθρώπου ἡ δικαιοσύνη σου

text_en: By reason of the multitude of oppressors they shall cry out: and shall wail for the violence of the arm of tyrants.
text_la: Propter multitudinem calumniatorum clamabunt, et ejulabunt propter vim brachii tyrannorum.
text_pt: Por causa das muitas opressões os homens clamam por causa do braço dos grandes.
text_el: ἀπὸ πλήθους συκοφαντούμενοι κεκράξονται βοήσονται ἀπὸ βραχίονος πολλῶν

text_en: And he has not said: Where is God , who made me, who has given songs in the night?
text_la: Et non dixit : Ubi est Deus qui fecit me, qui dedit carmina in nocte;
text_pt: Porém ninguém diz: Onde está Deus que me criou, que dá salmos durante a noite;
text_el: καὶ οὐκ εἶπεν ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας με ὁ κατατάσσων φυλακὰς νυκτερινάς

text_en: Who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, and instructs us more than the fowls of the air.
text_la: qui docet nos super jumenta terræ, et super volucres cæli erudit nos?
text_pt: Que nos ensina mais do que aos animais da terra e nos faz mais sábios do que as aves dos céus?
text_el: ὁ διορίζων με ἀπὸ τετραπόδων γῆς ἀπὸ δὲ πετεινῶν οὐρανοῦ

text_en: There shall they cry, and he will not hear, because of the pride of evil men .
text_la: Ibi clamabunt, et non exaudiet, propter superbiam malorum.
text_pt: Clamam, porém ele não responde, por causa da arrogância dos maus.
text_el: ἐκεῖ κεκράξονται καὶ οὐ μὴ εἰσακούσῃ καὶ ἀπὸ ὕβρεως πονηρῶν

text_en: God therefore will not hear in vain, and the Almighty will look into the causes of every one.
text_la: Non ergo frustra audiet Deus, et Omnipotens causas singulorum intuebitur.
text_pt: Certo é que Deus não ouvirá a vaidade, nem atentará para ela o Todo-Poderoso.
text_el: ἄτοπα γὰρ οὐ βούλεται ὁ κύριος ἰδεῖν αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὁρατής ἐστιν

text_en: Yea, when you shall say: He considers not: be judged before him, and expect him.
text_la: Etiam cum dixeris : Non considerat : judicare coram illo, et expecta eum.
text_pt: E quanto ao que disseste, que o não verás, juízo há perante ele; por isso espera nele.
text_el: τῶν συντελούντων τὰ ἄνομα καὶ σώσει με κρίθητι δὲ ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ εἰ δύνασαι αἰνέσαι αὐτόν ὡς ἔστιν

text_en: For he does not now bring on his fury, neither does he revenge wickedness exceedingly.
text_la: Nunc enim non infert furorem suum, nec ulciscitur scelus valde.
text_pt: Mas agora, porque a sua ira ainda não se exerce, nem grandemente considera a arrogância,
text_el: καὶ νῦν ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπισκεπτόμενος ὀργὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνω παραπτώματι σφόδρα

text_en: Therefore Job opens his mouth in vain, and multiplies words without knowledge.
text_la: Ergo Job frustra aperit os suum, et absque scientia verba multiplicat.
text_pt: Logo Jó em vão abre a sua boca, e sem ciência multiplica palavras.
text_el: καὶ Ιωβ ματαίως ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀγνωσίᾳ ῥήματα βαρύνει

text_en: Eliu also proceeded, and said:
text_la: Addens quoque Eliu, hæc locutus est:
text_pt: Prosseguiu ainda Eliú, e disse:
text_el: προσθεὶς δὲ Ελιους ἔτι λέγει

text_en: Suffer me a little, and I will show you: for I have yet somewhat to speak in God's behalf.
text_la: Sustine me paululum, et indicabo tibi : adhuc enim habeo quod pro Deo loquar.
text_pt: Espera-me um pouco, e mostrar-te-ei que ainda há razões a favor de Deus.
text_el: μεῖνόν με μικρὸν ἔτι ἵνα διδάξω σε ἔτι γὰρ ἐν ἐμοί ἐστιν λέξις

text_en: I will repeat my knowledge from the beginning, and I will prove my Maker just .
text_la: Repetam scientiam meam a principio, et operatorem meum probabo justum.
text_pt: De longe trarei o meu conhecimento; e ao meu Criador atribuirei a justiça.
text_el: ἀναλαβὼν τὴν ἐπιστήμην μου μακρὰν ἔργοις δέ μου δίκαια ἐρῶ

text_en: For indeed my words are without a lie, and perfect knowledge shall be proved to you.
text_la: Vere enim absque mendacio sermones mei, et perfecta scientia probabitur tibi.
text_pt: Porque na verdade, as minhas palavras não serão falsas; contigo está um que tem perfeito conhecimento.
text_el: ἐπ' ἀληθείας καὶ οὐκ ἄδικα ῥήματα ἀδίκως συνίεις

text_en: God does not cast away the mighty, whereas he himself also is mighty.
text_la: Deus potentes non abjicit, cum et ipse sit potens :
text_pt: Eis que Deus é mui grande, contudo a ninguém despreza; grande é em força e sabedoria.
text_el: γίγνωσκε δὲ ὅτι ὁ κύριος οὐ μὴ ἀποποιήσηται τὸν ἄκακον δυνατὸς ἰσχύι καρδίας

text_en: But he saves not the wicked, and he gives judgment to the poor.
text_la: sed non salvat impios, et judicium pauperibus tribuit.
text_pt: Ele não preserva a vida do ímpio, e faz justiça aos aflitos.
text_el: ἀσεβῆ οὐ μὴ ζωοποιήσει καὶ κρίμα πτωχῶν δώσει

text_en: He will not take away his eyes from the just , and he places kings on the throne for ever, and they are exalted.
text_la: Non auferet a justo oculos suos : et reges in solio collocat in perpetuum, et illi eriguntur.
text_pt: Do justo não tira os seus olhos; antes estão com os reis no trono; ali os assenta para sempre, e assim são exaltados.
text_el: οὐκ ἀφελεῖ ἀπὸ δικαίου ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ μετὰ βασιλέων εἰς θρόνον καὶ καθιεῖ αὐτοὺς εἰς νεῖκος καὶ ὑψωθήσονται

text_en: And if they shall be in chains, and be bound with the cords of poverty:
text_la: Et si fuerint in catenis, et vinciantur funibus paupertatis,
text_pt: E se estão presos em grilhões, amarrados com cordas de aflição,
text_el: καὶ εἰ πεπεδημένοι ἐν χειροπέδαις συσχεθήσονται ἐν σχοινίοις πενίας

text_en: He shall show them their works, and their wicked deeds, because they have been violent .
text_la: indicabit eis opera eorum, et scelera eorum, quia violenti fuerunt.
text_pt: Então lhes faz saber a obra deles, e as suas transgressões, porquanto prevaleceram nelas.
text_el: καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν καὶ τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν ὅτι ἰσχύσουσιν

text_en: He also shall open their ear, to correct them: and shall speak, that they may return from iniquity .
text_la: Revelabit quoque aurem eorum, ut corripiat : et loquetur, ut revertantur ab iniquitate.
text_pt: Abre-lhes também os seus ouvidos, para sua disciplina, e ordena-lhes que se convertam da maldade.
text_el: ἀλλὰ τοῦ δικαίου εἰσακούσεται καὶ εἶπεν ὅτι ἐπιστραφήσονται ἐξ ἀδικίας

text_en: If they shall hear and observe, they shall accomplish their days in good , and their years in glory .
text_la: Si audierint et observaverint, complebunt dies suos in bono, et annos suos in gloria :
text_pt: Se o ouvirem, e o servirem, acabarão seus dias em bem, e os seus anos em delícias.
text_el: ἐὰν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ δουλεύσωσιν συντελέσουσιν τὰς ἡμέρας αὐτῶν ἐν ἀγαθοῖς καὶ τὰ ἔτη αὐτῶν ἐν εὐπρεπείαις

text_en: But if they hear not, they shall pass by the sword, and shall be consumed in folly.
text_la: si autem non audierint, transibunt per gladium, et consumentur in stultitia.
text_pt: Porém se não o ouvirem, à espada serão passados, e expirarão sem conhecimento.
text_el: ἀσεβεῖς δὲ οὐ διασῴζει παρὰ τὸ μὴ βούλεσθαι εἰδέναι αὐτοὺς τὸν κύριον καὶ διότι νουθετούμενοι ἀνήκοοι ἦσαν

text_en: Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God , neither shall they cry when they are bound.
text_la: Simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei, neque clamabunt cum vincti fuerint.
text_pt: E os hipócritas de coração amontoam para si a ira; e amarrando-os ele, não clamam por socorro.
text_el: καὶ ὑποκριταὶ καρδίᾳ τάξουσιν θυμόν οὐ βοήσονται ὅτι ἔδησεν αὐτούς

text_en: Their soul shall die in a storm, and their life among the effeminate.
text_la: Morietur in tempestate anima eorum, et vita eorum inter effeminatos.
text_pt: A sua alma morre na mocidade, e a sua vida perece entre os impuros.
text_el: ἀποθάνοι τοίνυν ἐν νεότητι ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτῶν ἡ δὲ ζωὴ αὐτῶν τιτρωσκομένη ὑπὸ ἀγγέλων

text_en: He shall deliver the poor out of his distress, and shall open his ear in affliction.
text_la: Eripiet de angustia sua pauperem, et revelabit in tribulatione aurem ejus.
text_pt: Ao aflito livra da sua aflição, e na opressão se revela aos seus ouvidos.
text_el: ἀνθ' ὧν ἔθλιψαν ἀσθενῆ καὶ ἀδύνατον κρίμα δὲ πραέων ἐκθήσει

text_en: Therefore he shall set you at large out of the narrow mouth, and which has no foundation under it: and the rest of your table shall be full of fatness.
text_la: Igitur salvabit te de ore angusto latissime, et non habente fundamentum subter se : requies autem mensæ tuæ erit plena pinguedine.
text_pt: Assim também te desviará da boca da angústia para um lugar espaçoso, em que não há aperto, e as iguarias da tua mesa serão cheias de gordura.
text_el: καὶ προσέτι ἠπάτησέν σε ἐκ στόματος ἐχθροῦ ἄβυσσος κατάχυσις ὑποκάτω αὐτῆς καὶ κατέβη τράπεζά σου πλήρης πιότητος
