text_en: Your cause has been judged as that of the wicked, cause and judgment you shall recover.
text_la: Causa tua quasi impii judicata est : causam judiciumque recipies.
text_pt: Mas tu estás cheio do juízo do ímpio; o juízo e a justiça te sustentam.
text_el: οὐχ ὑστερήσει δὲ ἀπὸ δικαίων κρίμα

text_en: Therefore let not anger overcome you to oppress any man : neither let multitude of gifts turn you aside.
text_la: Non te ergo superet ira ut aliquem opprimas : nec multitudo donorum inclinet te.
text_pt: Porquanto há furor, guarda-te de que não sejas atingido pelo castigo violento, pois nem com resgate algum te livrarias dele.
text_el: θυμὸς δὲ ἐπ' ἀσεβεῖς ἔσται δι' ἀσέβειαν δώρων ὧν ἐδέχοντο ἐπ' ἀδικίαις

text_en: Lay down your greatness without tribulation, and all the mighty of strength.
text_la: Depone magnitudinem tuam absque tribulatione, et omnes robustos fortitudine.
text_pt: Estimaria ele tanto tuas riquezas? Não, nem ouro, nem todas as forças do poder.
text_el: μή σε ἐκκλινάτω ἑκὼν ὁ νοῦς δεήσεως ἐν ἀνάγκῃ ὄντων ἀδυνάτων καὶ πάντας τοὺς κραταιοῦντας ἰσχύν

text_en: Prolong not the night that people may come up for them.
text_la: Ne protrahas noctem, ut ascendant populi pro eis.
text_pt: Não suspires pela noite, em que os povos sejam tomados do seu lugar.
text_el: μὴ ἐξελκύσῃς τὴν νύκτα τοῦ ἀναβῆναι λαοὺς ἀντ' αὐτῶν

text_en: Beware that you turn not aside to iniquity : for this you have begun to follow after misery.
text_la: Cave ne declines ad iniquitatem : hanc enim cœpisti sequi post miseriam.
text_pt: Guarda-te, e não declines para a iniqüidade; porquanto isso escolheste antes que a aflição.
text_el: ἀλλὰ φύλαξαι μὴ πράξῃς ἄτοπα ἐπὶ τοῦτον γὰρ ἐξείλω ἀπὸ πτωχείας

text_en: Behold, God is high in his strength, and none is like him among the lawgivers.
text_la: Ecce Deus excelsus in fortitudine sua, et nullus ei similis in legislatoribus.
text_pt: Eis que Deus é excelso em seu poder; quem ensina como ele?
text_el: ἰδοὺ ὁ ἰσχυρὸς κραταιώσει ἐν ἰσχύι αὐτοῦ τίς γάρ ἐστιν κατ' αὐτὸν δυνάστης

text_en: Who can search out his ways? Or who can say to him: You have wrought iniquity ?
text_la: Quis poterit scrutari vias ejus? aut quis potest ei dicere : Operatus es iniquitatem?
text_pt: Quem lhe prescreveu o seu caminho? Ou, quem lhe dirá: Tu cometeste maldade?
text_el: τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ ἐτάζων αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα ἢ τίς ὁ εἴπας ἔπραξεν ἄδικα

text_en: Remember that you know not his work, concerning which men have sung.
text_la: Memento quod ignores opus ejus, de quo cecinerunt viri.
text_pt: Lembra-te de engrandecer a sua obra, que os homens contemplam.
text_el: μνήσθητι ὅτι μεγάλα ἐστὶν αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα ὧν ἦρξαν ἄνδρες

text_en: All men see him, every one beholds afar off.
text_la: Omnes homines vident eum : unusquisque intuetur procul.
text_pt: Todos os homens a vêem, e o homem a enxerga de longe.
text_el: πᾶς ἄνθρωπος εἶδεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὅσοι τιτρωσκόμενοί εἰσιν βροτοί

text_en: Behold, God is great, exceeding our knowledge: the number of his years is inestimable.
text_la: Ecce Deus magnus vincens scientiam nostram : numerus annorum ejus inæstimabilis.
text_pt: Eis que Deus é grande, e nós não o compreendemos, e o número dos seus anos não se pode esquadrinhar.
text_el: ἰδοὺ ὁ ἰσχυρὸς πολύς καὶ οὐ γνωσόμεθα ἀριθμὸς ἐτῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπέραντος

text_en: He lifts up the drops of rain, and pours out showers like floods:
text_la: Qui aufert stillas pluviæ, et effundit imbres ad instar gurgitum,
text_pt: Porque faz miúdas as gotas das águas que, do seu vapor, derramam a chuva,
text_el: ἀριθμηταὶ δὲ αὐτῷ σταγόνες ὑετοῦ καὶ ἐπιχυθήσονται ὑετῷ εἰς νεφέλην

text_en: Which flow from the clouds that cover all above.
text_la: qui de nubibus fluunt quæ prætexunt cuncta desuper.
text_pt: A qual as nuvens destilam e gotejam sobre o homem abundantemente.
text_el: ῥυήσονται παλαιώματα ἐσκίασεν δὲ νέφη ἐπὶ ἀμυθήτων βροτῶν

text_en: If he will spread out clouds as his tent,
text_la: Si voluerit extendere nubes quasi tentorium suum,
text_pt: Porventura pode alguém entender as extensões das nuvens, e os estalos da sua tenda?
text_el: καὶ ἐὰν συνῇ ἀπεκτάσεις νεφέλης ἰσότητα σκηνῆς αὐτοῦ

text_en: and lighten with his light from above, he shall cover also the ends of the sea.
text_la: et fulgurare lumine suo desuper, cardines quoque maris operiet.
text_pt: Eis que estende sobre elas a sua luz, e encobre as profundezas do mar.
text_el: ἰδοὺ ἐκτείνει ἐπ' αὐτὸν ηδω καὶ ῥιζώματα τῆς θαλάσσης ἐκάλυψεν

text_en: For by these he judges people, and gives food to many mortals.
text_la: Per hæc enim judicat populos, et dat escas multis mortalibus.
text_pt: Porque por estas coisas julga os povos e lhes dá mantimento em abundância.
text_el: ἐν γὰρ αὐτοῖς κρινεῖ λαούς δώσει τροφὴν τῷ ἰσχύοντι

text_en: In his hands he hides the light, and commands it to come again.
text_la: In manibus abscondit lucem, et præcepit ei ut rursus adveniat.
text_pt: Com as nuvens encobre a luz, e ordena não brilhar, interpondo a nuvem.
text_el: ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἐκάλυψεν φῶς καὶ ἐνετείλατο περὶ αὐτῆς ἐν ἀπαντῶντι

text_en: He shows his friend concerning it, that it is his possession, and that he may come up to it.
text_la: Annuntiat de ea amico suo, quod possessio ejus sit, et ad eam possit ascendere.
text_pt: O que nos dá a entender o seu pensamento, como também ao gado, acerca do temporal que sobe.
text_el: ἀναγγελεῖ περὶ αὐτοῦ φίλον αὐτοῦ κτῆσις καὶ περὶ ἀδικίας

text_en: At this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.
text_la: Super hoc expavit cor meum, et emotum est de loco suo.
text_pt: Sobre isto também treme o meu coração, e salta do seu lugar.
text_el: καὶ ταύτης ἐταράχθη ἡ καρδία μου καὶ ἀπερρύη ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτῆς

text_en: Hear attentively the terror of his voice, and the sound that comes out of his mouth.
text_la: Audite auditionem in terrore vocis ejus, et sonum de ore illius procedentem.
text_pt: Atentamente ouvi a indignação da sua voz, e o sonido que sai da sua boca.
text_el: ἄκουε ἀκοὴν ἐν ὀργῇ θυμοῦ κυρίου καὶ μελέτη ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐξελεύσεται

text_en: He beholds under all the heavens , and his light is upon the ends of the earth.
text_la: Subter omnes cælos ipse considerat, et lumen illius super terminos terræ.
text_pt: Ele o envia por debaixo de todos os céus, e a sua luz até aos confins da terra.
text_el: ὑποκάτω παντὸς τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀρχὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ φῶς αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πτερύγων τῆς γῆς

text_en: After it a noise shall roar, he shall thunder with the voice of his majesty, and shall not be found out, when his voice shall be heard.
text_la: Post eum rugiet sonitus; tonabit voce magnitudinis suæ : et non investigabitur, cum audita fuerit vox ejus.
text_pt: Depois disto ruge uma voz; ele troveja com a sua voz majestosa; e ele não os detém quando a sua voz é ouvida.
text_el: ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ βοήσεται φωνή βροντήσει ἐν φωνῇ ὕβρεως αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἀνταλλάξει αὐτούς ὅτι ἀκούσει φωνὴν αὐτοῦ

text_en: God shall thunder wonderfully with his voice, he that does great and unsearchable things.
text_la: Tonabit Deus in voce sua mirabiliter, qui facit magna et inscrutabilia;
text_pt: Com a sua voz troveja Deus maravilhosamente; faz grandes coisas, que nós não podemos compreender.
text_el: βροντήσει ὁ ἰσχυρὸς ἐν φωνῇ αὐτοῦ θαυμάσια ἐποίησεν γὰρ μεγάλα ἃ οὐκ ᾔδειμεν

text_en: He commands the snow to go down upon the earth, and the winter rain, and the shower of his strength.
text_la: qui præcipit nivi ut descendat in terram, et hiemis pluviis, et imbri fortitudinis suæ;
text_pt: Porque à neve diz: Cai sobre a terra; como também à garoa e à sua forte chuva.
text_el: συντάσσων χιόνι γίνου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ χειμὼν ὑετός καὶ χειμὼν ὑετῶν δυναστείας αὐτοῦ

text_en: He seals up the hand of all men , that every one may know his works.
text_la: qui in manu omnium hominum signat, ut noverint singuli opera sua.
text_pt: Ele sela as mãos de todo o homem, para que conheçam todos os homens a sua obra.
text_el: ἐν χειρὶ παντὸς ἀνθρώπου κατασφραγίζει ἵνα γνῷ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀσθένειαν

text_en: Then the beast shall go into his covert, and shall abide in his den.
text_la: Ingredietur bestia latibulum, et in antro suo morabitur.
text_pt: E as feras entram nos seus esconderijos e ficam nas suas cavernas.
text_el: εἰσῆλθεν δὲ θηρία ὑπὸ σκέπην ἡσύχασαν δὲ ἐπὶ κοίτης

text_en: Out of the inner parts shall a tempest come, and cold out of the north .
text_la: Ab interioribus egredietur tempestas, et ab Arcturo frigus.
text_pt: Da recâmara do sul sai o tufão, e do norte o frio.
text_el: ἐκ ταμιείων ἐπέρχονται δῖναι ἀπὸ δὲ ἀκρωτηρίων ψῦχος

text_en: When God blows there comes frost, and again the waters are poured out abundantly.
text_la: Flante Deo, concrescit gelu, et rursum latissimæ funduntur aquæ.
text_pt: Pelo sopro de Deus se dá a geada, e as largas águas se congelam.
text_el: καὶ ἀπὸ πνοῆς ἰσχυροῦ δώσει πάγος οἰακίζει δὲ τὸ ὕδωρ ὡς ἐὰν βούληται

text_en: Corn desires clouds, and the clouds spread their light:
text_la: Frumentum desiderat nubes, et nubes spargunt lumen suum.
text_pt: Também de umidade carrega as grossas nuvens, e esparge as nuvens com a sua luz.
text_el: καὶ ἐκλεκτὸν καταπλάσσει νεφέλη διασκορπιεῖ νέφος φῶς αὐτοῦ

text_en: Which go round about, wherever the will of him that governs them shall lead them, to whatsoever he shall command them upon the face of the whole earth:
text_la: Quæ lustrant per circuitum, quocumque eas voluntas gubernantis duxerit, ad omne quod præceperit illis super faciem orbis terrarum :
text_pt: Então elas, segundo o seu prudente conselho, se espalham em redor, para que façam tudo quanto lhes ordena sobre a superfície do mundo na terra.
text_el: καὶ αὐτὸς κυκλώματα διαστρέψει ἐν θεεβουλαθω εἰς ἔργα αὐτῶν πάντα ὅσα ἂν ἐντείληται αὐτοῖς ταῦτα συντέτακται παρ' αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

text_en: Whether in one tribe, or in his own land, or in what place soever of his mercy he shall command them to be found.
text_la: sive in una tribu, sive in terra sua, sive in quocumque loco misericordiæ suæ eas jusserit inveniri.
text_pt: Seja que por vara, ou para a sua terra, ou por misericórdia as faz vir.
text_el: ἐὰν εἰς παιδείαν ἐὰν εἰς τὴν γῆν αὐτοῦ ἐὰν εἰς ἔλεος εὑρήσει αὐτόν

text_en: Hearken to these things, Job: Stand, and consider the wondrous works of God .
text_la: Ausculta hæc, Job : sta, et considera mirabilia Dei.
text_pt: A isto, ó Jó, inclina os teus ouvidos; para, e considera as maravilhas de Deus.
text_el: ἐνωτίζου ταῦτα Ιωβ στῆθι νουθετοῦ δύναμιν κυρίου

text_en: Do you know when God commanded the rains, to show his light of his clouds?
text_la: Numquid scis quando præceperit Deus pluviis, ut ostenderent lucem nubium ejus?
text_pt: Porventura sabes tu como Deus as opera, e faz resplandecer a luz da sua nuvem?
text_el: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἔθετο ἔργα αὐτοῦ φῶς ποιήσας ἐκ σκότους

text_en: Do you know the great paths of the clouds, and the perfect knowledges?
text_la: Numquid nosti semitas nubium magnas, et perfectas scientias?
text_pt: Tens tu notícia do equilíbrio das grossas nuvens e das maravilhas daquele que é perfeito nos conhecimentos?
text_el: ἐπίσταται δὲ διάκρισιν νεφῶν ἐξαίσια δὲ πτώματα πονηρῶν

text_en: Are not your garments hot, when the south wind blows upon the earth?
text_la: Nonne vestimenta tua calida sunt, cum perflata fuerit terra austro?
text_pt: Ou de como as tuas roupas aquecem, quando do sul há calma sobre a terra?
text_el: σοῦ δὲ ἡ στολὴ θερμή ἡσυχάζεται δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

text_en: You perhaps have made the heavens with him, which are most strong, as if they were of molten brass.
text_la: Tu forsitan cum eo fabricatus es cælos, qui solidissimi quasi ære fusi sunt.
text_pt: Ou estendeste com ele os céus, que estão firmes como espelho fundido?
text_el: στερεώσεις μετ' αὐτοῦ εἰς παλαιώματα ἰσχυραὶ ὡς ὅρασις ἐπιχύσεως

text_en: Show us what we may say to him: or we are wrapped up in darkness.
text_la: Ostende nobis quid dicamus illi : nos quippe involvimur tenebris.
text_pt: Ensina-nos o que lhe diremos: porque nós nada poderemos pôr em boa ordem, por causa das trevas.
text_el: διὰ τί δίδαξόν με τί ἐροῦμεν αὐτῷ καὶ παυσώμεθα πολλὰ λέγοντες

text_en: Who shall tell him the things I speak? Even if a man shall speak, he shall be swallowed up.
text_la: Quis narrabit ei quæ loquor? etiam si locutus fuerit homo, devorabitur.
text_pt: Contar-lhe-ia alguém o que tenho falado? Ou desejaria um homem que ele fosse devorado?
text_el: μὴ βίβλος ἢ γραμματεύς μοι παρέστηκεν ἵνα ἄνθρωπον ἑστηκὼς κατασιωπήσω

text_en: But now they see not the light: the air on a sudden shall be thickened into clouds, and the wind shall pass and drive them away.
text_la: At nunc non vident lucem : subito aër cogetur in nubes, et ventus transiens fugabit eas.
text_pt: E agora não se pode olhar para o sol, que resplandece nas nuvens, quando o vento, tendo passado, o deixa limpo.
text_el: πᾶσιν δ' οὐχ ὁρατὸν τὸ φῶς τηλαυγές ἐστιν ἐν τοῖς παλαιώμασιν ὥσπερ τὸ παρ' αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ νεφῶν

text_en: Cold comes out of the north, and to God praise with fear.
text_la: Ab aquilone aurum venit, et ad Deum formidolosa laudatio.
text_pt: O esplendor de ouro vem do norte; pois, em Deus há uma tremenda majestade.
text_el: ἀπὸ βορρᾶ νέφη χρυσαυγοῦντα ἐπὶ τούτοις μεγάλη ἡ δόξα καὶ τιμὴ παντοκράτορος

text_en: We cannot find him worthily: he is great in strength, and in judgment, and in justice , and he is ineffable.
text_la: Digne eum invenire non possumus : magnus fortitudine, et judicio, et justitia : et enarrari non potest.
text_pt: Ao Todo-Poderoso não podemos alcançar; grande é em poder; porém a ninguém oprime em juízo e grandeza de justiça.
text_el: καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκομεν ἄλλον ὅμοιον τῇ ἰσχύι αὐτοῦ ὁ τὰ δίκαια κρίνων οὐκ οἴει ἐπακούειν αὐτόν

text_en: Therefore men shall fear him, and all that seem to themselves to be wise, shall not dare to behold him.
text_la: Ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes qui sibi videntur esse sapientes.
text_pt: Por isso o temem os homens; ele não respeita os que se julgam sábios de coração.
text_el: διὸ φοβηθήσονται αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνθρωποι φοβηθήσονται δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ σοφοὶ καρδίᾳ

text_en: Then the Lord answered Job out of a whirlwind, and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Dominus Job de turbine, dixit:
text_pt: Depois disto o SENHOR respondeu a Jó de um redemoinho, dizendo:
text_el: μετὰ δὲ τὸ παύσασθαι Ελιουν τῆς λέξεως εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ Ιωβ διὰ λαίλαπος καὶ νεφῶν

text_en: Who is this that wraps up sentences in unskilful words?
text_la: Quis est iste involvens sententias sermonibus imperitis?
text_pt: Quem é este que escurece o conselho com palavras sem conhecimento?
text_el: τίς οὗτος ὁ κρύπτων με βουλήν συνέχων δὲ ῥήματα ἐν καρδίᾳ ἐμὲ δὲ οἴεται κρύπτειν

text_en: Gird up your loins like a man : I will ask you, and answer me.
text_la: Accinge sicut vir lumbos tuos : interrogabo te, et responde mihi.
text_pt: Agora cinge os teus lombos, como homem; e perguntar-te-ei, e tu me ensinarás.
text_el: ζῶσαι ὥσπερ ἀνὴρ τὴν ὀσφύν σου ἐρωτήσω δέ σε σὺ δέ μοι ἀποκρίθητι

text_en: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me if you have understanding.
text_la: Ubi eras quando ponebam fundamenta terræ? indica mihi, si habes intelligentiam.
text_pt: Onde estavas tu, quando eu fundava a terra? Faze-mo saber, se tens inteligência.
text_el: ποῦ ἦς ἐν τῷ θεμελιοῦν με τὴν γῆν ἀπάγγειλον δέ μοι εἰ ἐπίστῃ σύνεσιν

text_en: Who has laid the measures thereof, if you know or who has stretched the line upon it?
text_la: Quis posuit mensuras ejus, si nosti? vel quis tetendit super eam lineam?
text_pt: Quem lhe pôs as medidas, se é que o sabes? Ou quem estendeu sobre ela o cordel?
text_el: τίς ἔθετο τὰ μέτρα αὐτῆς εἰ οἶδας ἢ τίς ὁ ἐπαγαγὼν σπαρτίον ἐπ' αὐτῆς

text_en: Upon what are its bases grounded? Or who laid the corner stone thereof,
text_la: Super quo bases illius solidatæ sunt? aut quis demisit lapidem angularem ejus,
text_pt: Sobre que estão fundadas as suas bases, ou quem assentou a sua pedra de esquina,
text_el: ἐπὶ τίνος οἱ κρίκοι αὐτῆς πεπήγασιν τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ βαλὼν λίθον γωνιαῖον ἐπ' αὐτῆς

text_en: when the morning stars praised me together, and all the sons of God made a joyful melody?
text_la: cum me laudarent simul astra matutina, et jubilarent omnes filii Dei?
text_pt: Quando as estrelas da alva juntas alegremente cantavam, e todos os filhos de Deus jubilavam?
text_el: ὅτε ἐγενήθησαν ἄστρα ᾔνεσάν με φωνῇ μεγάλῃ πάντες ἄγγελοί μου

text_en: Who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth as issuing out of the womb:
text_la: Quis conclusit ostiis mare, quando erumpebat quasi de vulva procedens;
text_pt: Ou quem encerrou o mar com portas, quando este rompeu e saiu da madre;
text_el: ἔφραξα δὲ θάλασσαν πύλαις ὅτε ἐμαίμασσεν ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτῆς ἐκπορευομένη

text_en: When I made a cloud the garment thereof, and wrapped it in a mist as in swaddling bands?
text_la: cum ponerem nubem vestimentum ejus, et caligine illud quasi pannis infantiæ obvolverem?
text_pt: Quando eu pus as nuvens por sua vestidura, e a escuridão por faixa?
text_el: ἐθέμην δὲ αὐτῇ νέφος ἀμφίασιν ὁμίχλῃ δὲ αὐτὴν ἐσπαργάνωσα

text_en: I set my bounds around it, and made it bars and doors:
text_la: Circumdedi illud terminis meis, et posui vectem et ostia,
text_pt: Quando eu lhe tracei limites, e lhe pus portas e ferrolhos,
text_el: ἐθέμην δὲ αὐτῇ ὅρια περιθεὶς κλεῖθρα καὶ πύλας

text_en: And I said: Hitherto you shall come, and shall go no further, and here you shall break your swelling waves.
text_la: et dixi : Usque huc venies, et non procedes amplius, et hic confringes tumentes fluctus tuos.
text_pt: E disse: Até aqui virás, e não mais adiante, e aqui se parará o orgulho das tuas ondas?
text_el: εἶπα δὲ αὐτῇ μέχρι τούτου ἐλεύσῃ καὶ οὐχ ὑπερβήσῃ ἀλλ' ἐν σεαυτῇ συντριβήσεταί σου τὰ κύματα

text_en: Did you since your birth command the morning, and show the dawning of the day its place?
text_la: Numquid post ortum tuum præcepisti diluculo, et ostendisti auroræ locum suum?
text_pt: Ou desde os teus dias deste ordem à madrugada, ou mostraste à alva o seu lugar;
text_el: ἦ ἐπὶ σοῦ συντέταχα φέγγος πρωινόν ἑωσφόρος δὲ εἶδεν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ τάξιν

text_en: And did you hold the extremities of the earth shaking them, and have you shaken the ungodly out of it?
text_la: Et tenuisti concutiens extrema terræ, et excussisti impios ex ea?
text_pt: Para que pegasse nas extremidades da terra, e os ímpios fossem sacudidos dela;
text_el: ἐπιλαβέσθαι πτερύγων γῆς ἐκτινάξαι ἀσεβεῖς ἐξ αὐτῆς

text_en: The seal shall be restored as clay, and shall stand as a garment.
text_la: Restituetur ut lutum signaculum, et stabit sicut vestimentum :
text_pt: E se transformasse como o barro sob o selo, e se pusessem como vestidos;
text_el: ἦ σὺ λαβὼν γῆν πηλὸν ἔπλασας ζῷον καὶ λαλητὸν αὐτὸν ἔθου ἐπὶ γῆς

text_en: From the wicked their light shall be taken away, and the high arm shall be broken.
text_la: auferetur ab impiis lux sua, et brachium excelsum confringetur.
text_pt: E dos ímpios se desvie a sua luz, e o braço altivo se quebrante;
text_el: ἀφεῖλας δὲ ἀπὸ ἀσεβῶν τὸ φῶς βραχίονα δὲ ὑπερηφάνων συνέτριψας

text_en: Have you entered into the depths of the sea, and walked in the lowest parts of the deep ?
text_la: Numquid ingressus es profunda maris, et in novissimis abyssi deambulasti?
text_pt: Ou entraste tu até às origens do mar, ou passeaste no mais profundo do abismo?
text_el: ἦλθες δὲ ἐπὶ πηγὴν θαλάσσης ἐν δὲ ἴχνεσιν ἀβύσσου περιεπάτησας

text_en: Have the gates of death been opened to you, and have you seen the darksome doors?
text_la: Numquid apertæ sunt tibi portæ mortis, et ostia tenebrosa vidisti?
text_pt: Ou descobriram-se-te as portas da morte, ou viste as portas da sombra da morte?
text_el: ἀνοίγονται δέ σοι φόβῳ πύλαι θανάτου πυλωροὶ δὲ ᾅδου ἰδόντες σε ἔπτηξαν

text_en: Have you considered the breadth of the earth? Tell me, if you know all things?
text_la: Numquid considerasti latitudinem terræ? indica mihi, si nosti, omnia :
text_pt: Ou com o teu entendimento chegaste às larguras da terra? Faze-mo saber, se sabes tudo isto.
text_el: νενουθέτησαι δὲ τὸ εὖρος τῆς ὑπ' οὐρανόν ἀνάγγειλον δή μοι πόση τίς ἐστιν

text_en: Where is the way where light dwells, and where is the place of darkness?
text_la: in qua via lux habitet, et tenebrarum quis locus sit :
text_pt: Onde está o caminho onde mora a luz? E, quanto às trevas, onde está o seu lugar;
text_el: ποίᾳ δὲ γῇ αὐλίζεται τὸ φῶς σκότους δὲ ποῖος ὁ τόπος

text_en: That you may bring everything to its own bounds, and understand the paths of the house thereof.
text_la: ut ducas unumquodque ad terminos suos, et intelligas semitas domus ejus.
text_pt: Para que as tragas aos seus limites, e para que saibas as veredas da sua casa?
text_el: εἰ ἀγάγοις με εἰς ὅρια αὐτῶν εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐπίστασαι τρίβους αὐτῶν

text_en: Did you know then that you should be born? And did you know the number of your days?
text_la: Sciebas tunc quod nasciturus esses, et numerum dierum tuorum noveras?
text_pt: De certo tu o sabes, porque já então eras nascido, e por ser grande o número dos teus dias!
text_el: οἶδα ἄρα ὅτι τότε γεγέννησαι ἀριθμὸς δὲ ἐτῶν σου πολύς

text_en: Have you entered into the storehouses of the snow, or have you beheld the treasures of the hail:
text_la: Numquid ingressus es thesauros nivis, aut thesauros grandinis aspexisti,
text_pt: Ou entraste tu até aos tesouros da neve, e viste os tesouros da saraiva,
text_el: ἦλθες δὲ ἐπὶ θησαυροὺς χιόνος θησαυροὺς δὲ χαλάζης ἑόρακας

text_en: Which I have prepared for the time of the enemy, against the day of battle and war ?
text_la: quæ præparavi in tempus hostis, in diem pugnæ et belli?
text_pt: Que eu retenho até ao tempo da angústia, até ao dia da peleja e da guerra?
text_el: ἀπόκειται δέ σοι εἰς ὥραν ἐχθρῶν εἰς ἡμέραν πολέμου καὶ μάχης

text_en: By what way is the light spread, and heat divided upon the earth?
text_la: Per quam viam spargitur lux, dividitur æstus super terram?
text_pt: Onde está o caminho em que se reparte a luz, e se espalha o vento oriental sobre a terra?
text_el: πόθεν δὲ ἐκπορεύεται πάχνη ἢ διασκεδάννυται νότος εἰς τὴν ὑπ' οὐρανόν

text_en: Who gave a course to violent showers, or a way for noisy thunder:
text_la: Quis dedit vehementissimo imbri cursum, et viam sonantis tonitrui,
text_pt: Quem abriu para a inundação um leito, e um caminho para os relâmpagos dos trovões,
text_el: τίς δὲ ἡτοίμασεν ὑετῷ λάβρῳ ῥύσιν ὁδὸν δὲ κυδοιμῶν

text_en: That it should rain on the earth without man in the wilderness , where no mortal dwells:
text_la: ut plueret super terram absque homine in deserto, ubi nullus mortalium commoratur;
text_pt: Para chover sobre a terra, onde não há ninguém, e no deserto, em que não há homem;
text_el: τοῦ ὑετίσαι ἐπὶ γῆν οὗ οὐκ ἀνήρ ἔρημον οὗ οὐχ ὑπάρχει ἄνθρωπος ἐν αὐτῇ

text_en: That it should fill the desert and desolate land, and should bring forth green grass?
text_la: ut impleret inviam et desolatam, et produceret herbas virentes?
text_pt: Para fartar a terra deserta e assolada, e para fazer crescer os renovos da erva?
text_el: τοῦ χορτάσαι ἄβατον καὶ ἀοίκητον καὶ τοῦ ἐκβλαστῆσαι ἔξοδον χλόης

text_en: Who is the father of rain? Or who begot the drops of dew?
text_la: Quis est pluviæ pater? vel quis genuit stillas roris?
text_pt: A chuva porventura tem pai? Ou quem gerou as gotas do orvalho?
text_el: τίς ἐστιν ὑετοῦ πατήρ τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ τετοκὼς βώλους δρόσου

text_en: Out of whose womb came the ice? And the frost from heaven who has gendered it?
text_la: De cujus utero egressa est glacies? et gelu de cælo quis genuit?
text_pt: De que ventre procedeu o gelo? E quem gerou a geada do céu?
text_el: ἐκ γαστρὸς δὲ τίνος ἐκπορεύεται ὁ κρύσταλλος πάχνην δὲ ἐν οὐρανῷ τίς τέτοκεν

text_en: The waters are hardened like a stone, and the surface of the deep is congealed.
text_la: In similitudinem lapidis aquæ durantur, et superficies abyssi constringitur.
text_pt: Como debaixo de pedra as águas se endurecem, e a superfície do abismo se congela.
text_el: ἣ καταβαίνει ὥσπερ ὕδωρ ῥέον πρόσωπον δὲ ἀβύσσου τίς ἔπηξεν

text_en: Shall you be able to join together the shining stars the Pleiades , or can you stop the turning about of Arcturus ?
text_la: Numquid conjungere valebis micantes stellas Pleiadas, aut gyrum Arcturi poteris dissipare?
text_pt: Ou poderás tu ajuntar as delícias do Sete-estrelo ou soltar os cordéis do Órion?
text_el: συνῆκας δὲ δεσμὸν Πλειάδος καὶ φραγμὸν Ὠρίωνος ἤνοιξας

text_en: Can you bring forth the day star in its time, and make the evening star to rise upon the children of the earth?
text_la: Numquid producis luciferum in tempore suo, et vesperum super filios terræ consurgere facis?
text_pt: Ou produzir as constelações a seu tempo, e guiar a Ursa com seus filhos?
text_el: ἦ διανοίξεις μαζουρωθ ἐν καιρῷ αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἕσπερον ἐπὶ κόμης αὐτοῦ ἄξεις αὐτά

text_en: Do you know the order of heaven , and can you set down the reason thereof on the earth?
text_la: Numquid nosti ordinem cæli, et pones rationem ejus in terra?
text_pt: Sabes tu as ordenanças dos céus, ou podes estabelecer o domínio deles sobre a terra?
text_el: ἐπίστασαι δὲ τροπὰς οὐρανοῦ ἢ τὰ ὑπ' οὐρανὸν ὁμοθυμαδὸν γινόμενα

text_en: Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, that an abundance of waters may cover you?
text_la: Numquid elevabis in nebula vocem tuam, et impetus aquarum operiet te?
text_pt: Ou podes levantar a tua voz até às nuvens, para que a abundância das águas te cubra?
text_el: καλέσεις δὲ νέφος φωνῇ καὶ τρόμῳ ὕδατος λάβρῳ ὑπακούσεταί σου

text_en: Can you send lightnings, and will they go, and will they return and say to you: Here we are?
text_la: Numquid mittes fulgura, et ibunt, et revertentia dicent tibi : Adsumus?
text_pt: Ou mandarás aos raios para que saiam, e te digam: Eis-nos aqui?
text_el: ἀποστελεῖς δὲ κεραυνοὺς καὶ πορεύσονται ἐροῦσιν δέ σοι τί ἐστιν

text_en: Who has put wisdom in the heart of man ? Or who gave the cock understanding?
text_la: Quis posuit in visceribus hominis sapientiam? vel quis dedit gallo intelligentiam?
text_pt: Quem pôs a sabedoria no íntimo, ou quem deu à mente o entendimento?
text_el: τίς δὲ ἔδωκεν γυναιξὶν ὑφάσματος σοφίαν ἢ ποικιλτικὴν ἐπιστήμην

text_en: Who can declare the order of the heavens , or who can make the harmony of heaven to sleep?
text_la: Quis enarrabit cælorum rationem? et concentum cæli quis dormire faciet?
text_pt: Quem numerará as nuvens com sabedoria? Ou os odres dos céus, quem os esvaziará,
text_el: τίς δὲ ὁ ἀριθμῶν νέφη σοφίᾳ οὐρανὸν δὲ εἰς γῆν ἔκλινεν

text_en: When was the dust poured on the earth, and the clods fastened together?
text_la: Quando fundebatur pulvis in terra, et glebæ compingebantur?
text_pt: Quando se funde o pó numa massa, e se apegam os torrões uns aos outros?
text_el: κέχυται δὲ ὥσπερ γῆ κονία κεκόλληκα δὲ αὐτὸν ὥσπερ λίθῳ κύβον

text_en: Will you take the prey for the lioness, and satisfy the appetite of her whelps,
text_la: Numquid capies leænæ prædam, et animam catulorum ejus implebis,
text_pt: Porventura caçarás tu presa para a leoa, ou saciarás a fome dos filhos dos leões,
text_el: θηρεύσεις δὲ λέουσιν βοράν ψυχὰς δὲ δρακόντων ἐμπλήσεις

text_en: when they couch in the dens and lie in wait in holes?
text_la: quando cubant in antris, et in specubus insidiantur?
text_pt: Quando se agacham nos covis, e estão à espreita nas covas?
text_el: δεδοίκασιν γὰρ ἐν κοίταις αὐτῶν κάθηνται δὲ ἐν ὕλαις ἐνεδρεύοντες

text_en: Who provides food for the raven, when her young ones cry to God , wandering about, because they have no meat?
text_la: Quis præparat corvo escam suam, quando pulli ejus clamant ad Deum, vagantes, eo quod non habeant cibos?
text_pt: Quem prepara aos corvos o seu alimento, quando os seus filhotes gritam a Deus e andam vagueando, por não terem o que comer?
text_el: τίς δὲ ἡτοίμασεν κόρακι βοράν νεοσσοὶ γὰρ αὐτοῦ πρὸς κύριον κεκράγασιν πλανώμενοι τὰ σῖτα ζητοῦντες

text_en: Do you know the time when the wild goats bring forth among the rocks, or have you observed the hinds when they fawn?
text_la: Numquid nosti tempus partus ibicum in petris, vel parturientes cervas observasti?
text_pt: Sabes tu o tempo em que as cabras montesas têm filhos, ou observastes as cervas quando dão suas crias?
text_el: εἰ ἔγνως καιρὸν τοκετοῦ τραγελάφων πέτρας ἐφύλαξας δὲ ὠδῖνας ἐλάφων

text_en: Have you numbered the months of their conceiving, or do you know the time when they bring forth?
text_la: Dinumerasti menses conceptus earum, et scisti tempus partus earum?
text_pt: Contarás os meses que cumprem, ou sabes o tempo do seu parto?
text_el: ἠρίθμησας δὲ αὐτῶν μῆνας πλήρεις τοκετοῦ ὠδῖνας δὲ αὐτῶν ἔλυσας

text_en: They bow themselves to bring forth young, and they cast them, and send forth roarings.
text_la: Incurvantur ad fœtum, et pariunt, et rugitus emittunt.
text_pt: Quando se encurvam, produzem seus filhos, e lançam de si as suas dores.
text_el: ἐξέθρεψας δὲ αὐτῶν τὰ παιδία ἔξω φόβου ὠδῖνας αὐτῶν ἐξαποστελεῖς

text_en: Their young are weaned and go to feed: they go forth, and return not to them.
text_la: Separantur filii earum, et pergunt ad pastum : egrediuntur, et non revertuntur ad eas.
text_pt: Seus filhos enrijam, crescem com o trigo; saem, e nunca mais tornam para elas.
text_el: ἀπορρήξουσιν τὰ τέκνα αὐτῶν πληθυνθήσονται ἐν γενήματι ἐξελεύσονται καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀνακάμψουσιν αὐτοῖς

text_en: Who has sent out the wild ass free, and who has loosed his bonds?
text_la: Quis dimisit onagrum liberum, et vincula ejus quis solvit?
text_pt: Quem despediu livre o jumento montês, e quem soltou as prisões ao jumento bravo,
text_el: τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ ἀφεὶς ὄνον ἄγριον ἐλεύθερον δεσμοὺς δὲ αὐτοῦ τίς ἔλυσεν

text_en: To whom I have given a house in the wilderness , and his dwellings in the barren land.
text_la: cui dedi in solitudine domum, et tabernacula ejus in terra salsuginis.
text_pt: Ao qual dei o ermo por casa, e a terra salgada por morada?
text_el: ἐθέμην δὲ τὴν δίαιταν αὐτοῦ ἔρημον καὶ τὰ σκηνώματα αὐτοῦ ἁλμυρίδα

text_en: He scorns the multitude of the city, he hears not the cry of the driver.
text_la: Contemnit multitudinem civitatis : clamorem exactoris non audit.
text_pt: Ri-se do ruído da cidade; não ouve os muitos gritos do condutor.
text_el: καταγελῶν πολυοχλίας πόλεως μέμψιν δὲ φορολόγου οὐκ ἀκούων

text_en: He looks round about the mountains of his pasture, and seeks for every green thing,
text_la: Circumspicit montes pascuæ suæ, et virentia quæque perquirit.
text_pt: A região montanhosa é o seu pasto, e anda buscando tudo que está verde.
text_el: κατασκέψεται ὄρη νομὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὀπίσω παντὸς χλωροῦ ζητεῖ

text_en: shall the rhinoceros be willing to serve you, or will he stay at your crib?
text_la: Numquid volet rhinoceros servire tibi, aut morabitur ad præsepe tuum?
text_pt: Ou, querer-te-á servir o boi selvagem? Ou ficará no teu curral?
text_el: βουλήσεται δέ σοι μονόκερως δουλεῦσαι ἢ κοιμηθῆναι ἐπὶ φάτνης σου

text_en: Can you bind the rhinoceros with your thong to plough, or will he break the clods of the valleys after you?
text_la: Numquid alligabis rhinocerota ad arandum loro tuo, aut confringet glebas vallium post te?
text_pt: Ou com corda amarrarás, no arado, ao boi selvagem? Ou escavará ele os vales após ti?
text_el: δήσεις δὲ ἐν ἱμᾶσι ζυγὸν αὐτοῦ ἢ ἑλκύσει σου αὔλακας ἐν πεδίῳ

text_en: Will you have confidence in his great strength, and leave your labours to him?
text_la: Numquid fiduciam habebis in magna fortitudine ejus, et derelinques ei labores tuos?
text_pt: Ou confiarás nele, por ser grande a sua força, ou deixarás a seu cargo o teu trabalho?
text_el: πέποιθας δὲ ἐπ' αὐτῷ ὅτι πολλὴ ἡ ἰσχὺς αὐτοῦ ἐπαφήσεις δὲ αὐτῷ τὰ ἔργα σου

text_en: Will you trust him that he will render you the seed, and gather it into your barnfloor?
text_la: Numquid credes illi quod sementem reddat tibi, et aream tuam congreget?
text_pt: Ou fiarás dele que te torne o que semeaste e o recolha na tua eira?
text_el: πιστεύσεις δὲ ὅτι ἀποδώσει σοι τὸν σπόρον εἰσοίσει δέ σου τὸν ἅλωνα

text_en: The wing of the ostrich is like the wings of the heron, and of the hawk.
text_la: Penna struthionis similis est pennis herodii et accipitris.
text_pt: A avestruz bate alegremente as suas asas, porém, são benignas as suas asas e penas?
text_el: πτέρυξ τερπομένων νεελασα ἐὰν συλλάβῃ ασιδα καὶ νεσσα

text_en: When she leaves her eggs on the earth, you perhaps will warm them in the dust.
text_la: Quando derelinquit ova sua in terra, tu forsitan in pulvere calefacies ea?
text_pt: Ela deixa os seus ovos na terra, e os aquenta no pó,
text_el: ὅτι ἀφήσει εἰς γῆν τὰ ᾠὰ αὐτῆς καὶ ἐπὶ χοῦν θάλψει

text_en: She forgets that the foot may tread upon them, or that the beasts of the field may break them.
text_la: Obliviscitur quod pes conculcet ea, aut bestia agri conterat.
text_pt: E se esquece de que algum pé os pode pisar, ou que os animais do campo os podem calcar.
text_el: καὶ ἐπελάθετο ὅτι ποὺς σκορπιεῖ καὶ θηρία ἀγροῦ καταπατήσει

text_en: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers, she has laboured in vain, no fear constraining her.
text_la: Duratur ad filios suos, quasi non sint sui : frustra laboravit, nullo timore cogente.
text_pt: Endurece-se para com seus filhos, como se não fossem seus; debalde é seu trabalho, mas ela está sem temor,
text_el: ἀπεσκλήρυνεν τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς ὥστε μὴ ἑαυτῇ εἰς κενὸν ἐκοπίασεν ἄνευ φόβου

text_en: For God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he given her understanding.
text_la: Privavit enim eam Deus sapientia, nec dedit illi intelligentiam.
text_pt: Porque Deus a privou de sabedoria, e não lhe deu entendimento.
text_el: ὅτι κατεσιώπησεν αὐτῇ ὁ θεὸς σοφίαν καὶ οὐκ ἐμέρισεν αὐτῇ ἐν τῇ συνέσει

text_en: When time shall be, she sets up her wings on high: she scorns the horse and his rider.
text_la: Cum tempus fuerit, in altum alas erigit : deridet equum et ascensorem ejus.
text_pt: A seu tempo se levanta ao alto; ri-se do cavalo, e do que vai montado nele.
text_el: κατὰ καιρὸν ἐν ὕψει ὑψώσει καταγελάσεται ἵππου καὶ τοῦ ἐπιβάτου αὐτοῦ

text_en: Will you give strength to the horse or clothe his neck with neighing?
text_la: Numquid præbebis equo fortitudinem, aut circumdabis collo ejus hinnitum?
text_pt: Ou darás tu força ao cavalo, ou revestirás o seu pescoço com crinas?
text_el: ἦ σὺ περιέθηκας ἵππῳ δύναμιν ἐνέδυσας δὲ τραχήλῳ αὐτοῦ φόβον

text_en: Will you lift him up like the locusts? The glory of his nostrils is terror.
text_la: Numquid suscitabis eum quasi locustas? gloria narium ejus terror.
text_pt: Ou espantá-lo-ás, como ao gafanhoto? Terrível é o fogoso respirar das suas ventas.
text_el: περιέθηκας δὲ αὐτῷ πανοπλίαν δόξαν δὲ στηθέων αὐτοῦ τόλμῃ

text_en: He breaks up the earth with his hoof, he prances boldly, he goes forward to meet armed men .
text_la: Terram ungula fodit; exultat audacter : in occursum pergit armatis.
text_pt: Escarva a terra, e folga na sua força, e sai ao encontro dos armados.
text_el: ἀνορύσσων ἐν πεδίῳ γαυριᾷ ἐκπορεύεται δὲ εἰς πεδίον ἐν ἰσχύι

text_en: He despises fear, he turns not his back to the sword.
text_la: Contemnit pavorem, nec cedit gladio.
text_pt: Ri-se do temor, e não se espanta, e não torna atrás por causa da espada.
text_el: συναντῶν βέλει καταγελᾷ καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀποστραφῇ ἀπὸ σιδήρου

text_en: Above him shall the quiver rattle, the spear and shield shall glitter.
text_la: Super ipsum sonabit pharetra; vibrabit hasta et clypeus :
text_pt: Contra ele rangem a aljava, o ferro flamante da lança e do dardo.
text_el: ἐπ' αὐτῷ γαυριᾷ τόξον καὶ μάχαιρα

text_en: Chasing and raging he swallows the ground, neither does he make account when the noise of the trumpet sounds.
text_la: fervens et fremens sorbet terram, nec reputat tubæ sonare clangorem.
text_pt: Agitando-se e indignando-se, serve a terra, e não faz caso do som da buzina.
text_el: καὶ ὀργῇ ἀφανιεῖ τὴν γῆν καὶ οὐ μὴ πιστεύσῃ ἕως ἂν σημάνῃ σάλπιγξ

text_en: When he hears the trumpet he says: Ha, ha: he smells the battle afar off, the encouraging of the captains , and the shouting of the army.
text_la: Ubi audierit buccinam, dicit : Vah! procul odoratur bellum : exhortationem ducum, et ululatum exercitus.
text_pt: Ao soar das buzinas diz: Eia! E cheira de longe a guerra, e o trovão dos capitàes, e o alarido.
text_el: σάλπιγγος δὲ σημαινούσης λέγει εὖγε πόρρωθεν δὲ ὀσφραίνεται πολέμου σὺν ἅλματι καὶ κραυγῇ

text_en: Does the hawk wax feathered by your wisdom, spreading her wings to the south?
text_la: Numquid per sapientiam tuam plumescit accipiter, expandens alas suas ad austrum?
text_pt: Ou voa o gavião pela tua inteligência, e estende as suas asas para o sul?
text_el: ἐκ δὲ τῆς σῆς ἐπιστήμης ἕστηκεν ἱέραξ ἀναπετάσας τὰς πτέρυγας ἀκίνητος καθορῶν τὰ πρὸς νότον

text_en: Will the eagle mount up at your command, and make her nest in high places?
text_la: Numquid ad præceptum tuum elevabitur aquila, et in arduis ponet nidum suum?
text_pt: Ou se remonta a águia ao teu mandado, e põe no alto o seu ninho?
text_el: ἐπὶ δὲ σῷ προστάγματι ὑψοῦται ἀετός γὺψ δὲ ἐπὶ νοσσιᾶς αὐτοῦ καθεσθεὶς αὐλίζεται

text_en: She abides among the rocks, and dwells among cragged flints, and stony hills, where there is no access.
text_la: In petris manet, et in præruptis silicibus commoratur, atque inaccessis rupibus.
text_pt: Nas penhas mora e habita; no cume das penhas, e nos lugares seguros.
text_el: ἐπ' ἐξοχῇ πέτρας καὶ ἀποκρύφῳ

text_en: From thence she looks for the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.
text_la: Inde contemplatur escam, et de longe oculi ejus prospiciunt.
text_pt: Dali descobre a presa; seus olhos a avistam de longe.
text_el: ἐκεῖσε ὢν ζητεῖ τὰ σῖτα πόρρωθεν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ σκοπεύουσιν

text_en: Her young ones shall suck up blood: and wheresoever the carcass shall be, she is immediately there.
text_la: Pulli ejus lambent sanguinem : et ubicumque cadaver fuerit, statim adest.
text_pt: E seus filhos chupam o sangue, e onde há mortos, ali está ela.
text_el: νεοσσοὶ δὲ αὐτοῦ φύρονται ἐν αἵματι οὗ δ' ἂν ὦσι τεθνεῶτες παραχρῆμα εὑρίσκονται

text_en: And the Lord went on, and said to Job:
text_la: Et adjecit Dominus, et locutus est ad Job:
text_el: καὶ ἀπεκρίθη κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ιωβ καὶ εἶπεν

text_en: Shall he that contends with God be so easily silenced? Surely he that reproves God , ought to answer him.
text_la: Numquid qui contendit cum Deo, tam facile conquiescit? utique qui arguit Deum, debet respondere ei.
text_el: μὴ κρίσιν μετὰ ἱκανοῦ ἐκκλινεῖ ἐλέγχων θεὸν ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτήν

text_en: Then Job answered the Lord , and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Job Domino, dixit:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει τῷ κυρίῳ

text_en: What can I answer, who has spoken inconsiderately? I will lay my hand upon my mouth.
text_la: Qui leviter locutus sum, respondere quid possum? manum meam ponam super os meum.
text_el: τί ἔτι ἐγὼ κρίνομαι νουθετούμενος καὶ ἐλέγχων κύριον ἀκούων τοιαῦτα οὐθὲν ὤν ἐγὼ δὲ τίνα ἀπόκρισιν δῶ πρὸς ταῦτα χεῖρα θήσω ἐπὶ στόματί μου

text_en: One thing I have spoken, which I wish I had not said: and another, to which I will add no more.
text_la: Unum locutus sum, quod utinam non dixissem : et alterum, quibus ultra non addam.
text_el: ἅπαξ λελάληκα ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ δευτέρῳ οὐ προσθήσω

text_en: And the Lord answering Job out of the whirlwind, said:
text_la: Respondens autem Dominus Job de turbine, dixit:
text_pt: Respondeu mais o SENHOR a Jó, dizendo:
text_el: ἔτι δὲ ὑπολαβὼν ὁ κύριος εἶπεν τῷ Ιωβ ἐκ τοῦ νέφους

text_en: Gird up your loins like a man : I will ask you, and you tell me.
text_la: Accinge sicut vir lumbos tuos : interrogabo te, et indica mihi.
text_pt: Porventura o contender contra o Todo-Poderoso é sabedoria? Quem argüi assim a Deus, responda por isso.
text_el: μή ἀλλὰ ζῶσαι ὥσπερ ἀνὴρ τὴν ὀσφύν σου ἐρωτήσω δέ σε σὺ δέ μοι ἀποκρίθητι

text_en: Will you make void my judgment: and condemn me, that you may be justified?
text_la: Numquid irritum facies judicium meum, et condemnabis me, ut tu justificeris?
text_pt: Então Jó respondeu ao Senhor, dizendo:
text_el: μὴ ἀποποιοῦ μου τὸ κρίμα οἴει δέ με ἄλλως σοι κεχρηματικέναι ἢ ἵνα ἀναφανῇς δίκαιος

text_en: And have you an arm like God , and can you thunder with a voice like him?
text_la: Et si habes brachium sicut Deus? et si voce simili tonas?
text_pt: Eis que sou vil; que te responderia eu? A minha mão ponho à boca.
text_el: ἦ βραχίων σοί ἐστιν κατὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἢ φωνῇ κατ' αὐτὸν βροντᾷς

text_en: Clothe yourself with beauty, and set yourself up on high, and be glorious , and put on goodly garments.
text_la: Circumda tibi decorem, et in sublime erigere, et esto gloriosus, et speciosis induere vestibus.
text_pt: Uma vez tenho falado, e não replicarei; ou ainda duas vezes, porém não prosseguirei.
text_el: ἀνάλαβε δὴ ὕψος καὶ δύναμιν δόξαν δὲ καὶ τιμὴν ἀμφίεσαι

text_en: Scatter the proud in your indignation, and behold every arrogant man , and humble him.
text_la: Disperge superbos in furore tuo, et respiciens omnem arrogantem humilia.
text_pt: Então o Senhor respondeu a Jó de um redemoinho, dizendo:
text_el: ἀπόστειλον δὲ ἀγγέλους ὀργῇ πᾶν δὲ ὑβριστὴν ταπείνωσον

text_en: Look on all that are proud , and confound them, and crush the wicked in their place,
text_la: Respice cunctos superbos, et confunde eos, et contere impios in loco suo.
text_pt: Cinge agora os teus lombos como homem; eu te perguntarei, e tu me explicarás.
text_el: ὑπερήφανον δὲ σβέσον σῆψον δὲ ἀσεβεῖς παραχρῆμα

text_en: hide them in the dust together, and plunge their faces into the pit.
text_la: Absconde eos in pulvere simul, et facies eorum demerge in foveam.
text_pt: Porventura também tornarás tu vão o meu juízo, ou tu me condenarás, para te justificares?
text_el: κρύψον δὲ εἰς γῆν ἔξω ὁμοθυμαδόν τὰ δὲ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ἀτιμίας ἔμπλησον

text_en: Then I will confess that your right hand is able to save you.
text_la: Et ego confitebor quod salvare te possit dextera tua.
text_pt: Ou tens braço como Deus, ou podes trovejar com voz como ele o faz?
text_el: ὁμολογήσω ἄρα ὅτι δύναται ἡ δεξιά σου σῶσαι

text_en: Behold behemoth whom I made with you, he eats grass like an ox.
text_la: Ecce behemoth quem feci tecum, fœnum quasi bos comedet.
text_pt: Orna-te, pois, de excelência e alteza; e veste-te de majestade e de glória.
text_el: ἀλλὰ δὴ ἰδοὺ θηρία παρὰ σοί χόρτον ἴσα βουσὶν ἐσθίει

text_en: His strength is in his loins, and his force in the navel of his belly.
text_la: Fortitudo ejus in lumbis ejus, et virtus illius in umbilico ventris ejus.
text_pt: Derrama os furores da tua ira, e atenta para todo o soberbo, e abate-o.
text_el: ἰδοὺ δὴ ἰσχὺς αὐτοῦ ἐπ' ὀσφύι ἡ δὲ δύναμις ἐπ' ὀμφαλοῦ γαστρός

text_en: He sets up his tail like a cedar , the sinews of his testicles are wrapped together.
text_la: Stringit caudam suam quasi cedrum; nervi testiculorum ejus perplexi sunt.
text_pt: Olha para todo o soberbo, e humilha-o, e atropela os ímpios no seu lugar.
text_el: ἔστησεν οὐρὰν ὡς κυπάρισσον τὰ δὲ νεῦρα αὐτοῦ συμπέπλεκται

text_en: His bones are like pipes of brass, his gristle like plates of iron.
text_la: Ossa ejus velut fistulæ æris; cartilago illius quasi laminæ ferreæ.
text_pt: Esconde-os juntamente no pó; ata-lhes os rostos em oculto.
text_el: αἱ πλευραὶ αὐτοῦ πλευραὶ χάλκειαι ἡ δὲ ῥάχις αὐτοῦ σίδηρος χυτός

text_en: He is the beginning of the ways of God , who made him, he will apply his sword.
text_la: Ipse est principium viarum Dei : qui fecit eum applicabit gladium ejus.
text_pt: Então também eu a ti confessarei que a tua mão direita te poderá salvar.
text_el: τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἀρχὴ πλάσματος κυρίου πεποιημένον ἐγκαταπαίζεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ

text_en: To him the mountains bring forth grass: there all the beasts of the field shall play.
text_la: Huic montes herbas ferunt : omnes bestiæ agri ludent ibi.
text_pt: Contemplas agora o beemote, que eu fiz contigo, que come a erva como o boi.
text_el: ἐπελθὼν δὲ ἐπ' ὄρος ἀκρότομον ἐποίησεν χαρμονὴν τετράποσιν ἐν τῷ ταρτάρῳ

text_en: He sleeps under the shadow, in the covert of the reed, and in moist places.
text_la: Sub umbra dormit in secreto calami, et in locis humentibus.
text_pt: Eis que a sua força está nos seus lombos, e o seu poder nos músculos do seu ventre.
text_el: ὑπὸ παντοδαπὰ δένδρα κοιμᾶται παρὰ πάπυρον καὶ κάλαμον καὶ βούτομον

text_en: The shades cover his shadow, the willows of the brook shall compass him about.
text_la: Protegunt umbræ umbram ejus : circumdabunt eum salices torrentis.
text_pt: Quando quer, move a sua cauda como cedro; os nervos das suas coxas estão entretecidos.
text_el: σκιάζονται δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ δένδρα μεγάλα σὺν ῥαδάμνοις καὶ κλῶνες ἄγνου

text_en: Behold, he will drink up a river, and not wonder: and he trusts that the Jordan may run into his mouth.
text_la: Ecce absorbebit fluvium, et non mirabitur, et habet fiduciam quod influat Jordanis in os ejus.
text_pt: Os seus ossos são como tubos de bronze; a sua ossada é como barras de ferro.
text_el: ἐὰν γένηται πλήμμυρα οὐ μὴ αἰσθηθῇ πέποιθεν ὅτι προσκρούσει ὁ Ιορδάνης εἰς τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ

text_en: In his eyes as with a hook he shall take him, and bore through his nostrils with stakes.
text_la: In oculis ejus quasi hamo capiet eum, et in sudibus perforabit nares ejus.
text_pt: Ele é obra-prima dos caminhos de Deus; o que o fez o proveu da sua espada.
text_el: ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ αὐτοῦ δέξεται αὐτόν ἐνσκολιευόμενος τρήσει ῥῖνα

text_en: Can you draw out the leviathan with a hook, or can you tie his tongue with a cord?
text_la: An extrahere poteris Leviathan hamo, et fune ligabis linguam ejus?
text_pt: Em verdade os montes lhe produzem pastos, onde todos os animais do campo folgam.
text_el: ἄξεις δὲ δράκοντα ἐν ἀγκίστρῳ περιθήσεις δὲ φορβεὰν περὶ ῥῖνα αὐτοῦ

text_en: Can you put a ring in his nose, or bore through his jaw with a buckle?
text_la: Numquid pones circulum in naribus ejus, aut armilla perforabis maxillam ejus?
text_pt: Deita-se debaixo das árvores sombrias, no esconderijo das canas e da lama.
text_el: εἰ δήσεις κρίκον ἐν τῷ μυκτῆρι αὐτοῦ ψελίῳ δὲ τρυπήσεις τὸ χεῖλος αὐτοῦ

text_en: Will he make many supplications to you, or speak soft words to you?
text_la: Numquid multiplicabit ad te preces, aut loquetur tibi mollia?
text_pt: As árvores sombrias o cobrem, com sua sombra; os salgueiros do ribeiro o cercam.
text_el: λαλήσει δέ σοι δεήσει ἱκετηρίᾳ μαλακῶς

text_en: Will he make a covenant with you, and will you take him to be a servant for ever,
text_la: Numquid feriet tecum pactum, et accipies eum servum sempiternum?
text_pt: Eis que um rio transborda, e ele não se apressa, confiando ainda que o Jordão se levante até à sua boca.
text_el: θήσεται δὲ διαθήκην μετὰ σοῦ λήμψῃ δὲ αὐτὸν δοῦλον αἰώνιον

text_en: shall you play with him as with a bird, or tie him up for your handmaids?
text_la: Numquid illudes ei quasi avi, aut ligabis eum ancillis tuis?
text_pt: Podê-lo-iam porventura caçar à vista de seus olhos, ou com laços lhe furar o nariz?
text_el: παίξῃ δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ ὥσπερ ὀρνέῳ ἢ δήσεις αὐτὸν ὥσπερ στρουθίον παιδίῳ

text_en: Shall friends cut him in pieces, shall merchants divide him?
text_la: Concident eum amici? divident illum negotiatores?
text_el: ἐνσιτοῦνται δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔθνη μεριτεύονται δὲ αὐτὸν φοινίκων γένη

text_en: Will you fill nets with his skin, and the cabins of fishes with his head?
text_la: Numquid implebis sagenas pelle ejus, et gurgustium piscium capite illius?
text_el: πᾶν δὲ πλωτὸν συνελθὸν οὐ μὴ ἐνέγκωσιν βύρσαν μίαν οὐρᾶς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν πλοίοις ἁλιέων κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ

text_en: Lay your hand upon him: remember the battle, and speak no more.
text_la: Pone super eum manum tuam : memento belli, nec ultra addas loqui.
text_el: ἐπιθήσεις δὲ αὐτῷ χεῖρα μνησθεὶς πόλεμον τὸν γινόμενον ἐν σώματι αὐτοῦ καὶ μηκέτι γινέσθω

text_en: Behold his hope shall fail him, and in the sight of all he shall be cast down.
text_la: Ecce spes ejus frustrabitur eum, et videntibus cunctis præcipitabitur.
text_el: οὐχ ἑόρακας αὐτὸν οὐδὲ ἐπὶ τοῖς λεγομένοις τεθαύμακας

text_en: I will not stir him up, like one that is cruel, for who can resist my countenance?
text_la: Non quasi crudelis suscitabo eum : quis enim resistere potest vultui meo?
text_pt: Poderás tirar com anzol o leviatã, ou ligarás a sua língua com uma corda?
text_el: οὐ δέδοικας ὅτι ἡτοίμασταί μοι τίς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἐμοὶ ἀντιστάς

text_en: Who has given me before that I should repay him? All things that are under heaven are mine.
text_la: Quis ante dedit mihi, ut reddam ei? omnia quæ sub cælo sunt, mea sunt.
text_pt: Podes pôr um anzol no seu nariz, ou com um gancho furar a sua queixada?
text_el: ἢ τίς ἀντιστήσεταί μοι καὶ ὑπομενεῖ εἰ πᾶσα ἡ ὑπ' οὐρανὸν ἐμή ἐστιν

text_en: I will not spare him, nor his mighty words, and framed to make supplication.
text_la: Non parcam ei, et verbis potentibus, et ad deprecandum compositis.
text_pt: Porventura multiplicará as súplicas para contigo, ou brandamente falará?
text_el: οὐ σιωπήσομαι δι' αὐτόν καὶ λόγον δυνάμεως ἐλεήσει τὸν ἴσον αὐτοῦ

text_en: Who can discover the face of his garment? Or who can go into the midst of his mouth?
text_la: Quis revelabit faciem indumenti ejus? et in medium oris ejus quis intrabit?
text_pt: Fará ele aliança contigo, ou o tomarás tu por servo para sempre?
text_el: τίς ἀποκαλύψει πρόσωπον ἐνδύσεως αὐτοῦ εἰς δὲ πτύξιν θώρακος αὐτοῦ τίς ἂν εἰσέλθοι

text_en: Who can open the doors of his face? His teeth are terrible round about.
text_la: Portas vultus ejus quis aperiet? per gyrum dentium ejus formido.
text_pt: Brincarás com ele, como se fora um passarinho, ou o prenderás para tuas meninas?
text_el: πύλας προσώπου αὐτοῦ τίς ἀνοίξει κύκλῳ ὀδόντων αὐτοῦ φόβος

text_en: His body is like molten shields, shut close up with scales pressing upon one another.
text_la: Corpus illius quasi scuta fusilia, compactum squamis se prementibus.
text_pt: Os teus companheiros farão dele um banquete, ou o repartirão entre os negociantes?
text_el: τὰ ἔγκατα αὐτοῦ ἀσπίδες χάλκειαι σύνδεσμος δὲ αὐτοῦ ὥσπερ σμιρίτης λίθος

text_en: One is joined to another, and not so much as any air can come between them:
text_la: Una uni conjungitur, et ne spiraculum quidem incedit per eas.
text_pt: Encherás a sua pele de ganchos, ou a sua cabeça com arpões de pescadores?
text_el: εἷς τοῦ ἑνὸς κολλῶνται πνεῦμα δὲ οὐ μὴ διέλθῃ αὐτόν

text_en: They stick one to another and they hold one another fast, and shall not be separated.
text_la: Una alteri adhærebit, et tenentes se nequaquam separabuntur.
text_pt: Põe a tua mão sobre ele, lembra-te da peleja, e nunca mais tal intentarás.
text_el: ἀνὴρ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ προσκολληθήσεται συνέχονται καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀποσπασθῶσιν

text_en: His sneezing is like the shining of fire, and his eyes like the eyelids of the morning.
text_la: Sternutatio ejus splendor ignis, et oculi ejus ut palpebræ diluculi.
text_pt: Eis que é vã a esperança de apanhá-lo; pois não será o homem derrubado só ao vê-lo?
text_el: ἐν πταρμῷ αὐτοῦ ἐπιφαύσκεται φέγγος οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ εἶδος ἑωσφόρου

text_en: Out of his mouth go forth lamps, like torches of lighted fire.
text_la: De ore ejus lampades procedunt, sicut tædæ ignis accensæ.
text_pt: Ninguém há tão atrevido, que a despertá-lo se atreva; quem, pois, é aquele que ousa erguer-se diante de mim?
text_el: ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐκπορεύονται λαμπάδες καιόμεναι καὶ διαρριπτοῦνται ἐσχάραι πυρός

text_en: Out of his nostrils goes smoke, like that of a pot heated and boiling.
text_la: De naribus ejus procedit fumus, sicut ollæ succensæ atque ferventis.
text_pt: Quem primeiro me deu, para que eu haja de retribuir-lhe? Pois o que está debaixo de todos os céus é meu.
text_el: ἐκ μυκτήρων αὐτοῦ ἐκπορεύεται καπνὸς καμίνου καιομένης πυρὶ ἀνθράκων

text_en: His breath kindles coals, and a flame comes forth out of his mouth.
text_la: Halitus ejus prunas ardere facit, et flamma de ore ejus egreditur.
text_pt: Não me calarei a respeito dos seus membros, nem da sua grande força, nem a graça da sua compostura.
text_el: ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἄνθρακες φλὸξ δὲ ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐκπορεύεται

text_en: In his neck strength shall dwell, and want goes before his face.
text_la: In collo ejus morabitur fortitudo, et faciem ejus præcedit egestas.
text_pt: Quem descobrirá a face da sua roupa? Quem entrará na sua couraça dobrada?
text_el: ἐν δὲ τραχήλῳ αὐτοῦ αὐλίζεται δύναμις ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ τρέχει ἀπώλεια

text_en: The members of his flesh cleave one to another: he shall send lightnings against him, and they shall not be carried to another place.
text_la: Membra carnium ejus cohærentia sibi : mittet contra eum fulmina, et ad locum alium non ferentur.
text_pt: Quem abrirá as portas do seu rosto? Pois ao redor dos seus dentes está o terror.
text_el: σάρκες δὲ σώματος αὐτοῦ κεκόλληνται καταχέει ἐπ' αὐτόν οὐ σαλευθήσεται

text_en: His heart shall be as hard as a stone, and as firm as a smith's anvil,
text_la: Cor ejus indurabitur tamquam lapis, et stringetur quasi malleatoris incus.
text_pt: As suas fortes escamas são o seu orgulho, cada uma fechada como com selo apertado.
text_el: ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ πέπηγεν ὡς λίθος ἕστηκεν δὲ ὥσπερ ἄκμων ἀνήλατος

text_en: when he shall raise him up, the angels shall fear, and being affrighted shall purify themselves.
text_la: Cum sublatus fuerit, timebunt angeli, et territi purgabuntur.
text_pt: Uma à outra se chega tão perto, que nem o ar passa por entre elas.
text_el: στραφέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ φόβος θηρίοις τετράποσιν ἐπὶ γῆς ἁλλομένοις

text_en: When a sword shall lay at him, it shall not be able to hold, nor a spear, nor a breastplate.
text_la: Cum apprehenderit eum gladius, subsistere non poterit, neque hasta, neque thorax :
text_pt: Umas às outras se ligam; tanto aderem entre si, que não se podem separar.
text_el: ἐὰν συναντήσωσιν αὐτῷ λόγχαι οὐδὲν μὴ ποιήσωσιν δόρυ ἐπηρμένον καὶ θώρακα

text_en: For he shall esteem iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
text_la: reputabit enim quasi paleas ferrum, et quasi lignum putridum æs.
text_pt: Cada um dos seus espirros faz resplandecer a luz, e os seus olhos são como as pálpebras da alva.
text_el: ἥγηται μὲν γὰρ σίδηρον ἄχυρα χαλκὸν δὲ ὥσπερ ξύλον σαθρόν

text_en: The archer shall not put him to flight, the stones of the sling are to him like stubble.
text_la: Non fugabit eum vir sagittarius : in stipulam versi sunt ei lapides fundæ.
text_pt: Da sua boca saem tochas; faíscas de fogo saltam dela.
text_el: οὐ μὴ τρώσῃ αὐτὸν τόξον χάλκειον ἥγηται μὲν πετροβόλον χόρτον

text_en: As stubble will he esteem the hammer, and he will laugh him to scorn who shakes the spear.
text_la: Quasi stipulam æstimabit malleum, et deridebit vibrantem hastam.
text_pt: Das suas narinas procede fumaça, como de uma panela fervente, ou de uma grande caldeira.
text_el: ὡς καλάμη ἐλογίσθησαν σφῦραι καταγελᾷ δὲ σεισμοῦ πυρφόρου

text_en: The beams of the sun shall be under him, and he shall strew gold under him like mire.
text_la: Sub ipso erunt radii solis, et sternet sibi aurum quasi lutum.
text_pt: O seu hálito faz incender os carvões; e da sua boca sai chama.
text_el: ἡ στρωμνὴ αὐτοῦ ὀβελίσκοι ὀξεῖς πᾶς δὲ χρυσὸς θαλάσσης ὑπ' αὐτὸν ὥσπερ πηλὸς ἀμύθητος

text_en: He shall make the deep sea to boil like a pot, and shall make it as when ointments boil.
text_la: Fervescere faciet quasi ollam profundum mare, et ponet quasi cum unguenta bulliunt.
text_pt: No seu pescoço reside a força; diante dele até a tristeza salta de prazer.
text_el: ἀναζεῖ τὴν ἄβυσσον ὥσπερ χαλκεῖον ἥγηται δὲ τὴν θάλασσαν ὥσπερ ἐξάλειπτρον

text_en: A path shall shine after him, he shall esteem the deep as growing old.
text_la: Post eum lucebit semita : æstimabit abyssum quasi senescentem.
text_pt: Os músculos da sua carne estão pegados entre si; cada um está firme nele, e nenhum se move.
text_el: τὸν δὲ τάρταρον τῆς ἀβύσσου ὥσπερ αἰχμάλωτον ἐλογίσατο ἄβυσσον εἰς περίπατον

text_en: There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him who was made to fear no one,
text_la: Non est super terram potestas quæ comparetur ei, qui factus est ut nullum timeret.
text_pt: O seu coração é firme como uma pedra e firme como a mó de baixo.
text_el: οὐκ ἔστιν οὐδὲν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὅμοιον αὐτῷ πεποιημένον ἐγκαταπαίζεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων μου

text_en: he beholds every high thing, he is king over all the children of pride .
text_la: Omne sublime videt : ipse est rex super universos filios superbiæ.
text_pt: Levantando-se ele, tremem os valentes; em razão dos seus abalos se purificam.
text_el: πᾶν ὑψηλὸν ὁρᾷ αὐτὸς δὲ βασιλεὺς πάντων τῶν ἐν τοῖς ὕδασιν

text_en: Then Job answered the Lord , and said:
text_la: Respondens autem Job Domino, dixit:
text_pt: Então respondeu Jó ao SENHOR, dizendo:
text_el: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ιωβ λέγει τῷ κυρίῳ

text_en: I know that you can do all things, and no thought is hid from you.
text_la: Scio quia omnia potes, et nulla te latet cogitatio.
text_pt: Bem sei eu que tudo podes, e que nenhum dos teus propósitos pode ser impedido.
text_el: οἶδα ὅτι πάντα δύνασαι ἀδυνατεῖ δέ σοι οὐθέν

text_en: Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have spoken unwisely, and things that above measure exceeded my knowledge.
text_la: Quis est iste qui celat consilium absque scientia? ideo insipienter locutus sum, et quæ ultra modum excederent scientiam meam.
text_pt: Quem é este, que sem conhecimento encobre o conselho? Por isso relatei o que não entendia; coisas que para mim eram inescrutáveis, e que eu não entendia.
text_el: τίς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ κρύπτων σε βουλήν φειδόμενος δὲ ῥημάτων καὶ σὲ οἴεται κρύπτειν τίς δὲ ἀναγγελεῖ μοι ἃ οὐκ ᾔδειν μεγάλα καὶ θαυμαστὰ ἃ οὐκ ἠπιστάμην

text_en: Hear, and I will speak: I will ask you, and you tell me.
text_la: Audi, et ego loquar : interrogabo te, et responde mihi.
text_pt: Escuta-me, pois, e eu falarei; eu te perguntarei, e tu me ensinarás.
text_el: ἄκουσον δέ μου κύριε ἵνα κἀγὼ λαλήσω ἐρωτήσω δέ σε σὺ δέ με δίδαξον

text_en: With the hearing of the ear, I have heard you, but now my eye sees you.
text_la: Auditu auris audivi te : nunc autem oculus meus videt te.
text_pt: Com o ouvir dos meus ouvidos ouvi, mas agora te vêem os meus olhos.
text_el: ἀκοὴν μὲν ὠτὸς ἤκουόν σου τὸ πρότερον νυνὶ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός μου ἑόρακέν σε

text_en: Therefore I reprehend myself, and do penance in dust and ashes.
text_la: Idcirco ipse me reprehendo, et ago pœnitentiam in favilla et cinere.
text_pt: Por isso me abomino e me arrependo no pó e na cinza.
text_el: διὸ ἐφαύλισα ἐμαυτὸν καὶ ἐτάκην ἥγημαι δὲ ἐμαυτὸν γῆν καὶ σποδόν

text_en: And after the Lord had spoken these words to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Themanite: My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends, because you have not spoken the thing that is right before me, as my servant Job has.
text_la: Postquam autem locutus est Dominus verba hæc ad Job, dixit ad Eliphaz Themanitem : Iratus est furor meus in te, et in duos amicos tuos, quoniam non estis locuti coram me rectum, sicut servus meus Job.
text_pt: Sucedeu que, acabando o Senhor de falar a Jó aquelas palavras, o Senhor disse a Elifaz, o temanita: A minha ira se acendeu contra ti, e contra os teus dois amigos, porque não falastes de mim o que era reto, como o meu servo Jó.
text_el: ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τὸ λαλῆσαι τὸν κύριον πάντα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα τῷ Ιωβ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος Ελιφας τῷ Θαιμανίτῃ ἥμαρτες σὺ καὶ οἱ δύο φίλοι σου οὐ γὰρ ἐλαλήσατε ἐνώπιόν μου ἀληθὲς οὐδὲν ὥσπερ ὁ θεράπων μου Ιωβ

text_en: Take unto you therefore seven oxen and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer for yourselves a holocaust , and my servant Job shall pray for you: his face I will accept, that folly be not imputed to you: for you have not spoken right things before me, as my servant Job has.
text_la: Sumite ergo vobis septem tauros et septem arietes, et ite ad servum meum Job, et offerte holocaustum pro vobis : Job autem servus meus orabit pro vobis. Faciem ejus suscipiam, ut non vobis imputetur stultitia : neque enim locuti estis ad me recta, sicut servus meus Job.
text_pt: Tomai, pois, sete bezerros e sete carneiros, e ide ao meu servo Jó, e oferecei holocaustos por vós, e o meu servo Jó orará por vós; porque deveras a ele aceitarei, para que eu não vos trate conforme a vossa loucura; porque vós não falastes de mim o que era reto como o meu servo Jó.
text_el: νῦν δὲ λάβετε ἑπτὰ μόσχους καὶ ἑπτὰ κριοὺς καὶ πορεύθητε πρὸς τὸν θεράποντά μου Ιωβ καὶ ποιήσει κάρπωσιν περὶ ὑμῶν Ιωβ δὲ ὁ θεράπων μου εὔξεται περὶ ὑμῶν ὅτι εἰ μὴ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ λήμψομαι εἰ μὴ γὰρ δι' αὐτόν ἀπώλεσα ἂν ὑμᾶς οὐ γὰρ ἐλαλήσατε ἀληθὲς κατὰ τοῦ θεράποντός μου Ιωβ

text_en: So Eliphaz the Themanite, and Baldad the Suhite, and Sophar the Naamathite went, and did as the Lord had spoken to them, and the Lord accepted the face of Job.
text_la: Abierunt ergo Eliphaz Themanites, et Baldad Suhites, et Sophar Naamathites, et fecerunt sicut locutus fuerat Dominus ad eos : et suscepit Dominus faciem Job.
text_pt: Então foram Elifaz, o temanita, e Bildade, o suíta, e Zofar, o naamatita, e fizeram como o Senhor lhes dissera; e o Senhor aceitou a face de Jó.
text_el: ἐπορεύθη δὲ Ελιφας ὁ Θαιμανίτης καὶ Βαλδαδ ὁ Σαυχίτης καὶ Σωφαρ ὁ Μιναῖος καὶ ἐποίησαν καθὼς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ κύριος καὶ ἔλυσεν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν αὐτοῖς διὰ Ιωβ

text_en: The Lord also was turned at the penance of Job, when he prayed for his friends. And the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.
text_la: Dominus quoque conversus est ad pœnitentiam Job, cum oraret ille pro amicis suis : et addidit Dominus omnia quæcumque fuerant Job, duplicia.
text_pt: E o Senhor virou o cativeiro de Jó, quando orava pelos seus amigos; e o Senhor acrescentou, em dobro, a tudo quanto Jó antes possuía.
text_el: ὁ δὲ κύριος ηὔξησεν τὸν Ιωβ εὐξαμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ καὶ περὶ τῶν φίλων αὐτοῦ ἀφῆκεν αὐτοῖς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἔδωκεν δὲ ὁ κύριος διπλᾶ ὅσα ἦν ἔμπροσθεν Ιωβ εἰς διπλασιασμόν

text_en: And all his brethren came to him, and all his sisters, and all that knew him before, and they ate bread with him in his house: and bemoaned him, and comforted him upon all the evil that God had brought upon him. And every man gave him one ewe, and one earring of gold.
text_la: Venerunt autem ad eum omnes fratres sui, et universæ sorores suæ, et cuncti qui noverant eum prius, et comederunt cum eo panem in domo ejus : et moverunt super eum caput, et consolati sunt eum super omni malo quod intulerat Dominus super eum : et dederunt ei unusquisque ovem unam, et inaurem auream unam.
text_pt: Então vieram a ele todos os seus irmãos, e todas as suas irmãs, e todos quantos dantes o conheceram, e comeram com ele pão em sua casa, e se condoeram dele, e o consolaram acerca de todo o mal que o Senhor lhe havia enviado; e cada um deles lhe deu uma peça de dinheiro, e um pendente de ouro.
text_el: ἤκουσαν δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ συμβεβηκότα αὐτῷ καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ πάντες ὅσοι ᾔδεισαν αὐτὸν ἐκ πρώτου φαγόντες δὲ καὶ πιόντες παρ' αὐτῷ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτόν καὶ ἐθαύμασαν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐπήγαγεν αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος ἔδωκεν δὲ αὐτῷ ἕκαστος ἀμνάδα μίαν καὶ τετράδραχμον χρυσοῦν ἄσημον

text_en: And the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. And he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
text_la: Dominus autem benedixit novissimis Job magis quam principio ejus : et facta sunt ei quatuordecim millia ovium, et sex millia camelorum, et mille juga boum, et mille asinæ.
text_pt: E assim abençoou o Senhor o último estado de Jó, mais do que o primeiro; pois teve catorze mil ovelhas, e seis mil camelos, e mil juntas de bois, e mil jumentas.
text_el: ὁ δὲ κύριος εὐλόγησεν τὰ ἔσχατα Ιωβ ἢ τὰ ἔμπροσθεν ἦν δὲ τὰ κτήνη αὐτοῦ πρόβατα μύρια τετρακισχίλια κάμηλοι ἑξακισχίλιαι ζεύγη βοῶν χίλια ὄνοι θήλειαι νομάδες χίλιαι

text_en: And he had seven sons, and three daughters.
text_la: Et fuerunt ei septem filii, et tres filiæ.
text_pt: Também teve sete filhos e três filhas.
text_el: γεννῶνται δὲ αὐτῷ υἱοὶ ἑπτὰ καὶ θυγατέρες τρεῖς

text_en: And he called the name of one Dies, and the name of the second Cassia, and the name of the third Cornustibii.
text_la: Et vocavit nomen unius Diem, et nomen secundæ Cassiam, et nomen tertiæ Cornustibii.
text_pt: E chamou o nome da primeira Jemima, e o nome da segunda Quezia, e o nome da terceira Quéren-Hapuque.
text_el: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὴν μὲν πρώτην Ἡμέραν τὴν δὲ δευτέραν Κασίαν τὴν δὲ τρίτην Ἀμαλθείας κέρας

text_en: And there were not found in all the earth women so beautiful as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
text_la: Non sunt autem inventæ mulieres speciosæ sicut filiæ Job in universa terra : deditque eis pater suus hæreditatem inter fratres earum.
text_pt: E em toda a terra não se acharam mulheres tão formosas como as filhas de Jó; e seu pai lhes deu herança entre seus irmãos.
text_el: καὶ οὐχ εὑρέθησαν κατὰ τὰς θυγατέρας Ιωβ βελτίους αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ὑπ' οὐρανόν ἔδωκεν δὲ αὐταῖς ὁ πατὴρ κληρονομίαν ἐν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς

text_en: And Job lived after these things, a hundred and forty years, and he saw his children, and his children's children, unto the fourth generation , and he died an old man , and full of days.
text_la: Vixit autem Job post hæc centum quadraginta annis, et vidit filios suos, et filios filiorum suorum usque ad quartam generationem : et mortuus est senex, et plenus dierum.
text_pt: E depois disto viveu Jó cento e quarenta anos; e viu a seus filhos, e aos filhos de seus filhos, até à quarta geração.
text_el: ἔζησεν δὲ Ιωβ μετὰ τὴν πληγὴν ἔτη ἑκατὸν ἑβδομήκοντα τὰ δὲ πάντα ἔζησεν ἔτη διακόσια τεσσαράκοντα ὀκτώ καὶ εἶδεν Ιωβ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ τετάρτην γενεάν

text_en: So Job died, {being} old and full of days.
text_pt: Então morreu Jó, velho e farto de dias.
text_el: καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν Ιωβ πρεσβύτερος καὶ πλήρης ἡμερῶν
